title: Bengals stock report: 4 ups, 2 downs and 1 big question after beating Bears The Bengals have good problems at receiver as backups shine, but there are still major questions about offensive line depth. Paul Dehner Jr.
summary:

CINCINNATI — This past week couldn’t have gone much better for coach Zac Taylor and the Cincinnati Bengals.
Two days after a dominant close to the joint practice against the Chicago Bears by the rebuilt defense, the roster depth Cincinnati is banking on as a weapon of attack this season showed off in a 27-9 win against Chicago.
Staff and players have discussed this as the deepest tea
full_text:
Rookie Colbie Young hauls in a touchdown pass against the Bears on Saturday night. Joseph Maiorana / Imagn Images
CINCINNATI — This past week couldn’t have gone much better for coach Zac Taylor and the Cincinnati Bengals.
Two days after a dominant close to the joint practice against the Chicago Bears by the rebuilt defense, the roster depth Cincinnati is banking on as a weapon of attack this season showed off in a 27-9 win against Chicago.
Staff and players have discussed this as the deepest team since Joe Burrow arrived — including Burrow himself. They’ve been largely proved right through eight quarters of preseason football.
Taylor had never won more than one game in a preseason. He will now shoot for the Bengals’ first undefeated preseason since 2006.
Here’s a look at what and who are trending up and down for the Bengals after Saturday’s win.
Cincinnati looked to reload the depth behind its stars at receiver, and Saturday night served as an exclamation point on that objective.
Dohnte Meyers, this training camp’s feel-good story , worked predominantly out of the slot, but he motioned everywhere across the line of scrimmage. He had five receptions for 41 yards and rushed once for 9 yards, all while returning kicks and punts with solid results.
Then, fourth-round pick Colbie Young eviscerated Bears cornerback Dontae Manning off the line of scrimmage and separated into the end zone for a 17-yard touchdown. He caught only three of eight targets, failing on multiple contested catches, which are typically his strong suit, but his touchdown provided a dramatic flash of his upside.
Then, his former Georgia teammate Noah Thomas broke free on the same route and hauled in an impressive diving touchdown in the back of the end zone from Sean Clifford.
Mitchell Tinsley, the breakout star of the 2025 preseason who earned a spot in the rotation last season for the Bengals, hasn’t been as flashy but still has Burrow’s trust in his second year in Cincinnati.
Josh Johnson and Clifford combined for 282 yards passing, three touchdowns and one interception. The receiver depth pops even for an 18-year NFL veteran.
“For sure, it starts with the top, though,” Johnson said. “You got guys like Ja’Marr (Chase) and Tee (Higgins) leading every day; it’s natural for everybody to raise their level of play because you watch those two guys go out and dominate daily. You see the younger guys; they just naturally pick up on it. (Receivers coach Troy Walters) does a great job of coaching them all really hard. What I love? They run. They all run. When you put pressure on the defense with guys running off the ball, it puts a lot of stress on them and helps a quarterback really see the space open up.”
The Bengals have tough decisions to make, especially considering the overflow of options at tight end. These are great problems to have, but perhaps somebody from these positions could be used to flip and shore up a lighter spot (see below)?
Neither player did anything notable in Saturday’s game. There were no standout plays or signature moments. Merely taking the field was the accomplishment.
All’s story is well documented as he played in his first game since Nov. 3, 2024, having had two ACL surgeries to repair all the damage in his knee. He’s been a full participant in practices throughout camp, but he can now check the box of returning to game action before he’s thrust into the mix in Week 1.
That was the objective and why the plan was for him to play only five snaps. The team and All both just wanted to check that box.
“It was definitely a little different getting out there,” All said. “You worry about the unknown and chance you get hurt, stuff like that, that’s always something you are aware of.”
Then there’s Lew, who was eased into camp a little bit at a time, moving from a few reps to a few series to a day with the first team and now returning to start at center. He tore an ACL at the conclusion of Auburn’s season last year, but Cincinnati still selected him in the fourth round, looking to put a successor to Ted Karras in the pipeline. He lasted until midway through the second quarter before giving way to Jacob Bayer.
Lew is expected to play again next week against the Eagles.
If Lew’s path continues, the Bengals can confidently write his name down as Karras’ backup to open the year.
“I feel good about this progression he has had,” Taylor said. “He’s done as well as we could have hoped with the limited time he’s got so far.”
Anyone who has watched a Bengals game in the last two years knows what bad tackling looks like. Defensive coordinator Al Golden might not have been fielding his starters, but those who did play were notably effective in getting the Bears to the ground.
That means a lot around these parts, with the Bengals desperate to fix that aspect.
“I thought we played really clean,” Taylor said. “We got guys on the ground. We will watch the tape and see how many missed tackles, but I thought guys did a great job leveraging the ball, getting guys on the ground.”
Coming off a productive week of practices, Newton started to feel momentum as he tries to claw his way back into the rotation to make the team.
Enjoying days, weeks and even months of good practices has never been an issue for Newton. The problems occur when the stadium lights come on and the game goes live. Those problems showed up again Saturday. Newton allowed Jahdae Walker to get open behind him, nearly falling over in the process for a 36-yard reception. Newton then added a poor effort on a missed tackle reminiscent of so many bad moments from the Bengals’ defenses of the past two seasons.
Newton needed to show he could do a better job translating practices to games. That did not happen.
On top of being demoted out of the pole position for the swing tackle spot, Ford endured an ugly combination of plays in the first quarter. The first play was a second-and-1 run up the middle for what would have been a first down. Instead, Ford was flagged for a hold that turned it into second-and-10. He was beaten instantly on the next play by Gervon Dexter, who flushed Johnson out of the pocket and forced an incompletion.
The veteran Ford was counted on entering camp to be the sixth man in the offensive line room, but plays like those have come far too often while eroding the team’s confidence in him coming off the bench.
The bottom line is that the backup offensive tackle position is a problem spot and Ford was supposed to be the one to solve it. He has not done that.
Ford is not alone in exposing the offensive line weakness on the depth chart. Taylor wasn’t exactly exuding confidence about those competing for the spot after the game.
“That’s still pretty open,” Taylor said. “There’s guys we are still looking at, and I wouldn’t say there are any decisions that we’ve made there.”
Is it time to look outside for offensive tackle help? A spot the Bengals never truly addressed this offseason continues to show up at every milepost. Early in camp, the performances from Ford, Andrew Coker and Javon Foster were disappointing. That prompted Jalen Rivers to kick back out to left tackle for a shot to prove he can play there. Saturday was a rough go for Rivers as he allowed multiple crunching hits on Johnson and committed a false start in the first half.
Foster allowed one as well on the right side and added a holding penalty. Coker tossed in a holding penalty, negating a long run in the second half. The Bengals hoped somebody among that group would step up and earn the role in camp, and as the opportunity dwindles to one preseason game left, it doesn’t look as if anyone will.
“If a backup tackle has to go in the game and we want to keep playing the way that we play, just got to be able to trust them in the game,” Taylor said. “There is plenty of competition there. We still got two weeks to go with it.”
Thus the question: Can de facto general manager Duke Tobin find a veteran another team is willing to part with in the next two weeks? Is…

title: The Browns are living in denial. Deshaun Watson has never been their answer at QB If Watson is named Cleveland's starter to begin the season, what's the upside? There wouldn't be anything to gain with him under center. Zac Jackson 1
summary:
Deshaun Watson was booed by the Browns' fan base during the team's preseason loss to the Bills. Nick Cammett / Getty Images
CLEVELAND — For months, the Cleveland Browns foolishly thought they could bring Deshaun Watson back for one more go with minimal distraction.
With a quarterback decision looming , Saturday reinforced that the Browns have been living in denial. Watson was booed multiple times by the home crowd in the preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills, and he responded in his postgame news
full_text:
Deshaun Watson was booed by the Browns' fan base during the team's preseason loss to the Bills. Nick Cammett / Getty Images
CLEVELAND — For months, the Cleveland Browns foolishly thought they could bring Deshaun Watson back for one more go with minimal distraction.
With a quarterback decision looming , Saturday reinforced that the Browns have been living in denial. Watson was booed multiple times by the home crowd in the preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills, and he responded in his postgame news conference by taking on the boos and the fans delivering them.
“I think the biggest thing is — I think you guys know too, and I think the whole world knows — it has nothing to do about the performance,” Watson said. “It’s a little bit more personal than that. So, I think that’s a disrespectful thing. So, yeah, I’m going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally. … And yeah, just move on.
“Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. And that same fan base, they cheered when I got hurt. So what does that have to do with anything about performance when a person gets hurt, especially for your own city and they cheer?”
Awkward and unseemly as the whole thing may be, the reaction actually has a lot to do with performance. Watson stunk for three seasons in Cleveland and missed a fourth while rehabbing from a twice-torn right Achilles tendon. He’s worked his way back to the field, but there’s clearly still work to be done by the team in explaining why Watson might be the best option as the battle with Shedeur Sanders for the starting job continues.
Browns owner Jimmy Haslam accurately called the Watson trade “ a swing and miss ” in March 2025, and everyone outside the building thought Cleveland would move on before this year. Nothing in any of Watson’s 19 previous performances in a Browns uniform indicated he’s suddenly going to ascend and elevate those around him after nearly two years away.
So it’s fair to wonder why the Browns didn’t have a better plan than Watson competing to start for a team clearly pointing to future seasons — after his contract finally expires.
The extra complications in the dynamics stem in part from Sanders’ popularity, in part from the fan base’s frustration with a perpetual quarterback carousel and, in large part, from the Browns giving up the farm to get Watson in 2022.
What appeared to be a window of contention crashed quickly, and in June the Browns traded Myles Garrett just six months after he set the NFL’s single-season sacks record and won his second Defensive Player of the Year award.
The Browns made the playoffs in 2023 despite Watson suffering a shoulder injury midseason. But they won just eight total games over the next two years, and Garrett didn’t want to be part of another rebuilding project. Or part of a team that still doesn’t have a quarterback four and a half years past the Watson trade.
The Browns should not act surprised that the fans booed Watson, who’s obviously not surprised himself. He said last week that he didn’t care about the boos that might be coming in his first game action in Cleveland in 22 months, but he clearly does. After he went 5-of-12 passing for 35 yards, an interception and a quarterback rating of 14.6 in four series versus Buffalo’s backups, he probably didn’t pick the best time to let on that he’s hearing and seeing everything said.
“It’s a mental battle every day,” Watson said when asked if he can defeat the negativity. “I feel like I get more love on road games than I do home games. So if it is my spot and Coach (Todd) Monken does name (me the starter), maybe it’s 17 away games then.”
Monken has said for months that he’s evaluating the quarterbacks on everything related to the operation and will ultimately choose the one who gives the Browns the best chance to move the ball and score points. But it’s fair to wonder now — at what was always supposed to be the end of six months of Monken hesitating to lean one way or another in an open, alternating competition — if Cleveland will finally have to weigh questions many on the outside have been asking.
What’s the upside here? What, really, is Watson thinking about his present and future in Cleveland? And does anybody really benefit from a first-year head coach dealing with his quarterback getting booed in his home stadium?
With the exception of one practice day in early August , Monken has alternated Watson and Sanders since the spring. When there wasn’t a clear winner in June, Monken decided both deserved the chance to continue competing this summer, with the idea of giving each a preseason start before making a decision.
Watson’s start, uncoincidentally, came last weekend in Chicago , and he led two scoring drives in six series. Sanders started Saturday at home, guiding a sharp touchdown drive and completing his first eight passes before an interception derailed another promising series.
Monken hesitated to make Monday the drop-dead date for a winner. But with three weeks until the season opener, it’s really past time for a decision to have been made.
At its core, the competition remains unsettled largely because neither player has convincingly outplayed the other and won the job. Monken said after Saturday’s game that he has to review the film and talk with his coaching staff about everything the quarterbacks have done since April.
For the first time, Monken and everyone atop the Browns’ organization are being forced to publicly confront the fact that Watson represents more of this team’s rancid past than anything to do with a future-facing program.
If Monken does decide to go forward with Watson, he’s going to have to be absolutely right — or things will get as strangely ugly as they did Saturday in preseason game No. 2.

title: Cowboys position analysis: What we learned about key position battles in preseason win Joe Milton and Shavon Revel had big outings Saturday against the Cardinals. Jonathan Mingo and Camden Brown continued battling at receiver. Jon Machota
summary:

The biggest position battles entering training camp for the Dallas Cowboys were starting cornerback, inside linebacker, No. 2 running back and backup quarterback.
Saturday night’s 34-13 preseason win at Arizona had some notable performances in all four areas.
Shavon Revel has been having an excellent camp. Not only has his surgically-repaired
full_text:
Shavon Revel intercepted this pass Saturday against Arizona. Revel has been one of the Cowboys' standouts this preseason. Christian Petersen / Getty Images
The biggest position battles entering training camp for the Dallas Cowboys were starting cornerback, inside linebacker, No. 2 running back and backup quarterback.
Saturday night’s 34-13 preseason win at Arizona had some notable performances in all four areas.
Shavon Revel has been having an excellent camp. Not only has his surgically-repaired knee looked healthy, but his overall confidence seems to be growing by the day. He made the first big play of the game Saturday as former Cowboys wide receiver Simi Fehoko slipped and Revel intercepted the Gardner Minshew pass. Revel returned the ball 22 yards to the Arizona 12. Dallas took a 7-0 lead three plays later.
DaRon Bland has one of the outside starting cornerback spots locked up. Revel is battling Cobie Durant for the other. Saturday was likely another confidence-booster for last year’s third-round pick. Regardless of that battle, both players are expected to play a lot this season. The cornerback depth isn’t great, but the top three spots look solid.
Jaishawn Barham didn’t play in last week’s preseason opener as he was working his way back from a groin injury early in camp. He played Saturday and looked every bit the player the Cowboys have been raving about. Barham pressured the quarterback, had a tackle for loss and a team-high five tackles in the first half. The third-round pick looks like he will have an immediate impact. Even if Dallas goes with DeMarvion Overshown and Dee Winters as its starting inside linebackers to open the season, Barham will get on the field. He’s too good of a playmaker to keep on the sideline.
Barham can make plays in all areas, but he’s best around the line of scrimmage. He showed on several plays against the Cardinals that he’s likely going to be a nightmare for opponents to block. Inside linebacker was a major position of need this offseason. Missing out on a big name in free agency looked like it would be an issue. But if Overshown can stay healthy and Barham can play like he did Saturday, the Cowboys might be just fine.
Javonte Williams is the obvious lead back. He’s had a good camp, looking ready to repeat the strong season he had a year ago. But the No. 2 spot has been a competition the last four weeks with no one really separating themselves.
Malik Davis seems to be the player the Cowboys are most comfortable with in that role at the moment. He started and played well, carrying five times for 29 yards and catching one pass for an 8-yard touchdown. But Jaydon Blue, who has the higher upside, also played well after Davis came out of the game. Blue carried 15 times for a game-high 75 yards. His quickness and athleticism were on display. The Cowboys just need to see more consistency from the second-year player.
My prediction is that Davis starts the season as the No. 2 back but Blue takes it over during the season. I think the Cowboys end up keeping four running backs: Williams, Davis, Blue and Hunter Luepke.
Joe Milton was the star of the night. The backup competition between Milton and Sam Howell saw Howell start last week and play the entire first half. Milton played the entire second half. On Saturday, those roles were reversed. Milton started and was outstanding, playing the entire first half. He was confident and calm in the pocket. He bought time with his feet to complete some monster throws.
His deep ball up the left sideline to Jonathan Mingo was perfect, resulting in a 53-yard touchdown. And he never came close to turning the ball over. Milton finished 9 of 13 passing for 179 yards, two touchdowns, a 151.4 passer rating and added a short TD run. Milton’s confidence seemed to be growing by the day during camp. He played well last week. But his performance Saturday will make it difficult for Howell (7 of 10 for 65 yards with an interception) to jump him. Maybe the Cowboys keep three quarterbacks, but if they go with only Dak Prescott and a backup, Milton should be that player.
“Joe has put together two really, really good halves,” Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said after the game. “Sam really made one mistake, (the interception) down in the red zone. He kinda got fooled on one and turned it over. That can’t happen. But this is long from over. We’re going back to Frisco, thankfully, get a chance to be home and put some more training camp days in. You got to give Joe his credit. He’s played really well the last two games, but we have a lot of confidence in Sam as well.”
One reason the Cowboys might not be able to keep three quarterbacks is because they could have to keep six wide receivers. CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy and KaVontae Turpin are roster locks. The fifth spot is coming down to veteran Jonathan Mingo and undrafted rookie Camden Brown. Brown has been more impressive, making highlight plays just about every day in practice and in both of their preseason games. But Mingo has also been playing well. This could be one of their most difficult roster decisions.
On offense, the Cowboys went with Milton, Davis, Mingo, Brown, WR Tyler Johnson, TE Luke Schoonmaker, LT Drew Shelton, LG Trevor Keegan, C Nick Leverett, RG Ajani Cornelius and RT Nate Thomas.
On defense, it was OLB Malachi Lawrence, OLB James Houston, DT L.T. Overton, DT D.J. Withers, DT Jay Toia, Barham, ILB Shemar James, Revel, CB Ameer Speed, S Alijah Clark and S Julius Wood.
“The wins are great,” Schottenheimer said. “I’ve always thought, because my dad said it, the preseason record is never remembered. But I think what we’ve shown the last two games is there’s a play style about this team, whoever’s in the game, and that’s one of physicality, effort, playing together, and I do think that we played that way tonight for really four quarters, and I’m proud of the guys for that.”

full_text:
Tanner McKee, center, and Andy Dalton are still competing for the Eagles' QB2 position. Gregory Fisher / Imagn
Saquon Barkley isn’t the only Philadelphia Eagles running back with some hops.
Have you heard of Carson Steele? The former undrafted rookie for the Kansas City Chiefs? The guy who opened Eagles training camp as the presumed fullback in first-time offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s new offensive system? The running back — yes, underline that now — who hurdled two New England Patriots defenders on separate touches in a 24-21 loss?
Well, now you have. Steele started his theatrics during a two-minute drill before halftime. He planted his foot on a route out of the backfield, hauled in a catch, then vaulted over Patriots cornerback Brandon Crossley to complete a 14-yard gain on what ended up being a touchdown drive. Steele then gave the Eagles a 21-17 lead with 3:46 left in the game by catching a wheel route along the right sideline and leaping over safety Eric Butler for a 20-yard score.
Philadelphia’s lead was short-lived. Patriots wide receiver Nick DeGennaro swept past Eagles cornerback Isaiah Bolden and hauled in a go-ahead 37-yard touchdown catch from Behren Morton with 1:03 left in the game.
The Eagles are 0-2 in the preseason. But Mannion’s offense showed more life in its second showing. The Eagles totaled 301 yards against the Patriots and 159 against the Baltimore Ravens. Mannion, who called the game from the booth for the first time, must also choose where he will operate on game day.
The Eagles will close out training camp at home on Friday against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The Eagles saw much more success from their backup offensive line than they did in their preseason opener against the Ravens.
Willie Lampkin, who started at center against the Patriots, was often leading the way. Will Shipley totaled 11 carries for 56 yards during the first two drives. “Wide zone” has taken center stage when discussing the Eagles’ overhauled run scheme, and for good reason, but Shipley’s runs were often between the tackles. This underscored how the Eagles still intend to run powerfully up the middle and are discovering strength in their interior depth.
Lampkin and right guard Jake Majors opened a running lane on the opening drive for Shipley’s 18-yard gain. On the second drive, Lampkin pancaked Patriots defensive tackle Isaiah Iton on a 7-yard Shipley carry. Third-round rookie Markel Bell, who started at right tackle, repeatedly washed down defenders on the drive, including on a 9-yard run from Shipley. Lampkin and left guard Drew Kendall punctuated the drive by pummeling Iton into the end zone, freeing Shipley for a 5-yard touchdown run.
. @willshipley2021 buries his way for the score! pic.twitter.com/iXvDrOk9y9
— Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) August 22, 2026
Lampkin and Kendall were sidelined after two drives — an indication that the coaching staff had seen enough. Mannion has said the team’s depth across the offensive line contains “a really good crop of young players” and that “it’s been exciting in this training camp to see them grow as players and see them get more and more opportunities.”
Depth at this position group is a major need for the Eagles, especially along the interior. Starting center Cam Jurgens (back) and left guard Landon Dickerson (knee) have managed injuries over the last two seasons and underwent stem cell therapy treatments in Colombia over the offseason.
Eagles wide receiver Darius Cooper rebounded from a quiet start to the preseason by recording three catches for 44 yards against the Patriots — all during the second offensive possession. Cooper caught a short second-and-7 crosser and turned upfield for a 25-yard gain. Later, on fourth-and-1 at the Patriots’ 40, Cooper created separation with an inward dig route for a 13-yard catch.
Cooper was an undrafted free agent when he made the initial 53-man roster last year. He is still fighting for a spot this year. The Eagles sought depth in the offseason by signing veterans Dontayvion Wicks, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore, then spent their No. 20 pick on Makai Lemon. Cooper is making his case to at the very least be among their top six options. Johnny Wilson, who managed a knee injury in training camp, reverted to the injured reserve after going unclaimed on waivers Friday.
Coach Nick Sirianni has maintained that the Eagles have not decided on the backup quarterback. But Andy Dalton has now started in both of the team’s preseason games. Sirianni said Saturday that Dalton went in first and has played less because he has more experience in the system.
The 16-year veteran’s wealth of experience and knowledge of Mannion’s style support Dalton’s positioning. His play in the preseason has not. He was 3-of-10 passing for 44 yards in three drives. All three completions occurred on the second drive, when Shipley ran the ball eight times for 33 yards and a touchdown. The Eagles totaled eight plays and 38 yards on Dalton’s other drives. Last week, they did not gain a first down within Dalton’s three drives.
Tanner McKee was more productive in seven drives. He completed 16 of 22 passes for 173 yards and two touchdowns. The disparity in playing time was notable. Fifth-round rookie Cole Payton received just one drive — a comeback attempt, down 24-21 with 57 seconds left in the game. Patriots edge rusher Quintayvious Hutchins surged around third-team right tackle Cameron Williams and knocked the football loose from Payton; Patriots defensive tackle Casey Rogers recovered the sack fumble to end the game.
McKee gave the Eagles a 14-10 halftime lead by directing a successful two-minute drill. McKee was 3-of-4 passing for 44 yards on a drive that lasted 1 minute, 4 seconds. The drive showcased the friendlier throws Mannion said will be featured in the revamped passing game, especially with running backs and tight ends. Yards after the catch are also more emphasized in the scheme. McKee completed two short passes to running back Steele, one for a 16-yard gain, another for a 14-yard gain. McKee then completed a wide receiver screen to Britain Covey for a 14-yard touchdown.

full_text:
Third-string quarterback Behren Morton led a go-ahead drive late in the fourth quarter — and served as the team's punter after Bryce Baringer left the game. Caleb Bowlin / Getty Images
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. — It sure seems as if New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel is going to sit most of the team’s starters through the whole preseason, leaving their first in-game snaps for the season opener in Seattle.
That meant Drake Maye, A.J. Brown and other key players were on the bench for the Patriots’ 24-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles at Gillette Stadium on Saturday night. After the starters didn’t play in the first two preseason games, it would be shocking if they saw action in the preseason finale in Cleveland next Thursday night. That game will be much more about those on the roster bubble.
Why would Vrabel not want to see his starters on the field?
“I don’t think we have a very deep team,” Vrabel said bluntly, suggesting he didn’t want to expose Maye or Brown to the possibility of injury. “So we have to make sure that … we’re doing everything that we can to keep our best players available.”
So while Saturday night may not have seen any action from the big names, it offered clarity as to how the roster will shake out with cuts coming by the evening of Aug. 30. Here is a look at the players who made good impressions, and the ones who are headed the wrong direction in the final few days before the 53-man roster is set.
Surely Vrabel — a player who moonlighted at tight end during his career as a linebacker — can appreciate a guy who can play in multiple phases.
On Saturday, Morton showcased his arm and leg, serving as a quarterback and punter.
As a high schooler in Texas, Morton primarily played quarterback and safety, but he also served as a kicker and punter. Against the Eagles, Morton showed that he’s not half bad with his leg, averaging 44.3 yards on three punts. The Pats used Morton there because punter Bryce Baringer “wasn’t feeling great” after his first two punts.
More importantly, Morton had some nice moments at quarterback, completing 13 of 17 passes for 129 yards, including a 37-yard touchdown to Nick DeGennaro for the go-ahead score with 57 seconds remaining.
The receiver entered Saturday night’s game on the right side of the roster bubble and seemed to solidify that positioning. Given his ability to back up DeMario Douglas (not to mention Douglas’ risk of injury given his size), Chism is likely one of seven wide receivers who will be on the 53-man roster.
Chism again showed his craftiness from the slot and his ability as a punt returner. At this point, it’s unlikely the Patriots could sneak him onto the practice squad, which makes a roster spot seem close to assured.
Chism caught all four of his targets for 45 yards while adding a 16-yard punt return and serving as one of the in-game captains for the opening coin toss.
The competition for the final few spots at cornerback remains open, but Saturday, Vildor showed why he deserves to stay.
In the first half, he stepped in front of an Andy Dalton pass for an interception, though the play came back after Gabe Jacas was flagged for roughing the passer. But Vildor didn’t get discouraged.
A couple of plays later, he broke on his receiver to perfectly break up a pass on third-and-10. Vrabel greeted him on the sideline with a big high five.
The rookie linebacker seems to be making a positive impression on coaches, considering his playing time in practice continues to increase and he has even gotten some run with the starters.
Obiazor seemed to be out of position on one swing pass against the Eagles. But with the pass defense he played on a breakup in the end zone on fourth down, it’s not hard to see why coaches think he has plenty of potential and believe he can contribute on special teams.
Namdi Obiazor breaks it up in the end zone on 4th down ‼️
PHIvsNE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/p7wPbP8BSv
— NFL (@NFL) August 23, 2026
OK, so it was a pretty uneventful day for the kicker, who hit a 41-yard field goal and all three of his extra points.
But after missing three field goals in the preseason opener, Borregales had a good week of practice, then did what he needed to do Saturday, at least lowering the temperature around him entering the season.
Saturday only furthered the notion that the Patriots’ interior offensive line depth is an issue. New guard Greg Van Roten didn’t play, but simply based on Saturday, Van Roten should probably be the team’s top backup guard.
Hudson had a rough opening to the game, drawing two holding penalties on the five-play opening drive. On the second drive, a miscommunication between him and center Jacob Rizy allowed a blitzer to burst through the line for a quick sack.
Hudson was probably on the right side of the roster bubble before this game, but he may be on the outside looking in now.
Maybe the only saving grace for Hudson is that Butler, the guard opposite him who had the most to gain, also struggled.
Tommy DeVito wanted to hit Kyle Williams down the left sideline on the second drive, but Butler was beaten, and DeVito was hit as he threw, causing the throw to go off target.
Van Roten joined the Patriots on Tuesday, so he wasn’t up to speed enough to play Saturday (he’s also a veteran who was a starter last season, so these preseason reps aren’t as important to him). But the Patriots will need Van Roten, who took snaps at center in warmups, if any of their starting interior linemen are injured this season.
After some shaky joint practices, Saturday was another rough day for New England’s linebacker depth. And it was Muma who seemed to show up most on the wrong side of Philadelphia highlights.
The Patriots had trouble all week stopping the run, and Muma looked like he missed some holes and some tackles Saturday night as the Eagles ran it well again. He may still nab a spot on the team, but it wasn’t a great night. The fact he was still playing deep into the fourth quarter on a night the starters were rested was not a good sign for him, either. On the final drive, he walked off with trainers with an apparent injury.

full_text:
Tanner McKee, center, and Andy Dalton are still competing for the Eagles' QB2 position. Gregory Fisher / Imagn
Saquon Barkley isn’t the only Philadelphia Eagles running back with some hops.
Have you heard of Carson Steele? The former undrafted rookie for the Kansas City Chiefs? The guy who opened Eagles training camp as the presumed fullback in first-time offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s new offensive system? The running back — yes, underline that now — who hurdled two New England Patriots defenders on separate touches in a 24-21 loss?
Well, now you have. Steele started his theatrics during a two-minute drill before halftime. He planted his foot on a route out of the backfield, hauled in a catch, then vaulted over Patriots cornerback Brandon Crossley to complete a 14-yard gain on what ended up being a touchdown drive. Steele then gave the Eagles a 21-17 lead with 3:46 left in the game by catching a wheel route along the right sideline and leaping over safety Eric Butler for a 20-yard score.
Philadelphia’s lead was short-lived. Patriots wide receiver Nick DeGennaro swept past Eagles cornerback Isaiah Bolden and hauled in a go-ahead 37-yard touchdown catch from Behren Morton with 1:03 left in the game.
The Eagles are 0-2 in the preseason. But Mannion’s offense showed more life in its second showing. The Eagles totaled 301 yards against the Patriots and 159 against the Baltimore Ravens. Mannion, who called the game from the booth for the first time, must also choose where he will operate on game day.
The Eagles will close out training camp at home on Friday against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The Eagles saw much more success from their backup offensive line than they did in their preseason opener against the Ravens.
Willie Lampkin, who started at center against the Patriots, was often leading the way. Will Shipley totaled 11 carries for 56 yards during the first two drives. “Wide zone” has taken center stage when discussing the Eagles’ overhauled run scheme, and for good reason, but Shipley’s runs were often between the tackles. This underscored how the Eagles still intend to run powerfully up the middle and are discovering strength in their interior depth.
Lampkin and right guard Jake Majors opened a running lane on the opening drive for Shipley’s 18-yard gain. On the second drive, Lampkin pancaked Patriots defensive tackle Isaiah Iton on a 7-yard Shipley carry. Third-round rookie Markel Bell, who started at right tackle, repeatedly washed down defenders on the drive, including on a 9-yard run from Shipley. Lampkin and left guard Drew Kendall punctuated the drive by pummeling Iton into the end zone, freeing Shipley for a 5-yard touchdown run.
. @willshipley2021 buries his way for the score! pic.twitter.com/iXvDrOk9y9
— Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) August 22, 2026
Lampkin and Kendall were sidelined after two drives — an indication that the coaching staff had seen enough. Mannion has said the team’s depth across the offensive line contains “a really good crop of young players” and that “it’s been exciting in this training camp to see them grow as players and see them get more and more opportunities.”
Depth at this position group is a major need for the Eagles, especially along the interior. Starting center Cam Jurgens (back) and left guard Landon Dickerson (knee) have managed injuries over the last two seasons and underwent stem cell therapy treatments in Colombia over the offseason.
Eagles wide receiver Darius Cooper rebounded from a quiet start to the preseason by recording three catches for 44 yards against the Patriots — all during the second offensive possession. Cooper caught a short second-and-7 crosser and turned upfield for a 25-yard gain. Later, on fourth-and-1 at the Patriots’ 40, Cooper created separation with an inward dig route for a 13-yard catch.
Cooper was an undrafted free agent when he made the initial 53-man roster last year. He is still fighting for a spot this year. The Eagles sought depth in the offseason by signing veterans Dontayvion Wicks, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore, then spent their No. 20 pick on Makai Lemon. Cooper is making his case to at the very least be among their top six options. Johnny Wilson, who managed a knee injury in training camp, reverted to the injured reserve after going unclaimed on waivers Friday.
Coach Nick Sirianni has maintained that the Eagles have not decided on the backup quarterback. But Andy Dalton has now started in both of the team’s preseason games. Sirianni said Saturday that Dalton went in first and has played less because he has more experience in the system.
The 16-year veteran’s wealth of experience and knowledge of Mannion’s style support Dalton’s positioning. His play in the preseason has not. He was 3-of-10 passing for 44 yards in three drives. All three completions occurred on the second drive, when Shipley ran the ball eight times for 33 yards and a touchdown. The Eagles totaled eight plays and 38 yards on Dalton’s other drives. Last week, they did not gain a first down within Dalton’s three drives.
Tanner McKee was more productive in seven drives. He completed 16 of 22 passes for 173 yards and two touchdowns. The disparity in playing time was notable. Fifth-round rookie Cole Payton received just one drive — a comeback attempt, down 24-21 with 57 seconds left in the game. Patriots edge rusher Quintayvious Hutchins surged around third-team right tackle Cameron Williams and knocked the football loose from Payton; Patriots defensive tackle Casey Rogers recovered the sack fumble to end the game.
McKee gave the Eagles a 14-10 halftime lead by directing a successful two-minute drill. McKee was 3-of-4 passing for 44 yards on a drive that lasted 1 minute, 4 seconds. The drive showcased the friendlier throws Mannion said will be featured in the revamped passing game, especially with running backs and tight ends. Yards after the catch are also more emphasized in the scheme. McKee completed two short passes to running back Steele, one for a 16-yard gain, another for a 14-yard gain. McKee then completed a wide receiver screen to Britain Covey for a 14-yard touchdown.

title: Three Bold Predictions For Cowboys vs Cardinals in Preseason Week 2
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Dallas Cowboys will be kicking off shortly at State Farm Stadium for Week 2 preseason action.
The Cardinals are hoping to give the Red Sea a show for their only home preseason battle of 2026, though the likes of Jacoby Brissett and other starting players won't be suiting up in Arizona. The same will go for the Cowboys, too.
With majority of backups playing , there's bound to space for eye-opening plays to happen — let's throw out some bold predictions for tonight:
This is shaping up to be a massive night in terms of offensive production.
The Arizona Cardinals and Dallas Cowboys both are capable of putting up points thanks to Mike LaFleur and Brian Schottenheimer. With majority of starters not playing for either side, that can lead to some sloppy defense from the Cardinals and Cowboys, respectively.
The result? Points galore, with two strong offensive minds in LaFleur/Schottenheimer running the show. It's preseason. It's vanilla. We get it — though the execution offensively mixed with poor defense leaves the door wide open for plenty of fireworks.
The Cardinals have firmly established their intentions (and ability) to run the ball, and run it well. Arizona, especially with Gardner Minshew and Kedon Slovis, will again look towards their bread and butter to keep the chains moving.
Knight's had an incredibly strong camp and has averaged five yards per carry across Arizona's two preseason games — though he's been unable to find the end zone.
With no Jeremiyah Love and likely no Tyler Allgeier or James Conner, Knight figures to get plenty of reps against Dallas. If he receivers similar opportunities, it could be a big night for Knight.
The Cardinals haven't had a truly electric return game in years, and while that could be the case with Devin Duvernay, it's likely we may not see him tonight.
If we don't, Arizona will deploy Ihmir Smith-Marsette — the backup receiver who is battling for a roster spot and effectively is their No. 2 return man behind Duvernay.
Smith-Marsette is a fast player with long strides, and with opportunities to impact both punt and kick return, he just needs a sliver of daylight to break one loose.
Tonight, we're calling our shot. Smith-Marsette might not house one for a touchdown, but he's a big play waiting to happen.

title: 5 Overlooked Cardinals With the Most to Gain vs. Cowboys
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are set to enter tonight's preseason matchup against the Dallas Cowboys with little starters set to take the field.
Head coach Mike LaFleur informed reporters earlier this week only a mix of guys likely to make major contributions will take the field . Exactly who those players are remains to be seen.
Yet that opens the door for hefty playing time for Arizona's backups, players who range from potential role players to bottom of the floor depth guys. With plenty of green grass available tonight, here's five overlooked Cardinals who have the most to gain.
After the injury to second-round pick Chase Bisontis, Gaines has a clear opportunity ahead of him to solidify himself as the immediate fill-in to practically all three interior spots along the Cardinals' offensive line.
Gaines has been running with the second team unit as a center but also has versatility to play both left and right guard. Hayden Conner is shaping up to be his only competition there alongside either Oli Udoh or Matt Pryor.
With a strong performance tonight, Gaines can leave no doubt on who Arizona should turn to if the Cardinals need an interior replacement.
Knight's one of the more heavily debated roster spots , as the Cardinals may or may not keep a fourth running back. With Trey Benson still sidelined with injuries, Knight clearly is over him in terms of roster chances.
Now, it boils down to Knight justifying his spot in the final 53, and that can be done in two ways: offensively and special teams. Not only does Knight need to run the ball well against Dallas, he also needs to prove he can contribute to special teams if he's going to stay up and avoid waivers or the practice squad.
If Knight can do both against the Cowboys, he might very well secure his spot.
We included both players on this list, as we couldn't choose just one. Brooks and Smith-Marsette are the top two leaders in the clubhouse for Arizona's WR6 spot — if they decide to keep a sixth receiver.
Some of that will boil down to roster manipulation and other areas of need, though Brooks and Smith-Marsette both have had respectively good training camp and preseason outings — strong enough to warrant a roster spot.
Brooks is thought to have pole position in the race, though Smith-Marsette also has special teams value as a return man. It's a multi-dimensional battle between those two and fighting against other players who are on the bubble as well.
BJ Ojulari simply hasn't found the form from his rookie season, which has seen the outside linebacker fall somewhat out of favor with the Cardinals' coaching staff. That's opened the door for Eku Leota.
Leota is one of the more surprising names who could make the team, especially given how stacked the room is with returning veterans ahead of him. However, he's had a strong training camp and has earned some first-team snaps with starters.
It's clear the Cardinals are searching for some sort of secondary option opposite of Josh Sweat. Can Leota keep climbing up the roster? A strong performance tonight won't put his name in concrete, though the scale would certainly tip in his favor.

title: Gardner Minshew Could Change His Cardinals Future vs. Cowboys
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals play host to the Dallas Cowboys today, marking what could very well be the final preseason outing of quarterback Gardner Minshew.
Minshew, second-string to starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, is set to play roughly the first half of tonight's battle at State Farm Stadium according to head coach Mike LaFleur . Kedon Slovis will anchor the second half.
There's typically not much value in preseason games beyond roster evaluation and shaking some rust off, though for Minshew, it could potentially be a defining moment of his Cardinals tenure — and beyond.
Minshew signed as a free agent this offseason on a one-year contract to be the secondary option in the room behind Brissett. Minshew's placement in the pecking order as a backup wasn't up for debate, though the arrival of third-round pick Carson Beck changed the outlook entirely.
Beck — as we previously discussed — will need every opportunity available in either preseason or regular season for the Cardinals to evaluate the rookie passer ahead of next offseason, where the organization could very well entertain another option at football's most important position.
Beck isn't playing tonight due to a ribs injury, though the overall sentiment remains: The Cardinals, whenever possible, will want to see their rookie quarterback.
That leaves Minshew in a precarious position — he's obviously the backup to Brissett while Arizona's front office will need to see Beck in action, leaving the former Pro Bowl passer in somewhat of a purgatory.
Yet uncertainty can bring opportunity, and if Minshew can play well tonight against Dallas, that just might change the outlook of his future in Arizona.
Minshew, by all accounts, would be the most likely trade candidate out of Arizona's quarterback room. Teams typically don't carry three quarterbacks on the active roster, though the organization is essentially forced to do so.
Every year, teams around the trade deadline are looking to rescue their room in some form or fashion. Whether it be replacing a recently injured starter to rescue a playoff push or simply supplementing depth, you'll typically see plenty of buzz and chatter around quarterback moves.
Minshew, thanks to his prior resume, cheap contract and outlook in Arizona, projects as a likely candidate to be moved if/when teams come calling.
When teams begin to explore options, they'll be looking at the most recent film — which will likely be Minshew's performance tonight against Dallas.
A good performance against the Cowboys won't immediately boost his trade value, and a poor outing won't instantly diminish interest from other organizations.
He performed well in Las Vegas, and if he can carry some of that success over tonight, that might just seal his fate as a potential trade target around the league later down the road.

title: 5 Biggest Questions Cardinals Need Answered vs. Cowboys
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals play host to the Dallas Cowboys today for preseason game No. 3 on 2026's schedule.
The Cardinals return to State Farm Stadium for the first time since ending training camp for their lone exhibition battle, as three of their total four preseason games are on the road.
Here's the five biggest things we're watching for when action begins at 7:00 PM AZ time.
The Cardinals' running back depth chart is established, at least at the top. Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier are 1A and 1B while James Conner figures to be the third back - when healthy.
Bam Knight has an opportunity to firmly establish himself among Arizona's pecking order as RB4, and if the Cardinals do indeed decide to keep four players at the spot, a strong performance from Knight (especially with Trey Benson still out due to injury) can really swing the pendulum in his favor.
That's not just speaking offensively, as he'll need to perform well as a special teams asset to justify his presence on the final 53-man roster.
Similar to running back, the Cardinals' receiver's room will have some tough decisions to be made. All of Marvin Harrison Jr., Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne are firmly established while Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil are considered to be safe, too.
If the Cardinals want a sixth receiver, that leaves one spot with numerous guys playing well at the moment. All of Jalen Brooks, Ihmir Smith-Marsette and Simi Fehoko are battling for what's considered to be the final receiver spot.
Similar to Knight, special teams will also play a factor in any of the aforementioned players making the roster. Brooks has been gaining momentum lately for the job after Smith-Marsette was training camp's early leader in the clubhouse.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said some starters will play while others won't. We know Jacoby Brissett won't participate, though most others (not related to injury at least) are still up in the air.
Who plays could be particularly telling, as it won't exactly be a glaring endorsement on those who will find themselves on the field for either depth chart or overall roster reasons.
Pay attention to whatever big names are playing tonight, it could be more meaningful than you think – especially with starters very likely not participating in next week's finale against Green Bay.
Darius Robinson and BJ Ojulari both entered the desert as high draft picks with potential that's been unfulfilled thus far. A mix of injuries and inability to impact the quarterback have held back the defensive end and outside linebacker, respectively.
Robinson and Ojulari both failed to impress last week in Las Vegas. Robinson again has had a strong training camp but didn't make noise against the Raiders while Ojulari, playing in both of Arizona's preseason battles thus far, hasn't quite been able to find his rookie season form.
One (if not both) needs to step up against the Cowboys to show some sign of progress ahead of their respective 2026 seasons. Back to back underwhelming performances won't cut it for either side.
The Cardinals' front seven needs somebody to emerge, and Robinson/Ojulari are near the top of that list.
Garrett Williams was activated off the PUP list this week, giving the Cardinals a much-needed boost in the secondary. Williams will man slot corner duties while also getting run in base sets opposite of Will Johnson.
Yet how will Arizona deploy its third cornerback when using Williams in the slot for 11 personnel matching? All of Denzel Burke, Starling Thomas, Max Melton, Sean Murphy-Bunting, Elijah Jones, and Kei'Trel Clark are battling for not only playing time, but also roster spots in yet another competitive room.
There hasn't quite been any standout performances thus far. If the Cardinals can get somebody — anybody — to elevate their game against the Cowboys, that might just help clear up the picture in some form or fashion.

Wingard safely feels like the guy opposite of Budda Baker, so perhaps some run on Saturday can be good for Taylor-Demerson's confidence more than anything.

title: Cardinals Panic Meter: Josh Sweat, Trey Benson and More
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are halfway through preseason play, and the organization has several different storylines surrounding the team under Mike LaFleur's watch.
Today, we're pulling out the panic meter and gauging some of the hottest issues in the desert. We'll evaluate a person's situation on a scale of 1-10 of how panicked we should actually be and dive into why:
Oftentimes a first-year head coach can wander through the walls of a facility aimlessly with no voice or direction. It's an intimidating seat with only 32 opportunities in the world, though LaFleur has very much shown the part of a head coach during the beginning stages of his tenure.
LaFleur has had several players praise his command and attention to detail during his first preseason. Mistakes have certainly been made and we've yet to see how he handles the inevitable adversity coming his way, though so far so good when it comes to the Cardinals' head coach.
The offense looks promising while the locker room has his attention, and at this point in the process that's all you can ask for.
Beck's ribs injury in the Hall of Fame Game came as a bit of a surprise given it reportedly happened earlier in action before he finished up the game. There were no indications of the injury after and Beck practiced fully through the next week before suddenly being ruled out hours ahead of last Thursday's clash against the Raiders.
Since then, Beck hasn't thrown in practice and has already practically been ruled out ahead of Saturday's tilt against the Cowboys. The Cardinals have downplayed the significance of the injury in press conferences and are confident everything will be just fine.
So are we, though it is interesting how the injury has progressed after initially Beck was fine. The ultimate reason we're not worried is the Cardinals are very likely just protecting their rookie quarterback after he had an impressive outing.
The best ability is availability, and Benson simply hasn't provided a ton of health this training camp or preseason. His meniscus recovery has seen limited participation in practice (with complete no-shows as of late) while he's unlikely to play at all in any of Arizona's final two games.
Benson's chances of making the roster are slipping away, though a placement on the PUP list could temporarily delay a tough decision with the former third-round pick if he's simply not healthy — which doesn't seem like the case at this point in time.
Bam Knight is clearly over Benson in the RB hierarchy at this point in time, and a trade/cut probably alooms whenever Benson is healthy.
Sweat's absence this entire offseason has been a massive storyline after his reported trade request months ago. That smoke has seemed to settle, though Sweat's still not practicing with the Cardinals ahead of the regular season, and that's raised some alarms.
We're concerned, but probably for different reasons.
Sweat was placed on PUP at the beginning of training camp with a knee injury and has consistently been given a verbal green light by LaFleur for his availability to begin 2026. Many are worried Sweat is unhappy with the team still with a potential trade looming.
That's not our concern. The Cardinals, to our knowledge, are simply protecting Sweat's knee and are trusting his process in terms of preparation. He's been working out on his own and in team meetings, according to various coaches.
Our hesitation resides in the fact of Sweat's ultimate physical readiness for Week 1. Sure, players can work out on their own all they want, but the physical demands of practice are a different level — and so too are NFL games.
Will two weeks really be enough for Sweat to be acclimated and ready to go on a full workload? Everybody in the desert better hope so, because if Sweat is on a pitch count or simply doesn't look on par with other star teammates, that's only going to lead to more questions.

title: Latest Tip Reiman Injury Update Has Tough Decision Looming for Cardinals
full_text:
Soon, the Arizona Cardinals may be forced with a tough roster decision regarding tight end Tip Reiman.
The former third-round pick isn't going to be released or cut, though a severe ankle injury suffered in October of last season still lingers. While he's been spotted rehabbing off to the side of Cardinals practices, his placement on PUP at the beginning of training camp hasn't changed.
That doesn't appear to be the case anytime soon, as Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Reiman likely isn't going to be ready for the regular season opener.
"No with Tip, but again he's progressing. There's just conversations [to be had]," LaFleur told reporters.
"Again, it's just day to day. He's putting in a ton of work as well, so that's just that's just day to day. He's a large man too, right? And putting a lot of force in that. There's the good days and there's the not as good days, but putting in a lot of work. We'll see."
That's a massive pivot from earlier in the offseason, when LaFleur said the Cardinals expected Reiman to be ready for training camp. Now, one of their best blockers is doubtful for the regular season opener and perhaps beyond.
The Cardinals have a massive decision coming on Reiman in terms of his status on the PUP list. If Reiman remains, he'll have to miss the first four games of the season.
"Those are the tough decisions, and you lean on the player to speak truth as well, and trust these guys," LaFleur said when asked if Reiman was going to stay on PUP.
"Tip is made of all the right stuff, so Tip's going to keep it real with us. But those are the decisions that have to be made for the reasons that you're saying."
Reiman figures to be a massive part of the Cardinals' efforts to establish the run.
"Another guy that I had a lot of respect for coming out of Illinois," LaFleur said earlier in the offseason.
"It's like some of those guys, when you get the job, you're like, 'Yes! I wanted him coming out of the draft!' and then you get to inherit him. I can say that easily about Tip because Tip is all of the right stuff in terms of how he approaches it and stuff like that. It was unfortunate what happened a year ago, but big piece of where I think we can go."

title: Garrett Williams' Return From Injury Gives Cardinals Boost at the Right Time
full_text:
ARIZONA — The return of Garrett Williams is here, and it couldn't have come at a better time.
The Arizona Cardinals activated Williams off the PUP list today as the slot cornerback is set to begin practicing for the first time in 2026 following an Achilles tear he suffered in late December of last year.
"We're going to take that one day at a time. The human element, a lot of work was put in first and foremost by him, and then a lot of people behind the scenes to get to this point," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters.
"So happy for him. He's had a smile on his face, we've known this day was coming for some time now, and it's time for the next step."
Williams' importance to the secondary can't be overstated. When healthy, he's one of the best slot cornerbacks in the league while his versatility to also play on the boundary and sometimes safety is often utilized under defensive coordinator Nick Rallis.
"It's really no different from a receiver that plays inside the numbers, inside the alleys, inside the paint. You got to be able to muck it up. You got to mix it up. You got to be physical. It's a different game than it used to be in there," LaFleur added.
"So he's got the size. He's got the want to. He's got the smarts. He's a good player, and we're excited to have him back."
Before injuries plagued Williams in 2025, he was graded among the best cornerbacks in Pro Football Focus' database — ranking behind just Trent McDuffie and Patrick Surtain entering the season.
"Definitely excited to get Garrett back," Cardinals captain Budda Baker said.
"He brings a lot of knowledge and always there in the right spot, always doing his job at a high level. Definitely special to get him back practicing with us. Of course, they'll take it easy on him, but definitely just to see him come back from that, it's definitely something very special. Just excited to have him doing our DB work and stuff like that."
Williams' arrival to the Cardinals secondary now will bump Sean Murphy-Bunting (who moved into the slot this spring) into backup duties for the spot while he'll occupy a boundary role opposite of fellow cornerback Will Johnson.
"We'll do what we see is necessary depending on where this thing kind of goes, but right now the plan is to play him inside," said LaFleur. "... He does some really good stuff on the inside. Not that he can't on the outside, but that's where we'll start."

title: 3 Winners and 3 Losers From Falcons' Dominant Win Over Colts
full_text:
The Atlanta Falco ns needed a response after a disappointing preseason opener and delivered one Saturday.
Atlanta dominated the Indianapolis Colts 34-6, showing considerably more energy and physicality after spending the week in Indianapolis for two joint practices. The victory also provided another important opportunity for players competing for roster spots to make their final impressions before cut day arrives.
With several position battles still unsettled, here are three winners and three losers from Atlanta's preseason victory.
Goodson continues to make his case for a roster spot.
The running back was one of Atlanta's most explosive offensive players Saturday, breaking loose for a 49-yard touchdown and providing the type of big-play ability the Falcons have seen from him throughout training camp.
His performance is particularly important because Atlanta's running back room has become more competitive following Trey Sermon's placement on injured reserve.
Goodson has consistently shown the ability to create explosive plays, and Saturday was another reminder that he shouldn't be overlooked when Atlanta makes its final roster decisions.
The Falcons already know what they have in Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. The question is who will earn the next spot.
Goodson is making a strong argument that it should be him.
Strand may have been the biggest winner of the afternoon.
The undrafted rookie quarterback put together another impressive performance, completing 12 of 17 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown while also rushing for a 16-yard score. He also delivered several impressive throws downfield, including a 36-yard completion.
Strand's performance continues to make the QB3 competition much more interesting.
Cooper Rush entered camp with the experience advantage, but Strand has repeatedly shown poise and playmaking ability. He now has legitimate momentum heading into the final preseason game.
Atlanta's quarterback room could look very different depending on what happens over the next two weeks.
And Strand is making sure the Falcons have a difficult decision to make.
Daniels continues to be one of the most intriguing young players on Atlanta's roster.
The rookie linebacker has been making plays throughout training camp and the joint practices, and Saturday gave him another opportunity to show that his development is translating to game action.
Daniels' emergence is especially important because Atlanta has been evaluating several players at linebacker while dealing with injuries elsewhere in the group.
He is giving the coaching staff a reason to consider getting him on the field sooner rather than later.
For a young player trying to earn a role, Daniels has done exactly what he needed to do during the preseason: make himself difficult to ignore.
Ojulari needed to stand out Saturday. Instead, he was relatively quiet.
That doesn't mean Ojulari played poorly, but in the current state of Atlanta's edge-rusher room, simply being solid isn't necessarily enough. The Falcons need someone to emerge after losing Jalon Walker for the season with a torn ACL and facing an eight-game suspension for James Pearce Jr.
Ojulari was expected to be one of the players capable of helping fill that void.
Saturday presented another opportunity to make that case, and he didn't consistently create the kind of impact that would separate him from the rest of the group.
That matters because players such as Keshawn Banks, Cameron Sample, Bralen Trice and others are trying to take advantage of the opportunities created by Atlanta's depleted edge room.
The Falcons recently added veteran Za'Darius Smith, further increasing the competition for snaps and roster spots.
Ojulari has the talent to be an important piece of this defense.
But with Walker out and Pearce unavailable for the first eight games, Atlanta needs its edge rushers to show they can create pressure.
The door is wide open. Someone needs to walk through it.
Tagovailoa didn't play Saturday, but that doesn't mean the questions surrounding him disappeared.
If anything, the quarterback situation became more interesting.
Tagovailoa struggled in Atlanta's preseason opener and then had an uneven start during the Falcons' first joint practice against Indianapolis. He improved during the second practice, but the overall evaluation remains incomplete.
Meanwhile, Michael Penix Jr. continues working his way back from his knee injury.
Penix has now been cleared to return to 11 on 11 work and that will now add to the competition.
That creates a potentially fascinating QB1 situation.
Tagovailoa currently has the advantage because he's healthy and has been able to participate. But if Penix returns and performs well, the Falcons could suddenly have a much more serious decision on their hands.
Tagovailoa needed to take control of the job.
His recent performances haven't completely accomplished that.
The next time he takes the field, the pressure will be even greater.
Harris wasn't necessarily a loser because of something he did Saturday.
He was a loser because of what happened around him.
The Falcons' projected starters weren't slated to play against Indianapolis, but Harris entered the game in the second quarter. That is notable because Harris has been working with the starting defense and is currently projected to be one of Atlanta's starting linebackers.
If Harris were firmly established as the unquestioned starter, there wouldn't be much reason to see him in a preseason game when most of the projected starters were being held out.
Instead, the Falcons gave him additional evaluation time.
And that's because the linebacker room is becoming much more competitive.
Daniels has continued to make plays throughout camp, while Harold Perkins Jr. has also shown flashes of the athleticism that made him such an intriguing addition to the Falcons' defense.
Harris still has the inside track to start.
But the gap may not be as wide as it appeared when training camp began.
The Falcons have young linebackers pushing for opportunities, and Harris now has to continue proving that he deserves to remain at the top of that competition.
The Falcons now have one more preseason game before the real roster decisions begin.
That game against Miami will be an important opportunity for the coaching staff to finish evaluating the roster and determine which players have done enough to earn a spot.
For players such as Goodson, Strand and Daniels, Saturday helped their cases.
For players such as Ojulari and the other edge rushers, there is still work to be done.
And then there are the bigger questions surrounding the quarterback room, where Penix's potential return could add another layer to the QB1 competition while Strand continues to push for QB3.
Next week represents one of the final opportunities for players to put something on tape before cut day is upon the Falcons.
At this point in the preseason, every snap matters.

title: Falcons Provide Major Update on QB Michael Penix Jr.
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons ’ quarterback battle is finally about to become a true competition.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski announced after the preseason game that Michael Penix Jr. has been cleared to participate in 11-on-11 work, removing the biggest obstacle that has prevented Atlanta from fairly evaluating Penix and Tua Tagovailoa for the starting quarterback job.
Penix has spent much of training camp working his way back from a knee injury that ended his 2025 season. He has participated in individual drills and 7-on-7 periods, but he had not been cleared for full-team work. That changes now.
For much of camp, the Falcons haven't been able to make a true comparison between their two quarterbacks.
Tagovailoa has been participating in full-team periods, playing in preseason action and gaining valuable experience in Kevin Stefanski and Tommy Rees' offense. Penix, meanwhile, has been limited while completing his rehabilitation.
Now Penix can finally operate in the same environment as Tagovailoa.
That means working against a live pass rush, navigating protections, making decisions under pressure and operating the offense in 11-on-11 situations.
Those are critical parts of evaluating a quarterback that simply can't be replicated in 7-on-7 work.
The Falcons can finally begin making a more complete comparison.
Tagovailoa still has an advantage because of the experience he has gained in Atlanta's offense and his ability to participate fully throughout camp.
However, he hasn't completely eliminated the questions surrounding the position.
Tagovailoa's preseason debut against Denver was underwhelming, and his first joint practice against Indianapolis wasn't particularly strong either. He did show improvement during the second joint practice, but the overall evaluation remains incomplete.
That makes Penix's return even more significant.
If Tagovailoa had consistently dominated throughout camp, Penix's return might have been less threatening to his position.
Instead, there remains an opportunity for Penix to make this a legitimate competition.
Penix doesn't need to immediately win every practice. His first priority will be showing the Falcons that he is physically ready to handle full-team work.
Once that is established, the evaluation becomes about performance.
Can Penix consistently move the offense? Can he handle pressure? Can he make the downfield throws that made him such an intriguing prospect coming out of Washington?
Those answers could determine whether he has a legitimate chance to reclaim the starting job. The Falcons still have time before the regular season, but not much.
Penix's clearance means the QB1 competition is no longer hypothetical. For the first time this offseason, Atlanta can truly evaluate both quarterbacks side by side.
And now, the pressure is on both Tagovailoa and Penix to prove they should be the ones leading the Falcons into Week 1.

title: 7 Exciting Takeaways as Jack Strand, Atlanta Falcons Dominate Indianapolis Colts
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons spent most of the last week in Indiana, including a pair of joint practices against the Indianapolis Colts. After nearly a week, the Falcons looked right at home on Saturday afternoon in their 34-6 win in Lucas Oil Stadium.
While preseason games aren't a predictor of future success, the Falcons looked like a more inspired, deeper unit than the one that was dominated by the Denver Broncos last year. Every phase of the team clicked against the Colts, including their much-maligned special teams.
With several position battles on the line, there were some impressive performances by players trying to make the 53-man roster, and maybe even earn a starting job.
Here are seven takeaways from the Falcons convincing win over the Colts
Obviously, most of the attention has been on Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr., but with both of those players out on Saturday, it was an opportunity for Cooper Rush and undrafted rookie Jack Strand to shine.
Rush was an efficient 10/11 to start the game, and then Strand came in and continued his impressive training camp with a dominating performance on Saturday.
He started the game 8/8 for 155 yards and a touchdown, including dropping one in the bucket with a beautiful over-the-shoulder pass to Juice Wells for 36 yards. He took off for a 16-yard rushing touchdown on the next play to put the Falcons up 31-6.
"Spike it, Jack!" Matt Ryan on the call for the TD 😂 FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/3KLcv5gxKJ
The Falcons only kept two quarterbacks on the initial 53-man roster last season . There’s just no way that can place Strand on waivers and hope to get him to the practice squad. The 6’5 and 240-pound Strand would be hoovered up by another team immediately.
Strand has played well enough that if Tagovailoa and/or Penix struggle early, fans will be calling for the rookie. Heck, they might be doing that already.
The Falcons had arguably the worst special teams unit in the entire NFL last year. They addressed every level of the special teams with a new punter, kicker, return man, and coordinator. Those changes showed in the first sequences of the game. Atlanta kicked off and got held. The Colts started their drive on the 18.
The defense held, and Zachariah Branch fielded a 48-yard punt and returned it five yards to the Falcons’ 38. After a kickoff and a Colts’ punt, the Falcons found themselves winning the early field position battle. They cashed in with a 51-yard field goal from new kicker Nick Folk.
Folk was signed as a free agent in the offseason after the Falcons struggled with place kicking the last two seasons. He's been the NFL's most accurate kicker for three consecutive years.  He hit another 50-yarder in the fourth quarter for good measure.
The ensuing kickoff looked like an instant replay. A Colts hold, and Indianapolis was on the wrong side of its 20-yard line.
Tyler Goodson took the Colts’ first kickoff at the four-yard line and returned it 37 yards to the 41. The Falcons were last in the NFL with 22.9 yards per return last season.
Atlanta didn’t punt until midway through the second quarter, but when they did, new punter Jake Bailey hit it 58 yards to the corner, and Darren Hall downed the ball on the Colts two.
The Falcons shined in every aspect of special teams after floundering last season.
A.J. Terrell, Avieon Terrell, and Mike Hughes may be the only cornerbacks guaranteed a spot on the roster. The battle for depth is tight, and Henderson had a good early showing after getting the start. He had tight coverage on the Colts’ first drive with a pass breakup on the left sideline, helping to force a punt.
On the Colts’ second drive, he made a quick open-field tackle on a third-and-five that forced a field goal instead of a first down.
With no Bijan or Brian Robinson, the Falcons aren’t exactly empty-handed at running back. Tyler Goodson and Nathan Carter are fighting for the No. 3 spot, and both have had moments in training camp.
Goodson has the marquee play so far with a 49-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. The left side of the line, led by tackle Michael Jerrell and guard Kyle Hinton, cleared the first line of defense, and Goodson did the rest. That entire drive was his, with a long kickoff return and touchdown run.
49 yards to the CRIB 😮‍💨 @tgood1110 FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/g2qiwB6zTr
The Falcons have four wide receivers who are veritable locks to make the team: Drake London, Jahan Dotson, Olamide Zaccheaus, and Branch. They could keep as many as six, depending on special teams, but the fifth wide receiver has clearly been Chris Blair this preseason.
Blair has been head and shoulders above the others vying for a spot on the 53-man roster. He led the team in receiving last week against the Broncos, and he had another solid showing on Saturday against the Colts, including an 18-yard reception over the middle from Rush as the first quarter was closing.
He also drew a pass interference in the end zone on 4th and three from the Colts’ six that set up Atlanta’s second touchdown.
Pro Football Focus recently ranked the Falcons' defensive line as the worst in the NFL. There’s not a headliner on this team, although Brandon Dorlus led all defensive tackles in the NFC with 8.5 sacks last year. But this unit is deep.
With Zach Harrison returning, Da’Shawn Hand and newcomer Maason Smith give the Falcons a good rotation and depth on the defensive line.
That said, Carlos Allen Jr. was the star in Indianapolis. He made noise during joint practices, and he was a menace on Saturday afternoon when he got his chance. A product of Douglass High School in Atlanta, Allen is roughly 6’1 and 300 pounds, and he is forcing his way into the conversation on the defensive line.
Christian Harris was penciled in as a starter at linebacker next to Divine Deablo, but frankly, Kendal Daniels has looked more impressive. Daniels was limited during OTAs and minicamp, but he’s gotten a lot of work with the first team, and he started today over Harris. He's the biggest of the linebackers, and he has excellent instincts.
Incoming: @KendalDaniels__ 😤 FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/gmRzRq71Xl
Edge rusher Azeez Ojulari seemed like a lock to make the 53, but Keshawn Banks has outplayed him across the duration of training camp and looked significantly more productive rushing the Colts’ quarterback than Ojulari.
Banks had five sacks for the UFL’s Orlando Storm last season.
The Falcons are on the road next week against the Miami Dolphins on Friday. Head coach Kevin Stefanski said the first and third games will include the starters. Expect to see several players from today's action working in the with the first team.
The 53-man roster must be set next Sunday, and there are plenty of jobs still up for grabs.
