title: Joe Brady's Prudent Choice Sitting Bills' Key Veterans vs. Browns in Delayed Game
full_text:
Buffalo Bills ' first-year head coach Joe Brady apparently saw enough during Thursday's joint practice on the road against the Cleveland Browns.
After the Bills' first-teamers made their presence felt on the practice field, a number of the veteran starters are watching the August 22 preseason game from the sideline.
"I told the team, I want to see how today's practice goes. Ideal world, a lot of the 1s would, hey, we get a great day's practice today, and we kind of go from there and I feel like they got the work they needed," said Brady prior to the August 20 joint session.
Franchise quarterback Josh Allen, who started the August 15 preseason opener by engineering back-to-back scoring drives, isn't getting any snaps against the Browns on Saturday in Cleveland. The five-time NFL MVP finalist looked fabulous spinning the football around the yard on Thursday by multiple accounts.
The Bills also held out offensive line starters left tackle Dion Dawkins, right tackle Spencer Brown, right guard O'Cyrus Torrence and center Connor McGovern, who has been out since August 8 due to injury . Notably, veteran center Lloyd Cushenberry, who started in place of McGovern last week, was also given the day off.
Buffalo tight ends Dawson Knox and Dalton Kincaid along with RB1 James Cook and WR1 DJ Moore remained on the sideline when the starting offense took the field.
Running back Ray Davis earned the start and opened the game with an eight-yard gain.
After four snaps, the game was delayed due to lightning in the area . Only 1:49 came off the first-quarter clock prior to referee Bill Vinovich sending both teams to the locker room.
Prior to the Bills' pregame warmups, multiple first-team defensive players were seen working out. That routine usually signals that those men won't see game action. Cornerback Christian Benford, safety Cole Bishop, edge rusher Greg Rousseau, nose tackle Deone Walker and edge rusher Michael Hoecht were in that group.
Wide receivers Khalil Shakir, Skyler Bell and Dante Pettis are all dealing with undisclosed lower body injuries, although none appear to be severe.
All three wide receivers went through on-field work with trainers prior to Saturday's game. The aforementioned McGovern and fifth-round rookie safety Jalon Kilgore were also involved. Veteran safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson was spotted on a stationary bicycle.
The Bills gave Alec Anderson the start at left guard as he battles against veteran Austin Corbett for first-team status.
Meanwhile, the rest of the starting line was comprised entirely of reserves with left tackle Tylan Grable, center Sedrick Van Pran Granger, rookie right guard Armaj Reed-Adams and fourth-round right tackle Jude Bowry.
With Kyle Allen getting the start, Shane Buechele is most likely set to play the second half as the Bills attempt to identify the best backup option .
The good news is that Josh Allen will get to spend the day with a clipboard. There's simply no benefit to exposing the franchise field general in a road exhibition. Had the game been at home, one could argue that Allen should take the opportunity to continue to become acclimated in the new stadium.
"Whatever Coach asks me to do. Obviously, whether I play or not, I'm going to be happy with the decision," said the five-time NFL MVP finalist Allen. "If I don't [play], I get to cheer on my guys, Kyle and Shane, going out there. Trying to be the best teammate I can be and give them anything that I can to help them out."

title: Bills vs. Browns Weather Delay: Updates on When Preseason Week 2 Game Will Resume
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills and Cleveland Browns are currently in the midst of a weather delay during the preseason Week 2 game on Saturday.
It started pouring at Huntington Bank Field just two minutes after the game started. It started out as a light rain before the skies opened up.
Not long after that, the referees called for a delay due to lightning strikes in the area, which can be dangerous for everyone on the field and in the stands.
WGRZ's Jonathan Acosta noted that there was also a "loud crack of thunder" before the delay was called.
Follow our tracker below for the latest updates on when the game will resume.
UPDATE: According to the broadcast, the plan is for players to be given a resume warning at 1:45 p.m., players will take the field to warm up at 2 p.m., and play is expected to resume by 2:15 p.m.
So, we have a target time, although bear in mind that this is the weather we're talking about and things can change.
We are still waiting for an update from the league on an expected time for the game to resume. We'll update this page once more information becomes available.
Weather delays in the NFL usually take upwards of an hour, so it could be about that long before play resumes.
Here's a look at the situation when the game was called.
#Browns v #Bills stopped due to lightning pic.twitter.com/fVGPpPWM5T
According to the NFL rule book , a delay can occur when a game is "imminently threatened" by the weather.
Weather conditions that can cause a delay include lightning and flooding. In the case of a lightning strike, a game is called if the strike occurs within 10 miles of the stadium.
The rule book also states that "the commissioner has the authority to review the circumstances of each emergency and to adjust the following procedures in whatever manner the commissioner deems appropriate."
This is the second time the Bills and Browns have met this week.
The two teams took part in a joint practice on Thursday , which served as the main reps for Bills starters, who are not suiting up during the preseason Week 2 contest.
"(Joint practice) is as regular season as it gets," head coach Joe Brady said of the session.
The Browns, on the other hand, are playing some starters, but the vast majority are not on the field for Cleveland. Most notably, both Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson are playing, with Sanders playing in the first half and Watson getting the second.
We may not see Bills starters for the rest of the preseason, as teams usually opt to sit their ones in the final preseason game.
Bills fans won't mind that at all after the injury issues the team dealt with last season.

title: Three Main Reasons Bills' Fans Should Watch Saturday's NFL Preseason Game vs. Browns
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills contest their lone away preseason game of the summer, visiting the Cleveland Browns for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on August 22.
It comes two days after the two teams held a joint practice on Thursday at the Browns' facility in Berea.
After putting them through a productive, competitive practice , Bills' first-year head coach Joe Brady will presumably elect to keep his veteran starters sidelined .
Here are the three most important reasons Bills' fans must watch on Saturday afternoon.
Assuming starting quarterback Josh Allen sits, second-string candidates Kyle Allen and Shane Buechele will each play one half.
"Whatever Coach asks me to do. Obviously, whether I play or not, I'm going to be happy with the decision," said the five-time NFL MVP finalist Allen. "If I don't [play], I get to cheer on my guys, Kyle and Shane, going out there. Trying to be the best teammate I can be and give them anything that I can to help them out."
Both have different advantages in what appears to be a wide-open competition .
When the Bills opened the preseason schedule against the Carolina Panthers on August 15, Kyle Allen, no relation to Josh, saw 27 snaps, going 14-of-16 passing for 108 yards. Over 25 snaps, Buechele finished 6-of-9 passing for 50 yards.
It's hard to hold a punting competition when the team goes an entire game without punting once. Such was the case when the Bills opened their preseason schedule against Carolina.
"I was hoping to probably to get some punts today," said Brady last Saturday.
Seventh-round rookie Tommy Doman was the lone punter to see the field in the exhibition opener, serving as the holder for Tyler Bass on kicks. Veteran incumbent Mitch Wishnowsky, who was fighting through minor injury, did not play.
Being that Doman held last week, it's possible that Wishnowsky fills that role in Cleveland. Although he was with the Bills in 2025, Wishnowsky never had the opportunity to hold for Bass, who missed the entire season due to injury.
On the other side last week, Carolina punted only three times, leading to one Bills' return opportunity — a 12-yarder by Mecole Hardman. Backup running back Ray Davis, who established himself as the primary kick returner last year, was waiting back for the first punt of the game, but it sailed over his head for a touchback.
"Ray, obviously, wants that role," said Brady. "I want to make sure, if a guy wants that, you let him go take it and go get it."
It was an impressive debut for first-year coordinator Jim Leonhard's defense against the Panthers.
With a new system in place and position battles unfolding at every level of the unit, the preseason reps are highly valuable this summer.
In particular, there is a huge opportunity for some of the younger players to make an impression during live game action. Fourth-round rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr is included in that group as he battles against Dorian Williams for the starting inside linebacker spot next to Terrel Bernard. Williams appeared to lose multiple matchups when dropping back in pass coverage against the Browns on Thursday.
The secondary is an area of heavy interest , too. Second-round rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun and undrafted rookie Kani Walker are both making the case for a place in the primary rotation. The Bills also have a roster competition happening at safety with veterans Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone looking to stick.
It's worth watching to see how the Bills defend the deep ball and Browns' rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion, who made multiple long catches against Leonhard's crew in 11-on-11 team drills.

title: Are Josh Allen, Bills' Starters Playing Preseason Week 2 vs. Browns?
full_text:
With another week of practice in the books, the Buffalo Bills are now turning their attention to the preseason Week 2 contest against the Cleveland Browns.
The Browns and Bills met for a joint practice during the week and it yielded positive results. Both teams got a ton of work in against one another and fights weren't an issue.
Last week, the Bills played Josh Allen and the starters in the preseason opener versus the Carolina Panthers, but can we expect the same this week?
Let's dive into the details and come up with an answer.
UPDATE: NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe reports that Josh Allen and most of the Bills' starters won't play in preseason Week 2.
Wolfe leaves the door open for "young starters" to possibly play, though.
"Josh Allen & most Bills starters will sit today, per source. A few young starters may play," Wolfe wrote. "Bills got good work out of starters in joint practice & preseason opener. (Evaluations) mainly on depth today."
Bills head coach Joe Brady wouldn't commit to an answer during the week, but he did equate the joint practice to significant reps for his team, so those reps could replace preseason action.
"(Joint practice) is as regular season as it gets," Brady said.
Browns head coach Todd Monken's comments about the starters were much more telling. He noted that he and Brady did talk about it and agreed that if they see enough from their starters, neither team would play the ones in preseason Week 2.
"Well we both talked about that," Monken revealed. "If we see out of our ones, our group, our older players, what we want to see on Thursday, they would not play in the game. We agreed upon that," Monken said.
There hasn't been any indication either coach was unhappy with the amount of reps or overall performance they saw out of their ones on Thursday, so chances are both teams will rest their starters.
Knowing that, we may have seen the last of the Bills' starters in the preseason, as teams usually opt to sit their ones in the final exhibition game.
With the ones likely to sit, this presents a huge opportunity for the players who are vying for depth roles or roster spots in general to show their stuff.
It's also another opportunity for the Bills' rookies to further get their feet wet as they try and build confidence ahead of their respective first seasons in the NFL.
Buffalo and Cleveland will kick off from Huntington Bank Field on Saturday at 1 p.m. ET.
After that, the Bills return to the practice field next week before the preseason finale on Thursday, Aug. 27, against the Pittsburgh Steelers, which is three days before cutdown day on Aug. 30.

title: Four Bills' Veterans in Danger of Losing Roster Spots Heading into Browns Matchup
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills had a busy few days this past week as the team held a second open practice to the public at the new Highmark Stadium on Tuesday in Orchard Park before traveling to Ohio for a joint training camp practice with the Cleveland Browns on Thursday afternoon.
The dual session was a precursor to Saturday’s preseason game between the two squads at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, Ohio, which will mark the second exhibition match of the summer for both franchises .
Cut-down day in the NFL is less than two weeks away on August 30, so the matchup with the Browns—although it may not count officially—will be critical for many players on the bottom half of Buffalo’s roster.
Here are four veterans who are in danger of losing their spots on the 53-man roster this season.
Coming into the offseason, many outside observers thought that former 2024 fifth-round pick Sedrick Van Pran-Granger would be in line for the top backup spot in Buffalo behind starting center Connor McGovern for the 2026 regular season.
And, with McGovern currently still sidelined with a soft-tissue injury that he sustained during Buffalo’s “Return of the Blue and Red” practice at Highmark Stadium on August 8, one would have thought it’d be Van Pran-Granger that stepped in during McGovern’s somewhat lengthy absence.
While that has happened on occasion, it’s mostly been recent free-agent signing Llloyd Cushenberry III that has slid into that role for the better part of two weeks for the Bills.
Things look to be going smoothly so far this summer for the former Bronco and TItan interior lineman, too, which shouldn’t be a surprise given that the 28-year-old has started 80 games since entering the league out of LSU in 2020.
The competition isn’t over yet, but Van Pran-Granger’s roster spot is officially on notice.
Might he end up as a trade candidate at the end of this month? There are a few NFL teams in need of centers after recent injuries in training camp, so it could happen.
Watch this player closely moving forward, Bills Mafia .
When the Bills signed seventh-year veteran safety Geno Stone to a one-year deal on March 16, it was a bit of a surprise, especially considering that Buffalo had just inked fellow veteran defensive back C.J. Gardner-Johnson to a one-year contract of his own on March 12.
Gardner-Johnson seemingly signed with the intention of being third-year safety Cole Bishop’s running mate this upcoming regular season in Western New York, so the extra addition of Stone was a bit puzzling by team president/ general manager Brandon Beane .
The 27-year-old started 53 regular-season games over the last five years between his time with Cincinnati and Baltimore, but so far this summer for the Bills he’s been stuck behind Gardner-Johnson and Bishop—in spite of injuries to both—while also being in a heated competition with players like Damar Hamlin, Sam Franklin Jr., and rookie Jalon Kilgore for a depth role.
Stone, even though he’s had prominent roles in previous years during his other NFL stops, just might be on the outside looking in when it comes to cut-down day in a little over a week.
He’ll need to show something to the coaching staff over the next two preseason games.
Not much really needs to be written here.
At the beginning of training camp at St. John Fisher University , it appeared as if the Bills were going to give veteran punter Mitch Wishnowsky every chance to win the punting job in Orchard Park, New York, this season.
However, since the end of July, seventh-round rookie Tommy Doman Jr. has silently been creeping his way toward capturing the starting job.
During Tuesday’s open practice to the public at Highmark Stadium, it was Doman Jr. who was up first during all of the punting drills, and he even received all of the holding reps during the preseason opener against the Carolina Panthers despite not getting the opportunity to punt during the game.
Needless to say, Doman Jr. will likely be the punter this season unless Wishnowsky can pull off a major comeback in the coming weeks.
It’ll be interesting to see.
Although second-year offensive lineman Chase Lundt entered the NFL as a bit of a tweener along the offensive line after being drafted by the Bills in the sixth round last spring, the former University of Connecticut offensive tackle somehow managed to earn a 53-man roster spot with Buffalo as a rookie.
He wasn’t very impactful, though, as he managed to only dress for two games all season long.
And, given that the Bills have since signed veteran interior lineman Austin Corbett in free agency earlier this spring, while also drafting rookie tackle Jude Bowry and rookie guard Ar’Maj Reed-Adams this past April, it’s not hard to see that Lundt’s time in Western New York might be short lived.
The 26-year-old hasn’t done much in terms of standing out—either negatively or positively—through training camp thus far, so in order to earn a roster spot again he’ll have to stand out in a big way over this final week-and-a-half stretch.
The preseason games against the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers are going to have huge implications for the 6-foot-7, 304-pound Texas native’s NFL future.

title: Four Bold Predictions For Bills vs. Browns in Preseason Week 2
full_text:
Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady hasn't said much about his plans for the starters in Week 2 of the preseason, but it doesn't seem likely they will play .
On Thursday, the Bills took on the Cleveland Browns in a joint practice and Brady was able to get his starters plenty of work. Coaches often praise these sessions, with Brady saying they are " as regular season as it gets ." That means we should see a steady dose of backups against the Browns, which is "as preseason as it gets."
While it might not be as exciting to watch the reserves, there are still plenty of reasons to tune in as several roster battles will unfold before our eyes . As players fight for their spot on the roster this weekend against Cleveland, here's a look at four bold predictions for their preseason Week 2 showdown.
Ray Davis made it clear to Joe Brady that he wants a crack at the punt return job and Brady said the backup running back will be in the mix. That could involve Davis getting a chance to return punts against the Browns. In this bold prediction, he makes the most of that by ripping off a return of 50-plus yards to prove he deserves a chance at the job in the regular season.
Tyler Bass missed the entire 2025 season after undergoing surgery to repair a sports hernia. Matt Prater filled in admirably last year, but the Bills are turning back to Bass this season. While the coaching staff has faith in the veteran kicker, Bass has the fans concerned after missing a 45-yard kick in the preseason opener.
He was 3-of-4 overall, but the concerns haven't died down, especially after missing two kicks during Thursday's practice . Expecting Bass to be in midseason form right now would be unrealistic, but the misses are unsettling, to say the least. In this bold prediction, which is admittedly less than ideal, Bass misses another sub-50 yard kick which leaves fans more concerned than ever about the kicking situation in Buffalo.
Second-year defensive back Jordan Hancock was one of the brightest stars last Saturday, recording four tackles with two going for a loss. Listed at safety, Hancock has been surging in the nickel role, proving himself worthy of a spot on the 53-man roster . Hancock is expected to spend more time at safety as he makes a case for his spot on the roster and in this bold prediction, he locks that spot up by recording a pick-six.
Rookie T.J. Parker recorded a sack during the Bills' first preseason game, which is unsurprising given how well he's played throughout the offseason. Parker, who was the 35th overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft isn't in line to start with Bradley Chubb and Greg Rousseau ahead of him, but he should get plenty of opportunities during his rookie season. In this final bold prediction, Parker records another sack as he shows why Buffalo targeted him in the draft as well as why he's going to be a heavy part of their EDGE rotation in 2026.

title: Bills' Roster Long Shot Impressing Again in NFL Preseason, Delivers Boom vs. Browns
full_text:
Making noise during the NFL Preseason is nothing new for running back Ian Wheeler, especially when the Buffalo Bills are involved.
Prior to joining the Bills earlier this summer, Wheeler played five preseason games for the Chicago Bears after signing as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2024. Two of those five exhibition matchups happened to be with Buffalo, and Wheeler has four career touchdowns against the Bills' preseason defense as a result.
This time, wearing a Bills' uniform, Wheeler accounted for arguably the most-notable play of the day during Thursday's joint practice against the Cleveland Browns in Berea.
With Bills' quarterback Shane Buechele flushed out of the pocket during a live team rep, Wheeler provided a safety valve along the right sideline. After pulling in a short pass from Buechele, the stout ball carrier turned upfield. Running parallel to the sideline, Wheeler challenged a Cleveland defender head on and lowered an audible boom.
Making Browns' safety Daniel Thomas the latest "Angry Run" victim, Wheeler bulldozed the veteran who landed on his backside as a result of the jarring hit that caused Bills' teammates to erupt in excitement. Watch the play courtesy of WGRZ's Jonathan Acosta .
"In practice, defense wants to thud. Offense, you gotta bring your shoulder pads, too. Typically, low man's gonna win in those scenarios. Like I said, he's a pretty low runner," said Bills' quarterback Josh Allen .
The Bears released Wheeler prior to the start of the 2025 regular season, and, following a short stay on the New Orleans Saints' practice squad, the Howard product resurfaced in the UFL this past spring .
Wheeler proceeded to average 5.4 yards per carry and rushed for six touchdowns over nine UFL regular season games. Helping the Louisville Kings capture the league title, the running back earned United Bowl MVP honors after rushing for 81 yards and the go-ahead touchdown on 10 attempts against the DC Defenders.
The Bills added Wheeler to their 90-man roster midway through June, creating a spot by designating undrafted rookie running back Desmond Reid as waived/injured.
Wheeler opened the preseason schedule by leading the Bills in rushing during their August 15 win over the Carolina Panthers. The hard runner totaled 41 yards and one touchdown on seven carries.
"He's a low runner. His center of gravity is really low. During the game last week, it felt like he was driving the pile by himself," said Allen.
Wheeler, who has yet to play in a NFL regular season game, will presumably get another prime exhibition opportunity on Saturday against the Browns in Cleveland. The August 22 kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET.
Wheeler is currently battling with Frank Gore Jr. while trying to break into Buffalo's Top 3.
"He's got a lot of power to him. Very excited to see what he can do these next couple weeks and next couple games," said Allen.

title: Panthers Have Not Given Bryce Young What He Needs in Make-or-Break Year 4
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have tried to support Bryce Young , especially once it became clear that he could not overcome an abysmal roster in 2023. They began adding pieces at various spots on offense to try to help. Unfortunately, in 2026, it's clear that it didn't work very well.
The first thing a team can do for its quarterback is give him weapons to throw to. The Panthers have done a passable job of that, but we can't pretend this pass-catching unit is elite. Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker are doing all the heavy lifting.
PFF ranked them 22nd in the NFL , and it's hard to disagree with the ranking. There aren't 22 better duos in the NFL than McMillan and Coker, but there are so many other players to consider, and for the Panthers, most of them are simply not very good.
"Beyond those two, there is very little proven talent to speak of in this receiving room. Tight ends Ja’Tavion Sanders and Tommy Tremble have combined for four straight PFF receiving grades in the 50.0s over the last two seasons," the blurb for the Panthers read.
The second thing a team can do for its quarterback is provide him with a good running game. The Panthers have tried to do that and probably believe that they have, but the numbers disagree. Even with Rico Dowdle last year, the running game was not good.
This year, PFF ranked them 27th , and it's once again hard to disagree. None of Chuba Hubbard, Trevor Etienne, or AJ Dillon has the explosiveness needed to really succeed in the NFL. Jonathon Brooks might, but he's a wild card.
"Question marks remain over the health of Jonathon Brooks, who has taken just nine handoffs since he was drafted 46th overall two years ago," the blurb read.
The final thing a team can do for its quarterback is protect him. The Panthers have done a better job of protecting Bryce Young than providing him weapons or a running game, but it's still not a good situation thanks to injuries.
In fact, PFF rightly noted that the Panthers' offensive line is a top-five unit most primed for regression. The line was very good in 2025, but it could be rough in 2026. There are a lot of talented players, but how well do they fit?
Some key losses, both injury-related and other, have tanked this line. Ikem Ekwonu, Taylor Moton, Austin Corbett, and Cade Mays, all of whom posted 66.0 or better PFF grades, are gone for right now.
"Ekwonu is expected to miss the majority of the season after suffering a ruptured patellar tendon in the playoffs, while Moton will be sidelined into the starting slate due to blood clots in his lung. Also, former starting center Cade Mays headed to Detroit, while Corbett is now in Buffalo," PFF analyst Bradley Locker wrote.
Locker noted that the Panthers added nice replacements in Monroe Freeling, Rasheed Walker, Sam Hecht, and Luke Fortner, but that's a lot of new additions to the line, and there's no telling how rookies Freeling and Hecht will fare in their first NFL seasons.
Simply put, the Panthers have tried and failed to surround Bryce Young with help. This is probably the best overall offense he's had in the NFL, but the bar is on the floor, and even with the talent they do have, there are major question marks.

title: Jonathon Brooks' Biggest Issue in Preseason Week 2 Could Limit Snaps With Panthers
full_text:
Running back Jonathon Brooks had a few standout moments in the Carolina Panthers' preseason Week 2 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, but it wasn't all good for him.
Brooks ripped off an 11-yard run during the contest, and he was able to find pay dirt for the first time in his career on a one-yard carry in the first quarter.
However, Brooks' pass-blocking left a lot to be desired. Brooks saw three pass-blocking reps, according to Pro Football Focus , and gave up two pressures and scored a putrid 6.6 grade.
Here's one of those snaps in which he gave up a pressure.
Jonathon Brooks has to be better in pass pro here. Bad whiff. This is likely a first down for Brycen Tremayne if Brooks does his job. Have to be better in this area if you're going to be reliable on third downs. #Panthers pic.twitter.com/wN2i57dpWn
Now, to be fair, Brooks did redeem himself in another pass pro rep later on, but his showing overall was not good.
It goes without saying that Bryce Young's life is going to be a lot harder if his running backs can't adequately block for him.
We saw that first hand in the clip above, as Young's throw was clearly impacted on a play that otherwise would have gained yardage if Young had a cleaner look.
More specifically for Brooks, he can't hope to see many snaps on third downs if his pass pro isn't up to snuff. If he doesn't improve, Brooks is going to cede even more work to Chuba Hubbard, who remains the favorite to lead the backfield at the start of the year, and quite possibly even Trevor Etienne or AJ Dillon.
PFF has charted four pass-blocking snaps in total for Brooks in the preseason. The third-year back had a successful rep in the previous preseason game, and had another in the second.
That said, the bad has been really bad thus far.
The good news for Brooks is that Etienne hasn't been much better with his pass pro snaps. Etienne has registered a 29.1 grade in two pass protection snaps this preseason, and he posted a 22.9 grade through three pass-blocking snaps last season.
Hubbard is the best and most proven blocker of the trio, but he isn't great in that area by any stretch after posting a lackluster grade of 46.8 in 2025.
All of this points to a pass protection problem in the backfield for the Panthers, and it's one they need to fix.
Outside of the clear struggles in pass protection, Brooks took a step forward in his second preseason game of the season.
He barely averaged three yards per carry and only finished with five carries for 18 yards, but those were still better numbers than last week. He also ripped off an 11-yard run when the right side of Carolina's offensive line opened up a nice hole for him.
That run, along with his score, will only help Brooks build confidence as the regular season approaches.

title: Carolina Panthers' Costly Offensive Line at Risk of Major Regression Soon
full_text:
The theme of the Carolina Panthers ' offseason has been change. Spending heavily in free agency , the Panthers entered training camp having spent the fifth-most money in the league on contracts.
Not only did Carolina make huge changes on defense, but on the offensive line, new faces are all over the line now and look to prove themselves on short-term deals.
As far as free agency goes, Carolina signed two new faces to the line. Rasheed Walker at left tackle, leaving Green Bay for Carolina, and Luke Fortner from the division rival Saints. The Panthers also used the 19th pick in the NFL Draft on Monroe Freeling, out of Georgia.
A revamped offensive line isn't always a positive. If anything, this unit only has more question marks than answers heading into the season.
PFF's Bradley Locker dropped his predictions for the five units in the NFL that could regress in 2026 on Thursday. On that list, the Panthers' offensive line, and rightfully so. The line is revamped, but while fresh faces can be a good thing, key starters from last season's 8th-ranked offensive line won't be on the field.
Including playoffs, Cade Mays started at center for the Panthers in 13 games. Since the Wild Card loss, Mays has departed Carolina, signing with the Detroit Lions. In the regular season, Mays logged 726 snaps and allowed 0 sacks.
Luke Fortner replaces Mays, a solid, experienced starter who played for the New Orleans Saints and Jacksonville Jaguars. Fortner posted a 72.5 PFF pass-blocking grade. That's the seventh-highest in the NFL for centers who qualify.
Taylor Moton was set to start at right tackle in 2026, but is currently dealing with blood clots . Moton is being replaced by a rookie to start the year. Monroe Freeling does have absurd upside and was selected in the first round. Rookie linemen usually have growing pains, and Freeling was supposed to be the backup left tackle.
The one silver lining is that Freeling has experience at right tackle, logging snaps there in his junior year. Freeling has also been open and honest about not caring where he plays; this was evident at the NFL Combine, when he took snaps at center.
Then theres new personnel at left tackle as well; Rasheed Walker takes over starting duties. Walker wouldn't have been needed if Ikem Ekwonu wasn't injured, though. Ekwonu will likely miss the entire 2026 season due to a torn patellar tendon suffered in the Wild Card loss against the Rams.
Playing 942 snaps in 2025, Ekwonu only gave up 5 sacks in the season. Now, in his first year in a new system, Walker is supposed to be a stable, and reliable piece of this pass protection, especially as he fights for a long-term deal, whether it's in Carolina or not.
Continuity is key for a successful offensive line. Carolina has clearly lost that to begin the 2026 NFL season. In the last two years, the Panthers are 0-2 to begin the season; that trend may very well continue if this unit struggles to gel out of the gate.
$102.3 million, thats how expensive the Panthers' offensive line is in 2026. Spending over 30% of the salary cap space on a unit means it needs to be not just good, but consistently good.
Carolina has multiple players who have just one year left on their deals, including Ekwonu, who is making a lofty $17.56 million this season whilst recovering from injury.
Regression up front also means regression from Bryce Young, who enters a pivotal contract season and is under more pressure than almost any other QB in the NFL. The last thing that the Panthers want to do is make any drastic moves. Now it's up to both Young and the trenches up front to step forward.

title: Carolina Panthers Crushed Jaguars, But Here's What Really Matters
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers easily handled the Jacksonville Jaguars in their third preseason outing to move to 2-1. Ordinarily, that result alone would be a good thing. But in the preseason, wins and losses don't matter, even if the Panthers happen to seemingly dominate. Here's what does matter, though.
Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan were a great duo last season. They terrorized the Jaguars in joint practice. They did it again in very sparse action in this contest, drawing a clear pass interference for a first down and making another big gain with McMillan working out of the slot. That gives the Panthers some interesting wrinkles to work with, especially after Chris Brazzell's injury.
We didn't expect AJ Dillon to make the roster, and he still might not. But he is making that a very hard decision to make. Trevor Etienne plays special teams, and that matters, but Dillon has been a force on the ground. He's been downright excellent as a backup, looking perhaps the best of all three main backs. He has potentially forced his way onto the roster, which is a huge achievement.
There was plenty of concern over last week's poor offensive showing sans Damien Lewis and Robert Hunt. If that had continued with them back in the lineup, there would be some major offensive problems. Fortunately, with them back, the offense ran much smoother. Protection was still an issue, but it was much better, especially in the middle.
the Panthers starting LB2 is not on the roster
The Panthers are having an LB2 competition between Claudin Cherilus and Trevin Wallace, and really, anyone could put their name in the ring. It's that open a competition. Tonight, without Devin Lloyd, was a good chance to analyze the contenders, and they were pretty much all bad. The Panthers don't need an ace linebacker there, but they don't have a starting-caliber player.
Does it really matter if the Panthers have several players capable of being a WR4-6? Not really, because NFL offenses don't use them like that. Still, Jimmy Horn and John Metchie have looked very solid as special teamers and on offense, and Ja'seem Reed didn't play, but he's been great, too. There's some depth at the back end.

title: Grading Bryce Young and Other Panthers QBs in Preseason Contest vs. Jaguars
full_text:
Preseason game No. 3 is in the books , and the Carolina Panthers looked better than ever on the road in Jacksonville. While half of Carolina's four touchdowns were on the ground, the quarterback play looked like a whole new unit compared to the road preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills .
In a dominant 34-17 win over the Jaguars, three QBs saw the field, and each of them was able to be productive and make impressive plays. None of Carolina's QBs made any catastrophic plays that resulted in turnovers.
The snap count for each QB wasn't very even, but all three put enough on film to earn grades. Here's how Bryce Young, Kenny Pickett, and Kyle Trask performed under the friday night lights in Jacksonville
Throwing just six passes, Young made the most of his limited action in Jacksonville. Young finished the game completing 5 of 6 pass attempts, totaling 49 yards.
Carolina's first drive wasn't pretty at all, but it was primarily because the pass protection was lacking. Young didn't panic with pressure coming his way, and made up for it on the second drive.
Carolina's franchise QB showed a little bit of everything: patience in the pocket before finding Tetairoa McMillan, scrambling away from defenders, and completing a short pass on the sideline.
Young found both Coker and McMillan, which is key as they build more chemistry heading into the 2026 season. McMillan almost scored a touchdown off a short pass from Young but was stopped at the one yard line.
Desicion making looked on point, and Young was able to be consistent and lead the Panthers down the field for what turned into a Jonathon Brooks 1-yard rushing touchdown.
It's important to note that Young and the first team offense played against the Jaguars second team defense, but that just means Young did was he was supposed to do.
Seeing the most game action of any Panthers QB. Pickett had some ups and downs early in the second quarter, but tightened up and led Carolina into multiple scoring drives.
Pickett finished the night 15/25, for 137 passing yards and a beautiful touchdown pass to Roc Taylor. Carolina's clear QB2's passer rating improved throughout the night, finishing at an 88.2.
60% completion percentage isn't anything to write home about, but Pickett was decisive and made plays when needed.
Pickett's connection with John Metchie III was the highlight of the night. The two connected on multiple chunk plays, and Metchie ended the night with 6 catches for 77 yards, leading Carolina.
Trask is the newest QB on the roster, being brought in after undrafted free agent Haynes King hurt his hamstring.
Trask did a lot of handing off the ball, but he completed all 4 of his passes for 52 yards and even threw a touchdown pass to Casey Washington. One play that stood out was also to Washington, where Trask rolled out to his right and completed a pass on the move for a first down.
Not much to grade, but nothing negative to takaway from Trask's performance either.

title: Major Takeaways from Carolina Panthers' Enormous Preseason Win vs. Jaguars
full_text:
Preseason games don't matter, and they certainly don't matter when teams use their starters versus backups. A lot of Carolina Panthers starters played, while plenty of Jacksonville Jaguars did not. Still, positive reps are positive reps, and negative reps are negative. Here's what we learned.
The Panthers opened up with a much better first drive, but it ended the same: with a punt. The reason? Pressure on every single passing play. Bryce Young avoided a couple of sacks with some nice movement, otherwise it would have been a truly ugly series once again. That has to get cleaned up.
Ironically, despite poor pass protection again, Bryce Young looked quite comfortable out there. He navigated the pocket really well to avoid the pressure, and his chemistry with the receivers was very solid. It was a very solid performance for the fourth-year QB, an encouraging sign after a lackluster preseason debut last week. He and Tetairoa McMillan picked up right where they left off in joint practice.
Travis Hunter, Trevor Lawrence, and other Jaguars starters didn't play, but some of the same secondary issues still cropped up. The zone scheme left some players wide open again, and even when they were covered, the Panthers struggled to make plays on the ball with their top defenders, most notably Mike Jackson, who has not had a great preseason. C.J. Williams gave the Panthers fits.
Princely Umanmielen made a great case to start last week opposite Jaelan Phillips. This week, without Phillips, he was a pest in the backfield once again. Pat Jones got a sack early on, but Umanmielen had multiple pressures and looked to be just as unblockable. He really might force the Panthers to put him on the field early and often this year.
I don’t think Jimmy Horn Jr. should be considered to be in a #Panthers roster battle with John Metchie, David Moore and/or Brycen Tremayne anymore Return value. WR value. Run blocking on the AJD tuddy. Hell, he was lead block on the kick return right before halftime.
What are the Panthers going to do with the final few WRs? Jimmy Horn Jr. is making his claim to be on the roster. He hasn't been exceptional as a receiver, but he's been very solid on special teams. That continued today, and he had a really good run on a trick play, which could be his role as it was last year.
The Panthers have a difficult decision on their hands. If we assume they're keeping three running backs, things are going to be tough. Trevor Etienne is good on special teams and as a receiver, but AJ Dillon has been very good this preseason, driving through contact and creating extra yards. It's going to comw down to the wire between those two behind Jonathon Brooks and Chuba Hubbard.
One of the things that kept a mediocre defense afloat last year an opportunistic streak. They forced a lot of turnovers. This year, they have the talent to survive without that, but it would still be good. In tonight's game, they forced two turnovers, the first two of the preseason. Chau Smith-Wade intercepted a pass and Cam Gill recovered a fumble forced by DeVonta Smith.

title: 7 Players to Watch While Panthers Look to Right Ship vs. Jaguars
full_text:
Tonight, the Carolina Panthers are taking on the Jacksonville Jaguars, and all eyes will be on Carolina after an underwhelming, to put it lightly, showing against the Buffalo Bills. Almost everyone needs to play better, but there are a few players we're watching closely to see how they do this week.
We were willing to give Bryce Young a pass for an inauspicious start to the preseason . The fourth-year QB has been great in camp, and the protection was abysmal during his nine snaps in the preseason. With his starting guards back, he should be better. Regardless, he needs to show something more, even if the cards are stacked against him.
Speaking of, both Damien Lewis and Robert Hunt are expected to play tonight. That's a huge development. Mostly, we're looking to see if the protection improves. There are some new pieces up front, but not these two. If their presence can stabilize things, great. If they can't, then this offensive line (and offense as a whole) is in big trouble.
So far, there's been no conversation about Pat Jones not starting. He is expected to return tonight after an injury absence and start opposite Jaelan Phillips. If he doesn't produce, those conversations might begin to crop up, especially since the Phillips-Princely Umanmielen pairing was absolutely electric last week against the Buffalo Bills.
This goes for Jaycee Horn as well, but we're not as concerned about him. Last week, Mike Jackson was beat in coverage plenty of times, as wide receivers were routinely wide open. The zone scheme doesn't seem to help, but he thrived in it in 2025. He and the team need Jackson to perform, as he's angling for a contract and the Panthers want to have success on the back end.
Monroe Freeling only played 10 snaps, so take this with a grain of salt, but he was not good last week. He posted a sub-40.0 PFF pass protection grade, though his run-blocking was fairly decent. That's got to improve. Freeling is the protector of the future, and the Panthers took a risk selecting him (one that has paid off with Taylor Moton's injury, but still), and he needs to prove himself.
It was impossible to get a read on the Panthers' first-team WRs last week because no one on offense made an impact in nine plays. But we know what Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker bring to the table. It's Xavier Legette who remains a wild card. What he does after a solid camp will be very telling.

title: Mike Jackson Will Get Paid; Should Panthers Foot the Expensive Bill?
full_text:
When the Carolina Panthers are through with the 2026 season, one of their biggest offseason decisions will be at cornerback, where the team will have to decide on what to do with Mike Jackson, who is entering the final year of his deal.
Initially signed to a cheap one-year deal in 2024, Jackson was re-signed on a two-year, $10.5 million contract in 2025 and went on to have a sensational season.
According to Pro Football Focus , Jackson's 80.9 coverage grade was third among all cornerbacks, and he gave up a completion rate of 55.6% and a passer rating of 72.9.
PFF also recently noted that Jackson is the 10th-highest graded player from 2025 who is entering a contract year in 2026.
On the surface, it would seem like paying Jackson to keep him around for the long haul is an easy decision, but that is not the case.
As great as Jackson was last season , there is no world in which the Panthers should unload a lot of money on him, especially before this season plays out.
After all, there's no telling if last season was a fluke and if Jackson will return to the lackluster form we saw in 2024.
Even if Jackson plays 2026 out and goes on to have yet another strong showing, the Panthers still should not be backing up the Brinks truck for him.
That's because Jackson is set to turn 30 in January and we all know that's the age when many players begin to decline.
The Panthers simply can't risk giving Jackson a lucrative, long-term deal, only to have his play significantly decline at the beginning or during the middle of his new deal.
Now, none of this is to say the Panthers shouldn't re-sign Jackson at all. If Carolina can get the veteran cornerback on a short-term deal that provides a reasonable bump in pay, it's worth keeping him around because finding a replacement could become expensive giving the rising cost of cornerbacks.
Spotrac estimates a three-year, $40 million deal for Jackson in his next contract. That amounts to about $13 million annually, which isn't bad but is still a bit too rich for our blood.
We'd be more comfortable in the range of a two-year, $20 million deal that doesn't have much, if any, commitment in the second year. That would amount to nearly double the previous deal Jackson received from Carolina.

title: 6 Things We're Looking For as Carolina Panthers Take on Jaguars
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers will look to turn things around in the preseason as they take on the Jacksonville Jaguars. The starters are once again expected to play, and they'll be looking to do better than three three-and-outs. Here's everything we're looking for tonight.
The offense flat-out struggled last weekend. This week, both Damien Lewis and Robert Hunt are expected to play, so the protection should be better. title: Panthers Predicted to Cut Haynes King in Potentially Catastrophic Mistake
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have some tough cuts ahead, as all NFL teams always do before the regular season begins. These players pour their lives into the team all summer, only to end up without a roster spot.
It can be painful. Some will be more painful than others. For the Panthers, the most painful, according to FanSided's Mark Powell and Zachary Rotman , is going to be Haynes King. Here's why that might be a costly mistake.
Haynes King has played in just the Hall of Fame Game so far, but he showed in that game that he is more than worthy of an NFL roster spot. The Panthers should grant him that, though he needs to get healthy to ensure he does make it.
FanSided authors Zachary Rotman and Mark Powell, however, see King as the "most painful" cut the Panthers are going to have to make. It certainly would be painful, and it might be something the Panthers should avoid.
"This performance has some Carolina Panthers fans dreaming of him potentially being Bryce Young's backup, and while sure, that's possible, is Dave Canales really going to have King, an undrafted rookie, leapfrog a far more proven option in Kenny Pickett on the depth chart?" they asked.
They answered their own question with doubt, adding that he could be stashed on the practice squad, but that's how players get poached for other teams, and King undoubtedly would be.
It is true that the ultimate goal of a backup quarterback should be to aid the starter. In that sense, the Panthers are probably happy with Pickett, who has a wealth of experience and knows plenty of offensive schemes.
But you just cannot let true talent go for nothing, and in this case, cutting King would be just that. You especially can't let talent go that could actually help the offense in more ways than one.
King, who stands 6'2" and weighs 212 pounds, would be a phenomenal short-yardage package QB. The Panthers experimented with Mitchell Evans taking those QB sneak snaps to protect the smaller Bryce Young, but why not an actual QB who knows how to take snaps?
Sure, that would indicate that the Panthers are doing a sneak, but so does putting a tight end under center. The alternative is not to have those plays available at all, which has hampered the Panthers under Dave Canales.
Additionally, having King in on those plays means the Panthers could do anything. He could execute a sneak, a handoff, a bootleg, or a pass play, so the defense would eventually be on its toes when he entered on third or fourth-and-one.
The Panthers' offense has never been creative enough to try anything like this, but one can imagine the sort of Taysom Hill-esque plays they could run with King. He said during the offseason that he's a QB and not a hybrid, but the Panthers could use him in fun two-QB plays.
The point is, King is actually talented. He's not likely to ever be an NFL starter, but he's certainly good enough to keep on a roster and should see the field occasionally for plays like the ones mentioned above.
Is the $4 million being paid to Pickett for his leadership and mentoring of Young worth losing the talent that King has?
Of course, we covered the difficult situation the Panthers are in with King's injury . How can they roster him if he doesn't get back on the field? But based on the talent we saw, they just can't afford to cut him outright unless there simply is no other option.

title: 4 Winners and 3 Losers From the Chicago Bears' Preseason Loss Against Cincinnati
full_text:
The Chicago Bears came out flat in the team's disappointing 27-9 loss in Cincinnati. The defense gave up chunk gains all night long, and the offense failed to get in the end zone.
They'll have plenty to clean up before the regular season kicks off on September 13. However, that's what the preseason is for, after all. They'll have another chance to work out the kinks next week against Tennessee.
While they didn't have a stellar showing by any means, that's not to say that there weren't any positive takeaways. A few players had standout performances on both sides of the ball. At the same time, others struggled MIGHTILY.
Who were some the most significant examples on both sides of the aisle?
Wide receiver Jahdae Walker only came down with one catch, but what a massive catch it was. His 36-yard spinning grab was the most explosive play in what was a far less-than-stellar offensive performance. He made up some ground on Kalif Raymond, who has a slight edge at WR3, in an under-the-radar position battle .
While Walker didn't have a flawless performance (he committed a false start late in the first quarter), his grab was a shining light in an otherwise flat showing. He'll probably have the night off next week against Tennessee.
Braxton Jones needed a quality performance last night to stake a claim on the starting left tackle job (at least until Ozzy Trapilo is ready to return to the lineup). Unfortunately, he fell well short of that goal. Bengals backup defensive end Cedric Johnson absolutely had him on skates at one point. That was also far from his only rough play of the night.
Braxton Jones my goodness man pic.twitter.com/HW2agfAFlT
At this point, it seems like Jones will still probably hold onto the LT job. However, he'll only win it by default. Jedrick Wills and Kiran Amegadjie didn't do anything to supplant him. Theo Benedet (who also didn't exactly show out) might get more of a look in next week's preseason finale against Tennessee, but he'd also only be a placeholder. This is clearly Trapilo's job once he gets the green light to return to action.
Linebacker D'Marco Jackson FLIES to the ball. All. The. Time. He racked up three tackles on the first drive, and two of them were right at the line of scrimmage.
Jackson has shown flashes in both preseason games and will probably play a key role on defense this season. He was arguably their best coverage linebacker last season after making his mark late in the year. Based on the early sample size, his run defense has improved (or he just got more comfortable in his role).
Running back Roschon Johnson had a solid showing last week against Cleveland . He also had a few solid runs early on against Cincinnati, finishing with 12 attempts for 42 yards. On top of the less-than-stellar yards per attempt (3.5), he also missed a wide open running lane that could've been a chunk play for the offense.
Roschon Johnson missed a huge hole on the left side. #DaBears pic.twitter.com/DG48Qf03hb
Was the run supposed to go to the right? Probably. That doesn't mean that a running back with even marginal vision would take the truck-sized lane to the left. It'll probably be a teaching point in film review this week. Salvon Ahmed, who had six attempts for 36 yards, looks like the clear leader for the RB3 job right now.
Is it premature to say definitively that the Bears found a gem with the sixth-round selection of Jordan van den Berg? At this point, it somehow doesn't feel that way (even if it logically 100% is). He received significant hype over the first few weeks of training camp and has now followed that up with two promising performances over their two preseason contests.
Four words. Jordan. Van. Den. Berg. pic.twitter.com/SRNPbcVIo3
Simply put, players of his size shouldn't move as fast as he can . The TFL shown above (which seemingly wasn't considered a TFL based on the stat sheet as of the time I'm writing this) made the highlight reel. It arguably wasn't even his most impressive play of the game, though. He outran defensive end Daniel Hardy to the edge and forced Sean Clifford, who ran a 4.62-second 40-yard dash at the 2023 NFL Scouting Combine, out of bounds short of the first-down line later in the game.
It was both a ridiculous feat of athleticism and an example of a rookie showing GREAT effort in a meaningless game. He played like he was fighting for a roster spot despite knowing full well that it's been locked up for weeks.
None of the Bengals' offensive starters saw the field last night. You'd think that the Bears' defense would've performed a bit better early on, considering many of their starters were on the field on the first drive. Nevertheless, Cincinnati's backup offense began the night with a 14-play drive that resulted in a field goal.
Both Bengals quarterbacks, Josh Johnson and Sean Clifford, had no issues finding open receivers all night long. They routinely picked on backup cornerback Dontae Manning, and he let up some chunk gains. So did undrafted rookie safety before he came down with an impressive interception in the fourth quarter. The blitzes were also choreographed practically every time they were called. There will be a lot for EVERYONE on defense to learn in reviewing the film for this one.
Dayo Odeyingbo looked awfully motivated against the Bengals. He followed up an extremely disappointing performance against Cleveland with a strong showing against Cincinnati. The 26-year-old leveled Josh Johnson with a bone-rattling hit early in the game, and was a problem for the Bengals' backup offensive line on a few other plays.
Ladies and gentlemen, I present to you, a motivated Dayo Odeyingbo pic.twitter.com/r4ElEibzNO
A healthy and impactful Odeyingbo would go a LONG way for Chicago's defense this season. Hopefully he can use the performance as a confidence booster and eventual launching point once the games start to count.

title: Perhaps It's Time for Ben Johnson and the Bears to Get Serious
full_text:
Let the panic begin. Sure, it's too early, but it will start nonetheless.
There's little doubt the Bears used quarterback Caleb Williams and starters against Cincinnati because they wanted to see sharper play than in Thursday's practice against the Bengals, especially by their offense.
From that end, they failed to meet their chief objective or numerous other ones in Saturday's 27-9 preseason loss to the Bengals.
The starting offense played one series and produced a 45-yard Cairo Santos field goal, but Williams was unsteady and went 2-of-5 for 28 yards. He missed a wide-open TD to tight end Colston Loveland in the process.
Keenum to Roush for 26 yards, Bears set up in Bengals territory headed into Q2. pic.twitter.com/2sGTA4tgaY
If the Bears had one other offensive objective it was seeing left tackle Braxton Jones block well. His actual blocks will be better left to grades from the film, but Jones was called for holding on a running play and the penalty helped kill what could have been a touchdown drive on the first team's only possession. He also got driven back into the passer by a bull rusher, a self-admitted problem of his while pass blocking.
Their left tackle situation did anythin but become more clear with this performance.
The running game inched along without a breakaway run, as Roschon Johnson started and gained 11 yards on three attempts behind the starting line. Johnson kept playing and finished with 42 yards on 12 carries.
If Ben Johnson wanted anything out of the game it was more consistency on offense after the 34-10 preseason opening win over Cleveland but the Bears went 1-for-7 on third down conversions in the first half and finished the game with 11 penalties for 81 yards.
If Caleb gets hurt I want Ben Johnson thrown under the jail https://t.co/ZrAnOVbbhJ
The Bears' first team defense didn't play in its entirety, but the remnants of it after a rash of training camp injuries did see time.
Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen used a mix of starters and backups, and pulled almost all of them by the second Cincinnati series. The exceptions were Gervon Dexter and Dayo Odeyingbo playing with backups against former Bears QB Josh Johnson and the backup Bengals offense.
The starters on defense allowed a drive to an Evan McPherson 25-yard field goal, and later the backups gave up three touchdowns and a field goal. Defensive back Dontae Manning got burned twice for touchdowns, one a 17-yarder to Colbie Young by Johnson and another for 20 yards by Sean Clifford to Noah Thomas. The other TD pass was a 6-yarder by Johnson given up  by Bears safety Skyler Thomas to Tanner Hudson. Thomas did get a bit of revenge late in the game with an interception.
. @Bengals fourth-round pick Colbie Young finds the end zone! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d6i7YLVH71
Even the special teams performance was lackluster. Cairo Santos missed a 53-yard second-half field goal try, his second field goal miss in preseason.
If the Bears wanted to get starters on the field for the preseason finale, no one would question it after this performance. It's unlikely to impact what Johnson decides, though.
Johnson let tight ends coach Jim Dray and defensive backs coach Al Harris call plays in the second half. They had no more success than Johnson and Dennis Allen in the first half.
It might be time to junk the gimmicks and legacy talk in order to focus on getting ready for the regular season. It's becoming larger and larger on the horizon.
They'll get two straight days off now before practicing again at Halas Hall to play Tennessee in the preseason finale. They need to come back and be a more serious, competitive football team.
Ben Johnson after watching one drive of the Bears starting offense and defense pic.twitter.com/LMhNxedxvL

title: Biggest Takeaways From Chicago Bears' Preseason Week 2 Loss to Cincinnati Bengals
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are one week closer to the start of the 2026 season after taking on the Cincinnati Bengals in the preseason Week 2 game on Saturday night, which Chicago lost, 27-9.
We were thrown a bit of a curveball ahead of the contest, as head coach Ben Johnson decided to play Caleb Williams and many of the ones on offense after it was assumed they wouldn't suit up.
"It will be good for him to go through the night game routine. He's prepared to play as long as he needs to for our offense," said Johnson.
Unfortunately, we didn't exactly get the performance we wanted to see out of the starters on offense, and the same can be said for the defensive side of the ball.
We'll go over that and more as we take a look at the takeaways from the Bears' preseason Week 2 loss to Cincinnati.
The Bears played their starters on offense for the opening series and the drive resulted in a field goal, which is better than no points but is not exactly the outcome you want against the Bengals' twos.
Caleb Williams completed 2-of-5 passes for 28 yards and those strikes went to Colston Loveland (10 yards) and Rome Odunze (18 yards).
The drive lasted eight plays and went for 33 yards. The Bears could have had more, but Williams missed Loveland on a pass down the seam.
Among the starters who didn't play on offense were Joe Thuney, Ozzy Trapilo, Luther Burden and D'Andre Swift. Trapilo is ramping up after being activated off the PUP list , Burden is dealing with a groin injury, and Swift's and Thuney's absences were not injury-related as far as we know.
Braxton Jones, Jordan McFadden and Roschon Johnson started in place of Trapilo, Thuney and Swift, respectively.
Chicago pulled its starters after the opening series
The Bears had some starters on defense for the first drive of the game and the Bengals still managed to work their way down the field despite not playing their starters.
The 14-play, 62-yard drive ended with a 25-yard field goal from Bengals kicker Evan McPherson. Not exactly a desired result against Cincinnati's backups.
There were a few standouts among the ones in Gervon Dexter and Dayo Odeyingbo, who recorded back-to-back pressures to help force a three-and-out for Cincinnati on the next drive.
Neither Jones nor Benedet helped their cause for the left tackle or swing tackle jobs on Saturday night.
Not only did Jones commit a holding penalty on the opening drive, he also got bullied by a Bengals edge rusher on the second series.
Braxton Jones rep in the 2nd drive. Ozzy Trapilo needs to get back soon! pic.twitter.com/QfzzAdhXMd
Benedet came in at left tackle after Jones played two series there and he didn't fare much better after posting back-to-back ugly reps.
Tough back to back snaps for Theo here. (Typo saying Ozzy 1st time around) Oversets in the pass pro then overreaches the run after. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/5HCY7TvTLn
What makes these showings even worse is the fact that Benedet and Jones worked against Cincinnati's twos.
The Bears probably don't feel any better about their tackle situation after this game. The hope is that Trapilo can get himself ready for Week 1 so Chicago doesn't have to depend on whoever wins the current left tackle competition.
It was a great night for the sixth-round pick, who showed a little bit of everything in his second preseason game.
The rookie showed up in the pass-rush with a pressure, had a run stop and he showed his elite athleticism by chasing down a ball carrier on another play. His strength was on full display, also, as van den Berg was regularly moving people at the line of scrimmage.
We no longer have to wonder if van den Berg will make the roster. Instead, we have to wonder how big of a role he's going to have.
Johnson once again worked ahead of Salvon Ahmed and handled the majority of the work in Chicago's backfield in the first half. Ahmed mixed in for five touches in the first two quarters.
Johnson wasn't particularly impressive, as he tallied 42 yards on 12 carries and added one catch for one yard, but the simple fact that he's still operating in front of Ahmed suggests he's still the favorite for the RB3 job.
Ahmed did have a strong showing, though, as he ripped off 36 yards on six carries and added three catches for 14 yards. His performances in the preseason thus far have been superior to Johnson's, so Ahmed still has a chance to beat him out.
If nothing else, Ahmed is locked into the RB4 spot if the Bears keep four running backs.
Walker has been competing for the WR4 spot this offseason and he might have just locked up the job with one catch.
Case Keenum dialed up a deep ball for Walker down the sideline in the second quarter and the second-year wideout made a great catch that showed his impressive hands and big-play ability.
Looks like the Bears got another playmaker emerging. pic.twitter.com/9AsURPOLTC
While we were already confident in projecting Walker for the WR4 spot, that catch just cemented our projection.
On top of disappointing showings from the ones on both sides of the ball, the backups didn't do any better.
After the starters came out, the twos and threes on offense didn't score a single touchdown and were only able to muster up six points. Keenum and rookie Miller Moss were under constant pressure.
On defense, Chicago gave up 24 points after the departure of the ones and cornerback Dontae Manning was torched for a pair of touchdown passes. The Bears' backups managed to make both Josh Johnson and Sean Clifford look like starting-caliber quarterbacks, which we know they are not.
Now, we know the Bears have a lot of injuries, so this wasn't the full allotment of twos and threes, but Chicago would still be wise to explore their options for more depth in free agency.

title: Nephi Sewell Injury Update: Latest News on Bears LB's Status in Preseason Week 2
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have an injury concern with linebacker Nephi Sewell in the first half of the preseason Week 2 game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
Sewell suffered an apparent right leg injury in the second quarter of the game and had to be carted off the field.
Follow our tracker below for the latest updates on Sewell's status after his injury.
As previously noted, Sewell had to be loaded onto a cart and was taken off the field.
The Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs reported that it appeared to be a right knee/leg injury for Sewell.
"Cart is coming out to assist LB Nephi Sewell," Biggs wrote. "They looked at his right knee/leg."
We'll update this page once more information is known.
This is the second injury Sewell has suffered in the preseason, as he exited last week's game early and was placed into the concussion protocol.
Sewell went undrafted out of Utah in 2022 and was initially signed by the New Orleans Saints and ended up spending the first four seasons of his career there.
In 30 games in New Orleans, Sewell tallied 26 tackles, four tackles for loss, one sack and one QB hit while playing mostly on special teams.
After Sewell was cut loose by the Saints in January of this year, the Bears scooped him up on the practice squad and later signed him to a futures contract to add him to the offseason roster.
Sewell has been battling for a backup spot on the Bears' 53-man roster but was more likely to land on the practice squad.
Sewell is the brother of Detroit Lions offensive tackle Penei Sewell and Bears linebacker Noah Sewell, who is currently on the PUP list while he works his way back from a torn Achilles suffered last season.

title: Why Caleb Williams is Playing For Bears in Preseason Week 2 vs. Bengals
full_text:
We have a bit of a surprise on our hands for the preseason Week 2 game between the Chicago Bears and Cincinnati Bengals, as quarterback Caleb Williams is going to play.
Head coach Ben Johnson had previously said he did not need to see Williams play in the preseason, but clearly he changed his mind and the former No. 1 overall pick will suit up.
"But do I need to see Caleb Williams in the preseason? No, I don't," Johnson said before preseason Week 1 .
Johnson did not indicate how many snaps and series Williams will get exactly versus Cincy, but we wouldn't be shocked if it's just one.
Here's why Johnson has chosen to play Williams on Saturday night.
When asked about why Caleb Williams is playing on Saturday night, Johnson had this to say on ESPN Chicago:
"It will be good for him to go thru the night game routine. He's prepared to play as long as he needs to for our offense," said Johnson.
When it comes to how many snaps Williams might see, Johnson was non-committal, per ESPN's Courtney Cronin .
"He's prepared to play as long as he needs to for our offense," Johnson said.
Cronin notes that Williams played 14 snaps in his preseason debut in 2025, and that also came after a joint practice, so he could be around that many against the Bengals.
Depending on how the offense does, that could be one series or a few.
This is a bit surprising considering the Bears just had a joint practice with the Bengals a few days ago and we assumed Chicago would be content with those reps.
But, as Johnson said, he wants to help Williams get into a routine, so here we are.
According to Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune , all but Joe Thuney and Ozzy Trapilo are playing along the offensive line.
Williams will have a good amount of weapons on hand, also with Rome Odunze, Cole Kmet, Colston Loveland and Kalif Raymond prepared to play.
Luther Burden is not playing because of his injury , and neither is D'Andre Swift, but his absence is not injury-related.
On defense, Hammond notes that T.J. Edwards, Grady Jarrett and Austin Booker are all in street clothes, so they won't be playing, either.

title: Kyle Monangai, Luther Burden and More Bears Injury News for Preseason Week 2
full_text:
With the Chicago Bears taking part in preseason Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals on Saturday, it's time for our latest injury round-up.
This week's round-up includes many of the same players as in past injury round-ups. Headlining this group is receiver Luther Burden, running back Kyle Monangai, and cornerback Kyler Gordon and Jaylon Jones.
On top of those players, we'll also see what the latest is on the guys who are on the PUP list.
Burden is dealing with a strained groin and ESPN's Adam Schefter reports he will not play for the entire preseason as a result.
Thankfully, Burden is slated to be ready for Week 1.
"Chicago WR Luther Burden III is expected to miss the preseason due to the strained groin injury he suffered Saturday, but the Bears believe he should be back for the team’s regular-season opener vs. the Panthers, per sources," Schefter said.
In the week leading up to preseason Week 2, fellow wideout Rome Odunze noted that Burden's recovery is "going well," so things appear to be moving in the right direction for him.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai would miss "multiple weeks" with his hyperextended knee.
We were, of course, cautious to fully bank on that report after Schefter whiffed on the Coby Bryant injury, but the Bears have since said something similar, with head coach Ben Johnson labeling Monangai as week-to-week.
While Monangai's injury doesn't appear to be a long-term issue, we still don't know what his status is for Week 1.
Gordon has been on the PUP list since the start of training camp and he has not taken part in any practice this offseason because of his unspecified calf injury.
When asked about Gordon during the week, Johnson kept it short and sweet, but he did not provide an actual update.
"There's nothing new to add right now," Johnson said when asked for an update.
"Yeah, I see him in the building," Johnson said when asked if he sees Gordon.
"Yep, there's a plan and he's working toward that plan," he added when asked if there's been any progress.
At this point, even speculating on how much longer Gordon could be out is futile. We'll just have to wait and see.
What we do know is that frustrations in the building are mounting . General manager Ryan Poles has admitted he is frustrated , and Johnson's short answers in recent weeks show he is, also.
Jones has been out since he exited the Aug. 6 practice early and has not taken part in a session since. He's dealing with an ankle injury.
Before kickoff on Saturday, the Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs reported that Jones was going work on the field with trainers, which is a good sign he's progressing in his rehab.
LB Keyshaun Elliott (back): Elliott has been on the PUP list since training camp started and missed time during OTAs and minicamp. NFL Network's Stacey Dales reported on Aug. 15 that the rookie could return to practice this week , but that didn't happen.
DL Shemar Turner (knee): Turner is working his way back from a torn ACL. The last we heard of him, Turner was doing rehab work on the side field at practice on Aug. 6. That is the most we have heard about him pretty much all offseason long.
DB Elijah Hicks (shin) : Hicks reported shin discomfort at the start of training camp. We haven't gotten any information lately, but as ESPN's Courtney Cronin reported on July 28, "the Bears do not see his injury as anything major."

title: 4 Things for Bears Fans to Watch in Preseason Week 2 Game vs Bengals
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are set to face the Cincinnati Bengals in their preseason Week 2 game tonight, but the Bengals have already announced that their starters won't play, which means the Bears are likely to follow suit. While disappointing for the fans, it's probably the right decision. Both teams got plenty of good work in this week during the Bears and Bengals joint practice session on Thursday.
Even with the starters on the sidelines, the Bears still have plenty of depth players and storylines that will be worth watching. Here are four in particular for Bears fans to pay attention to once the game kicks off.
One of the biggest breakout stars in Chicago's training camp this year has been wide receiver Kaden Davis. After bouncing around multiple teams in both the NFL and UFL since going undrafted in 2022, Davis landed in Chicago this year and has quietly had a terrific camp. He even earned praise from quarterback Caleb Williams for the work he's put in.
Davis already stood out in the Bears' preseason Week 1 win last Saturday with four catches for 88 yards. If he can put up a similar performance tonight, it's going to be very hard to cut him from the 53-man roster.
Last week, we learned that Ben Johnson is already planting his own coaching tree this preseason . Johnson turned over playcalling to wide receivers coach Antwaan Randle El, giving him some vital in-game experience that could help him in future job interviews. "I think he's got a chance to be an offensive coordinator in this league," Johnson said. "I think he's got a chance to be a head coach in this league."
Johnson went on to say that he may hand over playcalling duties again in the Bears' final two preseason games. And now that Bears fans know this, they can challenge themselves to pay attention to the playcalling trends in the second half and try to identify whether Johnson has indeed handed the call sheet to an assistant coach.
It's no secret that the Bears' defensive line remains a major question mark going into 2026. The lack of proven playmakers here is why Ryan Poles needs his big gamble on the secondary to pay off . But one encouraging development so far has been the emergence of Jamree Kromah. In last week's preseason game, Kromah dominated Cleveland's offensive line to the tune of six total tackles, two sacks, three tackles for loss, and two quarterback hits.
To be clear, no one's projecting Kromah to suddenly become a superstar pass rusher. However, if he's developed into a merely competent rotational piece, he could have an outsized impact on Chicago's defensive performance this year.
Undrafted rookie Miller Moss had a brief and shaky preseason debut last week, but he should get an extended look tonight against the Bengals with Williams likely sitting out and Tyson Bagent dealing with an injury, which was first reported by Mark Carman of CHGO Bears . While the QB2 and QB3 jobs remain firmly in the hands of Bagent and Case Keenum, respectively, Moss remains an intriguing player in his own right.
If Moss can showcase some growth against Cincinnati, he could make a case for himself to be retained on the practice squad where he can continue to develop while learning from Williams and Ben Johnson.
