title: Bears Rookies Who've Come the Furthest Since Training Camp Began
full_text:
When rookies come into their first rookie camp and the process of development begins, about anything can happen .
Injuries play a huge role in this. Last year Colston Loveland and Luther Burden III had to cope with the aftermath of injuries all offseason and failed to make impacts until the regular season hit the month marker. Then they more or less exploded.
Some rookies ascend differently. They gradually make the climb into position. They do it at different rates.
Here's a ranking of who has come the furthest among Bears rookies heading into Week 2 in preseason. It's also a gauge of who has the most ground to cover as preseason ends with the finale against Tennessee.
The missing player is fifth-rounder Keyshaun Elliott, who has been shelved throughout camp with a back injury. There must be something about fifth-rounders. The Bears never got a look at their fifth-round pick last year, cornerback Zah Frazier. And they never did.
Every Jordan van den Berg snap against Cleveland. 🎥: @itsfickybaby with the edit. I usually think Pro Day numbers are overblown. Just give me a football player. But when 310 pounds you run a 4.9 with a 36” vert, 9’11” broad 4.19 shuttle (craziest one btw 👀) and 35 bench reps…
Coaches have lauded his play throughout training camp, or at least since the players could wear pads. He did nothing to disappoint in the preseason opener, although his impact was probably less than in some of the more physical practices held. This isn't to suggest van den Berg is a special player. He simply had the longest climb to make of all Bears draft picks this year, and as a result any progress seems greater than it would for others drafted earlier.  He had only one tackle in the opening preseason game but the goal for his position is pushing the line of scrimmage back. The Bears had seven tackles for loss in the first game and he figured prominently in helping make those possible. The best way to put it is van den Berg has been physical, violent and made the most of every rep he has had. No one can say he is dominating at anything but in the first preseason game and in practices he makes a bigger impact than your average sixth-round pick.
Yessir Dillon Thieneman picks off Joe Burrow 👀 https://t.co/pIDOJBvkgp pic.twitter.com/h0NYbL3JJm
His interception off a deflection in practice at Cincinnati was exactly the kind of awareness and reaction they needed from a player who will eventually have most of the deeper safety responsibilities in this scheme. He continues to both struggle and impress, as any talented rookie would when thrust into action with starters on a daily basis in practice and in preseason. What he has done more than anything else is give consistent effort. "He's a guy that has came in and just worked," linebacker T.J. Edwards told reporters in Cincinnati. "He's got all the tools and all the things that they were saying about him in college, coming in with his speed and the physicality."
Malik Muhammad Every Snap From His NFL Debut pic.twitter.com/g9jxrZzH9D
Muhammad hadn't shown a lot early on in camp but within the last few weeks his versatility has been a real asset because of injuries He has had to play slot cornerback with starters and outside with backups. Although he doesn't figure to be an actual slot, his athleticism has been more and more apparent. "Well, you just try not to overload him between myself and (nickel cornerbacks coach) Cannon Matthews," said DBs coach Al Harris. "You just try not to give him too much, you know what I mean? "We have a complex scheme, so you got to give them the details, but also you got to remember that you know you want them to be functional in both spots."
For the sickos: I watched every pass-blocking snap from Bears rookie center Logan Jones. 24 snaps. Lotta good stuff. Only a couple rough reps. pic.twitter.com/pc7hxw1ks0
What can best be said about the second-rounder's play is he has always been there, taking every play with backups and learning the position at an NFL level. The Bears didn't run it especially well when he played last week and their pass blocking throughout the game was at issue. It hasn't been eyeopening but he hasn't had a steady stream of gaffes, either. Obviously, at this point he's not really taking away the starting center position from Garrett Bradbury as many preseason predictions had said. He needs to be ready because that's what his first season is about while Bradbury is playing.

Thomas' injury caused him to slip down this chart. He's back now and apparently healthy enough to begin to exhibit the speed he flashed before being hurt. The final preseason game might be a better chance for them to get a better look at his speed in game action as he has worked gradually back into the mix this week in practices but hadn't done a full all-out session since his return before they went to Cincinnati.
Roush makes his catches when he has the opportunity. He did have this ability at Stanford but all the Bears ever wanted to talk about from draft day on was his blocking. His blocking has looked solid except in one special teams drill when they asked him to hold a small blocking pad and he was smashed by Jeremiah Martin. Little did they know he would be logging more reps than just about anyone in the secondary. Thomas has had to become a fixture with the backups and even had a share of first-team reps. He has a lot more misses than hits but he's learning. What he needs to show in the end of preseason is special teams ability because this secondary injury situation won't last forever and then the need for all those rookie practice reps is diminished.

The Bears could easily decide to bring someone with more experience in for the regular season after roster cuts. This isn't a position where learning the system is a factor. He has generally been solid but a few snaps off the mark helped lead to Cairo Santos misses in practices. His snap on Santos' miss from 50 in the first preseason game wasn't spot-on.
Looked like Tory Taylor didn't handle the Beau Gardner snap very well on that missed 50 yard field goal by Cairo Santos.
The Vanilla Gorilla has been at the center of plenty of shoving in practice. He's willing to mix it up with veterans and rookies alike. title: Which Bears Bubble Players Could Play Their Way Onto the Roster vs. the Bengals
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will take the fireld for their seconde preseason contest on Saturday night when they travel to Paycor Stadium to take on the Cincinnati Bengals.
These two teams squared off for a joint practice on Thursday and by all accounts it was a productive session for both teams ahead of their exhibition showdown in preseason Week 2.
With the vast majority of the Bears' starters expected to sit, this is yet another golden opportunity for players vying for roster spots to show they belong on the 53-man roster or, at the very least, Chicago's practice squad.
With that in mind, here's a look at five players on the bubble who could cement their spot on the initial 53-man roster with a strong showing in preseason Week 2.
The common trend between all five players is the fact that they were standouts in preseason Week 1 , which is important to note because stacking good games in exhibition play is crucial.
Davis has routinely been a standout throughout training camp and he carried that momentum into preseason Week 1, when he led all Bears pass-catchers with four receptions for 88 yards, including a 41-yard reception that was the second-biggest gain of the game.
With likely only one spot up for grabs at wide receiver, if Davis can outperform both Maurice Alexander and Scotty Miller once again this week, he could cement his place on the 53-man roster early.
Lynch was one of the Bears' biggest standouts on defense in the preseason opener. He posted three pressures, including one QB hit, and finished with three tackles and one pass defensed and posted a solid Pro Football Focus run defense grade of 70.1.
Another thing helping Lynch's cause is the fact that he played in each spot upfront and we know how important versatility is for a backup. If he can have a repeat performance, Lynch might just garner enough attention to make the cut.
Kromah stole the show in the first preseason game after notching six pressures, two sacks, three tackles for loss and a pair of QB hits versus Cleveland. He also received a shoutout from head coach Ben Johnson.
"In a game like this, you see the get-off, the relentlessness, and you feel his presence every snap. The D-linemen were hooting and hollering for him because they see him making plays. He's such a hard worker who's been in the program for a minute, so seeing him have success on the field is huge," Johnson said of Kromah.
Kromah is strictly an edge rusher, which will make it a bit harder for him to secure a roster spot. But if he can continue to show he's got the ability to add some pass-rush juice for a defense that no doubt needs more of it, Kromah might find his way onto the 53.
Like Davis, Ahmed has been standing out on a daily basis at the team's training camp, and also like Davis he managed to shine during the preseason Week 1 contest.
Ahmed ripped off the game's biggest play with a 49-yard scoring strike on a screen pass from Case Keenum, and he added two carries for 17 yards for good measure.
He did, however, operate behind Roschon Johnson, who appears to be the favorite for the RB3 job going into preseason Week 2.
That said, Ahmed could still grab the RB4 spot if the Bears decide to keep an extra, the chances of which have been increased in the wake of Kyle Monangai's knee injury , which leaves his Week 1 status up in the air.
We also wouldn't rule out Ahmed straight up beating out Johnson for a roster spot, although Johnson's special teams prowess gives him a leg up over Ahmed, who only has 110 career special teams snaps as compared to Johnson's 386.
After a highly disappointing rookie season, Hyppolite was anything but guaranteed to secure a roster spot in 2026. But he helped his cause in a big way last week.
Hyppolite was the team leader in tackles with seven and he made a tackle for loss and notched a pass defensed. It was a strong showing for the 2025 fourth-round pick, who hasn't had many standout moments this offseason .
We know the Bears have three linebackers locked in with Devin Bush, T.J. Edwards and D'Marco Jackson. We would also pencil rookie Keyshaun Elliott in, but he has been injured throughout training camp and his Week 1 status is uncertain.
If Elliott can't get back healthy before Week 1, the Bears could have as many as two spots up for grabs on the 53 at linebacker, which only increases Hyppolite's chances of sticking. He can further assist in his cause with another strong showing on Saturday.

title: Are Caleb Williams, Bears Starters Playing in Preseason Week 2 vs. Bengals?
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will play their second exhibition game on Saturday evening when they meet the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium in Ohio in preseason Week 2.
Last week, the Bears did not play any starters on offense but we did see some of the ones on defense take the field, like Gervon Dexter, Dayo Odeyingbo, Devin Bush, Cam Lewis and Dillon Thieneman.
Will the Bears take the same approach against the Bengals in preseason Week 2? Or could Chicago opt to play even more or less starters than they did against the Cleveland Browns?
UPDATE: Ben Johnson has confirmed that Caleb Williams will be playing tonight, and based on our past updates below, he will be surrounded by a good amount of starters.
Ben Johnson just officially announced that Caleb is playing... "It will be good for him to go thru the night game routine. He's prepared to play as long as he needs to for our offense."
UPDATE: Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune reports notes that Luther Burden, Ozzy Trapilo, T.J. Edwards, Grady Jarrett, Tyrique Stevenson, Austin Booker and D'Andre Swift are not playing, as all are in street clothes on the sideline.
Meanwhile, Hammond adds that Caleb Williams, Rome Odunze, Colston Loveland and Kalif Raymond are in uniform , as is the Bears' starting offensive line outside of Thuney.
We might see a good amount of Bears starters on offense after all, but that hasn't been completely confirmed yet.
UPDATE: Williams is suited up and on the field with about 40 minutes to go before kickoff, so it appears there is a chance Chicago's starting QB will indeed play tonight.
Caleb Williams suited up @fox32news pic.twitter.com/eajJ0TNTB7
We should have a definitive answer soon enough.
We do not have a definitive answer to this question, but chances are the Bears will take a similar approach and sit Caleb Williams and the vast majority, if not all, of the starters this week.
Last week, head coach Ben Johnson cited the workload the team gets at joint practice with the Bengals as a factor in his decision, and by all accounts the Bears got in plenty of work in during the session.
"But we have a plan in place of the reps, the workload we want to get as a team between the joint practice with Cincinnati and the game reps as well," Johnson said.
Johnson also made it clear that he does not need to see Williams at all this preseason.
"But do I need to see Caleb Williams in the preseason? No, I don't," Johnson said.
On the offensive side of the ball, Braxton Jones is a projected starter to watch for possible reps on Saturday.
Earlier in the week, Johnson said that the left tackle competition was still open , so he might want to get a look at Jones, who was working his way back from an injury and didn't play in the preseason opener.
"As far as I'm concerned, the competition remains wide open and we'll continue to play that one out," Johnson said of left tackle.
Jones has long been considered the favorite in the competition, as he has received the majority of reps at left tackle with the ones during the offseason. However, his starting spot is now in danger thanks to the rapid recovery from Ozzy Trapilo , who is likely to return to his starting job when ready to play.
Other than Jones, we don't anticipate any other ones on offense taking the field. We could, however, see some starters on the defensive side of the ball.
The Bears might want to get Thieneman a bit more snaps under his belt ahead of his first season, but veterans like Lewis, Dexter, Odeyingbo and Bush, all of whom played last week, are now less likely to suit up because of the Thursday joint practice reps.
We should have a better idea of which starters are and aren't playing near kickoff, which is 6 p.m. CT.

title: Old Meets Young as 40-Year-Old QB Josh Johnson Connects with Youngsters Dohnte Meyers, Colbie Young in Bengals Win
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals scored a generational win Saturday night in their second preseason game, defeating the Chicago Bears 27-9 at Paycor Stadium.
Forty-year-old journeyman quarterback Josh Johnson started with Joe Burrow, Joe Flacco and the rest of the starters and key backups in street clothes, and the 2008 draft pick threw two touchdown passes, the first of which went to one of the younger players on the team, rookie wide receiver Colbie Young.
Johnson also found an “old man to young man” connection with first-year receiver Dohnte Meyers, targeting him six times for five receptions and 41 yards, with four of those catches coming on the opening drive when the Bengals backups drove through the Chicago starters for a 25-yard field goal by Evan McPherson.
“I think it’s always good to out there and show you can still make plays,” Johnson said. “In this business, people want to put labels on you and tags on you. Everybody thinks they have the right answers.
“The one person I know who has the answers is the man above,” Johnson added. “For me, when I wake up with an opportunity, that means it’s purposeful.”
Johnson went 15 of 23 for 156 yards with touchdown passes of 17 yards to rookie wide receiver Colbie Young and 6 yards to veteran tight end Tanner Hudson, the latter of which came with 23 seconds left in the first half, earning him the rest of the night off.
“Josh, I thought played excellent and finished with a nice touchdown drive at halftime,” Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. “I probably would have played him into the third quarter, but I just thought he played real clean and so I got Sean (Clifford) in there in the second half.”
Clifford opened the second-half by taking the Bengals on a six-play, 75-yard drive that ended with his 20-yard touchdown pass to undrafted rookie receiver Noah Thomas.
Taylor praised Clifford in his postgame news conference, saying the local product hasn’t had more than 10 reps throughout training camp and still went and played well.
Johnson’s reps haven’t been that limited, but they’ve been scarce. Yet he still was able to lead a scoring drive against Chicago’s starters in addition to the back-to-back touchdown marches.
“I’m grateful because my whole career has kind of gone like this,” Johnson said. “If you are a man of faith or have any relationship with God, you know the things he puts us through is for a reason. Now I’m 40 and I can look back at things I was going through at 22 that are helping me now in how I prepare and understand that reps might not be there for me.
“But what are the other ways I can still have opportunities to bring a calm to yourself and go out there and play confidently? (God) just kept nudging me to say, ‘You know, tis might be what it is for you. But where there’s a will, there’s a way. My whole career has been kind of been like, ‘You’ve got to get out of the mud.’ Now I’m just kind of used to it.”
Johnson said there a couple of plays he would have like to have back, one of which was a miss to a wide-open Meyers that had a chance to be an explosive play, which would have made the CFL imports night even more impressive.
Johnson said all of the quarterbacks have been talking about Meyers since OTAs.
“Dohnte pops off the film,” he said. “I think now you're just seeing him put his mind with his ability, and that's a great sign for a young player to be able to do that as quickly as he's doing it.
“All of the quarterbacks have confidence in him,” Johnson added. “You don’t need to say a lot when you’ve got Joe speaking out about him, Flacco always throwing the ball to him, and when I get out there, we throw the ball to him. There’s a reason. He’s been showing me there are no limitations to his game.”
Johnson could get another long look in the preseason finale Friday at Philadelphia with the starters and backups not expected to play again.

title: 'God Blessed Them' - Colbie Young, Dohnte Meyers Earn Major Praise From Josh Johnson After Beating Bears
full_text:
Josh Johnson had an impressive showing in Saturday's 27-9 Bengals win over the Bears.
The preseason outing went very well for the third-stringer as he fed a pair of young receivers, Dohnte Meyers and Colbie Young, for the majority of the first half.
Johnson finished with 156 yards and two touchdowns, one to Young and one to Tanner Hudson. He is impressed with Meyers and Young, who combined for eight catches, 89 yards, and the touchdown across 14 targets.
Johnson went in depth on the game with Dan Hoard on ESPN 1530.
"They just keep making plays, and now they're starting to be consistent in their habits," Johnson said. "Lining up right, being in the right spots, being on time, And your trust just continues to grow because you know they're gonna do what they're supposed to do, and the rest is up to them, man. God blessed them with a lot of heart. He blessed those guys with a lot of ability, and they're going out there, and they're showing it."
Young was excited about his scoring moment and the outing overall.
"Just keep stacking days; never, get too ahead of yourself. Stay level-headed and keep growing," Young said about the outing before touching on his touchdown with ESPN 1530's Tony Pike. "Yeah. When you win at the line, it makes it easier at the top of the catch to finish. I mean it was a great play by Josh right there, just putting it right in the bread basket. It made it easy for me."
Johnson is feeling early strong vibes from this team as they take it day by day entering the final week of preseason.
He will probably play a lot again on Friday against Philadelphia after Joe Burrow got major work in against the Bears on Thursday. Joe Flacco has his second-string role locked up after what he did in relief of Burrow last season.
"Yeah, we headed in the right direction," Johnson concluded. "I understand it's a long season, and I understand the process is about what you do every day. And what we're doing right now is we're focused on the moment, and we're checking the boxes in the moment. And with every team I've been around that does that, over time it works out in your favor. I think we just have to stay in the moment and keep taking it one day at a time."
Cincinnati will try to complete an undefeated preseason next Friday in the city of brotherly love.

title: Zac Taylor Details Cashius Howell Absence, Swing Tackle Battle Following Bears Preseason Clash
full_text:
The Bengals don't have another injury to monitor on defense as training camp rips into the back-half sessions. Rookie defensive end Cashius Howell limped a bit at the end of joint practice on Thursday and did not dress for the second preseason game on Saturday, but it was just because he's gotten so many reps in recent weeks.
Zac Taylor spoke to the media after the game and updated his status along with other comments about the 27-9 outing for Cincinnati .
"Yeah, just decided to hold him out. He's got a ton of reps over the last couple of weeks, and we just held him out," Taylor said about Howell
Cincinnati rolled out an all-backup lineup during the latest contest against Chicago. Names like Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers continued to flash, while the back end of the edge-rushing hierarchy got long looks for Cincinnati in Howell's absence.
Taylor noted the backup swing tackle battle is still open entering the final week of the preseason.
Andrew Coker, Jalen Rivers and Cody Ford are fighting for that role.
"If a backup tackle's got to go in the game, and we want to keep playing the way that we play, you just got to be all trusted in the game. And so I think there's plenty of competition there, and we still got two weeks to go with it," Taylor said about what he wants to see from someone who captures the job.
All eyes are on the defensive injuries that include, Shemar Stewart, Bryan Cook, and Dax Hill. We will get more updates on them next week, but the backups shined in the blowout win at home.
"I thought our guys did a great job leveraging the ball, getting the ball to the ground. Did a good job taking away some some downfield throws, making them check it down underneath. So I just thought overall that they they played very clean," Taylor said.
Cincinnati is off on Sunday as they prepare for another week of training camp in the dog days of August. They close the preseason at Philadelphia next Friday.

title: Duke Tobin Sends STRONG Message About Barrett Carter and Demetrus Knight Jr.
full_text:
The Bengals didn't add a starting linebacker this offseason, opting to stick with Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr.
Did they make the right decision? Are they looking to add a linebacker before the start of the regular season?
Bengals Director of Player Personnel Duke Tobin joined the preseason television broadcast on Saturday night and shared a ringing endorsement for both Carter and Knight. He also made it clear that both players still have plenty to prove.
Both Carter and Knight are resting on Saturday with their starting jobs set. Tobin made it clear the Bengals have seen everything they hoped to see from both players during training camp.
"They've commanded the defense is what we really wanted to see, and and they have taken those next steps," Tobin told Anthony Munoz and Mike Watts . "They've got to do it in the regular season. That that's what they've got to do. We believe in them. We think we got some guys behind them that have really taken a good step, throughout the course of this camp as well."
It's a ringing endorsement. Will it translate to the regular season? That's the question that both guys need to answer.
Tobin isn't alone. Ja'Marr Chase also praised the young linebackers this week.
When asked about the young backers, Chase praised both guys.
"They've just been playing a little faster. As you can tell, they know what they're doing more," Chase said on Thursday. "And then last year, obviously, they were rookies coming in trying to learn and pick it up, and then they're captains of the defense, giving out the plays. So now they're more vocally leading. They're more confident calling the play. They're more confident running around, making plays. Their adjustments, and you can see it. They're having fun out there, screaming, and that's what you want from linebackers."
The Bengals' defense has improved in a major way this offseason. From Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen to Bryan Cook and Kyle Dugger—they've added proven pieces that should make life easier on Knight, Carter and the rest of the defense.
Watch Tobin's full comments here .
Carter may end up becoming a captan. He's the leader in that linebacker room and on defense. title: Bengals Ranked Outside NFL Top Teams in 3-Year Future Power Rankings
full_text:
ESPN's NFL team unveiled its annual three-year look-ahead power rankings for the entire league this week. Cincinnati isn't high on the list amidst a pretty all-in 2026 season for the franchise.
The Bengals checked in at No. 17 on the list after restructuring Joe Burrow's contract this season and putting in plenty of chips to the center of the table for a solid shot at winning a Super Bowl.
Cincinnati has one of the league's longest lists of 2027 free agents entering this season.
"Based on snap counts from last season, the Bengals have the NFL's largest free agent class in 2027. Free-agents-to-be include cornerbacks DJ Turner and Dax Hill; safety Jordan Battle; running backs Chase Brown and Samaje Perine; and offensive linemen Ted Karras and Dalton Risner," Aaron Schatz noted .
Cincinnati has had the same QB, HC, and (all but name) GM for this entire decade.
That continuity could be a boon or blow over the next few years.
"The current Bengals braintrust of coach Zac Taylor and general manager Duke Tobin has had a long time to produce consistent team success," Ben Solak wrote. "And the Bengals' middling ranking here reflects those inconsistent results. But the defense and offensive line are healthier now than they've been in years, and quarterback Joe Burrow seems to be a reinvigorated leader of the organization accordingly."
The Bengals obviously have to improve on defense over this span, or it will be difficult to rise from the middling morass.
It would be shocking if this unit stays in the bottom three over the next few years (barring injury), given the investment and stronger knowledge of Al Golden's system.
"Everything is riding on the improvement of a defense that was at or near the bottom of the league in every meaningful category," Louis Riddick wrote. "The front office did just about everything it could in a single offseason to improve the defense up front, starting with trading away a top-10 pick for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II. He must give the Bengals a quality return on investment, both in terms of his direct and indirect impact on the defense. If not, there could be major changes in Cincinnati on and off the field."
If Cincinnati wins the Super Bowl this coming year, who cares what happens the rest of the decade? Rings and banners are forever and garner plenty of breathing room for any short-term falloffs in one of the highest-parity leagues on earth.
A BIG if: going Burrow's entire career without lifting a Lombardi Trophy would be as big a disappointment on the other end.

title: Ja'Marr Chase Highlights 3 Bengals Improving The Most During 2026 Training Camp
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase offered extended comments to the media on Thursday following Cincinnati's joint practice with the Bears, including big praise for a trio of defenders.
He feels cornerback DJ Turner II, Demetrius Knight Jr., and Barrett Carter have taken big steps forward since last season.
"Most improved. I'll probably say DJ, just overall, that I've seen," Chase noted. "I'll probably say DJ and, hmm, a linebacker, our two rookie linebackers (now second-year players). They've been playing really, really fast and physical lately, and I've been noticing it. So those two guys, yeah."
He expanded more on the linebacker improvement as Cincinnati tries to go from 2025's NFL-worst linebacker play to average or better this fall.
"They've just been playing a little faster. As you can tell, they know what they're doing more," Chase explained. "And then last year, obviously, they were rookies coming in trying to learn and pick it up, and then they're captains of the defense, giving out the plays. So now they're more vocally leading. They're more confident calling the play. They're more confident running around, making plays. Their adjustments, and you can see it, man. They're having fun out there, screaming, and that's what you want from linebackers."
It's another notch in the improvement pole for those two massively important parts of the defense.
The strategy was clear this offseason: Beef up the defensive front ahead of Carter and Knight with Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen to make their lives easier (and faster on the field).
That was on full display as Cincinnati closed out the Bears practice with multiple Caleb Williams turnovers. Chicago was a playoff team last year and is a borderline team to go dancing again (46% chance of making the playoffs on ESPN's FPI). Pulling that off against a near-contender brings heart eyes to their offensive teammates.
On the outside, Turner is shaping up to be the team's clear CB1, with a contract extension possible ahead of this season.
"It was just for him to find, but I mean, obviously, we all knew what he was like," Chase said about Turner. "That's why we drafted him, and it was just a moment in time for him to find his true colors and play within himself."
The starters get a couple of off days this weekend before diving back into training camp next week.

title: Joe Burrow Doubles Down on Bengals' Need for More Urgency: 'I'm Playing for My Job'
full_text:
Joe Burrow has spent the offseason making it clear that the Cincinnati Bengals can't afford to waste another year.
The urgency has shown in how Burrow has approached his leadership. The star quarterback has become more vocal and demanding behind the scenes . He recently said he's "tired of saying next year" after Cincinnati missed the playoffs in three consecutive seasons .
Burrow took that message a step further during a recent feature with ESPN's Marry Smith, revealing to Smith that he feels the same pressure as everyone else in the organization.
"Yeah, I'm right there with them," Burrow told Smith. "I think, you know, I've tried to instill an urgency in the room, a palpable pressure — because we have guys playing and coaching for their jobs this year, and that's how I'm looking at it. I'm playing for my job this year."
It's a notable comment from the franchise's face, but it aligns well with Burrow's consistent approach during the offseason.
The Bengals went 6-11 last season and responded by aggressively reshaping their defense, adding Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe, and Bryan Cook. They then selected Cashius Howell in the second round of the NFL Draft and later added cornerback Tacario Davis. Burrow has repeatedly expressed confidence in the roster , even saying the team has "everything we need."
That leaves little room for excuses.
"I think guys want to go out and be great," Burrow continued . "If you don't have urgency on the day-to-day to get better and go and attack every single drill and rep with the intent to get better, you're not going to get there. So we have the team to do it this year, and so we have to take advantage of the opportunity."
Burrow has previously called this the deepest Bengals roster of his career and compared its potential to his 2019 LSU team, which went undefeated and won the National Championship. Now, the difficult part: turning that talent into wins.
After three straight seasons without a playoff appearance, Burrow is approaching the 2026 season like it's do-or-die. It's no longer just another year in Cincinnati — Burrow is treating it as if that window needs to be taken advantage of right now.
If that doesn't happen, his Bengals teammates and coaches could be looking for new teams, and Burrow could find himself in the middle of the rumor mill.

title: Cleveland Browns QB Grades Following Pitiful Preseason Loss to the Buffalo Bills
full_text:
Mother Nature did its best to prevent the Cleveland Browns from playing on Saturday. Yet the skies eventually cleared after a lightning delay and the game was on against the Buffalo Bills in front of a sparse but vocal crowd.
The offense, led by Shedeur Sanders in the first half, even had an opening-drive touchdown to open things up. Unfortunately, everything went downhill fast after that initial drive.
So how did the quarterbacks play throughout all four quarters?
Sanders actually held his own in the first half. He finished 9/11 for 76 yards and had a touchdown pass. The concern was his interception that bounced off the hands of Jermaine Terry and into the arms of Damar Hamlin.
Damar Hamlin snags it out of the air for the INT on Shedeur Sanders 👀 (Via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/OpHpZ2ueWt
The footage will be analyzed ad nauseam by Sanders fans, as the ball was possibly tipped by a defender at the line of scrimmage. The pass was ultimately behind Terry, who should still arguably have made the catch. A better throw would have erased all doubts.
He finished the half with a whimper, but still put up solid numbers given he was playing with backups. He did not seize the job, but he did not hand it to Watson either.
Watson came in during the third quarter and was playing alongside individuals who will likely soon be cut by the team. The rationale behind that decision by Todd Monken remains a confusing one.
One would think a quarterback of Watson's perceived caliber would find a way to avoid mistakes and run a stable offense. That was far from the case as he went a dreadful 5/12 for 36 yards and an interception that he sailed over the head of his intended receiver.
Te'Cory Couch with the INT! BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/UQXxepOOG7
The fans were booing him loudly and it was overall a very ugly scene. What doesn't make sense is how he goes fromt his performance to being named the Week 1 starter. Monken may have to give Watson the start on Thursday just to see if he can bounce back.
Dillon Gabriel entered the game late and went a total of 0/1. He obviously has no chance of being the Week 1 starter, but it's still possible he wins the backup job if the front office decides to move on from either Watson or Sanders.
That may seem unlikely, but anything is possible given what fans have seen from the quarterbacks so far this summer.

title: 5 Winners and 5 Losers From Browns vs. Bills Preseason Game
full_text:
In a rain-filled “backup bowl” the Cleveland Browns rested their starters against the Buffalo Bills and provided a glimpse of their depth battles that mattered more than score.
Although team wins and losses do not matter in the preseason, here are the winners and losers that do matter.
Head coach Todd Monken said at the beginning of the game “let it rip”  to Sanders before his assumingely last audition prior to a starting quarterback being announced for week one. Sanders looked poised in the first-half.
On a 4th and 2, the offensive line gave him plenty of time and he hung in the pocket waiting for an open receiver. He eventually got one and delivered a strike for a first down. Sanders again stood in the pocket and waited for a wide-open Luke Floriea for an easy touchdown. Sanders did throw one interception, which was thrown behind the tight end. He ended the day going 9 for 11 for 74 yards with one touchdown and one interception. “Overall today was a pretty good day,” said Sanders.
Watson got to play the third quarter and the first drive of the fourth. His first two drives went three and out. The team was moving on his third drive, but he threw into traffic and a little high. The ball hit the receivers hands, but ultimately wound up in the hands of the Bills for an interception. He also overthrew an open Malachi Corley what could have been a big gain,
His defensive back coach described Coats Jr. as a “contact seeker … and is as versatile of a defensive back as he has been around.” Browns Defensive Coordinator, Mike Rutenberg tells his players “way to hunt”, which he describes as “the ball is our oxygen… we need it to live, so we are always just hunting the ball.” Coats Jr. has taken that phrase to heart as he always seemed to be around the ball when he was on the field.
Raheim “Rocket” Sanders averaged 2.6 yards per rush in the first half on 12 carries. Ahmani Marshall averaged 2.3 yards per carry in the third quarter. Both players are competing for the third-string running back and neither separated themselves.
The massive, oft-injured, tackle got the start at right tackle. He handled the defensive end on almost every play and imposed his big frame on smaller rushers. He is attempting to break through to be a starter and he put together a good game on Saturday.
Monken has cancelled practices early out of frustration during two-minute drills. The offense got the ball with two minutes left in the half and for the first time in the game, they looked discombobulated. On top of the sloppy play was a holding penalty and the Browns punted without gaining a first down.
The other side of the ball was not any better. The Bills picked on cornerback Tre Avery for a 37-yard pass. The Bills then scored a touchdown on the next play with multiple missed tackles with 15 seconds left of the half. The Browns are a young team and they have to take a deep breath at the end of halves in order to limit those mistakes.
The former Ohio State Buckeye played his first two snaps at defensive end. On the first play he broke through the right tackle and chased Bills’ quarterback Kyle Allen towards the sideline, causing a short throw for a one-yard gain. On the very next play, Hall Jr. used an inside move on the right tackle and got free to record the half’s lone sack.
The depth on defense, or lack thereof, was on display versus the Bills. The Browns got outscored 17-0 in the second half. Offensively, the backup offensive lineman KT Levenson gave up the edge on a couple of plays and false started twice in the fourth quarter.
There were no pre-snap penalties on offense in the first three quarters for the Browns. Monken has been preaching about using the quarterback’s cadence to cause penalties on the defense. The Bills jumped offsides twice.
Sanders was named a captain for the game. He thought he was called captain because he was the starter for this week. Sanders did not realize he would represent the team at mid-field for the coin toss. “I didn’t know I was captain of the coin toss… it was a laughing moment with coach Monken,” Sanders said on the sideline.
The Browns play their final preseason game on Thursday, August 27 at 8:00 P.M.

title: Browns Ownership Sends Message To Nick Chubb Following His Retirement
full_text:
Nick Chubb is back in the news and unfortunately, it's not because he is making a triumphant return to the Cleveland Browns. Instead, he has announced his retirement from the NFL.
Chubb is calling it a career at the age of 30 and starting the next chapter of life. That chapter will involve plenty of praise from his former team.
JW Johnson, Jimmy Haslam's son-in-law and part of the Browns ownership group, appeared on the pregame show before Saturday's preseason matchup against the Buffalo Bills. He spoke directly to Chubb about the organization's plans to honor the running back.
ready to welcome Nick back with open arms 🧡 #BUFvsCLE on News 5 pic.twitter.com/uhhZ2SRIpf
"Hell of a career, we're excited to get him back here and have him retire as a Brown as he rightfully should," Johnson said. "Nick, if you're watching and listening we're excited to get you back and get you back here as a Brown."
Chubb has been retired for less than a full 24 hours and the Browns are making it clear they want him to be involved with the team moving forward. That is fantastic to see and makes perfect sense given how hard he worked during his seven seasons in Cleveland.
The running back spent the 2025 season with the Houston Texans and to plenty of Browns fans, the sight of him in a different jersey just felt weird. Now that he is retiring the Browns can claim him as one of their own once again.
The Haslams have not had much success on the field during their ownership tenure. However, they do seem to care and making a statement on Chubb right away is a nice gesture.
Chubb had four consecutive Pro Bowl seasons from 2019-2022. He ran for over 1,000 yards in each of those seasons and was playing at an All-Pro level. That unfortunately all changed in 2023 after he took a low hit from Minkah Fitzpatrick that led to a season-ending knee injury.
Chubb's success came to a crashing halt, but he is retiring both young and healthy. He can now focus on his next chapter and perhaps being an active member of the Browns alumni. It would not be shocking for him to be honored in 2026 and perhaps with a permanent item like a statue when the new stadium opens in a few years.
If anything, the Chubb conversation is a nice distraction from the quarterback competition that may never end.

title: 3 Big Things Browns Fans Should Watch for in Second Preseason Game vs. Bills
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns went up against the Buffalo Bills on Thursday in a joint practice and will see them again Saturday afternoon in Week 2 of the preseason.
The Browns' preseason opener was a bit of a dud and fans are hoping to see improvement across the board. Several key things stand out as the most important aspects to watch for Saturday in Cleveland.
It's best to start with the most obvious of all. Fans will be locked in analyzing the play of Shedeur Sanders as he gets the start. The only caveat is that he will not be playing with many starters around him.
The same will also be true for Deshaun Watson when he comes in during the second half. That makes the overall evaluation more difficult, however, general trends will still emerge.
Shedeur is at a disadvantage playing with backups and will be expected to raise the talents and production of those around him. If he can't, the job is likely Watson's. But if he can thrive and throw several touchdowns, the competition gets that much more interesting.
The Browns gave up 34 points in last week's preseason opener against the Chicago Bears. That was mostly from the second and third-team defense, but is nothing to scoff at.
The defense was already thin to start, and the fact Alex Wright was carted off during Thursday's joint practice only raises the alarm bells surrounding the unit's overall depth.
#Browns DE Alex Wright injured his ankle in practice today. Trainers looked him over for about 5 mins before he was carted off the field. 🎥: @Matt_Bove pic.twitter.com/XrTIDabOK3
The Browns defense has its stars in Denzel Ward, Grant Delpit, Jared Verse, and Carson Schwesinger.  But what about the players behind them? Another bad performance may mean Andrew Berry needs to make cuts and revamp several spots on defense before the season even begins.
The Browns are in the midst of a quarterback competition and head coach Todd Monken began last week's game with three consecutive run plays.
Shedeur Sanders was jeered in Thursday's joint practice for his reliance on check-down throws. Fans will want to see if Monken opens things up Saturday, allowing Sanders to show off his skills and not just that he can complete short passes.
Coaches usually don't like to show off much of the playbook in preseason action. But these are unique circumstances and fans will want to see if Monken gives Sanders a chance. Going with a very conservative set of play calls may indicate he is protecting his young quarterback, who may not be ready just yet.

title: Former Browns Superstar Nick Chubb Announces NFL Retirement
full_text:
Nick Chubb remains a legend among Cleveland Browns fans. That legend will only grow now that he has officially announced his retirement from the NFL.
The news dropped Friday night after Chubb took to Instagram to wrap up an amazing career.
The news began circulating Friday night after Chubb's heartfelt post on Instagram.
NFL veteran RB Nick Chubb has announced his retirement. https://t.co/P5ba01302L pic.twitter.com/FRquDAZJUW
The best part of his announcement is how he mentions he wants to end his career on a healthy note. That is great news for someone who suffered several serious injuries during his career. He is only 30 years old and has his whole life in front of him.
Chubb was with the Browns from 2018-2024 and quickly became a fan favorite due to his hard-nosed, no-nonsense style of play. His four consecutive Pro Bowl seasons from 2019-2022 helped build his reputation as well.
His best year in a Browns uniform came in 2022 when he ran for 1,525 yards and 12 touchdowns. That led to him being named an All-Pro. Unfortunately, injuries would derail his next two seasons in Cleveland and cut short an all-time run of success.
He spent the 2025 season with the Houston Texans and was clearly a shell of his former shelf, but still ran for 506 yards in a reserve role.
Chubb being retired means the Browns can officially begin honoring him as soon as this year. He is at the same level as someone like Joe Thomas and will hopefully decide to be associated with the team for years to come. Perhaps the team can reveal his statue when the new stadium opens.
His career began to hit its decline in 2023 after he was tackled by the Pittsburgh Steelers' Minkah Fitzpatrick in a brutal collision that led to a season-ending knee injury. This was in addition to the serious knee injury he suffered in college with the Georgia Bulldogs. The fact he was even so dominant in the NFL was surprising to some due to that initial injury.
The Browns deciding to let him leave in free agency was controversial to some fans, but it appears to make football sense in hindsight. He spent seven of his eight NFL seasons with the Browns, so any ill will can fade away and he can take his rightful spots among the team's legends.
The fact he is doing so with his health intact is the best news of all.

title: 3 Critical Competitions (And 2 That Aren’t) as Browns Near the End of Training Camp
full_text:
With the conclusion of 2026 training camp just a few days away, the Cleveland Browns still have some figuring out to do on several fronts .
The quarterback competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders has taken all the headlines by storm, but there are a few other position battles still ongoing this late into the year.
Here are three other position battles that remain critical for the Browns’ upcoming regular season, plus two that are not, as Cleveland focuses on wrapping up the preseason.
Alex Wright’s injury during a joint practice with the Bills couldn’t have come at a worst time for the Browns, with the team already scrambling and losing out on a couple of notable free agency signings over the past few days -- Jadeveon Clowney and Za’Darius Smith chose to go elsewhere after visiting Berea.
An already suspect depth situation behind newcomer Jared Verse gets substantially worse, with Isaiah McGuire, Julian Okwara and undrafted free agents Khordae Sydnor and Logan Fano as the next best options. McGuire would seem like the clubhouse leader to take over Wright’s snaps for however long he’s out, but Cleveland has one big problem on its hands right now.
Isaiah Bond has been one of the revelations of training camp, and Luke Floriea has been turning heads, as well. The starting trio of Jerry Jeudy, KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston is all but set in stone for Cleveland, but the battle for the next few spots is still ongoing, with Gage Larvadain and Tyal Wallace very much in the running, too.
The significance of this battle could transcend the upcoming campaign, as whomever secures the fourth spot could be in line for a promotion to a starting gig if Cleveland decides to part with the underperforming Jeudy in the not so distant future.
Expectations are high for the Browns with Harold Fannin Jr. as the team’s top tight end, but it gets real murky afterwards. The Browns were one of two teams in the NFL using multiple tight end sets for over 50 percent of their offensive plays last year, and while it was expected for that number to go down a bit this year under a new offensive coordinator, the depth chart is far from set.
Free agency addition Jack Stoll is now on IR, joining Brenden Bates. That leaves Blake Whiteheart to battle it out with draftee Carsen Ryan for the top backup spot, after fellow rookie Joe Royer left the team for personal matters. Since Whiteheart is more of a blocker, while Ryan is more of a receiver, it looks like both be called upon early and often.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was viewed by many as a first-round talent, so finding him in the second round was already a coup for the Browns. Nonetheless, he hasn’t taken over one of the two starting safety spots in Cleveland just yet -- those still belong to Grant Delpit and Ronnie Hickman.
Nonetheless, expect to see a ton of McNeil-Warren on the field in big nickel situations, as the Browns find ways to make room for the former Toledo playmaker on defense.
The battle for the center position between Luke Wypler and rookie Parker Brailsford seems settled for now, with Elgton Jenkins taking the spot instead of staying at guard as Monken had previously intended. That will move Teven Jenkins up to right guard, again, while Zion Johnson takes the left side. The tackle positions are also set, with Tytus Howard on the right and first-rounder Spencer Fano on the left side.
For a moment, there seemed to be doubt in regards to Fano being able to hold that position down, or having to revert back to Dawand Jones, but Monken said an altercation between Verse and Fano helped convince him the rookie was ready.
KT Leveston will likely be the top backup on the inside, while rookie Austin Barber takes a backup spot as right tackle. That means that the most probable lineup being projected after April’s draft will be the one starting Week 1 for the Browns.

title: 3 Free Agent Pass Rushers That Make Sense For Browns After Alex Wright's Injury
full_text:
When the offseason began, there weren't many questions surrounding the Cleveland Browns' defensive line.
For all anyone knew, future Hall of Famer Myles Garrett would still be lacing up his cleats and trotting out in front of The Dawg Pound at Huntington Bank Field.
But just months later, with the upcoming 2026 regular season right in sight, things look very different.
Unfortunately, while the front office did go out and add rising star edge rusher Jarod Verse, the depth around him has depleted quickly. Alex Wright, who was expected to be the go-to starter opposite Verse, went down recently with a lower-leg injury.
Here are three free agent edge rushers the Browns could target to replace Wright:
Reddick is entering his 10th season of NFL action, having signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in his most recent campaign.
Due to knee and ankle injuries, he ended up missing four games in the heart of the season, but when healthy, he was terrorizing opposing quarterbacks. He contributed 31 tackles, six for a loss and 2.5 sacks, with six quarterback hits along the way.
He finished the year with an 11.1% pressure rate, which showed just how valuable his presence was on the line, even if he didn't post similar numbers to years past.
Across his nine total seasons of professional ball, Reddick has totalled 455 tackles, 77 for a loss and 61.5 sacks for a loss.
While he is approaching that veteran-type role, bringing him to Cleveland on a relatively cheap deal isn't a bad idea in the short-term.
The idea of bringing in Bosa h as been floated around all offseason for the Browns.
Attending The Ohio State University, the 31-year-old returning to Ohio would be a perfect way to approach the back half of his career.
A five-time Pro Bowler and 2016 AP Defensive Player of the Year, Bosa would give the team a major veteran presence in the locker room. Pairing him with players like Verse and linebacker Carson Schwesinger would give them another boost of experience on defense.
Across 10 years of action with the Los Angeles Chargers and Buffalo Bills, Bosa has totaled 372 tackles, 96 for a loss and 77 sacks. He has also routinely found his way into situations to jump on turnovers, recovering 22 fumbles. He led the league in 2025 with five.
While Joey's brother Nick shared that he may not play this season, Cleveland should at least explore bringing him back to the state where he made his impact on the sport of football most known.
At 30 years old, Barnett still has plenty of football ahead of him, with the veteran showing no signs that his career is nearing its end just yet.
Battling to stay healthy and on the field at times, though, Barnett has posted 216 tackles, 57 for a loss and 34 sacks across the last nine seasons. He has also posted five sacks in each of the last two seasons, all while hitting the quarterback 17 total times.
He would join a Browns team that he has some familiarity with, having been coached by newly added defensive line coach Jacques Cesaire back in 2023 while playing with the Houston Texans.
Cleveland's front office could explore a one-to-two-year deal with Barnett, giving him a chance to settle into the scheme as the Browns continue to try and grow up a talented bunch of youngsters around him.

title: Shedeur Sanders Received Strong Criticism in Browns-Bills Joint Practice
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns met up with the Buffalo Bills Thursday for a joint practice before the two teams square off on Saturday. As always, the focus for Browns fans was on the quarterback battle between Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson.
The Bills were well aware of this and one beat reporter on the scene shared a strong take directed toward Sanders shared by a Buffalo defender.
ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi shared what one Bills defender had to say when playing against Sanders.
Overheard from a Bills defender: “This s*** checkdown city!”
"This s*** checkdown city!" was overhead on the field.
To translate, the Bills defender was calling out the fact Sanders was only able to throw short passes on the day. Reporter Tom Withers confirmed this sentiment as C.J. Gardner-Johnson had a critique of his own from the sidelines.
Bills S C.J. Gardner-Johnson not practicing but talking all kinds of smack. Earlier he was yelling "Check-down King" in the direction of Sanders on the sideline.
The Bills are an elite team and joint practices are known to get chippy. Browns fans may just be worried that even in a practice format, Sanders was unable to go deep or even get the time to let the play develop.
Videos from the practice do show Sanders completing several good passes, but again, the Bills defenders clearly saw something to let their jeers be heard.
Sanders ia a polarizing figure and opposing defenders were not shy last year about doing his "wrist up" celebration in his face. He is an easy target and it makes sense the Bills were trying to get in his head on Thursday.
The real test will be Saturday in actual gameplay. Sanders will be without many of his starters on offense and will be tasked with carrying the load in what will be his best and final chance to prove he should be the Week 1 starter. Throwing short checkdowns all day will not show off his talents.
Watson appears to be the favorite to start Week 1 and the fact Sanders is starting Saturday with mostly backups does not bode well for his chances. If he was going to be the starter it would make sense for him to get some game reps with the first team.
Yet there is no way of truly knowing how head coach Todd Monken feels. He wants to win and if Sanders lights up the Bills on Saturday , he may go with the young quarterback as his starter. The fact no one has pulled away to this point means the decision could truly come down to how Saturday goes.

title: How the Browns Actually Fared in Joint Practice Against Buffalo Bills
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns held their own in an impressive showing at Thursday afternoon’s joint practice against the Buffalo Bills.
After practice, Browns head coach Todd Monken perfectly summarized how the team looked.
“It didn’t look like we were out of place,” Monken said. “It looked like we belonged.”
Don’t be fooled, these are two teams heading in very different directions to start the 2026 campaign. The Bills have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations with MVP candidate Josh Allen at quarterback and one of the top defenses in the league. The Browns are a team hoping to exit their rebuild, having won just eight games across the last two seasons. This offseason, Browns general manager Andrew Berry neglected to address Cleveland’s quarterback question mark and traded away Myles Garrett, arguably the greatest defensive player of this generation.
But for one hot, sticky Thursday afternoon, the Browns looked like they belonged against the Bills – for the most part.
Expected starting quarterback Deshaun Watson threw a red zone interception and Shedeur Sanders was taunted by Buffalo’s defenders for turning the joint practice into “checkdown city.” On the other practice field, Allen was easily carving up Cleveland’s beat up defense, which lost Alex Wright to a lower leg injury that the team feared could be season threatening. During the competitive 11-on-11 session at the end of practice, Allen capitalized on a coverage bust and connected with tight end Dalton Kincaid for a long, easy touchdown.
But Cleveland’s defense fell on a fumble and returned it the other way. The offense featured both rookie receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, who caught long passes that moved the sticks. Dylan Sampson and Raheim Rocket Sanders had a tremendous showing running the football with a few huge runs, as Quinshon Judkins was held out of this practice dealing with a minor injury. Left tackle Spencer Fano looked the part and won almost every rep throughout practice, consistently improving during his rookie training camp.
It wasn’t a flashy practice. Outside of a Taylen Green goal line fade touchdown pass to Tylan Wallace, neither team had any super viral highlights. Afterwards, Monken expressed gratitude for both teams handling themselves so professionally, as it was a productive day of work for both teams.
“That’s how a joint practice is supposed to look,” Monken said.
The Browns will face the Bills on Saturday afternoon at Huntington Bank Field for their second preseason game. Sanders is getting the start at quarterback, but not many other starters, outside of some of the rookies, are expected to get any run.

title: Recent Cleveland Browns Signee Opts to Enter College Football Transfer Portal
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns continue to seek depth at the tight end position. That explained the recent signing of Dae'quan Wright, who went undrafted out of Ole Miss in 2026.
The 6-foot-4 tight end was an intriguing signing, but will not be a member of the Browns this season. The reason why has fans and analysts talking about the state of college football.
Wright is part of a group of athletes who were successfully granted a restraining order to return to college after heading to the pros. In the past, signing an NFL contract automatically prevented a player from returning to college football. Now, the courts are weighing in to decide the matter.
Reporter Matt Zenitz shared the news that Wright had officially entered the transfer portal.
Cleveland Browns tight end Dae’Quan Wright has entered the college transfer portal, @chris_hummer and I have learned. The former Ole Miss star is currently on the Browns’ roster. pic.twitter.com/0uvkWI7zk4
We saw players drafted to the NBA return to college basketball last year, and now the same appears to be coming for college football. The move comes in response to new NCAA eligibility rules giving players five years in college. The odd aspect of this is the fact Wright was in NFL camps this summer, gained experience, and will now take that to a lower level of competition.
This is a complex situation and one that will go through the courts and force the NCAA to decide if this is fair. But what does it mean for the Browns ?
It's not like Wright was a top draft pick or someone who was going to be a savior on offense in 2026. But this does create a new precedent where players can test the NFL waters, only to return to college football if they have remaining eligibility.
NFL training camps may now be used as a place for players to show off their skills, only to enter the college transfer portal and receive a nice payday from a university.
Essentially, this changes the whole undrafted free agent process. Teams may now be hesitant to give roster spots to players who still have a fifth year of college eligibility remaining.
The ramifications are much more serious for the college game than the pro game. However, it is still a new wrinkle for NFL GMs to deal with as they build their rosters during the summer.
Wright's departure continues the Browns' current search for tight end help, as the unit is incredibly thin behind Harold Fannin Jr. this season.

title: Why I’m Buying Early Dallas Cowboys Hype Around Caleb Downs
full_text:
First-round picks are supposed to make a difference, so it’s no surprise that the Dallas Cowboys are expecting a ton out of their two 2026 selections in the opening round. And while the hopes are high for No. 23 pick Malachi Lawrence , the other defender taken 12 spots higher is destined to be “special.”
That’s the opinion on Ohio State All-American Caleb Downs by those who matter. The rookie safety out of Ohio State shined during the Oxnard portion of training camp and impressed in the preseason opener.
The Cowboys are counting on Downs to be a linchpin in the defensive revival for a squad with Super Bowl ambitions . That may be a lot to put on someone without any NFL experience, especially joining a defense that was historically awful last year, but there is something about Downs that matches the hype.
“ He’s constantly making the right decision ,” first-year defensive Christian Parker said. Those words were uttered back during rookie minicamp in May. Not much has changed.
Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer and Parker have consistently praised Downs for his ability to communicate on the field – rare for a 21-year-old rookie – as well as his high football IQ, versatility, preparation, playmaking and athleticism.
The defense will look drastically different this year. In addition to Parker transitioning the unit to an aggressive 3-4 scheme, the Cowboys made a splash by signing future Hall of Fame pass rusher Von Miller , locking up defensive tackle Quinnen Williams, and potentially rolling out as many as eight new starters .
Downs is officially a safety, but that position hardly defines his importance and impact on the field. He’ll be everywhere.
“He’s a corner sometimes, he is safety sometimes, he’s a backer sometimes,” Parker said . “He’s a defensive end when he’s blitzing. You want to have a guy who has natural instincts and ability to feel the game and play football.”
The proof is in the peers, at least in what they have to say. That’s no shortage of accolades when it comes to Downs.
“Man, he’s a dog, man,” edge Rashan Gary said recently on Good Morning Football . “It’s early, but he’s a pro’s pro, from how he, take notes to the man from how he asks questions to how he wants to be on top of the details. … So just from being a natural leader, he’s a great guy, and I just can’t wait for him to keep on growing and striving because we’re gonna need him.”
Going against All-Pro receiver CeeDee Lamb every day in practice could be demoralizing for a lesser player, if he wasn’t built for it. Downs is.
“Every play he gets a chance to line up against him, he feels like he’s going to win that rep, and that’s the type of mentality we want on this defense,” fellow safety Malik Hooker said . “Especially coming from a guy that we’re expecting to play a lot, and not only play a lot, but to be a difference maker in our defense.”
Downs echoes the Super Bowl chorus of owner Jerry Jones and his teammates. Those are the goals, and Downs tracks to be one of the focal points if and when the Cowboys end their championship drought.
A lot that has to go right for the Cowboys to get there. Don’t bet on Downs not being up for it.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Cowboys' Dominant Preseason Week 2 Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are now two preseason games deep into their exhibition slate after beating the Arizona Cardinals on Saturday night in preseason Week 2, 34-13.
The Cowboys didn't play their starters once again, but we did see the team's draft picks in action, with the exception of Caleb Downs, who got the night off after playing last week.
Among those draft picks was linebacker Jaishawn Barham, who was one of the biggest standouts of the contest in what was his preseason debut after injury kept him out in preseason Week 1.
We'll talk about Barham's performance and much more as we take a look at the biggest takeaways from the Cowboys' exhibition victory over Arizona.
Davis saw the field before both Phil Mafah and Jaydon Blue, which was not the case last week, and he had the best overall showing of Cowboys backs on Saturday night when it mattered most.
Davis tallied five carries for 29 yards (5.8 yards per carry) over the first two quarters and, maybe more importantly for a player who has had questions about his pass-catching abilities, Davis recorded an eight-yard touchdown reception.
Davis also showed his chops in pass protection by successfully picking up a blitz, which is more evidence he's the best pass protector at running back outside of Javonte Williams.
Brian Schottenheimer & co have hinted that Malik Davis is in the RB2 competition after last week’s performances by Jaydon Blue and Mafah Somewhat out of necessity Malik Davis was getting the 2nd reps this week Certainly seems the part tonight - started (but rotated with) Blue pic.twitter.com/lo92PUGzzU
In the same span, Blue posted nine carries for 45 yards (five yards per carry) and didn't record a catch. Blue did, however, look better as a runner than he did last week and finished with 15 carries for 75 yards, so he had a strong night, also.
This race is still close, but we're giving the edge to Davis for now after he showed more and was the more consistent runner when he rotated snaps with Blue over the first two quarters before not seeing a single touch in the second half.
As for Mafah, he didn't see a single carry until the fourth quarter, so he's clearly the RB4 right now.
If we didn't know any better, we would have guessed that Barham was an experienced starting linebacker because he looked the part on Saturday night.
It didn't take long for Barham to make his presence felt, as he had two tackles, one tackle for loss and a pressure on a blitz over the first two series of his NFL debut.
Look at Barham knife through the defense for this TFL. His ability to diagnose and react is eye-opening.
Barham makin’ plays right away #DALvsAZ | @JaishawnBarham 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/kuZmG9kwXv
This is just silly from Jaishawn Barham pic.twitter.com/z5KARJ4qGS
My. Goodness. This man is going to be a problem.
In all, Barham finished with five tackles, including one for loss. We have seen enough and he doesn't need to play another preseason snap. That's how good he looked.
As if his night couldn't be any more impressive, Barham also wore the green dot , which is a huge vote of confidence.
At this point, nobody should be writing Dee Winters' name in pen for the starting job next to DeMarvion Overshown. Barham is very much alive for that job, and we're already convinced he should get it after what we saw in preseason Week 2.
Even if he isn't technically the starter, Christian Parker is going to find a way to get Barham involved plenty.
Joe Milton started tightening the gap between himself and Sam Howell for the QB2 job after playing better in preseason Week 1 , and we believe Milton has pulled ahead after an outstanding showing in preseason Week 2.
Milton completed 9-of-13 passes for 179 yards and two scores through the air while adding a rushing touchdown, also.
His best throws of the night were an absolute dime to Jonathan Mingo for a 53-yard scoring strike, and a 70-yard completion to Camden Brown that saw Milton throw across his body on the run to find Brown, who did the rest.
Joe Milton III put his arm on full display tonight 🚀 9/13, 179 YDS, 3 Total TDs, 0 INT. What team needs to call up Dallas for Milton? pic.twitter.com/U1Nq7Drx8c
All of that and we didn't even mention how Milton could have had another scoring drive on the opening series if not for a drop by Zack Kuntz.
Through two preseason games, Milton has completed 21-of-28 passes (75%) for 289 yards and four total touchdowns.
Howell did not fare as well after completing 7-of-10 passes for 65 yards and one interception on what was a poor decision from the veteran signal-caller.
In fairness to Howell, his protection wasn't anywhere near as good as Milton's was, but even taking that into account, Milton was still clearly the better player for a second week in a row.
If the Cowboys are only going to keep five wide receivers, neither Camden Brown nor Jonathan Mingo made that decision any easier.
As we already mentioned, Brown and Mingo were both on the other end of Milton's best passes of the night, with Mingo's going for his first career touchdown (yes, you read that correctly: Mingo hadn't scored either a preseason or regular season touchdown).
It's hard to fathom the Cowboys cutting Mingo given what they invested in him in the 2024 trade, and with Mingo having a good offseason. We also can't see the Cowboys cutting Brown after what he has shown in training camp and the preseason, which should lead to him getting claimed if he gets cut.
Don't be surprised if the Cowboys keep six wide receivers, which seemed highly unlikely going into the offseason with how strong Dallas is atop the depth chart.
Revel only saw one drive in the game, but he made the most of it and kept the good times rolling in what has been a strong offseason for him .
The 2025 third-round pick notched his first career interception on a pass from Gardner Minshew. Granted, the Cardinals wide receiver fell down, but Revel was in the perfect spot.
For good measure, Revel returned the pick 22 yards to set the Cowboys up for an easy scoring drive.
Don't look now, but the Cowboys might actually be deep at the cornerback position if Revel and DaRon Bland can rebound, and if Cobie Durant plays at the level he has throughout the offseason.
After an abysmal showing in preseason Week 1 , the twos along the offensive line were much better in the first half this week.
The Cowboys started Drew Shelton, Trevor Keegan, Nick Leverett, Ajani Cornelius and Nate Thomas from left to right. The changes from last week were Shelton and Thomas swapping spots and Leverett starting over T.J. Bass, who got the night off.
Milton had enough time to throw and wasn't sacked, and there were holes to run through in the ground game, something we couldn't say last week.
Sure, the Cardinals are a bad team and their backups don't present much of a challenge, but that does not totally erase just how encouraging this performance was.
The Cowboys had 13 penalties in the preseason opener but managed to reduce that number big time on Saturday.
Dallas was far more disciplined against the Cardinals, with the team totaling just four penalties for 20 yards. That was a much-needed showing after the abomination that was last week.
For the second straight week, we didn't see any communication issues or other big miscues from Parker's defense like we have seen from Cowboys units the past two years.
Dallas made a pair of stops in the red zone to hold Arizona to field goals and Arizona only found pay dirt once and scored 13 points. The Cardinals also barely crossed 300 yards of offense.
Yes, all of this came against Arizona's backups, but the Cowboys didn't have their starters out there, either. Considering the circumstances, this was another impressive showing.

title: Fan-Favorite Cowboys Rookie Jaishawn Barham Given Major Responsibility in NFL Debut
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham will make his NFL debut in the preseason Week 2 game against the Arizona Cardinals and will be given a big responsibility, also.
Ahead of kickoff, head coach Brian Schottenheimer told sideline reporter Kristi Scales that Barham will be wearing the green dot for Dallas.
"Cowboys rookie (linebacker) Jaishawn Barham will be getting an opportunity to wear the green dot and call the defense tonight, according to (Kristi Scales)," The Athletic Jon Machota relayed.
Of course, wearing the green dot means Barham will be calling plays, which is a huge vote of confidence for a rookie and shows he has a good amount of trust from the coaching staff, which is a great sign when it comes to how he's developing.
The Cowboys entered the offseason with multiple question marks at linebacker, including the uncertainty around who would wear the green dot .
DeMarvion Overshown is slated to wear it when the season starts, but the Cowboys need to give themselves as many options as possible just in case an injury occurs.
It appears Barham is now one of those options, and the Cowboys have been giving others looks throughout training camp.
The third-round pick has missed some time in training camp with an injury, but Barham has been a consistent standout when he has been on the practice field.
We've seen Barham do a little bit of everything, with the rookie flashing his abilities as a run-stopper and pass-rusher, and he has even made some plays in coverage.
We're not sure the Cowboys could have asked for much more than what they have seen out of Barham thus far and the future is looking bright for him early on.
While Barham still has a chance to beat out Dee Winters for the starting job next to Overshown, chances are he's going to begin the season as the LB3.
That said, Barham should still have ample opportunities to see the field because of his versatility.
On top of being able to line up at inside linebacker, Barham has the ability to take snaps at edge rusher, which makes him an intriguing chess piece for defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
But, first things first, he's got to show that he's more than just a good practice player by showing out in the next two preseason games. That quest begins on Saturday night.

title: Will Dallas Cowboys Play Von Miller vs Cardinals in NFL Preseason Week 2?
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are in Glendale this weekend for a late-night showdown against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Arena as Week 2 of the NFL preseason winds down.
Dallas and Arizona are set to kick off at 10:00 p.m. ET on the NFL Network, with a majority of the team's starters set to watch the contest from the sideline.
But while the team's star players will not be suiting up for Saturday's game, there have been some questions about the team's newest addition: Super Bowl MVP and future Pro Football Hall of Famer Von Miller , who signed with the team earlier this week.
The 8-time Pro Bowler has seen very limited action during training camp, with only a handful of reps during practice, but he made an immediate impact. Unfortunately, it looks like fans will have to wait until the regular season to see Miller going full speed for the Cowboys.
Miller had just a handful of snaps during practice in Oxnard, but he wasted no time making an impact. In his limited reps, Miller found a way to get after the quarterback and create pressure.
When it comes to Saturday's game, however, don't expect to see him play. Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News previously said the " goal is to get him ready for Week 1 ."
Despite bringing him along slowly, the Cowboys are happy with what they have seen from the veteran since arriving in Oxnard. Defensive coordinator Christian Parker had nothing but praise for Miller after his first two practices with the team.
“Ultimate professional. Phenomenal teammate. And obviously he can still get after the quarterback and play at a high level as an all down player," Parker said of Miller. "We’re not really putting a cap on what could be this year, we’re gonna let that kind of handle it itself. But we definitely feel good about that edge room and feel good about the addition.”
It's been fun seeing Miller get to live out his dream of being a member of the Cowboys since signing with the team, but hopefully the anticipation of seeing him suit up with the star on his helmet will have a big payoff with on-field production that will help take the defense to the next level.
