title: Rising? Falling?: Packers Stock Report Before Critical Closing Stretch of Camp
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The biggest week of Green Bay Packers training camp is here.
The Packers will play at the Denver Broncos on Friday night. Next week, they will host the Arizona Cardinals for a joint practice on Wednesday before playing them in the final preseason game on Friday.
Those will be the closing arguments for players competing for a starting job or a place on the roster. General manager Brian Gutekunst will cut the roster to 53 players on Sunday, Aug. 30.
With those competitions in mind and using our camp-opening Lock-O-Meter as a guide, here’s who’s rising and who’s falling.
Kyle McCord entered training camp competing with Kyron Drones to be the No. 3 quarterback. McCord made short work of Drones by showing he’s the more polished and, more importantly, poised quarterback. A season-long spot on the practice squad is his to lose.
“One thing about the NFL is you really never know what’s going to happen next,” he said this week. “Obviously, getting drafted to Philly last year, you think you’re going to spend four years there and then, boom, end up in Green Bay a year later. I think the thing is to continue to put your head down and keep working, and that ultimately leads you to success and puts you exactly where you need to be.”
MarShawn Lloyd hasn’t missed a day. Not during OTAs. Not during minicamp. Not during training camp.
After two years in which he basically lived on injured reserve and atop a stationary bike to stay in shape, Lloyd not only is going to make the roster but he’s on track to be the No. 2 back behind Josh Jacobs.
That’s exactly what the Packers envisioned when they signed Jacobs and drafted Lloyd in 2024.
“Emotions were high,” Lloyd said before the Pittsburgh game. “I was ready to go. It was fun. I was juiced up. I was listening to music. I was in it, I was in the zone. It was fun. I didn’t play a lot but it was good being able to get hit and run the ball. It was fun. It was good being out there with them.”
The Packers let Rasheed Walker go in free agency and handed the starting job to Jordan Morgan. So far, so good.
Morgan hasn’t been great, but the Packers should go into the season with few worries about their blind-side protector. What matters is how Morgan is trending, and that’s all positive.
“I think we’re very comfortable with him there,” general manager Brian Gutekunst said. “He’s going to have to go out and do it over full season and year in and year out. But he’s done a really nice job through the spring, really nice job so far. I’m looking forward to getting some more reps here in the preseason and then get ready for the regular season.”
After two seasons as a backup – he had played only six snaps on offense in the first 33 games of his NFL career – Jacob Monk has gone from entering training camp on the roster bubble to being the presumptive starting right guard for Week 1 at Minnesota.
The Packers acquired Darian Kinnard from the Eagles for a sixth-round pick at the end of training camp last year. After playing in only three games in his first three seasons, Kinnard played in 17 games with four starts last year.
Kinnard re-signed with the Packers this offseason, collecting a $1 million signing bonus. He’s in a bit of a precarious position while dealing with an ankle injury that sidelined him for most of the Pittsburgh game and presumably will keep him out at Denver.
What might save him are the struggles of the next player on this list.
Last year’s second-round pick started at right guard down the stretch last season. He played inconsistently but there was absolutely no reason to believe he wouldn’t start again at right guard. Really, the only question was how much he’d grow in Year 2 on the job.
Instead, Belton lost the starting job to Monk. He might replace Kinnard as the swing tackle, but he’s barely played any left tackle during training camp and has really struggled at right tackle. Did the Packers blow it on a second-round pick? Is Belton simply reeling from losing his starting job and having to change positions?
John Williams was like a bonus draft pick. A seventh-round pick last year, a back injury that required surgery sidelined him for the offseason program, training camp and most of the regular season. He didn’t practice with the team at all until he was designated for return from injured reserve for the final three weeks.
Williams spent the offseason and the start of training camp playing center and guard. Now, he’s been locked in at left tackle – his position at Cincinnati – with the No. 2 offense. He hasn’t been great but his versatility could be a tremendous asset.
“You’re always looking for guys that can play the tackle position, and I think he’s gone in there and done his job,” coach Matt LaFleur said the day after the Pittsburgh game.
A sixth-round pick last year, Warren Brinson didn’t get on the field until Week 6. He became a key role player during the second half of the season, playing 20-plus snaps in each of the final eight games, but he didn’t make much of an impact.
He’s made a lot of impact this summer, though. He probably has more pressures than any of the interior players. He added three more pressures along with stout run defense against the Steelers.
“You used the word confident,” defensive run-game coordinator DeMarcus Covington said this week. “I do think confidence is built in when you’re doing it over and over and over. He’s able to do it in practice over and over and over, so that’s helping him build his confidence.
“So, it’s not just talking about it. He’s actually out there performing within practice and doing it, so I believe the same thing. Hopefully, he’ll continue to excel and what we’re going to need him to do is keep rising and showing up every single day, attacking the grind and making sure he’s ready for whenever his number’s called.”
Entering camp, the belief was Jonathan Ford and Nazir Stackhouse would be competing to be the backup nose tackle to rookies Chris McClellan.
Instead, Ford – making the proverbial fifth-year jump – has put himself in position to be the starter due to his impact play against the run.
“I feel like this camp,” Ford said, “I came with the mentality that I’m going to try to get a job as much as I can and show my talents in a defense that favors me as a bigger guy that I can go out and anchor the run and move guys in the run game.”
When training camp began, nobody thought Anthony Campbell and Jaden Crumedy would be in position to make the roster. Campbell barely played in two seasons at the University of Miami and went undrafted in 2025. Crumedy was a sixth-round pick by Carolina in 2024 who joined the Packers after last season.
Instead, they’ve been part of the big story of training camp, which is the unexpected power by the defensive tackles. Campbell has been a constant menace on the practice field. Crumedy has, too, though to a lesser extent, but his position flexibility could work in his favor.
Their play might force the Packers to go heavy with heavy guys.
“That is a really good group, and I think the effort level there has been really good, and they’ve been performing each and every day,” general manager Brian Gutekunst said this week. “Those big guys, when you have more than enough, that’s very unusual, so we’re excited about those guys.
“With the opportunities they’re given – because they’re not all given the same – performing at a high level, making plays. That position, sometimes your job isn’t to go make the play. Sometimes, it’s to allow others to make plays and doing what the coaches are asking them to do. They’ve all done a really nice job.”
Brenton Cox went undrafted in 2023 and was the big beneficiary of the Preston Smith trade in 2024 with four sacks during the final seven games of the season. Last year, however, Cox suffered a groin injury in Week 1 and wound up playing in only four games.
During training camp, Cox has probably been the most productive edge rusher – with the caveat that most of his reps have come against…

title: Second-Year Jump? Not So Much for Packers’ Jonathan Ford in Chase for Roster Spot
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Coaches love talking about their players taking a big jump in their second season.
This week, general manager Brian Gutekunst called a player’s third season a “benchmark.”
That makes Green Bay Packers nose tackle Jonathan Ford the ultimate outlier.
A seventh-round pick by Green Bay in 2022, Ford didn’t make the roster during his rookie training camp, spent the season on the practice squad and didn’t play in a game. In 2023, Ford didn’t make the roster, spent the season on the practice squad and didn’t play in a game. In 2024, Ford once again didn’t make the roster. He opened the season on the practice squad before being poached by the rival Bears and playing in the first four games of his career.
Ford played in eight games for Chicago last year before he was released late in the season. The Packers, in desperate need of a run-stopping defensive tackle, brought him back. In the final game of his fourth season in the NFL, he made his Packers debut.
“I felt honored,” Ford said this week. “When I left, to be honest, I didn’t think I was ever going to be back. The fact that I was able to come back and jump right in the mix and finish those games with this team, it was a wonderful thing for me to be with a team and organization that favors you and that feels good about you as a player.
“I think that’s the main thing is having confidence and being with people that see you as a good player.”
The Packers see Ford as a good player. Ford got the start against Pittsburgh in the preseason opener and has taken most of the first-team reps at nose tackle over the past week. With the second preseason game coming up at Denver on Friday night, Ford has put himself in position to do a couple things he failed to do in 2022, 2023 and 2024.
First, making the 53-man roster. Second, being a factor.
“I feel like my process has been totally different from different camps I’ve been in throughout the years,” he said. “I do feel like my chances are whatever they are if I come out and stack days. I don’t really focus on too many things that I can’t control. I just control the things that I’m capable of doing, and that’s going out there on the field and handling my business.”
What does he mean about his process?
“Just my whole approach,” he said. “I feel like this camp, I came with the mentality that I’m going to try to get a job as much as I can and show my talents in a defense that favors me as a bigger guy that I can go out and anchor the run and move guys in the run game.”
Ford is, indeed, a bigger guy. His listed weight of 338 pounds is tied with fellow defensive tackle Jordon Riley for the biggest player on the roster.
That size will be a big asset – pun intended – in the heart of Jonathan Gannon’s defense.
“You need a big nose,” Ford said. “You need a guy that’s able to anchor the run and move side to side well, and I think I’ve been doing pretty good taking the coaching from Coach V.O. [Vince Oghobaase] and D.C. [DeMarcus Covington] and J.G., obviously, giving us tips and bringing those things out on the field and repping it every day and getting better at it.”
Ford had two tackles against the Steelers, including a tackle for loss that helped force a punt. That’s been his training camp in a nutshell. He’s not just a big man taking up a couple blockers to free up the linebackers. He’s been a playmaker.
“I see a guy that’s really matured as not only a football player but as a person,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “He is a load inside and he’s done a really nice job playing the nose position and defeating blocks. He’s been pretty impactful throughout camp.”
While Ford downplayed his spot in the race for a roster spot, the 27-year-old did find validation in getting an opportunity to run with the No. 1 defense. The key, he said, has been his consistency.
“Every day, I’ve put something on tape,” he said. “Every day, I try to make a play, I try to do something to affect the offense. So, I think for me, just being consistent day to day. Just taking what I learned in the meeting room, what I learned in individuals out in team period, and it shows up in games, and I’ve just been kind of in my zone and in my flow state.”
Ford knows there’s no time to relax. The depth at defensive tackle has been unexpectedly good, which means Ford isn’t the only player who’s been a standout. He knows he must finish strong. That starts with Friday night’s game against the Broncos and ends with the joint practice and preseason game against the Cardinals next week.
“Just consistency,” he said of what he needs to show the next two weeks. “I think that’s the biggest thing in this league is being consistent and being able to show coaches you can do it snap after snap.
“If you have a bad snap, you can correct it – take the corrections, bring it back on the field and do it the right way that coaches coached you do it. I think the biggest thing for me is being consistent and showing that I’m a player down in and down out and I can do my job and do it at a high level.”
With a strong camp, Ford has set himself up to be the rarest of the rare.
In a league that chews up and spits out young players who make little or no impact during their first couple seasons, Ford’s steadfast approach has put himself in position to make the ol’ Year 5 jump.
“Just being able to have those opportunities and being able to just show that I can play,” he said. “I’ve had my ups and downs, and I’ve been in schemes that I probably wasn’t really favored in. So, the fact that I was able to come back here and show that I can play in this scheme and do everything I can, I think that’s been the biggest thing for me, just being comfortable.
“Being comfortable not in the sake of slowing down and not going as hard but being comfortable in knowing that they want me to play in this position and they want me to do the best I can at this position. So, for me, I just think going out there and going hard, that’s what I owe this defense.”

title: Texans' QB3 Spot Looks Less Certain After Raiders Preseason Game
full_text:
The Houston Texans' QB3 spot was shaken up significantly earlier last week when second-year signal-caller Graham Mertz went down with a torn ACL , effectively ending his 2026 campaign.
In the days following, the Texans went on to sign veteran quarterback Brett Rypien , an experienced name at the position who became an easy favorite to fill into that QB3 spot for the season and play the next couple of preseason games to prove that he's worth it.
But with week two of the preseason down against the Las Vegas Raiders , there's a chance that the Texans' QB3 outlook now looks a little more complicated than expectations were shaping up after the Rypien signing.
In Rypien's Texans debut, his performance wasn't exactly exemplary. He played the entire second half of the game and entered as Houston was up 20-3, and proceeded not to score another point.
In all, Rypien completed six of his 10 passes for 44 yards, was sacked twice, threw an interception on the last drive of the game, and lost one of his two total fumbles on the night. Houston would be outscored 19-0 in the second half and drop their second preseason game in a row.
For a performance in which the quarterback is battling for staying power and a roster spot for Week 1, it's not exactly the most ideal outing. C.J. Stroud had a strong performance, Mills played well in his first quarter reps, but Rypien fell short of expectations.
Of course, it's one preseason outing, and Rypien probably isn't going to get many snaps for Houston this season anyways. There are certainly other pressing matters to address around the roster.
But for the Texans, at the very least, Rypien's lackluster day might just open up the question of whether or not they should add another name to the position for their third and final preseason game to add some more competition under center.
The Texans have three routes they could take for their QB3 position: they roll with Rypien, they bring in another name off the free agent market or via trade, or they simply carry two quarterbacks into Week 1 with C.J. Stroud and Davis Mills.
All three have a real possibility of being the end result. The outcome that can't be ruled out is the Texans bringing in just two quarterbacks for Week 1 if they can't find a strong enough QB3 in the time between now and cutdown day.
However, it's certainly a bit more complicated of a situation compared to what Houston entered their second preseason game with.
When it comes to the Texans' first and second quarterbacks on the depth chart, there are no doubts about who will be the two filling things out. But that third spot––whether it ends up being Rypien, someone else, or nobody else––will remain one of the bigger question marks in the days ahead of cutdown day at the end of August.

title: Predicting Texans' WR Depth Chart After Shepard, Jones Signings
full_text:
The Houston Texans' wide receiver room has taken a bit of a different shape from where things stood this time last week.
Jayden Higgins is out for the season with a torn ACL. Guys like Tank Dell and Jaylin Noel are still slowly recovering from their respective injuries . And just recently, the Texans added two new veteran wide receivers onto their 90-man roster: Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones.
The #Texans are signing veteran WRs Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones, sources tell me and @RapSheet . Both impressed in a workout today and join the mix in Houston after the loss of Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL. pic.twitter.com/oYlmSVJ4BT
So now feels like about as good a time as any to break down how the Texans' wide receiver room is expected to shake out, how the depth chart could be ordered, and who might be in (or out) of the 53-man roster picture once cuts arrive at the end of the month.
Let's sort through everyone on the Texans' roster at wide receiver and see where they stand less than 10 days out from cutdown day:
With or without Jayden Higgins on the field, Nico Collins was always going to be bound for the most snaps as the Texans' X wide receiver, and the most targets in the offense as a whole. But without Higgins there to complement him as his No. 2, there's a chance that Collins could be en route to the best season of his career.
Last season, Collins had over 1,100 yards and 71 receptions with six touchdowns in 15 games. There's a good chance he surpasses all three of those marks in 2026, so long as he's able to remain healthy.
This is right where you'd expect to see Higgins in the Texans' depth chart. Now, the offense has to pivot, and the wideout with the best chance to fill the void that he leaves is fourth-year veteran Xavier Hutchinson.
Hutchinson is coming off a career season in 2025 with over 400 receiving yards, has been with C.J. Stroud in Houston every year since he arrived in 2023, and has the ideal skillset to complement Collins on the opposite side of him in the offense––even if not as athletically gifted or as explosive as Higgins is.
Jaylin Noel is slowly returning to the Texans' lineup after suffering a hamstring and a finger injury at the start of training camp . And as long as he's good to go for Week 1 of the regular season, he's the clear favorite within this wide receiver room to take the most reps in the slot.
The second-year wideout could have a case to be one of the Texans' biggest breakout candidates since Higgins' injury. He's a young pass-catcher who's due for a huge jump in snaps offensively, had a similarly productive offseason to Higgins, and Houston invested a good bit into him last year as a third-round pick. He'll be someone to keep an eye on in the weeks ahead.
Once cutdown day hits, the Texans' wide receiver room could come down to six to seven names. Four of those––Collins, Hutchinson, Noel, and Dell––are virtual locks. So the final two to three are widely up for grabs.
I think of the two newest signings, Sterling Shepard has a better chance to make it to Week 1 . He's been more productive than Zay Jones in recent seasons, even if Jones fits a better physical profile to what the Texans need. Lewis Bond has been a camp star worthy of a 53-man spot, and a veteran like Justin Watson might now be more valuable to have with Higgins out.
Zay Jones could still make it to the 53-man roster, but he needs to prove that he can still remain on the field consistently at 31 years old, while also being a productive pass-catcher at this point in his career. Since 2023, he's played in 208 games and averaged less than two catches and 25 yards per game.
Jared Wayne is also someone to keep a close eye on . He's been someone making noise throughout camp and in preseason, and as a 6-foot-3, 210-pound wideout, maybe the Texans could value him as a bigger target to have in the room, who's also been around the building since 2024.
These five wide receivers are still listed on the Texans' 90-man roster, but don't exactly have an inside track to make it past cutdown day at the end of the month.
Perhaps a practice squad nod is in store for one or multiple of them. Daniel Sobkowicz has been someone many have liked when he was picked up as a UDFA in April , so maybe he finds his way in there. But when compared to the nine players clearly sitting ahead of them in the pecking order, it doesn't feel like anything more is within reach for anyone in this tier.

title: Texans Announce Release Date for New Rivalries Uniforms
full_text:
The Houston Texans have announced the release date for their newest Rivalries uniforms for the 2026 NFL season .
And it looks like the release of those new uniforms for Houston sits right around the corner.
The Texans put out a promotional video for their upcoming uniform release, where players around the roster reacted to the new threads for the first time.
And in that video, the Texans revealed that those uniforms will be officially unveiled to the public on Tuesday, August 25th .
No peekingggg 👀 pic.twitter.com/oC1xmJDmy6
The reviews from some of the players were clearly positive, which could be a sign of things to come for next week’s reveal.
"That s---- gas," said Tank Dell.
"Oh, that's tough," was what Reed Blankenship said.
"I can get jiggy with that," came from Kamari Lassiter.
And along with the release date and the reaction video from the players, the Texans also released a new teaser for the new uniforms on the horizon––where the uniform was described as a set that'll seek innovation, being different, and "the most Houston thing that you've ever seen on the gridiron."
Houston, this one’s for you 🤘 pic.twitter.com/LmCAaELDCv
With the Texans set to receive their Rivalries uniforms for next season, it'll be one of five uniforms that Houston will be able to wear throughout the year: their typical home and away jerseys, their all-red alternates, and their dark-blue "Space City" themed uniforms, and now, another set of alternates.
On most weeks, the Texans will be wearing their typical home and away uniforms as they typically do. But for three weeks throughout the season, Houston will bring out those alternates.
For their Rivalries set, that'll come during their Week 11 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts , a game that'll take place on Thursday Night Football at Houston in Reliant Stadium for one of the Texans' more exciting games throughout the regular season altogether.
The NFL first kicked off Rivalries uniforms across the league for the 2025 season, where the league and Nike released eight new uniforms for the AFC East and the NFC West to wear one time throughout the year for three seasons in a highlighted divisional matchup.
And the theme of those uniforms was designed to put together a more unique, modern look for each team that wore them. Nike describes the Rivalries uniforms from last season as ones that "celebrate storied local traditions and unite fan communities with designs unique to select cities and teams."
After the first two divisions got their uniforms last year, the AFC South and the NFC North would be next up on the list to receive their Rivalries uniforms in 2026. In 2027, the AFC West and NFC East will get their own.
But following a long and anticipated wait , the release of those uniforms for the 2026 slate is right around the corner for the Texans and every other team in this wave of announcements.
Expect the reveal for the Texans' Rivalries uniforms to come at 9 a.m. CT on Tuesday morning, along with the other seven teams in the mix who are in for their own.

title: Nick Chubb Retires From NFL After One Season With Texans
full_text:
Nick Chubb, the former Houston Texans running back, has officially called it a career in the NFL.
According to an emotional social media post from Chubb, the 30-year-old runner will be retiring from the NFL after eight seasons of playing.
Chubb was one of the top stars at his position throughout the first few years of his time with the Cleveland Browns. He had four straight seasons logging over 1,000 yards on the ground, and had over 8,000 yards from scrimmage throughout his career since 2018.
The best season of Chubb's career came with the Browns in 2022, where he found his way to over 1,500 yards on the ground and 13 total touchdowns.
And it was at the tail-end of that career of Chubb's where he played one season with the Texans––a campaign that came off an injury-riddled 2023 and 2024 season with the Browns, and signed late in the 2025 offseason after Houston first learned about a foot injury suffered by Joe Mixon.
Chubb, in his retirement post, said that he wanted to end his career on a healthy season and on a winning team. And with the Texans back in 2025, he was able to do just that.
Chubb played 15 games with the Texans throughout the 2025 season, ultimately totaling 122 carries for 506 yards and three touchdowns.
He was a top-two runner in Houston's offense throughout the season next to rookie Woody Marks, which came as a result of the season-ending injury that Mixon suffered earlier in the offseason .
All things considered, with a tenure that came on short notice and after an injury-riddled season the year before, Chubb's 2025 campaign wasn't too bad of a turnout.
He was healthy throughout most of the season, a productive player in his role as a bruising, powerful complement to a smaller, explosive back in Marks, and a steady veteran Houston could rely on in a room that lacked depth and overall firepower.
Eventually, Houston would call it a wrap on their partnership with Chubb this offseason . His one-year deal came to an end, and the Texans didn't have interest in running it back for 2026 as they would turn in another direction at running back for the season ahead.
At the same time, it's not to say that Chubb's time in Houston could be considered a failure. From Chubb's perspective, that brief period with the Texans is a bit of a perfct statement to end to his career on.
The presence Chubb brought to Houston for the 2025 season won't stack up to his Cleveland days, where he emerged as one of the most powerful and explosive backs in the NFL that powered an otherwise lackluster Browns offense for multiple years.
But his one-year period with the Texans does mark an important time in his turbulent career: a quiet, yet graceful end to one of the league's more unlucky stars health-wise in recent memory, but an ending he's also able to make happen on his own terms.

title: Texans Sign Pair of Free Agent WRs After Jayden Higgins Injury
full_text:
The Houston Texans have added not one, but two wide receivers from free agency after learning that second-year wideout Jayden Higgins would be missing the 2026 season with a torn ACL .
According to a report from NFL Network 's Mike Garafolo, the Texans are signing veteran wide receivers Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones.
The two wide receivers were in Houston for a workout on Friday, and reportedly performed well in each of their showings.
The #Texans are signing veteran WRs Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones, sources tell me and @RapSheet . Both impressed in a workout today and join the mix in Houston after the loss of Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL. pic.twitter.com/oYlmSVJ4BT
Therefore, the Texans bring in both to their 90-man roster, and have a pair of veteran wide receivers who can compete for a spot past cutdown day, which now sits a little under two weeks away.
The Texans were due to add more depth at wide receiver after the Higgins injury . And with these two signings, Houston wanted to go with the approach of adding a couple of older, experienced guys to the position. Both Shepard and Jones are 31 years old or older and have at least nine years of NFL experience.
Shepard comes off of two years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after spending eight seasons of his career with the New York Giants, where he found his place as a depth option at receiver.
In 2025, Shepard played in 13 games to collect 39 receptions for 371 yards and a touchdowns, which turned out to be a more productive and more efficient season than his 2024 campaign in Tampa Bay.
As for Jones, he's played for four franchises across his nine years in the league, most recently with the Arizona Cardinals from 2024 to 2025.
His past two seasons in Arizona have been a little more limited compared to what he's seen in earlier seasons of his career, but he is not too far removed from his 2022 campaign with the Jacksonville Jaguars, where he saw 121 targets, 83 receptions, and over 800 receiving yards.
Both might be in the back-nine of their careers with some of the better years of production behind them, but clearly, the Texans liked what they saw from both Shepard and Jones in their recent workouts, and they each could have a case to be worthy of a 53-man roster spot in Houston if they continue to perform well.
Even after the Texans decided to add a couple of veterans here in Shepard and Jones, that certainly doesn't put them out of the race to trade for another pass-catcher in the days ahead, especially as roster cuts loom closer and closer.
Earlier on Friday, the Texans were linked to potential trades for New England Patriots wide receiver Kayshon Boutte , as well as Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman–– according to KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson –– each of which would rank ahead of Shepard and Jones in the event they came to Houston.
But until the Texans decide to make another move to the position, Shepard and Jones can add a couple of wide receivers who are proven serviceable guys in the league who can compete for a roster spot in camp, and get snaps in preseason next week against the Carolina Panthers.
Are either in a favorable spot to make the 53-man roster come time for next weekend's cuts? It depends on what their next week of production looks like in practice and in-game. However, based on the track record they've shown through their career and the shallowness of the Texans' wide receiver room, the chances of either of them making the cut are far from zero.

title: Texans 53-Man Roster Projection 3.0: How Jayden Higgins' Injury Changes Things
full_text:
The Houston Texans have two of their three preseason games in the books.
And after a couple of preseason games , a joint practice with the Las Vegas Raiders, and a whole lot of training camp practices since the end of July, there's been a few noteworthy changes around what to expect for the Texans' 53-man roster cutdown.
One of those, of course, is the newest injury suffered by second-year wide receiver Jayden Higgins, effectively ending his 2026 season. That absence for Higgins can certainly create a bit of a ripple effect as to how this 53-man roster changes because of it.
At this point, cutdown day is less than two weeks away––sitting at the end of the month on August 30th. The clock is ticking before the Texans are tasked with making some tough decisions around the roster, and determining who are the 53 players best suited to be on the roster come Week 1 against the Buffalo Bills .
Let's break down a brand-new 53-man roster projection based on what we've seen since the start of camp:
(2): C.J. Stroud, Davis Mills
The Texans could decide to roll into the year with Brett Rypien as their QB, but as of his latest showing against the Raiders, he hasn't presented any compelling evidence as to why he should be in line to have a 53-man roster spot.
Perhaps the Texans could sign somebody else to compete for that spot on the depth chart, or give Rypien an extended run in preseason game three. As of now, though, I don't think he's locked into a spot by any means.
(3): David Montgomery, Woody Marks, Jawhar Jordan
The Texans did feel likely to give British Brooks a roster spot here. But he broke his foot earlier in training camp , and doesn't have a clear timetable for his return. So right now, Houston could be primed to keep three backs onboard for Week 1.
Noah Whittington could have a chance to make it past the cut, but there might be a better possibility he hits the practice squad instead of a call-up to the 53-man roster. Jawhar Jordan is also injured at the moment, but feels more likely to be ready to go for the regular season as opposed to Brooks.
(6): Nico Collins, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell, Lewis Bond, Justin Watson
Here's where the Texans' roster sees the biggest change since last week: now Jayden Higgins means Houston’s wide receiver room could turn out a little bit slimmer , and of course, not quite as strong as it looked to start training camp.
Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson are due for even bigger roles than they were before. Lewis Bond feels way more settled into a 53-man roster spot, and Justin Watson could be the last name to squeeze in. Jared Wayne, while a preseason standout, could be geared towards the practice squad, unless Houston wants seven wideouts..
(4): Dalton Schultz, Marlin Klein, Foster Moreau, Cade Stover
Brevin Jordan seems to have been dealing with an injury through the past couple of weeks, so there are no guarantees he'll be ready for Week 1. But even if he were, these four guys have seemingly set themselves apart as the top four names in the Texans tight end room.
The biggest surprise of anyone here? Second-round rookie Marlin Klein, who had the Texans' biggest play of the day offensively in Week 1 of the preseason, then proceeded to lead Houston in catches against the Raiders. There's a better and better chance he begins the year as TE2 on the depth chart .
(4): Aireontae Ersery, Braden Smith, Trent Brown, Blake Fisher
As to who starts at right tackle might still be a bit of a mystery. But based on Blake Fisher's recent performance in joint practice against the Raiders, there's a world where the 2024 second round pick might be getting looks for a 53-man roster spot to provide extra depth at a position that already has some question marks.
Especially with the health concerns that both Braden Smith and Trent Brown have dealt with throughout their careers, Fisher provides a little extra insurance at the position in the event either of them misses time.
(6): Keylan Rutledge, Evan Brown, Ed Ingram, Wyatt Teller, Jarrett Patterson, Febechi Nwaiwu
The combination of Keylan Rutledge and Evan Brown starting on the inside of Houston's offensive line has gained some traction since their second preseason game against the Raiders. Even if Brown doesn't start over Wyatt Teller, though, it feels pretty likely that both of them will make the 53-man roster.
Then, Houston will likely have to decide between Jarrett Patterson and Jake Andrews for that final spot. Considering the Texans just guaranteed more money on Patterson's contract for next season, that might be a sign there are plans in store for him this season.
(5): Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter, Jadeveon Clowney, Logan Hall, Dominique Robinson
Houston could bring another edge rusher in here for extra depth behind their top three guys, but no one else within the Texans' current roster has stood out besides Dominique Robinson . He's one of three players on the roster to record a sack in two preseason games.
Thought that Dominique Robinson played well on Thursday and was definitely the best of the DEs. He played well against the run, which is the main thing to watch for that DE4 spot where he is competing with Dylan Horton & Solomon Byrd. pic.twitter.com/P60cF4jgDa
Regardless, the Texans will be set to play Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter, and Jadeveon Clowney a large share of the snaps off the edge. So adding another backup next to Robinson as a DE5, as Logan Hall could take more snaps on the interior, might not be the biggest need for Houston's Week 1 roster.
(5): Sheldon Rankins, Tommy Togiai, Kayden McDonald, Mario Edwards, Naquan Jones
The majority of the reps in the Texans' defensive tackle room should be going to the top three names on the depth chart. Kayden McDonald might be third in the pecking order to start, though it certainly wouldn't be a surprise to see him rise to the top by the end of his rookie season.
But considering Houston went out of their way to re-sign veteran Mario Edwards to the roster in training camp, along with Naquan Jones' positive production in camp in the preseason, rostering both of them to expand into a five-man defensive tackle room isn't totally unreasonable.
(5): Azeez Al-Shaair, Henry To'oTo'o, Wade Woodaz, Marte Mapu, Jake Hummel
When it comes to the Texans' LB3 battle, the leader in that race has clearly emerged to be fourth-round rookie Wade Woodaz . That was emphasized in Houston's preseason game against the Raiders when Woodaz ran back an interception on Fernando Mendoza for an 80-yard touchdown for their best defensive play of the game.
OPEN UP A CAN OF WOODAZZZZZZ 🤯 📺: @nflonespn pic.twitter.com/Ke0lrYupPs
Marte Mapu and Jake Hummel are both tenured veterans and proven special teams contributors that feel likely to get the call on the 53-man roster as well. The toughest cut in the room? Rookie linebacker Aiden Fisher, who might be better slated for a practice squad spot early in the season.
(5): Derek Stingley Jr., Kamari Lassiter, Jaylin Smith, Tremon Smith, Alijah Huzzie
The Texans' cornerback room, if constructed like this, can host a great combination of star power and depth that can compete with some of the better units around the league at the position––especially when an All-Pro like Derek Stingley sits atop the depth chart.
The one name here who's seen some of the most praise in training camp is Alijah Huzzie, who feels due to be the Texans' backup nickel corner and a special teamer. UDFA Collin Wright remains a name to watch as well, though his recent injury could cloud his status moving into the season.
(5): Reed Blankenship, Calen Bullock, Jalen Pitre, Kamari Ramsey, Jaylen Reed
The top three of these safeties are locks and due for a big role. The other two guys in the room, Kamari Ramsey and Jaylen Reed, are both extremely appealing young pieces for the future, and can work into the defense in rotational roles and contribute on special teams throughout the 2026 campaign.

title: Texans Could Make Notable O-Line Change After Raiders Preseason Game
full_text:
The Houston Texans spent a ton of time reworking their offensive line this offseason.
After trading Tytus Howard to the Cleveland Browns , signing multiple veterans in free agency, and even drafting multiple interior offensive linemen, this unit looks a whole lot different than it did this time last year.
And after the dust had settled this offseason, one primary offensive line configuration had emerged as the most likely starting group that Houston entered Week 1 with: Aireontar Ersery and Trent Brown at right tackle, Wyatt Teller and Ed Ingram at guard, and rookie Keylan Rutledge at center.
However, after just two preseason games, it seems like the Texans could have a chance to make a shift on their offensive line that would be a little different than those initial projections––and it doesn’t involve their right tackle spot.
According to KPRC2's Aaron Wilson, the Texans are giving "serious consideration" to the idea of starting Keylan Rutledge at left guard, while Evan Brown starts at center.
#Texans are giving serious consideration to this offensive line configuration of Evan Brown at center, Keylan Rutledge at left guard, but no final decisions made. As Cole Popovich has said, they have time to land on their top five guys https://t.co/DuAPW7N6wH
The Texans have previously stated that while there isn't an exact timetable to determine a starting offensive line, they'll certainly have it ready to go once they're preparing for their first game against the Buffalo Bills.
But this bit of intel tells us that the Texans' interior offensive line could be set to switch things up compared to expectations entering training camp.
Houston opted to start the duo of Rutledge and Brown in their second preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Thursday, where they played next to Ersery Ingram and Trent Brown on the first drive of the day.
Since the Texans signed former Pro Bowler Wyatt Teller on a two-year deal this offseason, most have slotted him in as the most likely candidate to claim that left guard spot.
Teller has played right guard throughout his time with the Cleveland Browns, but with Ed Ingram already settled on the right side in Houston, Teller was expected to flip over to the other end.
He was paid $16 million over his two-year deal, and has over 100 career starts with two Pro Bowl selections to his name, setting him up to be an easy-startable, plug-and-play guy even in the back-nine of his career.
Then, Rutledge could be the one to slide over to center , so long as he could make the transition from his college position of left guard.
If not, last year's starter, Jake Andrews, is still on the roster, so he could be someone who retains his spot until the rookie can slide over to center, or is ready to get called up to the first unit.
Houston might have other plans in mind for their starting offensive front, though. Their other veteran interior lineman signed from this offseason, former Arizona Cardinals starter Evan Brown , has been making noise throughout camp and preseason that's put him on the map to start.
He's someone that, while on a one-year deal, has positional versatility to play either guard or center, and has started nearly 70 games at three positions throughout his seven-year career.
The Texans clearly like what he brings to the table, and might just be giving him a real chance to start at center against Buffalo.
That decision to start Brown would also allow the Texans to hand the starting job to their rookie, Keylan Rutledge, on the left side of him at guard, and play a position geared more towards his natural skillset as a right guard at Georgia Tech.
A ton of time still remains before the Texans determine their official starters for that Week 1 game.
Another preseason game and a joint practice against the Carolina Panthers, along with the entire events of roster cutdown day, are still on the horizon. A ton of things could change on the Texans' offensive line from where they stand now.
However, at the very least, based on where the Texans' competition upfront stands now, there are three starting jobs at left guard, center and right tackle that still seem widely undetermined as to who will be starting there to begin the regular season.
But as for Keylan Rutledge, he feels pretty destined to get a call-up. And for Evan Brown, his chances of getting a starting nod his way seem to keep on growing.

title: Texans' DeMeco Ryans Breaks Silence on Jayden Higgins' ACL Injury
full_text:
The Houston Texans are expected to be without second-year wide receiver Jayden Higgins for the 2026 season after he suffered a torn ACL earlier this week .
The injury was suffered on a play in the Texans' joint practice with the Las Vegas Raiders. Higgins initially left practice on Tuesday with a knee injury suffered after going down on a play covered by cornerback Eric Stokes, yet he was able to walk off the field under his own power.
Fast forward a bit, Houston's 2025 second-round pick is out for the year, and the Texans' offense will now be looking a little bit different from what was expected heading into training camp.
It's a huge loss for the Texans that arose even before the second game of their preseason slate, let alone their first game of the regular season.
And after Houston's second preseason outing against the Raiders , head coach DeMeco Ryans spoke about Higgins' injury for the first time since the news was reported.
"Very unfortunate news with Jayden going down with the torn ACL. He'll be out for the year––and it hurts," Ryans said on Thursday night.  I feel like every time I've gotten up and talked, I've highlighted Jayden Higgins because of the work that he's done at OTAs, throughout training camp."
"He was one of our best players, if not arguably the best player on the field when he's been out there. So it's a significant loss for us. We've got a void to feel there, and it won't be easy to fill the void that Jayden is leaving behind.
Ryans isn't wrong. He has talked about and highlighted Higgins a ton throughout the Texans' offseason and training camp as one of their premier playmakers.
Back at OTAs, Ryans emphasized how much Higgins had taken advantage of the time he's had throughout the offseason, and made it clear he was due for a bigger role this season because of it.
"[Jayden] Higgins has done a really great job of taking advantage of the offseason," Ryans said of the second-year wideout in June. "Really coming back in shape. He's looking bigger, stronger, faster–– which is what you expect for a second-year player of his caliber."
"He's definitely taken advantage of it. I'm really excited to see what it's going to look like this season. I know he's going to have a really good year based on how he looks right now."
Higgins has been fully expected to take control of the Texans' WR2 spot on the depth chart on the opposite side of Nico Collins. The second-year pass-catcher, after a solid first season, had an extremely productive offseason where he looks both physically and technically refined compared to his 2025 self.
In 2025, Higgins played all 17 games to log 41 receptions, 525 yards, and six touchdowns, eventually turning into one of the Texans' more featured targets in the offense next to Collins and tight end Dalton Schultz.
However, that's now a player the Texans will be without for the foreseeable future. His 2026 campaign is over, really before it even started, and Houston will now be tasked with searching for answers as to what to do next within their wide receiver room.
Could that solution come via trade? Would a good fit be able to emerge from the free agent market? Will someone else already on the Texans' roster step up to the occasion?
Time will tell how the Texans attack their wide receiver room next , and who might become the team's second-leading pass-catcher at the position like Higgins was expected to be.

title: 3 Winners, 2 Losers From Texans' Second Preseason Game vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Houston Texans dropped their second preseason game of the year against the Las Vegas Raiders, 20-22, as a fourth-quarter comeback from the Raiders would end up stuffing this Texans team short of a win on their home field, and thus takes their preseason record to a whopping 0-2.
There was a lot to take away from this game for the Texans, though. Several offensive starters played in the first quarter , multiple big plays went down in the second quarter, and we saw many players' stock go up and down throughout who might be looking for a big role or a 53-man roster spot.
Let's break down three winners and two losers from the Texans' preseason loss to Las Vegas:
The Texans' starters that played on the offensive end––including Woody Marks––only appeared in one drive; a bit less than they were expected to play heading into the night. But part of that decision to cut things short might've been sparked because of the excellent drive seen from this scoring attack, really spearheaded by the efforts of Marks.
Marks carried the ball four times for 37 yards and caught a pass for eight yards, with his highlight play of it all stemming from his final carry of the night, which was a 20-yard touchdown run in the first quarter that really showcased his explosiveness and ability to make plays after contact.
4️⃣ punches it in for 6️⃣ 📺: @nflonespn pic.twitter.com/is4eFuTbDm
If Marks can continue to run as effectively and as efficiently as he did on Thursday against Vegas, it's going to be increasingly tough for the Texans to keep him off the field getting deeper into the regular season .
The Texans had to go out and bring in another quarterback this past week after Graham Mertz went down with a season-ending ACL tear in last week's preseason game. They landed on veteran free agent Brett Rypien , and in his first game with Houston, things didn't pan out exactly as ideally as he would've hoped.
Rypien completed 6 of his 10 passes throughout the night for a total of 44 yards, lost a fumble in the middle of the third quarter, and threw an interception in the final drive of the game. He was also sacked twice for a total of 16 yards.
Perhaps a slow start is to be expected for Rypien, considering he's been in the building for just under a week, but performances like that could very well be what prompts the Texans to go search for another quarterback to compete for that third spot on the depth chart.
There's no question that the Texans' biggest defensive play of the night came from rookie linebacker Wade Woodaz, who ran back an interception on Fernando Mendoza 80 yards for a touchdown in the Raiders' first offensive drive of the game, leading to an early 14-0 lead from Houston.
TEXANS PICK-6 ALERT 🚨 LVvsHOU on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/li2QM4hEah
For Woodaz, it was a play showcasing exactly why the Texans were first interested in him as a fourth-round pick back in April's draft: he's a playmaker on the defensive end with a combination of great size and speed that can be dangerous in the right situation.
If Woodaz can continue to keep up similar production and make big plays, you can expect him to be the one who places atop the leaderboard on the roster to land the Texans' LB3 spot on the depth chart by the time Week 1 rolls around.
The Texans, only playing Marks one drive and resting David Montgomery throughout the night, split their reps in the backfield between Owen Wright and Noah Whittington. Neither back was especially stellar, and that's especially so for Whittington, who had the least productive day of any runner on either side.
He tied the game-high for nine carries, but was last for yards per carry (outside of quarterbacks), with a total of 11 yards and 1.2 yards per attempt.
It's nothing to panic over as it relates to the Texans' running back room. Their top three options on the depth chart in Montgomery, Marks, and Jahwar Jordan either didn't play or barely played in this game. But for Whittington's stock as a fringe RB3/RB4 in this offense, a better performance could've made his roster security look a lot better right now.
The Texans rested all of their defensive starters on Thursday night, so it's not a surprise that the unit finished the game with a total of one sack. That won't be much of a normal sight in the box score once the regular season kicks off.
But that one sack the Texans did seek out was from their second-round selection from earlier this offseason, Kayden McDonald, who took down Fernando Mendoza for an 11-yard sack on the first play of the second quarter.
KMAC WITH THE SACK 😮‍💨 📺: @nflonespn pic.twitter.com/kOks1uMcrW
McDonald is looking to claw his way into more and more snaps within the Texans' defensive line rotation for his rookie season, and showing he can bring pressure on the quarterback from the interior is huge for any defensive tackle . So these types of plays show up in film, and might just help push his stock in the right direction.

title: Texans Linked to Trade for Patriots WR After Jayden Higgins Injury
full_text:
The Houston Texans could be due for an addition to their wide receiver room following the recent injury to second-year wideout Jayden Higgins.
During the Texans' joint practice with the Las Vegas Raiders earlier this week, Higgins suffered a torn ACL that will effectively end his 2026 season .
Texans WR Jayden Higgins suffered torn ACL in Tuesday's practice. (via @RapSheet ) pic.twitter.com/udrGmoaNND
The 2025 second-round pick was expected to be Houston's WR2 behind Nico Collins in what was set to be a big year for him individually. Instead, he sees his campaign come to an end before it even starts.
But with that sobering injury to Higgins in mind, the door is now open for the Texans to potentially add another target for C.J. Stroud within the next couple of weeks before the regular season, thus allowing this passing offense to not lose a step for the year ahead.
And already, one name––who's been in trade talks this offseason already––has emerged as a candidate that the Texans could consider for their recent questions at the position: New England Patriots wide receiver Kayshon Boutte.
According to NFL Network 's Ian Rapoport, the Texans stick out as a team that "makes sense" to trade for Boutte following the injury that Higgins suffered earlier this week.
Rap: Kayshon Boutte "makes sense" as a potential trade candidate for Texans following Jayden Higgins injury. pic.twitter.com/k9ukQcMIIM
Now, that doesn't mean the Texans have called the Patriots and their front office about the chance to trade for Boutte. However, the opportunity might be on the horizon here in the next few days if Houston were interested in an outside addition at wide receiver.
Boutte comes off a couple of strong seasons in New England, and now enters his fourth year pro after logging back-to-back 500-yard campaigns.
In 2025, Boutte played in 14 regular-season games en route to the Patriots' latest Super Bowl appearance, and collected 33 receptions, 551 yards, and six touchdowns.
While not exactly the same physical profile in terms of the size and speed that Higgins has––Boutte is 5-foot-11 while Higgins is 6-foot-4––the Patriots wideout does offer a few similarities to Higgins that could interest the Texans to make an acquisition.
He's a starting-quality pass-catcher, is only 24 years of age, is a solid threat in the red zone, and can be a wide receiver who's capable of lining up on the outside opposite of Nico Collins, even as a smaller plater at his position.
Right now, those outside wide receiver duties currently expected to be on the Texans' roster , other than Collins, will be left up to Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell , who still haven’t suited up for a preseason game, without a trade or a signing to bring in somebody else.
If Boutte were up for grabs for the right price, you can connect the dots on what Houston adds up to be a landing spot worth watching.
There is one wrinkle in the Boutte-to-Houston fit, as appealing as it might be on the surface.
That's Boutte's current contract situation, which, really, is part of the reason that the Patriots now have interest in trading him in the first place.
Boutte is in the final year of his rookie contract worth a little under $4 million in 2026. After this season, he'll be due to hit free agency and find a payday to come his way. And on a Patriots team that just signed Romeo Doubs and traded a first-round pick for A.J. Brown, that might not be the best roster to find that next contract with.
So the Patriots, if they didn't see any future plans involving him, could go out to trade him before this season. He's been placed in multiple trade rumors this offseason, and perhaps the Texans could be interested. But inevitably, they will be the ones tasked with paying him that next contract come 2027.
If Boutte were to be traded to the Texans, and he performed well, then a second contract might not be able to be ruled out. But once next offseason rolls around, Houston will have Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell also as free agents as-is. Nico Collins will also be due for an extension, and of course, C.J. Stroud will be as well if this season goes as planned for him.
Houston would be giving up assets in a trade for Boutte, have him in the building for at least one season, but could end up seeing him walk in free agency after one year.
Of course, that short-term fit can still work for this season , especially in a situation where Jayden Higgins is back healthy in 2027. But would the Texans be able to strike a deal for Boutte without giving up significant assets? Such a move could be easier said than done.
At the very least, Boutte's name should be on the radar of Texans' fans until the team finds a solution for their recent injury to Higgins.
He's become a consistent producer at the position for the past two seasons in New England, is still under 25 years old, and might be able to come in on a reasonable price to Houston to help alleviate the pressure that's recently emerged at wide receiver.
But that reasonable price point should be a factor that's emphasized. Because if the Texans don't envision a fit with Boutte past this season, trading noteworthy assets to the Patriots to acquire him could be a squeeze that's not worth the juice, and turning to another option might just make more sense.

title: 4 Winners, 3 Losers From Colts' Loss to Falcons: Rookie WR Stands Out
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts had little to write home about in their 34-6 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Saturday, but a handful of players did positively stand out.
The Colts had more losers than they did winners, with position groups as a whole being questioned throughout , so instead of touching on each individual who had an uninspired performance, we're narrowing it down to the team's three biggest losers.
Follow along as I break down each winner and loser of the Colts' brutal preseason loss against the Atlanta Falcons.
The Colts could have an all-star starting cornerback in Sauce Gardner, Charvarius Ward Sr., and Justin Walley, but don't sleep on Cam Taylor-Britt.
Taylor-Britt exited training camp as the de facto CB4 who can slide in at nickel or boundary cornerback if called up, and only continued that upward trajectory during the Colts' preseason loss to the Falcons.
He had four tackles (three solo) against Atlanta on Saturday, and his impressive run fits and sticky coverage looked exactly like each of the practices at Grand Park over the past few weeks of training camp.
Lou Anarumo welcomed Taylor-Britt back to defense after their years together with the Cincinnati Bengals, and it appears that
The Colts' kicking competition between veterans Blake Grupe and Spencer Shrader has taken a wildly interesting turn.
Grupe exited training camp as the clear favorite to win the team's starting placekicker job after he made 90% of his practice kicks, and Shrader just barely eclipsed a 70% rate.
It's felt like Grupe's job to lose, and after two preseason games, that reality may be setting in.
Spencer Shrader is now 4-for-4 on field goal attempts through two preseason games after going 2-for-2 with a long of 53 yards in the Colts' loss to the Falcons. On the other hand, Grupe missed a 36-yard attempt in the same game and now falls to 0-for-2 on such kicks during preseason play.
It'll be fascinating to see how STC Brian Mason decides to judge their overall performances, because Shrader's ability on gamedays may just give him the edge after all.
The Colts' last pick (7th-round, 254th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft, wide receiver Deion Burks, had an intriguing showing against the Atlanta Falcons.
Burks was viewed as a potential draft steal early on, but had been quiet throughout training camp. With Alec Pierce's extended absence opening the door for the Colts' wide receiver room, the hope was that Burks would shine brightly in an otherwise dark situation, but even with increased usage, he struggled to prove himself.
Against the Falcons, Burks had just four receptions for 19 receiving yards, but proved to be a reliable option regardless. There were also two penalties by teammates that hurt Burks' day: an offensive penalty that wiped out a strong first-down reception, and one on special teams that took back a strong kick return.
Burks didn't have an all-time statistical performance that suggests he's a lock for the team's final roster spot at wide receiver, but he still showed the biggest increase in stock of anyone on the roster.
Injuries and a new defensive scheme have prevented third-year linebacker Jaylon Carlies from establishing himself as a starting NFL linebacker, but so far throughout the preseason, and specifically as of recently, he's come along nicely.
Carlies exited Colts training camp on a high note , with consecutive practices as the defense's starting linebacker suggesting that an unforeseen emergence could be in order.
He had stacked strong practice performances throughout the last week of training camp, and particularly during the Colts' two-day joint practice with the Falcons , and looked to be a leader for the defense's opening at starting linebacker .
Carlies continued his newfound consistency on Saturday against the Falcons, leading the team with six tackles (five solo). Rookies CJ Allen and Bryce Boettcher have had moments of their own throughout training camp, but recently, it seems like Jaylon Carlies is earning a starting spot before our eyes.
The Colts have been betting on second-year defensive end Jaylahn Tuimoloau to take a massive step forward to earn the starting role opposite budding star Laiatu Latu.
Although Tuimoloau shined early in training camp, he has since been a mainstay reserve option. Veteran Arden Key has all but shored up the starting spot in question, and that's hardly due to his positive play, but rather because Tuimoloau has done nothing to suggest he's worth betting on as a first-time, full-time starter in his second season.
Tuimoloau has shown little to nothing in pass rush against backup pass protectors through two games of preseason play thus far, but it's his poor showing in run defense that is most concerning.
The Colts traded a 6th-round pick for cornerback Mekhi Blackmon during last year's preseason to bolster their cornerback room.
Blackmon started in eleven games for the Lou Anarumo's Colts defense in 2025 and had some promising moments throughout, but it's been a completely different story through two preseason games ahead of the 2026 regular season.
Blackmon had two coverage infractions against the New England Patriots in the team's preseason opener, and that continued in Saturday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.
He's clearly in his head at this stage of the preseason, which is bad for any professional athlete, but especially for an NFL cornerback. Teams are targeting him early and often through two preseason games, and such poor play begs the question: Will Mekhi Blackmon make the initial 53-man roster?
Colts' second-year quarterback Riley Leonard has been neck and neck with Anthony Richardson throughout the summer as they battle for the QB2 role behind Daniel Jones, but the two preseason games so far suggest that he's losing ground.
Richardson clearly outshined Leonard during the Colts' preseason opener against the New England Patriots last week, but this week was much different given that both quarterbacks struggled behind an atrocious offensive line.
Neither Leonard nor Richardson had a statistically promising showing against the Atlanta Falcons on Saturday, but the former especially struggled.
Leonard went 7-for-14 for 62 passing yards during his first-half run with the Colts' second-team offense, and for the most part looked lost against the Falcons.
He was given an opportunity to bounce back in a big way this week, but another lackluster showing suggests that he's slipping out of favor in the Colts' QB2 decision.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Colts Preseason Loss to Falcons: Depth Gets Questioned
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts were routed by the Atlanta Falcons 34-6 in their preseason matchup on Saturday.
It was the sloppiest, flattest performance of the preseason, and it has made me question whether their depth can hang if called upon during regular-season play in 2026.
The good news is that the Colts dominated the Falcons during their two-day joint practice at Grand Park earlier this week, which means their starting units definitely have some promise brewing for Week 1's arrival on September 13. However, if the Colts want to make any semblance of noise in the playoffs, their immediate depth will need to step up, and today's showing suggested otherwise.
Follow along as I break down my biggest takeaways from the Colts' uninspired preseason performance against the Falcons.
The Falcons were in complete control of today's game, totaling 461 yards of offense compared to Indy's 164. Lou Anarumo's defense isn't responsible for the offense's lack of production, but it didn't make matters easier.
Atlanta was 9-for-17 on third downs and averaged 6.7 yards per play against the Colts. Falcons QBs Cooper Rush and Jack Strand went a combined 22-28 for 297 passing yards, 1 passing touchdown, and 1 sack through the air.
The Colts entered the summer with a ton of unproven players at linebacker, but have since churned out a solid room from top to bottom. Rookie Bryce Boettcher and veteran Jaylon Carlies had some promising moments in Saturday's bout against the Falcons, and while the linebacker room as a whole didn't have many highlights, if any, they weren't the main reason for the defense's poor performance.
Lou Anarumo's second-team pass rush and secondary combined for a brutal day overall. Veterans CB Cam Taylor-Britt and DT Colby Wooden proved to be the strong backup options they've shown to be throughout training camp, but everyone else's performance said the opposite.
Second-year DE Jaylahn Tuimoloau and veteran CB Mekhi Balckmon were the biggest examples of this, as Saturday's showing made for back-to-back uninspired preseason performances.
The Colts have a ton to iron out before the regular season arrives, and determining the pecking order for their defensive depth chart now feels like a top priority.
The Indianapolis Colts’ backup offensive line largely featured the same unit from start to finish against the Falcons on Saturday, and their uninspired showing reaffirms how dire things look outside of their starting five.
No Jalen Farmer or Luke Tenuta played a role in such negative play, and quarterbacks Riley Leonard and Anthony Richardson struggled as a result. The pair of offensive signal callers had some lowlights on their own, but it was mainly the line’s poor play that caused such dysfunction.
Quality backup linemen are hard to come by in the NFL, but the Colts have been one of those teams in recent years with at least a couple of viable options available. Farmer and Tenuta have flashed as solid options, but outside of them, Indy is left praying that each of their starting five will start in all 17 games in 2026.
The Colts' kicking battle throughout training camp has become Blake Grupe's job to lose , and after two preseason games, Spencer Shrader has rebounded, making it an impossible decision.
Grupe has nailed 90% of kicks during training camp, while Shrader has barely eclipsed the 70% mark, but the preseason showings suggest the opposite trajectory.
In the Colts' preseason matchup against the Falcons on Saturday, Shrader nailed both of his field goal attempts (48 and 53 yards), while Grupe missed a 37-yard attempt wide right.
Shrader is now 4-for-4 on field goal attempts (long of 61) during preseason play, whereas Grupe is now 0-for-2.

title: Winners and Losers From Colts Joint Practices vs. Falcons
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts wrapped up their ninth and final training camp at Grand Park Sports Campus this week with two joint practices with the Atlanta Falcons.
The Colts performed like the better team throughout the two practices. Both sides of the ball racked up their fair share of wins against a Falcons team that is full of questions.
Here are the winners and losers from the joint practices.
Daniel Jones has been wildly impressive throughout training camp, and that continued against the Falcons this week.
Jones was a perfect 15-of-15 passing in Wednesday's practice as the Falcons had no answers for the Colts' passing attack. While he came back down to earth on Thursday, going 3-of-4 in 11-on-11 drills, Jones still led a scoring drive in a two-minute situation in the final period of the day.
It's hard to imagine what more Jones could have done during training camp. Indy's QB1 looks as sharp as ever, showing off pinpoint accuracy and a command of the offense. Jones is still less than nine months removed from tearing his Achilles, yet the injury seems like an afterthought at this point due to his level of play.
While Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward Sr. are the big names amongst the cornerback group, it has been Justin Walley who has made the most highlight plays. Walley continued his standout camp against the Falcons, battling with Pro Bowl wide receiver Drake London on numerous occasions.
While London made a highlight grab over Walley on Wednesday, the second-year cornerback responded on Thursday with a crucial pass breakup in 7-on-7 work and a would-be pick-6 in 11-on-11s. Walley's playmaking ability has become a regular occurrence in training camp, and the Colts believe it will translate to Sundays as well.
While Lou Anarumo has been rotating the linebacker group most of training camp, Jaylon Carlies was with the starting defense for both joint practices. Carlies had a strong showing in the preseason opener and continued to make plays against the Falcons .
Carlies came up with an interception of Michael Penix Jr. in 7-on-7s that fired up the defense. Carlies also made an impact as a blitzer, forcing Tua Tagovailoa into a few bad throws. The young linebacker is finally healthy and ascending at the right time, and it may lead to a starting role in the regular season.
If there was one area that the Colts struggled with against the Falcons, it was the running game . None of Jonathan Taylor, Seth McGowan, or Ulysses Bentley IV could find much running room behind the Colts' offensive line. The Falcons did a great job getting off of their blocks and meeting the Colts' running backs at or behind the line of scrimmage.
The Colts definitely have some things to clean up in their ground attack. It is hard to get a full read of the running game in practice when there is no tackling. Regardless, the Colts will need to be a threat on the ground with Taylor and the offensive line if the offense is to replicate last season's success.
Tyler Warren has been one of the standouts of training camp and was poised to continue his dominance against the Falcons' defense. Unfortunately for Warren, the Pro Bowl tight end slipped and injured his groin during a drill at the beginning of Wednesday's practice. Warren did not practice on Thursday as a result.
Fortunately, Warren seems to have escaped serious injury and is expected to miss only a week's worth of action. The Colts should have their tight end back and healthy for their Week 1 matchup with the Baltimore Ravens. Warren is expected to be a massive part of the Colts' offense this season and looks ready to ascend amongst the elite at his position.

title: Colts Could Have Their Starting Linebackers, and One Will Surprise You
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have officially concluded their 2026 training camp after their second joint practice with the Atlanta Falcons.
Plenty of storylines come to mind, but an interesting one is the situation at linebacker for Lou Anarumo's defense.
Indianapolis Colts on SI publisher Noah Compton was at the practices and noticed something interesting about this spot on the depth chart: Akeem Davis-Gaither and Jaylon Carlies appear to be the duo that Anarumo may go with as his starters for Week 1 against the Baltimore Ravens.
"Veteran linebackers Akeem Davis-Gaither and Jaylon Carlies conclude Colts training camp as defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo's starting duo in the middle of the field.
This makes back-to-back-to-back practices with them as the starters, and although Anarumo has been regularly rotating the room throughout training camp, their consistent placement on top of their strong play suggests this could be the Week 1 pair come September 13."
Back-to-back practices for LBs Jaylon Carlies and Akeem Davis-Gaither rolling with the #Colts starting defense. It’s been a constant rotation throughout training camp, but still worth noting.
Fellow rookie linebacker, Bryce Boettcher, also had a good training camp and even put together a solid performance in Indy's first preseason game of the year against the New England Patriots.
However, it looks like Davis-Gaither and Carlies are on track to start for Anarumo's defense against Lamar Jackson and the Ravens.
Indy's second-round investment, CJ Allen, missed nearly all of training camp with a hamstring injury. This caused him to get behind the eight ball, which opened opportunities for other linebackers like Carlies to shine.
While it isn't much of a surprise to hear that Davis-Gaither is on track to be a starter, the fact that Carlies has emerged as a candidate to join Davis-Gaither is.
Carlies showed some glimpses of a possible difference-maker during his rookie year in 2024. He played 10 games, logged 36 tackles and showed promise in pass coverage.
However, 2025 was a rough year for Carlies. He underwent shoulder surgery and followed that up with an ankle injury that sidelined him. He finished with just one tackle in three games.
Fast-forward to 2026 and Carlies didn't just make a full recovery from his ankle injury, but has apparently thrived in a way that few expected.
The assumption is that once Allen is up to speed, he'll be the starting linebacker next to Davis-Gaither. However, this was the opportunity that Carlies needed to display what he can do in Anarumo's defense.
Compton had this to say about Carlies and his performance through training camp.
He also briefly detailed how Davis-Gaither seamlessly transitioned into Anarumo's defense after spending five seasons with the defensive coordinator in Cincinnati (2020-2024).
"Carlies has really come on as of late, especially in pass coverage, with a strong day on Sunday trickling into the team's final practice, where he picked off Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr.
Davis-Gaither had been a steady hand throughout camp, with his familiarity within Anaurmo's defense from their days together in Cincinnati showing up on the field."
The linebacker position saw plenty of rotation, but it seems like Davis-Gaither and Carlies are currently the duo to start for Anarumo.
Anything can change, especially with the Colts still having two preseason games left before they kick off their regular season on September 13th.
We'll see how things pan out, but this isn't the duo I expected to be frontrunners to start at the defensive second level, especially Carlies.
