title: 5 Things to Watch as Rams Take on Saints in Preseason Week 2
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to play the New Orleans Saints in the preseason on Saturday. Following a win against the Kansas City Chiefs with several standout performances , there will be plenty to watch on Saturday. Here are five things to watch as the Rams take on the Saints in Week 2 of the preseason.
Last week against the Chiefs, rookie quarterback Ty Simpson impressed to say the least. He went 21-for-25 for 190 yards and two touchdowns. Simpson looked sharp and gained confidence with every throw. Now, against the Saints on Saturday, Simpson will need to show that he can follow that up with another strong performance.
If Simpson plays well against the Saints, it’s going to be difficult for the Rams to continue to justify having Stetson Bennett ahead of Simpson. If Simpson once again looks sharp, there’s a chance he overtakes Bennett for the backup quarterback role.
Following last week’s game against the Chiefs, running back Dean Connors instantly became a fan favorite . Connors caught two touchdowns and looks like someone who could push for the fourth running back spot on the depth chart.
While Connors was good as a pass catcher out of the backfield, he only averaged 3.7 yards per carry and needs to improve in pass protection if he’s going to push for a roster spot. Jarquez Hunter also looked good when he was on the field. Connors is likely a candidate for the practice squad, but many will be intrigued to see how he follows up last week’s performance.
The Rams got a good performance from their special teams unit last week. Harrison Mevis went 2-for-2 while Ethan Evans started to find his rhythm. The turning point in the game was arguably Xavier Smith’s 40-yard punt return to set the offense up with good field position. It may only be the preseason, but it will be nice to see some special teams consistency. If the Rams can carry that into the regular season, it will be a positive.
It’s never a bad thing when the head coach names you specifically in their press conference and that’s exactly what happened with safety Nick Andersen. McVay mentioned Andersen as someone who stood out on tape. Still, the defense was relatively quiet last week.
The Rams are looking for their “Dean Connors” on defense. Is that Wesley Bailey on the edge or Nikhai Hill-Green at linebacker? Al’Zillion Hamilton had a pass breakup last week, but an interception would go a long way. Fans are still waiting for their ‘preseason darling’ on defense, and the Rams need someone to step up.
It’s unlikely that the Rams play any of their key offensive line depth in this game. Keagen Trost strained his hamstring last week. However, the Rams still need to find some developmental options for the practice squad, especially if Alaric Jackson is suspended early in the season. That’s not to say that anybody playing on Saturday will eventually start this season, but finding some developmental options for the practice squad is needed.
Last week, this was a group that played well. Austin Blaske was a standout at guard and tackle. The Rams also got good tackle play out of Bryce Henderson. Things can typically get messy with the third and fourth-string offensive line, but they opened up lanes in the run game and kept Simpson clean against the Chiefs. If Blaske plays well again, the Rams may have found a developmental option at tackle.

title: Ty Simpson Can Force Rams’ Hand in Backup QB Battle With Strong Performance vs. Saints
full_text:
Throughout much of training camp, the Los Angeles Rams appeared to have a backup quarterback battle between Stetson Bennett and first-round pick Ty Simpson. However, while the media covered it like an active position battle, it became increasingly clear that the Rams didn’t view it that way at all.
The Rams have had an unconventional rotation at quarterback throughout the summer with Matthew Stafford practicing every other day. Still, on days in which Stafford didn’t practice, Bennett led the first-team offense while Simpson got the reps with the backups. When Stafford did practice, Bennett led the second-team and Simpson’s reps were more limited.
It was never a situation in which Bennett and Simpson were splitting the reps as the QB2. There was a clear pecking order and Bennett was in the lead. The priority for the Rams was bringing Simpson along at his own pace rather than focusing on an unnecessary position battle at the backup quarterback spot.
With that said, it may be a competition that the Rams can no longer ignore. During the preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs, there was a clear gap between Bennett and Simpson, and it wasn’t the one reflected on the depth chart. Simpson went 21-for-25 for 190 yards and two touchdowns while Bennett looked uninspiring in his two drives.
For much of training camp, the Rams could somewhat hide Simpson and Bennett from the national media and public eye. That was not the case after last Saturday’s preseason game against the Chiefs. If Simpson follows up that performance against the New Orleans Saints, it becomes increasingly difficult to justify keeping him behind Bennett.
This appears to be something on the mind of the Rams’ coaching staff as well. While the Rams have given Bennett all of the backup reps this offseason, that changed on Thursday. During Thursday’s joint practice , Bennett and Simpson split the backup reps. Bennett got 13 reps with the second-team offense while Simpson got 12.
After practice McVay was adamant that it was only because of a lack of available reps.
“It was exclusively because there were so many less reps,” said McVay. “Dave and I and the rest of the coaching staff will sit down and figure out how we want to approach the game once we're able to look at the film, but it was really more of a reflection of less reps and that's what that entailed.”
Even if it was due to a lack of reps, the Rams haven’t taken that approach all summer. It does seem notable as it is the first time since the start of training camp that the two have evenly split reps.
Nobody would have been surprised if Simpson had eventually surpassed Bennett by the end of the preseason. However, after the conclusion of training camp, it appeared that wasn’t going to be the case. The Rams consistently spoke glowingly about Bennett throughout camp.
Just as the Las Vegas Raiders’ tone has changed around Fernando Mendoza, the Rams’ tone has changed around Simpson. Throughout the entire draft process and majority of the offseason, the Raiders said that Mendoza wouldn’t play early in the season. Following the Raiders’ game on Thursday, head coach Klint Kubiak was not ready to name a starter.
Now, Simpson isn’t going to start over Stafford by any means. Still, McVay said on draft night that Simpson would compete with Bennett. Throughout camp, Bennett had been operating as the team’s backup quarterback . Heading into Saturday’s game against the Saints, that no longer appears to be as written in stone as it once was.
Simpson’s performance against the Chiefs was certainly encouraging . The rookie appeared poised and comfortable in the offense as he threw with confidence and accuracy. For the most part, his technique and footwork were sound. If he follows that up with a strong performance against the Saints, the Rams will have a problem that they will no longer be able to ignore.
“Even when you just say, ‘Alright, looking at last week, Ty did a great job. Stetson did what he could.’ I think it is important to be able to get a fair opportunity for those guys to run the offense with enough snaps,” said McVay. “But more than anything, it's just playing real live football for a guy that hasn't played a lot of it other than preseason games.”
Heading into the offseason, it made sense for the Rams to make Simpson earn everything. Given that Bennett had been in the offense for three years, it made sense to respect his experience and place on the team as well. He sat behind Jimmy Garoppolo for two years and deserved the opportunity.
However, Simpson’s upside might be too hard to ignore, especially if he’s showing that he can operate the offense. It may have only been a preseason game against backup and back-of-the-depth-chart players. That also doesn’t mean that the performance didn’t matter. Had Simpson thrown two interceptions instead of two touchdowns, the narrative would be much different.
Saturday will be a good test for Simpson. It’s one thing to play well in his debut, but can he build on that and follow it up with another solid game? If Simpson can do that, the Rams may have to seriously consider making him the backup quarterback behind Stafford.

title: Is Aaron Donald’s Uncertain Future Handcuffing the Rams?
full_text:
One of the biggest stories throughout training camp for the Los Angeles Rams has been whether Aaron Donald will return to the team. While the possibility seems increasingly likely, no official decision has been made. A timeline of Donald's potential return remains unclear.
The Rams would certainly welcome Donald back with open arms if he decided to return. However, as the team continues to wait, it also impacts their ability to make other moves and figure out how he works in the current defense.
That’s not to say that the Rams need to put a deadline on a Donald decision. Head coach Sean McVay has remained consistent in that Donald has earned the right to go through his process .
“I would love to be able to have all this stuff figured out, but like I told you guys from the beginning, he's earned the right,” said McVay on Thursday. “I know he's feeling good and I think he will continue to work out. I'm hopeful that we'll have some answers on that sooner than later.”
While the Rams will continue as is if Donald doesn’t return, the possibility somewhat handcuffs their ability to do anything until he decides. The Rams are currently facing potential suspensions to wide receiver Puka Nacua and offensive tackle Alaric Jackson. If either player is suspended, especially Jackson, the Rams will need to have the option of adding a player.
As it stands, the Rams would owe Donald $30 million in the case that he decides to return. It’s unlikely that Donald plays on $30 million, but the Rams also only have $15 million in cap space. There are things the Rams can do to open up cap space.
For example, the Rams could restructure Davante Adams’ contract to open up around $11 million. They just extended Kyren Williams last offseason, but restructuring his contract would open up around $6.5 million. That alone would give the Rams approximately $30 million, which would be enough to sign Donald and give them some space to work with during the season.
Being able to add Donald and a player like Taylor Decker at left tackle is unlikely. Cameron Heyward has a cap number of $23.5 million in 2026 at 37 years old. That wouldn’t be a crazy number for Donald despite being out of the league for two years. If Decker were to come back, he’d want starting left tackle money, which is at minimum $15 million and likely more. It would be very difficult for the Rams to do deals for both.
The Rams would certainly prefer Donald over Decker. With recent injuries to Laremy Tunsil, it’s possible waiting for Donald could result in the Rams missing out on a player like Decker . That’s arguably already been the case at wide receiver. Despite the Rams needing an experienced third wide receiver given Nacua’s situation, they have missed out on Stephon Diggs and Keenan Allen.
Pending Jackson’s potential suspension, it would certainly be disappointing if the Rams were to miss out on Decker because they’re waiting on Donald. Once Donald makes his decision and the structure of his contract is worked out, the Rams can see what flexibility they have to sign other players. Until then, their options are limited while they await Donald’s decision.
As McVay mentioned, Donald has earned the right to go through his process and ensure that his body is where it needs to be before making a decision. The Rams also aren’t going to put a deadline on him making that decision. If Donald wants to come back, the Rams will have him back whether that’s before Week 1 or in Week 15 for a playoff run.
While the Rams would like to have Donald on the practice field to start working in with the defensive line, it’s not something they’re going to force. Defensive coordinator Chris Shula may want to start figuring out how Donald fits in the defense and see how it looks. With that said, figuring out how to use Donald isn’t complicated.
When it comes to the situations around Nacua and Jackson, the Rams are unable to make a move in preparation for either situation until Donald’s decision is made. Despite the uncertainty around all three situations, getting Donald back would be the priority. Still, until Donald makes his decision official, the Rams are left operating with one hand tied behind their back.

title: How Likely Is a Suspension for Rams WR Puka Nacua?
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams get closer to Week 1, there is a lot of anticipation around whether wide receiver Puka Nacua will get suspended by the NFL. While the NFL a nnounced a handful of suspensions last week , Nacua was not among those included. However, that doesn’t mean that a suspension isn’t in the realm of possibility.
If the Rams were to be without Nacua, it would obviously be a huge detriment to the offense. A serious argument could be made that Nacua should have won the Offensive Player of the Year last season. He’s one of the best wide receivers in the NFL
Nacua has been under investigation by the NFL for actions that occurred on New Year’s Eve. The Rams wide receiver is currently part of a civil case in which he is alleged to have bitten a woman on the shoulder while intoxicated and then made an unprovoked antisemitic remark.
Earlier this week, Nacua’s trial for the civil case was set for March 2028. While the NFL typically allows for the legal process to play out before making a decision, it will likely rely on its own investigation to make a decision.
The fact that Nacua’s trial has been pushed to 2028 makes his case anything but straightforward. While Nacua has admitted to the bite, he says it was horseplay. The context around the bite is the question, which currently makes it a “he said, she said” situation.
Last week, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that it’s possible Nacua doesn’t play Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.
“Cases I believe are now being reviewed include that of the Rams’ wide receiver Puka Nacua,” said Schefter. “It's possible when the Niners and Rams play in Australia, it’s within the realm of options that Puka doesn’t play in that game.”
It really all comes down to what the NFL finds in its investigation. The NFL could interview witnesses of the incident to come to a conclusion. Even still, a lot of the information around the case is unverified. Yes, Nacua has admitted to the bite, and there is a photo.
However, Nacua’s attorney, Levi McCathren, has questioned the authenticity of the photo via the LA Times . “The marks look more like her back pressed against his face than an actual bite,” said McCathren.
During the incident, the woman alleged that Nacua yelled a provocative antisemitic remark. That is also unverified, as Nacua’s lawyer claims to have multiple witnesses who can vouch that he did not make the remark.
Earlier this year, the NFL closed its investigation into allegations made in a civil case involving Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice. The lawsuit alleged a pattern of physical violence, and Rice’s former girlfriend posted photos of the bruises. The NFL announced that there was insufficient evidence that Rice broke the Personal Conduct Policy after the woman signed an affidavit stating that the couple had a verbal argument, but he did not punch her.
Just because the NFL dismissed Rice’s case doesn’t mean they’ll do the same with Nacua . They are two different cases. However, both involve allegations made through civil lawsuits rather than criminal charges. That leaves the NFL to determine whether there is enough evidence to suspend Nacua through its own investigation. Any discipline imposed on Nacua would therefore come from the NFL based on its own findings.
It’s also worth looking at Jameis Winston’s 2018 incident , in which he inappropriately touched an Uber driver and made an unwanted sexual advance. The NFL investigation at the time found the driver’s account of the incident consistent and credible. Winston was suspended for three games.
Nacua getting suspended all comes down to what the NFL finds in its own investigation and whether it believes the context around the bite is credible. The NFL also doesn't have to make a decision before Week 1 .  If Nacua is suspended, the NFL could also look at the Rams wide receiver checking himself into rehab as a mitigating factor. That doesn’t mean that Nacua wouldn’t get suspended at all. However, his suspension could potentially be reduced from three games to two, or from two games to one, especially considering it would also be his first offense..
When it comes to the likelihood of Nacua getting suspended, it truly feels like a coin flip. The case is far from straightforward and it’s impossible to know what the NFL has found in its own investigation. Based solely on the information that is publicly available, it would be difficult to say that a suspension is more likely than not. Until that decision comes, the Rams will have to prepare for Week 1 knowing there remains at least a possibility that one of their best offensive players won’t be available.

title: Behind Enemy Lines: Getting to Know the Saints Ahead of Rams Preseason Matchup
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams held a joint practice with the New Orleans Saints on Thursday before the two teams go head-to-head in the preseason on Saturday. Before Saturday's game, we got together with Saints On SI publisher, Doug Joubert to answer some questions.
Saints players smile w hen you bring up Staley's scheme . Every one we've spoken to, from Cam Jordan to Kool-Aid McKinstry, has talked about how free they feel within his system. The defensive men speak about "flying to the ball" and "playing at full speed." Now in their second year playing in Staley's D, the players comment on how they are at the next step in the defensive installation: not thinking about what to do next, just do it.
Besides Chris Olave, fresh off a new contract extension, and #3 receiver Devaughn Vele, a big-bodied possession type of receiver, draft picks Bryce Lance (who sat out last week due to some training camp bumps and bruises) and Barion Brown have shown the most promise through camp. Both Brown and Lance can fly, but they have both shown promise on crossing routes. However, they truly are stretch-the-field kind of guys. Tyson and Shough were really starting to gain a connection through camp. Both credit a Summer trip to San Diego to visit with Hall of Fame quarterback Drew Brees, who walked them (along with a few other offensive players) through what he would do to get ready for a season. There is no doubt Shough will miss Tyson's athletic abilities . However, there is no question that Shough is the starting QB. The race right now is for who will be 2nd string: last year's beginning-of-the-year starter Spencer Rattler or former overall 2nd pick in the 2021 draft Zach Wilson.
Shough has looked sharp. Against a solid #1 Cowboys defense on Tuesday, he was able to toss a pair of touchdowns and some beautiful touch passes when a receiver split a sideline zone. He seems to have a true feel for Moore's offense, doesn't second-guess himself, and shows a confidence that belies only being in the league for two years. Now, he is 26-years old (turning 27 in late September), so that is a factor. Saints fans are ready for his next step in the process of being the team's starting quarterback. They were tired of the "quarterback-du-jour" system since Brees retired. When Shough led the pre-game huddle on the field (even though he was not playing in the game and was dressed down), the Superdome fans went bananas.
No doubt the two we're looking at closely are the aforementioned wide receiver position and running backs. With Tyson out for an undetermined amount of time as of this writing, the battle for the #3 and 4 slot will be hot and heavy. We're expecting six wide receivers to be kept on the final 53-man roster, one of which we'll talk about next.
Wide receiver Bub Means. He was drafted by the Saints in the 5th round in 2024, but injuries have sidelined him for most of his young career. In preseason game #1 last week, Means was the highest-graded receiver by PFF and the 2nd highest-graded run blocker, only behind starting tackle Asim Richards. Means is considered a bubble candidate , even with the injury to Tyson, but his play against Jacksonville has definitely moved his meter.

title: Which Raiders WRs Can Step Into Bigger Roles This Season
full_text:
Wide receiver has been a problem for the Las Vegas Raiders for the last year or so.
The team does not have many proven options on the perimeter. If Las Vegas wants to have success passing the football, it will have to come from the tight end position for now.
Klint Kubiak is an intelligent offensive mind, but he can only scheme so much without the talent to scare opposing defenses. The team has not had much success passing the football during the 'meaningful' preseason snaps, something he wants to change.
Who will step up in the wide receiver room? Whoever it is, it needs to happen fast.
The most obvious answer would be Jalen Nailor, the big-money free-agent signing who had a defined role as a depth receiver with the Minnesota Vikings. However, Nailor hasn't had many opportunities as a top receiver, so we don't know what he'll look like in this role.
Nailor is undoubtedly talented, improving his hands during his years in the NFL and beating defenders with his speed. Kubiak should have a role for him one way or another, but the team would like it if he isn't limited as a pass-catcher.
The best-case scenario is that Nailor becomes worth the money the team is paying him, and he breaks out in a big way, expanding his route tree and becoming a serious threat to defenses in more ways than one. That hasn't happened yet, but the season hasn't started.
It wasn't the rookie season Jack Bech expected, but a new offensive system and better quarterback play should elevate the talent that made him a second-round pick last year.
Bech has impressive route-running ability and ball skills, but he wasn't able to show those off last season due to the poor offensive infrastructure. The Raiders are banking on him to take a step forward in the offense, which would be a big boost for their passing game.
The Raiders would love it if Bech developed into a true X-receiver, because it would take attention away from Brock Bowers. Somebody needs to step up in that room, and Bech is a prime candidate.
There are no sure things in Las Vegas' wide receiver room, so someone will have to come out of nowhere.
Rookie Malik Benson has gotten some shine during training camp, and he's collected three receptions for 44 yards through two preseason games. His speed and big-play ability make him a prime candidate to be a serious threat in the passing game.
Tre Tucker, who enters his final season on his rookie contract, also figures to be a consistent presence again. It may earn him a second contract with the Silver and Black.
The Raiders would love it if Dont'e Thornton Jr. could provide more in his second season than in his rookie year, as he has the height, weight, and speed to be a serious threat in the passing game.
Las Vegas needs help in the passing game, or this offense won't get off the ground. We will see who steps up when the season kicks off.

title: Raiders Training Camp Report 24: Finishing Strong for the Future
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders are coming down the stretch toward the finish of 2026 training camp, and to use an old Vegas adage, “The price of poker is going up,” with just three practices left.
GM John Spytek has given Raider Nation genuine hope in how he is undertaking the franchise's reformation and attacking the future.
This Raiders rebuild is built on proven football intelligence, long-term thinking, and thorough strategy.
Klint Kubiak was the clear choice for this job through the prism of what Spytek wanted, and after the team’s critical second preseason game versus the Houston Texans, he let the fans in on his thinking as it relates to all things Raiders.
Going against a team that all reasonable parties see as an NFL playoff-caliber franchise, and many see as a Super Bowl contender, can either make or break a team. It was a highly productive three days, and Kubiak agreed.
"Oh yeah. Well, I'm so glad we got the practice against them. That was really important for our team to spend that time in Houston and get some really good work against a different scheme and a really good coaching staff."
"Caleb Rogers in particular, he just needs to continue to get reps as a young player to improve. He has all the talent that you're looking for. We’ve just got to keep getting him better. I like how he works, like the kind of teammate that he is, and he has a bright future ahead of him."
DE Maxx Crosby is an elite player, an unblockable force of nature who wreaks havoc on everything he touches on the football field. So, does Kubiak see him taking his first action all preseason versus the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday? Here’s a hint: No!
"I think all players need the reps. I'm not going to be giving him any though."
Aidan O’Connell has suffered more than any other player from the inconsistency and instability of this franchise over his career. Kubiak understands this, values the asset that Aidan O’Connell is, and thinks it is time for others to follow suit.
Coach Kubiak: "That's a great point. I think we've said all offseason how much we value Aidan [O'Connell], and what a heck of a second half. He goes out and leads us to 19-point half and two 90-plus yard drives in the fourth quarter. He did it with his teammates, but he was a big part of it and was very happy for him."
I projected in my last 53-man roster article that the Silver and Black will keep 10 defensive backs. Four safeties and six cornerbacks. I still feel that way, and with 60% of those ten being young players (rookies, first- or second-year), and four of them (40%) being actual rookies, Kubiak understands the youth movement he is leading.
That said, he sees the strides made in Houston and a promising future ahead.
“As far as the secondary, overall, as a defense, I thought we took a step forward last night. I think we’ve got a lot of good work in the joint practice covering some new guys, and those guys need another game under their belt against San Francisco to continue to get better."
NFL executives swooned over Fernando Mendoza coming out of Indiana in the last NFL Draft, and he is even more impressive today than he was then. No one in this organization, on or off the record, has done anything but appreciate him or his skill set.
With that, Kubiak knows he is only in the early stages of his career, is mature beyond his age, and is getting better after a tough game in Houston.
"I think if you sat in our quarterback meeting the night before the game, listened to him go through his progressions and reads and adjustments, I was very impressed with how prepared he has made himself. That whole quarterback room, led by Coach [Mike] Sullivan and Andrew [Janocko], have done an excellent job of being prepared. I was pleased with watching the tape."
"I really like what he did on third down. We were only one of five on third down in the first half. However, we did drop the ball twice, and we threw one short of the sticks on third-and-long. He had really good ball placement on the first third down of the game with a guy in his face. So, in the critical downs, I thought he was playing his best. There are things that we must get corrected that will be addressed ASAP."
Kubiak has a vision from the field as a head coach, but as a film junkie, a lot stands out on tape that you can’t see from the field. So I asked him, after watching the film, what he noticed that maybe didn't stand out from the field.
"Well, resilience. The resilience sticks out because we shot ourselves in the foot. We had nine penalties, five on special teams. The first half was atrocious."
"We started slow on both sides of the ball, and in the NFL, it's all about winning the game. And so, we gutted it out and found a way to win, and that's how this whole season's going to be. All these games come down to the wire, and you get to learn a lot about players in practice, but you learn a whole lot more, and when the live bullets are flying in a game, and I learned a lot about guys in a good way last night."
One mantra of the Raiders organization this offseason is the need for the defense to get the ball back not just through stops, but through takeaways. In Houston, they had two strip sacks and two takeaways. Kubiak addressed that and assessed his defense as well.
"As a team, being plus one in the turnover margin, that's how you win games. So, with Rob [Leonard] taking it away, with our offense protecting the ball, that's how you win. You've obviously got to score, but you've got to, you got to win the turnover battle. That was a huge part of the game."
I have maintained, since before training camp, the importance of getting young players reps. As camp progressed and you transition to the regular season, there are fewer and fewer reps for young players not on the first string.
Kubiak pulled back the curtain on the reality of reps getting cut, and getting his rookie QB and other young players quality reps as they tighten up now.
"Yeah, it's a great point, and as to God's honest truth, you're right. We have experience as coaches on developing guys when they're not starting a game if they don't start a game. So, it's staying early, leaving late. It's using some technological tools at your disposal, but it's really a lot of Coach [Mike] Sullivan spending some early mornings and long nights with Fernando [Mendoza] and Aidan [O'Connell]."
"But then you can build in young guy reps into your practices. There are things you can do. It's never as good as getting all the reps in practice, but you do the best you can with what you got."
Fernando Mendoza is coming from a completely different offensive scheme at Indiana, and one thing people wondered about him in the NFL is the game-defining pre-snap read that separates the good from the bad. Kubiak didn’t mince words when evaluating the rookie.
"Yeah, well, he got us a penalty on the second play of the game. I was not happy with the cadence, so we've got to get better there."
I have said that since they signed QB Kirk Cousins, barring a trade offer that makes it mandatory that they move him, the team is expected to carry three QBs on the 53-man roster. I detailed it in my pre-training camp roster position preview. Kubiak discussed it in detail on Friday.
"Those guys are going to make us make hard decisions, which is a great thing, that competition. We're talking through it. It's part of the discussion."
"Yeah, it helps a lot. These game reps are the most valuable ones that we can use. It's not just the defensive tape, but how they're performing on special teams, because so many guys in those positions have to prove their worth on teams. Guys that we can trust. So, it was very helpful for many guys."
Kubiak is a blunt truth-teller who holds everyone to the standard he holds himself to, and coaches to. He won’t tolerate a lack of discipline and stupid unforced penalties. He hasn’t been thrilled to see so many (nine versus Houston) and wasn’t afraid to call anyone and everyone out. How do you fix…

title: What Anusiem IR Status Means for Raiders Going Forward
full_text:
For a second consecutive season, the Las Vegas Raiders have sustained an injury to a defensive back on their roster who served as a depth piece. Las Vegas had an impressive come-from-behind victory against the Houston Texans on Thursday, but it came at a cost.
Las Vegas improved after a week in Texas, but they also have decisions to make. The Raiders' trip to Texas confirmed areas they must improve on the field. Yet, Las Vegas was forced to make a roster move following what was otherwise a positive and productive trip to Houston.
The Raiders battled back from a double-digit deficit to beat the Texans . However, late in the game, cornerback Chigozie Anusiem suffered a lower-body injury after being dragged down from behind on a punt. He was recently placed on injured reserve, ending his 2026 season.
Over the next few weeks, Las Vegas will continue developing the cornerbacks on the roster. They will also make a coinciding move, with cornerback possibly being the focus. Still, Las Vegas cannot sustain injuries to an unproven group of cornerbacks , with the season just weeks away.
There are two sides to Anusiem's injury. On one hand, he played zero snaps on defense for the Raiders last season, while playing 13% of the team's special teams plays. He was listed on Las Vegas' most recent depth chart behind rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses.
He was likely to be featured again in a reserve role this upcoming season and may have been on the roster bubble with cutdown day fast approaching. Making the practice squad was likely his best bet. Still, the Raiders' secondary is the biggest question mark the team has heading into the 2026 season. Anusiem's injury may not amount to much.
However, as the unit continues to put the pieces together, it is clear that this process will take well into the regular season. Cornerback is a position the Raiders cannot take any more losses at, as it is already the team's most significant weakness. Still, they continue to look to improve as a unit.
“As far as the secondary, overall, as a defense, I thought we took a step forward last night. I think we’ve got a lot of good work in the joint practice covering some new guys, and those guys need another game under their belt against San Francisco to continue to get better,” Kubiak said following Thursday’s win over the Texans.

title: How Few Things (Currently) Set in Stone for Kubiak's Raiders
full_text:
After an offseason full of changes, offseason programs, and training camp, the Las Vegas Raiders' coaching staff plans to take every bit of time allotted to them to put the finishing touches on their roster. As the final preseason game approaches, Klint Kubiak and the Raiders are just getting started.
Despite several notable roster additions on both sides of the ball, Las Vegas entered the offseason with too many roster holes to adequately fill in one offseason. They have spent weeks of practice implementing their new roster and coaching staff additions, while further developing their reserves.
As the Raiders look to turn things around in 2026 and beyond, they will need players at all levels of the depth chart to step up. Las Vegas will depend heavily on the sizeable roster additions it made, but will equally need the depth on the roster ready to contribute when needed.
Week 1 is right around the corner, and aside from center, left tackle, tight end, running back, and punter, most positions on the field have significant questions that remain. There will be plenty of opportunities for players looking to earn a roster spot or additional playing time.
The Raiders used their practice and preseason game against the Houston Texans to get a better look at the players further down on their depth chart. With cutdown day approaching, Kubiak noted that resting their starters against Houston was part of the coaching staff's plan all along.
“Yeah, that was the plan all along. When we have those joint practices, they get so many reps that joint practice is the game and the guys understood that going in and that's how we decided to play it," Kubiak said the day after the game.
A 17-point comeback win orchestrated nearly solely by reserve players gave Las Vegas' coaching staff a quality look at the players they have to choose from this season. The Raiders' preseason games will be the best chance for many of those players to earn a roster spot.
Las Vegas has answered many of the questions they faced heading into the offseason. Yet, many more have arisen since. Still, Kubiak and his staff plan to take their time working through the roster-building process. Soon, though, tough decisions will be made.
Over the past few months, the Raiders' moves have confirmed that they have a detailed plan in mind for every aspect of their rebuild. This is especially the case for Kubiak's first season at the helm, as Las Vegas is determined to build a more competitive team from the ground up.
In just under two weeks, the Raiders will begin trimming down their roster. Although a handful of positions have been figured out and several more appear to be, Kubiak believes that refusing to name starters, even at positions where starters are clear, benefits the team as a whole.
"I just don't think it ever benefits a player to know that they've have a spot secured, and if there's always a little bit of uneasiness about that, that benefits the whole team, the player and the team,” Kubiak said.
“And as far as the secondary, overall, as a defense, I thought we took a step forward last night. I think we’ve got a lot of good work in the joint practice covering some new guys, and those guys need another game under their belt against San Francisco to continue to get better.”
The Raiders have shown improvement with each practice in training camp and seem to show the most improvement after each preseason game. With one more exhibition matchup remaining before the regular season, Kubiak and the Raiders continue to put in the work on and off the field.
Soon, Las Vegas will take the field for their first regular-season game of the Kubiak era. Until then, the Raiders will take each day to improve in the different areas they have struggled in during practice and the preseason. The depth chart will naturally work itself out from there.
The Raiders are gaining further clarity about the roster that was quickly revamped over the offseason. With a need for further development still apparent, it will be interesting to see how the Raiders' roster and depth chart shake out later this month.

title: Raiders Still Working Through All Levels of QB Competition
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders added two quarterbacks to the roster this offseason with a plan in mind to start veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. They were forthcoming about their plans to develop Mendoza behind Cousins until further notice.
Yet Klint Kubiak has been equally adamant that there is competition at nearly every position on the roster and that there is a legitimate quarterback competition. Tuesday's practice and Thursday night's preseason game against the Houston Texans added credence to that notion.
Signing Cousins and drafting Fernando Mendoza, while also having veteran quarterback Aidan O'Connell still on the roster, solidified the position group. Las Vegas is more set at quarterback entering the 2026 season than they have been since at least the 2023 season.
Las Vegas has position battles going on at several positions on both sides of the ball. Yet, all eyes are on the Raiders' quarterbacks. Not only is it the most critical position on the field, but it is also the one position Las Vegas has had the most instability at in recent seasons.
During training camp and the team's first two preseason games, each of Las Vegas' quarterbacks has had bright moments. Kirk Cousins has shown an early understanding of Kubiak's offense. The veteran quarterback led an efficient opening touchdown drive in Las Vegas' first preseason game.
Mendoza has played generally well in practice. The rookie had a solid first preseason game and a rocky second ; both games showed his long-term potential. O'Connell led the Raiders to a 19-0 second-half run against the Texans on Thursday, staking his claim in the battle.
As the Raiders head into their final preseason game, a home matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, they are still trying to decide who will start at quarterback in Week 1. After acknowledging that the starting position is Cousins' to lose last week, Kubiak recently explained further.
"We got another week, we're playing. I don't anyone to be comfortable in their job. It should always be that way from all positions. We'll just keep going forward," Kubiak said following Thursday night's comeback win over the Texans, when asked about the Raiders' starting quarterback battle.
All three quarterbacks provide something different. Cousins provides experience in various offenses and prior history with Kubiak and Andrew Janocko. Mendoza possesses the best arm of the three quarterbacks; O'Connell is a solid backup quarterback in the National Football League.
Following Thursday night's win, Kubiak shared his thoughts on the position group, noting how well Mendoza and the other Raiders signal callers have prepared ahead of practices and preseason games.
“I think if you sat in our quarterback meeting the night before the game, listened to him go through his progressions and reads and adjustments, I was very impressed with how prepared he has made himself,” Kubiak said.
“That whole quarterback room, led by Coach [Mike] Sullivan and Andrew [Janocko], have done an excellent job of being prepared. I was pleased with watching the tape. I really like what he did on third down."
The Raiders' 17-point comeback win over the Texans may have only been a preseason victory, but it was Kubiak's first as a head coach, and it was largely led by the Raiders' offense. The 19-point second half was a sign of what the Raiders hope to be able to do regardless of who is at quarterback.
Kubiak was hired for his ability to create and sustain productive offenses. It will take further development at the quarterback position to ensure that happens. If Thursday was any indication, Las Vegas has the potential to stay afloat with any of the three quarterbacks on their roster.
Following their win over the Texans, Kubiak put his first win as a head coach into perspective. His father, Gary Kubiak, is the Texans' all-time winningest head coach.
“It means a lot to our team, you know? We needed to have that game, especially after that first half. Seen flashes of that from our guys in practice. For them to go do it on a Thursday night game, that's very rewarding to see those young men play their hearts out in the second half," Kubiak said.

title: Raiders Mailbag: Expectations and Identity of the Franchise
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The most important week of the Las Vegas Raiders' entire offseason is this coming week, and there is plenty to talk about.
The third and final preseason game is Thursday night at Allegiant Stadium against the San Francisco 49ers, and the next three days will feature the most important practices of camp.
A lot is on the line in this Raiders' rebuild, including the battle for the few remaining roster spots and the molding of Klint Kubiak’s first 53-man roster, which will be unveiled in exactly one week.
With that in mind, via social media, I asked Raider Nation to sound off on the franchise, and in a big way, you did.
So let’s dig into some of those sentiments and answer some of your questions.
Simple Uncle Hondo, who are we? What is our identity on either side of the ball?
There were so many terrific comments, but none stood out to me more than this one.
In my seven years, I have learned that for this fan base, being a Raider is not merely fandom; it is a way of life.
This is a franchise that, for the first time in decades, is showing restraint, discipline, and a true commitment to excellence that is not just words but action.
2026 is a rebuilding year. They will take their lumps with young coaches and players making young coaches' and players’ mistakes.
They expect and will demand improvement with zero compromise, but understand every mistake this season is a lesson learned that won’t need to be repeated in 2027.
2027 will add free agents and multiple NFL Draft picks for a “get right” year, setting the foundation for a 2028 season in which they expect a playoff berth and, subsequently, to be a contender.
When you clearly delineate those expectations, you will see each loss and mistake of 2026 as a seed for future success, and not as mere mediocrity, as in the past, or as futility. When you understand the scope of what this season is, you will be able to enjoy it as the laying of a foundation, and not merely as a one-year campaign.
DEFENSE GETTING CONSISTENT PRESSURE ON THE QB
This is a sentiment many fans share. Rob Leonard was widely seen across the NFL as one of the rising defensive position coaches ready for a shot at being a coordinator.
As a first-year DC, he will have a learning curve, as will Klint Kubiak in the head-coaching chair.
But the reality remains that the defensive line is far from what it will look like in 2028, when they expect to be a perennial playoff team, and of the projected 10 defensive backs (four safeties, six cornerbacks), four are rookies, one is a sophomore, and the third is entering his third year.
I disagreed with not playing the starting defense (minus Maxx Crosby, Nakobe Dean, and Quay Walker) versus the Texans, but that was a Klint Kubiak call.
Only one starter played in that game, in which the Silver and Black defense gave up just 13 points to a team many feel is a Super Bowl contender.
While the Raiders' defense is far from a finished product, it is not as bad as some make it out to be, and the sky is not falling.
GM John Spytek offers genuine and tangible hope, and you must understand that he will not make long-term sacrifices for superficial glory. He is playing chess and thinking strategically in the long term, so don’t sacrifice that for temporary pleasure that could hurt the future.
Hurting the future salary cap by giving away assets or capital for a 2026 win that takes one away from 2028 is not only useless; it is also counterproductive, and the Raiders are no longer shooting themselves in the proverbial foot.
Who are the @Raiders going to pick with their top 5 pick in next year's draft
Simply put, the Raiders aren’t taking shortcuts this year, and the more losses they get, the more they set the stage for success in the 2027 NFL Draft.
A year before they took him, I told you they were targeting TE Brock Bowers. Same with QB Fernando Mendoza last year, and I have reported many times that they covet Ohio State Buckeyes WR Jeremiah Smith next year.
I covered Calvin Johnson in Detroit, and I can tell you the NFL sees Smith as a generational talent like Johnson and Larry Fitzgerald.
Imagine every loss this year getting you closer to pairing your prized rookie QB that NFL executives loved with a generational WR1 in Smith in 2027.
Don’t lose sight of a Mendoza-to-Smith connection, and you will sleep better with every loss and learning curve of 2026.

title: Raiders Game Review: Key Takeaways From Thursday's Comeback Preseason Win
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders followed up their sluggish preseason debut with a dramatic come-from-behind victory against the Houston Texans, 22-20. It was a wild game that featured notable individual displays from key players and important evaluations for the Raiders' young roster.
Klint Kubiak has his first unofficial win as the Las Vegas Raiders head coach, while his No. 1 draft pick, quarterback Fernando Mendoza , showed signs he could be on the field much sooner than we realize. I spent time re-watching the Raiders' victory, and I'm here to share my key takeaways from Thursday night's triumph. Let's take a look.
This was not the best performance for the 2026 No. 1 overall draft pick, as Mendoza went 8-of-15 for 86 yards, a pick-six, was pressured numerous times, and took a sack after miscommunication from the left guard and center on how to block Kayden McDonald.
This was an important game for Mendoza’s evaluation process. Against a well-coached Texans defense that has always featured excellent depth, he attacked all three levels of the field and displayed the remarkable poise and toughness that were key to winning the Heisman Trophy and the National Championship last season.
There are some plays he would like to have back, including the pick-six to Texans linebacker Wade Woodaz, but it was a fairly impressive display, by my account, on second look. Let’s go back to the interception—Mendoza made the right decision attempting to check down to Mike Washington Jr., who had initially sat in the middle of the field.
As Mendoza was in his throwing motion, Washington began moving to his right, making it look as though the quarterback was late to the middle of the field, which is a big no-no for passers, especially with the tight confines in this area of the gridiron. I loved that the arm arrogance was on display again, as he was ripping some throws to the intermediate and deeper portions.
Mendoza needed to learn how to take hits in the pocket, and the Texans were the perfect opponent for that. This game showed why there’s a preference for Kirk Cousins to play early in the regular season over Mendoza, but don’t be surprised if we see the Raiders change their stance.
Whew, buddy, we have a live one at running back. Raider Nation should be excited about what they have seen of Washington for the last two preseason games, as the fourth-round rookie from Arkansas is showcasing what could make him a standout running back in the NFL.
I liked how he followed his blockers only to accelerate and get to the sideline with burst and physicality. He was lowering his shoulder and delivering hits, displaying awesome contact balance and leg churn to create extra yards after contact. While Washington is not Derrick Henry, the running style is nearly identical in a smaller frame.
The Raiders need to find a way to consistently rotate Ashton Jeanty and Washington this season; this duo has the chance to be a special one that teams will struggle to defend and tackle.
I came away impressed with Rogers, who had a sound game at right guard. He is in a competition with Jackson Powers-Johnson for the starting job, and with JPP absent in this game, Rogers did what he needed to do to make the conversion a difficult one for Kubiak.
I liked how well Rogers was getting his hands fit and punching with timing and accuracy at the point of attack. His pass sets were steady, and there was sufficient leg drive in the run game. When he wasn’t dealing with a responsibility in pass protection, he was always looking for work and helping out right tackle Trey Zuhn III.
There were moments when Rogers was in stalemates, and his leverage could’ve been better in any facet. Again, this was impressive tape to watch, and another good showing next week could help earn him the Week 1 gig at right guard.
The Raiders' second-round draft pick from Arizona looked like a seasoned veteran on Thursday night.
On his first impactful play of the game early in the first quarter, Treydan Stukes was aligned as a split-high defender and showcased incredible instincts to quickly jump the crossing pattern by the tight end on the Texans, then displayed his closing speed to the ball carrier when CJ Stroud checked the ball down to Xavier Hutchinson, resulting in a physical tackle for loss.
It feels like Stukes has grown a lot since the early portion of camp, which is an encouraging sign as he looks for significant playing time early this season.
It is hard for me to imagine the Raiders and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard keeping guys like Stukes, with his closing speed, athleticism, high-end instincts, and playmaking ability off the field. He aligned at free safety and nickel at multiple points against Houston, and that versatility could make him a chess piece for Las Vegas’s defense this fall.

title: Why Raiders' Offensive Line Must Take Shape in 2026
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' offensive line must improve significantly before the team even thinks about being in the postseason.
The Raiders have had one of the worst offensive lines in the league over the last few seasons, whether due to injuries or to players not adapting to the scheme. No matter the case, the level of play has been inexcusable.
That's why legendary offensive line coach Rick Dennison was hired to join Klint Kubiak's staff. Dennison is a multiple-time Super Bowl-winning coach, and Kubiak just helped the Seattle Seahawks win a title because of how efficiently they ran the football.
General Manager John Spytek took a major swing during free agency, signing center Tyler Linderbaum to a three-year, $81 million contract, making him the highest-paid interior offensive lineman in NFL history. The Raiders hope Linderbaum's elite play can stabilize the interior.
The team also gets Kolton Miller back healthy after he missed most of the 2025 season due to injury. The Raiders allowed more than 60 sacks and couldn't run the ball to the left side in his absence.
Miller and Linderbaum are the only Raiders with guaranteed starting spots on this offensive line. Right tackle DJ Glaze is penciled in as the starter as of now, but competition always pops up, so we won't know until Week 1.
Las Vegas has two intriguing second-year players in Caleb Rogers and Charles Grant, who both played sparingly in their rookie seasons. Rogers is fighting for a starting role, while Grant could also see more action in 2026.
Third-round rookie Trey Zuhn III has been impressive in the preseason, and he is challenging for a starting spot. Zuhn played center and tackle at Texas A&M, but he is most likely to play guard for the Raiders.
These players are the most intriguing offensive linemen on the team, and they will most likely make up the starting lineup. Others have the chance to be swing tackles and provide quality depth.
Outside of Miller and Linderbaum, the Raiders' offensive line is full of unknowns. Kubiak, Dennison, and the Raiders' entire offensive staff have work to do to determine who will play the most.
The rest of the offense depends on it. The Raiders are beginning a new era under Kubiak and a revamped offense that shows a lot of promise. The trenches must be improved.

title: Why Mendoza's Pick-Six Response What Raiders 'Expect'
full_text:
Thursday night was an up-and-down experience for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in the Las Vegas Raiders' 22-20 win over the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium.
During his postgame press conference, head coach Klint Kubiak spoke on Mendoza's outing and what he needs to learn moving forward.
Could the No. 1 overall pick have been better on Thursday night? Absolutely. The interception was a poor throw and decision by Mendoza, but some circumstances need to be taken into account when fairly assessing his performance.
In one half of action, Mendoza completed 8-of-15 passes for 86 yards and one interception. On the surface, that looks like a very disappointing performance. However, two things contributed to Mendoza's and this offense's overall struggle to gain any traction.
First, Las Vegas started its second-unit offensive line against the majority of the Texans' starting defense. It was quickly apparent that the protection up front was out of its depth against one of the league's deepest defenses. Mendoza was under duress countless times on Thursday night, forcing him to abandon the play and throw the ball into the sidelines to avoid a sack. Secondly, Malik Benson had two costly drops that would have extended drives.
Overall, Mendoza could have played better , but more importantly, he continues to show development in playing from under center, and his arm talent, anticipation, and pre-snap recognition are above average. Right now, signs point toward Kirk Cousins opening the season as the starting quarterback, but Mendoza could start games at some point this season.
Regardless, if you're a Raiders fan, your confidence in Mendoza and the direction of this organization shouldn't waver based on what transpired on Thursday night. Given that Houston's defense is elite and the rookie quarterback played with the second-unit offense, excluding Jalen Nailor, I'm not concerned in the slightest about how he played in his second career preseason game.

title: How Raiders' Mendoza Can Use Struggles to Advantage
full_text:
Fernando Mendoza and the Las Vegas Raiders were having a solid opening drive against the Houston Texans on Thursday night.
Mendoza hit Jalen Nailor on a 22-yard pass for a chunk gain, while Mike Washington Jr. continued to impress with another long run. It looked like Las Vegas was on its way to scoring on the opening drive.
Then, Wade Woodaz happened.
Houston's rookie linebacker took advantage of poor footwork and a late read from Mendoza, jumping in front of the check-down and taking the interception back the other way for a pick-six.
It wasn't much better for the Raiders' future franchise quarterback in the rest of the half, as he completed only eight passes for 86 yards and didn't lead a touchdown drive. It ended up not mattering because the Raiders came back and won in the second half, thanks to Aidan O'Connell.
However, O'Connell isn't the future starter in Las Vegas; Mendoza is . The Raiders need him to learn from this performance and move forward.
That's exactly what he has the chance to do: use this outing as a learning experience and improve as he heads into his next game.
One of the first things I noticed when O'Connell led the comeback (or, really, when any other player had a big play) was that Mendoza was there cheering them on and being a supportive teammate. Oftentimes, young players will hang their heads, but Mendoza is more mature than that.
This kind of performance illustrates exactly what minority owner Tom Brady got on his soapbox about last year when it comes to quarterback development: if the Raiders were competing for a playoff spot, and Mendoza had that kind of game, it may outright ruin his confidence.
The Raiders will give Mendoza meaningful reps in the preseason because the outcome of the game doesn't matter, allowing him to get real game action without debilitating consequences. It is good for him to get games like this out of the way, so they don't happen when meaningful team aspirations are on the line.
Mendoza and the Raiders take on the San Francisco 49ers next week. We will see how Klint Kubiak approaches playing starters or how he divvies up the snaps among his quarterbacks, but Thursday showed that Mendoza needs more snaps to bounce back.
No one should overreact to how Mendoza played, but it is perfectly reasonable to say he must play better. He has one more preseason game to do that.

title: Four Winners And Four Losers in the Miami Dolphins Preseason Loss Against the New York Giants
full_text:
Now that the second game of the preseason is in the books for the Miami Dolphins, it's time to look at those who left a decent impression and those who are running out of time to prove that they belong here.
With most of the big-name starters out for this game, it opened the door for Miami's reserves to get the spotlight. The opportunity presented itself, but a 26-3 loss to the New York Giants only reinforced the constant criticism of the Dolphins' depth.
Again, it's wise to never overreact to what you witness in the preseason. In this instance, however, it would be nice to have something to overreact to. And the defense isn't safe, either. At the very least, some names on both sides of the ball walked away from this with something to be proud of.
Let's address the elephant in the room: There's no clear-cut winner to come from this offense. To say Coleman is a major winner is a stretch, but from the limited sample size we saw, at least there was some good.
Two catches for 32 yards off five targets isn't amazing, but his 30-yard one-handed grab while being interfered with might have been the only offensive bright spot of the game. It brings a similar vibe to the reception that Caleb Douglas pulled off against Washington a week ago.
The fifth-round pick out of Missouri appears to be keeping up the new tradition of rookie receivers making spectacular catches in the preseason. For Miami's sake, they could use even more of these young receivers taking advantage of the opportunities given to them.
With De'Von Achane not playing in this game and Ollie Gordon II exiting early with an injury, this was Wright's moment to prove that he should be considered the main backup runner.
That did not happen. Even before Gordon got injured, the running game looked off. Wright did not fix the issue, recording 9 yards on six carries. More egregious than that, however, was his fumble, having the ball stripped away on first contact and adding to his consistent problems with ball security.
On special teams, Wright looked decent with a couple of kick returns. But the depth of the running back position has taken a massive hit. If Gordon is seriously hurt, Wright did not do himself any favors in making people believe he can be the main backup.
Woodard had a sneaky good performance in this game with an exceptional play that has done great PR - a fumble recovery in the red zone that killed a drive that began on Miami's 39-yard line. Similar to Coleman's catch, it might have been the biggest highlight on defense the whole night.
Woodard didn't see a ton of action in this game, but he was fast and physical when he was near the ball. He racked up five total tackles, four of them being on his own. He was one of the few defenders who stood up to New York's ground game. On special teams, he made a pair of tackles on punt coverage, though one of them was negated by a holding penalty.
He came into this summer trying to earn a spot on the practice squad, and that's where he'll most likely end up. But he led the team in total tackles last week and kept up the momentum against the Giants. If he can pop off one more time in the preseason against Atlanta, he might just sneak into the 53-man roster.
It almost seems unfair to note either quarterback as one of the biggest losers of this game because of weapons like Tutu Atwell struggling from the jump. This has been a brutal summer for Atwell, who ended the day with no yards on no receptions — straight cardio.
The story of the night for Atwell was his inability to reel in targets. He had two drops against the Giants — one was contested, while the other was a straight miss on third down, which would have been helpful considering Bradley Pinion had to punt from inside the end zone to close out that drive.
Miami almost needs to be grateful for what they've gotten out of the rookie receivers so far in the preseason, because a lot of the veteran pass-catchers they've brought in haven't lived up to expectations. Atwell is, unfortunately, high on that list.
The quarterback room needed someone to give it hope in case something were to happen to Malik Willis. Quinn Ewers is still dealing with a groin injury, so the Dolphins turned to Miller once again and got clear improvement from a week ago.
Miller's performance was miles better than what he and Ewers put on last week, especially considering the shortcomings of just about everyone around him. He recorded 60 yards off six completions with no interceptions. Both of his sacks were nearly impossible to avoid, and he can't control the drops his receivers managed.
He threw some accurate passes and wasn't afraid to get out of the pocket, leading the team on the ground with 18 rushing yards. That said, his decision-making is still under question, with some completions just so happening in double coverage.
Yet another week where the backup offensive linemen didn't impress, and they got significantly more time to do so against the Giants. Heck struggled to contain the Giants' pass rush, and even when Gordon managed a gritty run before he got hurt, Heck wiped it off the board with a holding penalty.
Since Heck was signed back in March as an unrestricted free agent, he's been an experiment that has struggled all camp. There have been little to no flashes of progress in either preseason game, though you can say the same thing for a good chunk of the reserve linemen Miami has to offer.
Yep, we're at this point as far as winners go. Miami only scored three points today, and they were off the foot of Patterson on a 53-yard field goal attempt.
Patterson was certainly an accurate kicker in 2025, converting 27 of 29 field goals. The sample size is small, with just this field goal and an extra point last week against Washington. However, it looks like he's continuing to be a reliable answer on special teams, exactly what Miami wants at the position long-term after releasing injured veteran Zane Gonzalez back on August 19.
As a wide receiver, Washington made the most of his single target, a contested catch for 12 yards. But this placement is solely for his work as a returner, muffing a punt in the final two minutes to close out the game - a fitting end to Miami's performance as a whole against the Giants.
This muffed punt made no real impact on the game. But all in all, Washington is running out of time to prove that he can be a reliable weapon to the coaching staff. Miami is clearly impressed with what they've seen from Coleman, Douglas, and even Chris Bell now that he's off the non-football injury list.
Instead, this is the second straight week that Washington is featured on one of these lists, and that's not a good thing.

title: Dolphins Preseason Game 2 Instant Takeaways: Miller, Coleman, Injuries, and More
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins' shaky preseason showing continued at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday when they faced the New York Giants in a battle featuring a whole lot of backups.
The 26-3 loss once again illustrated the Dolphins' well-chronicled but still alarming lack of depth, which wasn't helped by a couple of first-half injuries.
Unlike the preseason opener, the Dolphins didn't have a brilliant first drive on which to build because this one was rough from start to finish.
-- Zero issues from here about the idea of sitting starters for this second preseason other than the rookies — Kadyn Proctor, Chris Johnson, Jacob Rodriguez included. They're young players and could benefit from the experience of a home game, even in the preseason.
-- Of course, this backfired with rookie fourth-round pick Trey Moore when he sustained an apparent ankle injury while hitting QB Jameis Winston on a pass rush. It would be easy to second-guess here and suggest the Dolphins should have sat their rookie starters as well, but that's playing the results. We'll be doing enough second-guessing the rest of 2026 that we don't know to overdo it here.
-- While Cam Miller looked better in practice the past week or so, this game showed the Dolphins have a major backup QB issue if Quinn Ewers doesn't get his game back on track. Period. As we've said with Ewers, though, it's unfair to put all the blame on Miller because it's not like he got a ton of help.
-- For one thing, the running game was brutal. And that was before Ollie Gordon II left the game with what appeared to be an oblique injury (teams aren't required to announce injuries during the preseason).
-- Jaylen Wright has had ball security issues in his time with the Dolphins, and his fumble before contact was  not ideal — to say the least.
-- Miller also wasn't helped by his receivers, most notably Tutu Atwell, whose rough summer continued. It remains very difficult to see how the former Miami high school star will make the 53-man roster.
-- The Dolphins have been churning the roster over the past couple of weeks, and maybe what we've seen with their depth in the preseason is an indication there's still work to do there. The Dolphins backups again didn't match up against the Giants backups, and that's in every facet of the game.
-- Backups or not, it's pretty depressing that the Dolphins didn't even have 100 yards of total offense in the first three quarters.
-- And on defense nobody emerged as a potential playmaker despite the Giants basically having the ball the whole game. This is why the Dolphins will keep looking for more players, like they did when they claimed a Colts cornerback on the day of the game.
-- Not sure what to make of Willie Gay Jr. getting so many snaps beyond the team being short at linebacker, but him not being able to make more of an impact perhaps what was most telling.
-- But, hey, Riley Patterson did nail that 53-yard field goal attempt in the first half.
-- So there was something positive, right?
-- And guess we should mention new linebacker Cam Riley's tackle for a 5-yard loss on a running play early in the fourth quarter too. But on the very next play Riley missed a tackle to allow an extra 6-7 yards on a 14-yard reception.
-- A muffed punt by Tahj Washington just inside the two-minute warning was a pretty fitting way to end things for the Dolphins before the Giants mercifully just kneeled to end this game — actually this mismatch.
-- This game was Exhibit A for those who want to reduce the number of preseason games because it was a tough watch. And that's being very kind.
-- The best news of all is there's only one of these left before the real games start on the second weekend of September.
-- The Dolphins, though, need to use all the time they have to upgrade their roster. This game against the Giants was just another example the non-starters just aren't good enough.

title: 10 Players to Watch in Second Dolphins Preseason Game
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins will be back in action when they take on the New York Giants at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday afternoon, and it will provide another opportunity to evaluate those players fighting for roster spots.
At this stage of the summer, GM Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley probably have a good idea what the bulk of the Dolphins' 53-man roster will look like, but they certainly could be swayed by strong individual performances here and there.
After the front-line players got a lot of work during the joint practice Thursday, we'd expect backups and younger players will be at the forefront for the second of the preseason games, along with some veterans who maybe have yet to cement their roster spot.
With that in mind, here is our list of 10 players to watch in this second preseason game, which kicks off at 4 p.m. ET.
Is it possible that Miller could play his way onto the 53-man roster? That remains to be determined, but the fact remains that he has looked much better in the last several days than earlier in camp, and Quinn Ewers' struggles and current groin injury maybe have opened the door for him. This is a huge game for him.
Tolbert and Tutu Atwell were the two veteran wide receivers of note the Dolphins added in the offseason, but neither has distinguished himself this summer to the point where their roster spot should be considered secure.
All rookie draft picks, regardless of what coaches might say, get a bit more leeway than other players during training camp and at roster cut time, but it doesn't mean their spot is guaranteed. And the reality is that Traore has dropped a few passes this summer and shouldn't be considered a lock to make the roster. A strong performance against the Giants could change that.
Likewise, Campbell needs to string together some good performance to make the roster as a sixth-round pick and he should get an elevated role after fellow guard James Ester was waived-injured Thursday.
Herman is a rookie like Traore and Campbell, but he was undrafted, which shouldn't get him the benefit of the doubt. Yet Herman has played himself into a position where the Dolphins coaches are going to be thinking hard about whether they should keep him as the lone fullback on the roster (instead of going the H-back route when they want to use two backs in the backfield).
Mulbah hasn't been around very long, but he's certainly looked the part, both in the preseason game against Washington and in practice. There sure does appear to be something to work with when it comes to the former Jets player.
The seventh-round pick from Iowa really has come on of late and he has played himself clearly into the picture at the fairly thin edge position. Another solid outing against the Giants could help put him over the top.
The former UFL interception leader is trying to make his way in a safety room that's lacking proven commodities and now also might include rookie fourth-round pick Kyle Louis after he got work at that position all week.
See Burns. The same comments would apply, except that Moore led major college football in interceptions last year, not the UFL. But his situation is almost identical to that of Burns.
It's going to be awfully difficult for any young defensive tackle to make the Dolphins 53-man roster when the team already has three second-year players who all were draft picks — Kenneth Grant, Jordan Phililps, Zeek Biggers — particularly considering Matthew Butler's strong training camp showing. But Cooper at the very least deserves a spot on the practice squad based on what he's shown so far and maybe he won't be cuttable if he shines against the Giants.
