title: 8 Studs, 3 Duds From First Half of Eagles Preseason Game At Patriots
full_text:
The second preseason game for the Philadelphia Eagles started off significantly better than the first. Not only did the Eagles score points, they dominated the line of scrimmage and moved the ball downfield.
This was a fun first half of football for second team players , and perhaps some roster spots were solidified . These were the studs and duds in the first half.
Enjoy our content? Make Eagles On SI a Preferred Source to see more stories from us on Google: https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=si.com
On Will Shipley's 18-yard run in the first quarter, Bell was able to get leverage on Gabe Jacas -- dominating the pass rush from Jacas and created the hole for Shipley's run. This was an outside zone run, set up by Bell and Jake Majors sealing the inside. Willie Lampkin also had a nice block to set up the run too.
Nice seal on the edge from #Eagles rookie OT Markell Bell and Willie Lampkin also gets a nice reach block on the DT on this outside zone run from Will Shipley. pic.twitter.com/dDbxhxVLsP
Bell set up a couple Shipley runs in the first quarter, two of which combined for 23 yards. He's massively improved as a run blocker this summer, and it's showing at a new position in right tackle.
Didn't take long for Hall to make his presence felt at defensive tackle. Hall had back-to-back tackles on his first two plays of the game, getting into the backfield and making two tackles on the first two snaps of the game.
For Hall to have that awareness and instinct early in the game is a good sign. He should be on a 53-man roster somewhere.
Did Shipley benefit from the right side of the Eagles offensive line? Absolutely, but this is why Shipley is going to make the roster. Shipley hit the hole hard in the first half, responsible for a lot of big runs that paced the Eagles offense.
Will Shipley gets the first points of the game 🦅 PHIvsNE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KR7HkyFlq4
Shipley had nine carries for 51 yards in the first quarter. He had nine carries for 33 yards on the Eagles' 13-play, 77 yard touchdown drive in the second quarter -- capped by a 5-yard touchdown run. Shipley and the Eagles offensive line were simply dominant in the first half.
Lampkin was impressive in the first half at center, getting leverage on Patriots defensive tackle Eric Gregory in spite of his small stature. The Eagles have a backup center and guard in Lampkin, who has the technique and tenacity to thrive in the NFL.
Lampkin played a massive role in the Eagles averaging 5.1 yards per carry on their first two possessions.
Where would the Eagles passing game be without Cooper? Getting a longer look as the top wideout on Saturday with Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore getting the night off, Cooper made some plays that may have sealed his spot on the roster.
A 25-yard catch from Cooper on a playaction was the highlight, as Cooper was able to get open on a crossing route underneath to beat Patriots linebacker Chad Muma and turn that into a big gain. Cooper had three catches for 44 yards in the first half -- and was open on other routes too.
Darius Cooper breaks a tackle, stays in bounds, and picks up 25 💨 PHIvsNE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DNlcX7TXsg
Another preseason game Robinson has "come alive," per Vic Fangio. Robinson played late into the first half, but had three quarterback hits and two sacks for the Eagles. Robinson was arguably the best defensive lineman on the field in the first 30 minutes.
Robinson is expected to make the team since he's a fourth-round pick from last season. He beat Mehki Butler and Jacob Rizy on a third-down sack in the second quarter, a play that demonstrates how to make a roster.
2 games, 2 sacks for Ty-Rob 💪 pic.twitter.com/AvpbiQf9a1
This was an impressive first half for Robinson. He should have a roster spot locked up.
For weeks in practice, the chatter was what the Eagles see in Majors. The answer came on Saturday night, as Majors was dominant in blocking at right guard.
Majors was just as vital towards creating the holes for Shipley as Willie Lampkin and Markel Bell were. The right side of the Eagles offensive line were excellent in the first half. Majors may have a shot at making this team.
If the Eagles are looking for a fullback, they may have found one in Steele. Entering the game in the second quarter for Will Shipley, Steele had three catches for 33 yards -- including an impressive hurdle on a 14-yard reception that wowed the Eagles sideline.
Carson Steele hurdle! PHIvsNE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/lWL2sUpwu9
Steele also had four carries for 15 yards. If the Eagles are looking for a receiving fullback, they may have found their guy in Steele.
Back-to-back poor throws by Dalton on the Eagles first offensive series set the tone for his night. Dalton overthrew an open Darius Cooper on second-and-5 at the Eagles' 45, then followed with a overthrow to Eli Stowers on third-and-5 (on the next play). This wasn't a good look at all for Dalton as he's battling for the QB2 job. Stowers did a good job of getting open on a corner post and Dalton flat out missed him.
Dalton looked better on the second series, but going to Darius Cooper helped. Cooper had three catches for 44 yards on the second drive, Dalton's first three completions on the night.
Dalton almost threw interceptions on consecutive plays, but was bailed out by a roughing the passer call on the first one and Kindle Vildor almost had the second one. Quez Watkins was open on the play, but Dalton had a bad throw.
The numbers on the night? 3-of-10 for 44 yards (45.2 rating). Not good for Dalton's chances to win the QB2 job.
The one chance Covey has to make the roster is via punt returner. Covey would likely still be on the practice squad as a punt returner, but he has to field punts cleanly. Muffing the opening punt isn't a good sign for Covey, a veteran in this league who is a good punt returner when healthy.
Covey did average 10.0 yards per punt return in the first half, but the muffed punt was the play that can't be made when fighting for a roster spot.
Did Covey make up for the muffed punt? He did have a 14-yard touchdown catch on a wide receiver screen late in the first half. The play showed how Covey moves between defenders, so he has value on the roster if he returns.
Brittain Covey gives the Eagles the lead 🦅 PHIvsNE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZhRtrDRQbl
Thomas was the victim on a 69-yard touchdown pass from Tommy DeVito to Kyle Williams late in the first half. The veteran cornerback easily got beat by Williams on a go route for the touchdown -- a play cornerbacks shouldn't get beaten by that easily.
. @tommydevito007 goes DEEP to @k_mmoneyyyy 😤 📺: WBZ pic.twitter.com/1cEo0iuTBT
A long shot to make the roster, Thomas showcases the lack of depth the Eagles have at cornerback behind the starters -- and all the injuries they have at the position. This wasn't an ideal play for Thomas.

title: Why Johnny Wilson Can Still Return To Eagles After Being Waived This Year
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles waived Johnny Wilson with an injury settlement on Friday . There's still a chance Wilson could return to Philadelphia.
Since Wilson cleared waivers, the Eagles reverted him to injured reserve just 24 hours later. Wilson would be out for the entire 2026 season and could return for 2027 -- if Wilson remins on injured reserve all season.
How can Wilson return to the Eagles this year? If the Eagles and Wilson work out an injury settlement, Wilson can sign with any team immediately or return to Philadelphia after the injury settlement is reached. There would also be an additional three weeks taxed on as a penalty.
So there is a chance Wilson could be back, although the Eagles and Wilson will likely move on.
Heading into the start of training camp, Wilson was one of the front runners to earn the WR5 spot. The Eagles needed a blocking receiver and a receiver with size given the state of the wide receiver position. Without Wilson on the 53, the tallest receiver amongst the top-7 is Dontayvion Wicks.
Perhaps this is why there's a chance Wilson could return when he's healthy. If the Eagles don't find wide receiver depth on the trade market or after the roster cutdown deadline, an injury settlement is an option. This is unlikely to happen, given the extent of Wilson's knee injury is unknown.
Wilson was on track towards making the team last season before severe knee and ankle injuries ended his year. He hasn't played a game since 2024 and was looking to play in his first preseason game in over a year, before another knee injury set him back.
The Eagles have a battle for the final wide receiver spot. Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore are battling for one of the spots on the roster, and Darius Cooper is trying to hold onto his roster spot.
Cooper was one of the best receivers early in camp and has a role on this team as a blocking receiver. The Eagles have moved Cooper down to the second team in the past week, giving Brown and Moore opportunities with the firts team.
Brown and Moore aren't the same player, but can play the same role as a WR4. Neither are specialized in doing the physical work at wide receiver, similar to what Wilson did as a blocker and red zone threat.
Cooper has played that role this summer, even though he's significantly smaller than Wilson . Brown and Moore earned the first team reps in the joint practices this week due to DeVonta Smith and Makai lemon working their way back from hamstring injuries.
The battle for two wide receiver spots will come down to the final practices. The Eagles are likely to keep five receivers based on roster construction, which makes this battle even more intriguing.
The final week of practice will be crucial for Brown, Moore, and Cooper.

title: Why Eagles Need To Consider Trading Or Signing WR Prior To Week 1
full_text:
Wide receiver was always at the forefront of the Philadelphia Eagles offseason.
This is the price a team pays when giving up a talent in A.J. Brown. Moving on from Brown was always going to be difficult, as a crucial aspect in his game is lacking in this current room.
Brown stood at 6-1, 226 pounds, but played like he was 6-4, 250 when the pads were on. His physicality stood out like a sore thumb, giving the Eagles that dynamic at wide receiver.
This current group doesn't have that presence -- at all.
With the Eagles waiving Johnny Wilson on Friday, they parted ways with their tallest and biggest receiver at 6-6, 228 pounds. Now that Wilson is off the roster, the Eagles sorely lack in height and weight at wide receiver.
These are the top-7 wideouts on the Eagles, listed by height and weight.
There isn't a top-7 wide receiver on this roster that is over 6-1, nor one that weighs over 210. Cooper is likely to make the roster, but he's not a lock (and he's the receiver that weighs 210). Wicks is the tallest of the top-7 receivers at 6-1.
Perhaps this is how the Eagles designed their revamped their wide receiver room. For a team that's going to base their offense on the run game and the offensive line, the Eagles need a bigger body at wide receiver.
They need to make a trade or sign a free agent before the regular season. The Eagles need to add physicality at wide receiver, along with the other roster holes they have.
Enjoy our content? Make Eagles On SI a Preferred Source to see more stories from us on Google: https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=si.com
The Eagles aren't going to create a roster spot for one of their bigger wideouts on the 90-man roster. The biggest receiver on the 90-man is Erik Ezukanma (6-2, 206), so the options internally at the position are thin.
Cooper should play the blocking wideout with his physicality, but he doesn't have the height for that role (5-11). There just isn't any options at wide receiver, which is why the external option comes into play.
One of the tight ends could always move to add more physicality at wide receiver. Eli Stowers (6-3, 239) could add that presence in the slot, but he's had trouble creating separation this summer. The rookie also needs to work on his blocking.
The Eagles could also go into more "12 personnel" with Johnny Mundt (6-4, 245). Do the Eagles really want Mundt on the field that much, especially when he has a reputation as a blocker and not a pass catcher?
This is where the external option comes into play.
The Eagles would have to wait until after the roster cutdowns to see who they can sign as a free agent. The current free agent pool is slim, as bigger wideouts with the size of Wilson are hard to find.
Perhaps the Eagles look to acquire another tight end, adding needed depth to that position and who can be an improvement over Mundt in the TE2 role. That allows Mundt to play the role as that extra blocker and Stowers to add to the wide receiver room in a hybrid receiver/tight end role with his size and athleticism.
The trade route prior to the roster deadline is always an option, and general manager Howie Roseman has made pre-roster deadline deals frequently. If Roseman sees an opportunity to add talent, he'll do it.
The Eagles don't need a star. They need a player that can provide much-needed depth and do the dirty work at wide receiver. They thought Wilson was going to be that player, but knee problems kept persisting.
Finding height and physicality at receiver is an underrated part of their offense, but a necessity if this team is going to base their offense around Saquon Barkley and the offensive line.
The Eagles can wait around and play this situation out, for the next few weeks at least.

title: Why Vic Fangio Is Right To Call  Inside Linebacker Eagles’ Deepest Defensive Position
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — In what might be a surprise unless you understand his background, well-regarded Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio highlighted the strength of his inside linebacker group while in Foxborough for joint practices with the New England Patriots.
In fact, Fangio declared Bobby King’s room as “probably” the deepest position on his defense.
Conventional wisdom tilts toward defensive tackle where star-level players Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis are supplemented by Moro Ojomo, Byron Young and Ty Robinson, who is starting to come on of late.
Then you have edge defender, where free-agent pickups Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa are making life bearable as supplements to Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith while Jonathan Greenard works through his sprained pec.
Even outside cornerback looks set if proven veteran Jonathan Jones can make it back from a shoulder injury to provide valuable insurance for Quinyon Mitchell and Riq Woolen.
Despite that Fangio turned to ILB which is led by All-Pro Zack Baul and ascending second-year player Jihaad Campbell. From there LB3 Jeremiah Trotter Jr. is in the running for best backup on the team, while Smael Mondon is another second-year player the Eagles like.
Fangio previously warned the media not to sleep on Chance Campbell, and Deontae Lawson has taken on the mantle of best undrafted signing this year.
“Our ILB position is probably our deepest position on defense,” Fangio said. “We’ve got Trotter and Smael, that are two good quality players. [Chance] Campbell, been hurt for a while, but I think he’ll be back out there today, and Deontae.
“So, I feel good about those guys.”
Fangio specifically praised Trotter’s growth, noting the third-year player is “reaping the benefits of being in the system for three years” with faster processing and sharper instincts—qualities he noted as essential for an inside linebacker.
The assessment carries added weight given Fangio’s extensive track record developing elite linebackers across decades in the NFL.
Fangio began his NFL coaching career as the New Orleans Saints’ linebackers coach from 1986 to 1994, where he guided the legendary “Dome Patrol.”
That group—outside linebackers Rickey Jackson and Pat Swilling alongside inside linebackers Sam Mills and Vaughan Johnson—is widely regarded as one of the greatest linebacking corps in league history.
The four combined for 18 Pro Bowl selections and 10 first-team All-Pro honors under Fangio’s tutelage. In 1992, all four were selected to the Pro Bowl, the first time in NFL history that four players from the same team and position group earned the honor.
Jackson and Mills later reached the Pro Football Hall of Fame, while Swilling was named the 1991 Associated Press NFL Defensive Player of the Year.
Fangio recently penned the foreword for long-time Eagles reporter Paul Domowitch’s book on Mills: “Just Give Me a Chance To Fail.”
Later, as defensive coordinator of the San Francisco 49ers from 2011 to 2014, Fangio oversaw another standout pair of inside linebackers in Patrick Willis and NaVorro Bowman.
Both Willis and Bowman earned multiple Pro Bowl nods during Fangio’s tenure and are remembered among the most dominant interior linebackers of their era.
Fangio’s linebacker expertise even extended to a 2009 stint as Baltimore Ravens linebackers coach, where he worked with first-team All-Pro and Hall of Famer Ray Lewis.
With that pedigree coaching the position, Fangio’s endorsement of the current Eagles inside linebacker room would indicate flexibility in personnel packages and insurance against injuries, allowing the veteran coordinator to continue refining a defense that has become a hallmark of the organization under his leadership.

title: Nick Sirianni Keeps the Red Flag: Why the Eagles Coach Won’t Hand Off Challenge Duties
full_text:
The NFL is giving head coaches a new option to lighten their load on game days—especially those who get too deep in the play-calling weeds.
Starting in the 2026 season, a quiet but meaningful tweak to the rulebook allows the head coach to designate one staff member before kickoff to throw the red challenge flag.
Under the updated rule: “The head coach or head coach’s pregame challenge designee can initiate a challenge by throwing a red flag onto the field of play before the next legal snap or kick.”
Previously, only the head coach could carry and toss the flag (a practice dating back to the modern instant-replay system’s introduction back in 1999). The designee must be named to officials pregame and holds the responsibility for the entire contest, meaning no mid-game switching if a mistake happens.
The head coach can still make the final call via headset communication with the booth and sideline staff of course. The change simply offloads the physical act of throwing the flag.
The league made the adjustment as a summer rulebook clarification that did not require an owners’ vote. It comes after 151 coaches’ challenges in 2025, the highest total since 2019.
Proponents note it could help coaches focused on play-calling avoid distractions and reduce emotion-driven decisions if they put ego aside and delegate the responsibility.
For play-callers who stay very hands-on with the offense, handing off a game-management task—essentially a free pass on one more mechanical burden—can free the kind of mental bandwidth to get getting the next play in without a hiccup.
Some coaches have already been doing a version of this unofficially for years (Bengals coach Zac Taylor has let his chief of staff handle it since 2019). Others, however, view the optics and accountability in a different fashion.
Enter Nick Sirianni. For the Eagles’ CEO head coach, surrendering an important game-management responsibility is a non-starter.
Asked about the rule change Thursday before the Eagles’ second joint practice against the New England Patriots, Sirianni quickly dismissed the idea of handing the flag to an assistant.
“I’m definitely going to keep that,” Sirianni said.
The veteran coach then reached into his memory bank for a moment that demanded a split-second feel and immediate action. In 2022 at Washington, receiver DeVonta Smith hauled in a ball over his shoulder. The Eagles hustled to the line and snapped quickly while then-Commanders coach Ron Rivera was still throwing his challenge flag. Philadelphia essentially beat the challenge.
“We actually beat the challenge,” Sirianni explained. “In my eyes, the way we need to do it, the way the Philadelphia Eagles are going to do it, is I just want that direct communication so if I have to get the flag out quick.”
Sirianni downplayed any claim of elite flag-throwing speed but stressed confidence in handling the moment himself.
“I’m not saying my release is really quick. I’m not saying anything like that, but at least I can get that out quick,” he said. “That’s just my feeling on it of what we’re going to do. I know sometimes it comes down to just little tenths of seconds to be able to get that flag out per the 2022 Washington game.”
Sirianni’s stance aligns with several other CEO coaches who have already indicated they’ll keep the flag (including Dan Campbell, and Mike Vrabel), citing accountability and the value of communication.
Whether more coaches eventually embrace the new flexibility remains to be seen, but for the Eagles in 2026, the red flag stays firmly in Sirianni's hands.

title: 6 Eagles Position Battles Still Up For Grabs Vs. Patriots
full_text:
The joint practice portion of training camp is complete.
After an intense two practices in Foxborough with the New England Patriots, the Philadelphia Eagles wrap up their week up north with the preseason game Saturday night. This matchup is about the second and third team starters getting an opportunity to play after the first team butted heads all week.
This is a critical game for some position battles where starting jobs aren't on the line. The Eagles have to fill out their 53-man roster, so this preseason game goes a long way towards winning those battles.
The Eagles have quite a few position battles that still need to be determined with a week left in training camp. These are the position battles to watch on Saturday as you tune in to the Eagles' second preseason game.
The contenders: Andy Dalton, Tanner McKee
Dalton is the front runner for this job and the expected starter in Saturday's game. He's taken the majority of the QB2 snaps in practice, even though the Eagles have split the second team reps between Dalton and McKee.
While Dalton didn't fare well in the preseason opener, he seems to have a better feel for the offense than McKee. Dalton knows how to get the ball out quickly and keep the pace moving. He should see an extended run on Saturday.
McKee will get a lot of playing time as well. This battle is coming down to the final week of camp.
The contenders: Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore
The first question being asked here. Where is Darius Cooper?
Cooper is expected to be on this roster , but his role has been established as a WR5. He's not expected to see many snaps when the games count. That can't be said for Brown or Moore, who are batting for the WR4 spot -- and a spot on the roster.
The Eagles have $5 million reasons not to part ways with Brown, but Moore is making it difficult for him to cut. Both players will see some snaps tonight in the early going.
While the Eagles could keep Brown and Moore, that may come at the expense of Cooper. Both players are fighting for roster spots in the final week.
The contenders: Johnny Mundt, Eli Stowers
This isn't as much of a battle, even though Stowers is a secodn-round pick. Stowers has struggled to get open this summer, and his blocking is a work in progress. He's batting against himself for playing time and not being a healthy scratch.
Mundt is the de facto TE2, and didn't play in the preseason opener. He may not play on Saturday either.
This game is about Stowers developing confidence and demonstrating he's playable come Week 1. Stowers will be getting a significant amount of snaps in this one.
The contenders: Markel Bell, Fred Johnson
Bell has separated himself from Johnson as the tackle who would replace Lane Johnson or Jordan Mailata if either need a few plays. He's acclimated himself well to right tackle and the Eagles had him there over Johnson in the team portion of the joint practices.
Johnson is still a valuable swing tackle, but the Eagles need to develop Bell as he's the successor to lane Johnson at right tackle. The Eagles need tackle depth, and Johnson provides that.
Bell should see a lot of right tackle on Saturday, with Johnson on the left side. The Eagles could switch both up at some point in the game too.
The contenders: Kelee Ringo, Mac McWilliams
The depth the Eagles have at cornerback is being significantly challenged . Jonathan Jones is the top backup behind starters Quinyon Mitchell, Cooper DeJean, and Tariq Woolen, -- yet he may be out a while due to a shoulder injury.
The injuries have mounted behind Jones. Jakorian Bennett has a knee injury and Tariq Castro-Fields played through a heel injury before landing on injured reserve.
Ringo may make this roster by default since he's an excellent special teams player. McWilliams is fighting for a roster spot as well. Both players should see a lot of playing time on Saturday.
If Jones is healthy, this battle doesn't exist. Instead, the Eagles have two players fighting for a roster spot -- and a critical part of the secondary.
The contenders: Andre Sam, Cole Wisniewski, Maximus Pulley
Due to the injuries at cornerback, the No. 4 safety spot comes into play. The Eagles have a reason to keep just three safeties -- Andrew Mukuba, Marcus Epps, and Michael Carter -- and provide depth to other areas of the roster.
The Eagles are going to have to consider another safety, maybe even two if Carter goes down to cornerback for added depth. This is where Sam, Wisniewski, and Pulley come in.
Sam has been the best of the bunch and has hung around on the practice squad for years. He's developed smoothly and may be ready for a role on the 53-man roster. Wisniewski just returned to practice after missing nearly three weeks with a hamstring injury and Pulley has stood out as an undrfated free agent.
Kapena Gushiken, another undrafted free agent, is also in the mix as an extra defensive back -- since he can play the slot and safety. Gushiken is also a good special teams player.
This battle is wide open, and all four players will see extended playing time on Saturday.

title: 5 Eagles Who Can Play Their Way Off the Bubble In Preseason Showdown With Patriots
full_text:
The second week of the preseason is upon us and with that, it gives players on the Eagles' roster bubble a chance to show they're worthy of a 53-man spot. Having said that, it also puts pressure on those who might be on the outside looking in to perform in the game to redeem themselves after poor practices.
Here are five players who could potentially play themselves off the roster bubble and get back into the 53-man roster conversation .
Enjoy our content? Make Eagles On SI a Preferred Source to see more stories from us on Google: https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=si.com
Last year's fourth-round pick out of Nebraska has been unable to translate his skillset to the NFL that made him a second-team All-Big Ten selection his senior season after racking up seven sacks and 12 TFLs. However, he has stacked a few good practices together getting the attention of defensive coordinator Vic Fangio.
"He came to life," Fangio told reporters when talking about the defensive tackle's recent performance. "He's been on life support since he's been here, but he came to life and hopefully that will continue."
Robinson played 47 snaps at defensive tackle in last week's loss to the Ravens tied with Zion Wilson, for most in the position group and tied for third-most of any player on defense. Both Robinson and Wilson are battling one another for a spot as one of the backup defensive tackles for the Eagles.
If Robinson can show some life Saturday against the Patriots, it would bode well for the 25-year-old.
Cooper appeared to be a candidate to more than likely make the roster with the way he performed during training camp leading up to the first preseason games. Making noteworthy catches, running strong routes and seemingly earning the trust of Jalen Hurts it seemed as if Cooper was safe from being on the bubble.
However, in last week's game, the second-year undrafted free agent played the most snaps out of any wide receiver (29) so the team could get a longer look at him.  That was more than three times the number of snaps for both Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore (7), who compared to Cooper, needed more to prove based on practice performances.
However, it seems like Brown's roster spot is more secure than it initially appeared and perhaps the veteran Moore has a slight advantage at this particular juncture of the summer.
Cooper caught two passes for 21 yards but had a key third down drop in the 24-7 loss to Baltimore. He may need to continue to perform well both in camp and in the games to solidify a spot as the WR5.
The fifth-round pick out of UCF last year has been solid during training camp and has earned some praise from Fangio, which goes a long way when it comes to the veteran coordinator, saying that the second-year CB has "matured".
McWilliams got a ton of playing time last week due to Jakorian Bennett getting injured. McWilliams has already earned some first-team reps in practice and will look to continue his momentum on Saturday continuing to battle for a spot in the cornerbacks room that has the likes of Bennett, newly signed Isaiah Bolden, Tariq Castro-Fields, Ambry Thomas and Shawn Wade all vying for one of the final corner spots on the roster.
The fifth-round pick out of North Dakota State provided the only spark in the team's 24-7 loss to Baltimore where the offense was stagnant. The dual-threat quarterback went 4-for-9 passing for 37 yards and a touchdown along with 45 rushing yards. His two best plays were a 17-yard scramble to keep the scoring drive alive which was capped by a six-yard pass from Payton to wide receiver Erik Ezukanma late in the final quarter.
The coaching staff and front office have a good idea on what Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee bring to the table despite lowly performances last week in their backup quarterback battle. However, the Eagles may want to give Payton more runway or at least a series or two earlier in Saturday's game with a better supporting cast to try and get a better evaluation.
It's hard to imagine the Eagles carrying four quarterbacks on the initial 53-man roster, although Howie Roseman did acknowledge the possibility. That speaks to the intrigue that Payton provides in his long-term development while McKee is on his final year of his rookie deal.
Gushiken generated some buzz as of late after earning first-team reps earlier in the week and making the most of them. Starting out at the JUCO level before transferring to Washington State and then Ole Miss, the undrafted free agent showed great instincts on the field last Saturday. He recorded five tackles with one of them being an impressive solo stop against a larger running back in Adam Randall who is listed at 6-foot-3, 240-pounds compared to the 5-foot-9, 198-pound Gushiken.
He will have added competition with the return of this year's seventh rounder Cole Wisniewski back from his hamstring injury. While a lot has been made about who will win the second safety battle between Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II, Gushiken could have a lane to pass the rest of the competition including J.T. Gray, Maximus Pulley and Andre Sam for a depth safety spot.

title: Rising? Falling?: Eagles Stock Report Heading Into Critical Stretch of Camp
full_text:
The biggest stretch of Philadelphia Eagles training camp has arrived.
There are two more preseason games to go, but they are crucial for the final roster spots. A few roster spots are still up for grabs , along with some positions that have a few openings.
Now is the time for players to make an impression . In a what have you done for me lately league, better off finishing strong than struggling to the finish line.
Whose stock is rising and falling heading into the final week of camp? There are a few candidates.
Enjoy our content? Make Eagles On SI a Preferred Source to see more stories from us on Google: https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=si.com
At this stage in training camp, it's hard to envision Lampkin not making the 53-man roster. Lampkin has been a bulldog in practice, using his smaller size to his advantage and has consistenly won battles on the interior of the offensive line.
Whether it's center or guard, Lampkin has performed well. He has a spot on this team.
There was an opening for the No. 3 guard spot heading into camp and Kendall seized that opportunity. He's the first player to come in at left guard, center, and right guard for the starters.
Kendall has become a reliable pass blocker and better processes reading the defensive line. He's the top option on the interior heading into Week 1.
Moore continues to make the case he should be on this roster, and is making tings very difficult for the Eagles. How does a team cut a player from a team after having a productive summer? Hollywood Brown's contract plays a role in Moore's future.
All Moore can do is stack good days. If he's consistently good, hard to leave him off the roster as a WR4 or WR5. There's a spot for him on this team.
Ringo may make this team by default due to the injuries at cornerback. The Eagles simply need a proven cornerback behind the starters on the 53 -- and Ringo provides that.
Besides that, Ringo stacked up a few good practices -- and a good preseason game -- last week. Ringo is also an excellent special teams player so he should make the 53 based on that reputation.
Would be shocking if Ringo doesn't make the 53 at this stage.
Shipley had a strong week in the joint practices, the highlight being a long touchdown on a wheel route that was one of his best plays of camp. Thanks to the Dameon Pierce hamstring injury, Shiple has taken full advantage of the open reps at RB3 -- and likely sealed his roster spot.
Even a poor preseason performance shouldn't hurt Shipley at this rate. He just needs to continue stacking good practices over the final week.
The Eagles tried Hinton at guard this offseason, hoping he can be a swing tackle and make the roster due to position versatility. Hinton has struggled at tackle and guard, and doesn't appear there will be a roster spot waiting for him.
Willie Lampkin and Drew Kendall has both passed Hinton on the pecking order. So has John Ojekwu. Tells you all you need to know.
All of a sudden a pectoral injury the Eagles weren't concerned about being long term may last into Week 1. The Eagles are certainly preparing for Greenard not being ready for the opener, and will have to make a roster decision regarding the PUP by August 30.
Time to brace a slow start for Greenard this season, whenever he hits the field. He still needs time to get into game shape as well. The Eagles don't need Greenard in the short term, but will if they want to win a Super Bowl.
Cooper should be on this team, yet he's not going to be the WR3. The Eagles starting Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore with Dontayvion Wicks this week gave both players reps with the first team, but they also have a more valuable skill set than Cooper.
All Cooper needs is a good week of practice to make the team, but he's filling out the final wide receiver spot on this team more than anything else. If the Eagles have to play Cooper a significant amount of snaps in any game, the wide receiver position is in trouble.
Stowers has struggled throughout the summer, most notably with his pass blocking and inability to get open. The catches Stowers makes are quick passes, and he struggles to gain separation downfield.
The Eagles may have to start Stowers as a TE3 and a healthy scratch, but there isn't much depth at tight end on this roster. Stowers is going to be have to figure things out fast.
The QB2 battle isn't over in the slightest, but Andy Dalton is getting more opportunities than McKee this late in the game. Dalton is getting more reps with the second team than Mckee and played the opening quarter in the preseason opener.
McKee doesn't appear to firmly grasp the offense and has been inconsistent with his throws. His timing hasn't been as fluid as in years' past either. He should still be on the roster based off how Cole Payton is playing, but the QB2 hopes are fading.

title: Steelers Might Have Long-Term LB Solution Developing
full_text:
In an inside linebacker room that has an uncertain future, Carson Bruener might be setting himself up as a major piece of the puzzle for the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Bruener, whose father, Mark, played tight end for the Steelers from 1995 to 2003 and later become a scout for the organization, was a seventh-round pick out of Washington in the 2025 NFL Draft.
The 25-year-old appeared in all 17 of Pittsburgh's contests during his rookie campaign, logging 287 snaps on special teams in the process.
Bruener finished with just one defensive rep on the year, but if his play from the team's preseason game against the New York Jets can carry over into the regular season, he may force himself into a larger role moving forward.
After recording 52 total snaps in the preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers (per Pro Football Focus ), Bruener was on the field for just 17 reps vs. New York.
Nine of those snaps came on defense, and he certainly maximized his opportunity over that sample size.
On the Jets' last drive of the first half, Bruener first broke up a pass that was intended for Jelani Woods before bull-rushing Kene Nwangwu in the backfield and sacking Cade Klubnik on the very next play.
New York proceeded to miss a 59-yard field goal as time expired in the half, and Bruener was perhaps the leading reason why the Jets were kept off the board in that instance.
During his halftime interview with Missi Matthews, Mike McCarthy went out of his way to highlight Bruener's performance.
"Well, I mean, there's still a lot of ball," McCarthy said . "There's a lot going on here. One thing we really emphasized was finishing plays. I thought Carson Bruener, that's what we're looking for... We need more of that throughout the second half."
With the recent addition of Elandon Roberts, who was also impressive against the Jets , it appears likely that the Steelers will include five inside linebackers on their initial 53-man roster.
As the fifth option amongst that group behind Patrick Queen, Payton Wilson, Cole Holcomb and Roberts, Bruener isn't going to be featured much on defense, if at all.
Because Queen and Roberts are slated to become free agents after the season ends while Wilson and Holcomb will both be in the final years of their deals, however, Pittsburgh should be incentivized to keep giving Bruener auditions and see how he progresses as the only player at the position group under contract beyond 2027.
He's taken some clear steps forward from where he stood as a rookie, and at a position like inside linebacker where it takes time to adapt and grow at the NFL level, the assumption is that Bruener is only going to continue to improve from here.
It's too early to declare that Bruener could turn into a long-term starter for the Steelers, but at the very least he's putting himself on the radar beyond his usual special teams duties.

title: Steelers Need to Have Kick Returner Replacement Ready
full_text:
As inconceivable as it was even a matter of weeks ago, Pittsburgh Steelers rookie Kaden Wetjen might be on thin ice.
On the penultimate play of the first quarter, the fourth-round pick fumbled on a punt return and nearly handed the New York Jets fantastic field position at the Steelers ' 31-yard line.
Wetjen was bailed out after it was ruled that New York was out-of-bounds before it gained possession of the ball upon recovering it. That doesn't mean it wasn't still a huge mistake for him, however.
Head coach Mike McCarthy didn't shy away from delivering a pointed evaluation of where Wetjen stood earlier in the week either, telling reporters that, "we've got to get him to clean up his everyday stuff, the mental errors."
Wetjen's 74-yard catch and five-yard touchdown in the preseason opener led to some intensified optimism surrounding his offensive impact, but with no catches against the Jets and with McCarthy clearly asking for more from him, it's hard to feel confident in where he stands at the moment.
If Wetjen doesn't work out as a return man, and it's still far too early to know whether or not that'll be the case, who could Pittsburgh turn to as his replacement(s)?
Both Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle have experience returning kicks as recently as the 2025 campaign, with the former going for 205 yards on eight attempts while the latter posted 197 yards on eight returns last year.
Warren is currently listed as the second-team kick returner while Dowdle is the second-team punt returner and third-team kick returner on Pittsburgh's depth chart .
Should the Steelers try and avoid giving either of their top two running backs too heavy of a workload in that department, perhaps Roman Wilson could emerge as a punt return option after putting in some work in that role throughout training camp this summer.
Another running back in Travis Homer, who has a real shot of making the 53-man roster, has returned 19 kicks for 473 yards and a touchdown during his NFL career. Just two of those tries have come since the beginning of the 2021 campaign, though.
The issue there is that Homer has been the personal protector on the punt team, and Pittsburgh may not want to pull him out of that spot so that he can return punts instead.
Seventh-round rookie Eli Heidenreich is increasingly unlikely to crack the 53-man roster.
In a scenario where Wetjen's handle on the return man duties is relinquished, however, Heidenreich would immediately become a prime candidate to take over in his place.
The Navy product and Pittsburgh native only returned nine kicks with one fair catch on a punt during his time in college, but he worked as a return man during training camp and has the tools to potentially thrive in that role.
Max Hurleman, who's on the wrong side of the roster bubble and returned a combined 62 kicks and punts throughout his college career, would be another name to watch. He brought back two kicks for 58 yards alongside a punt for 14 yards against the Jets  and has some juice back there that could be worth tapping into for the Steelers.
D'Shawn Jamison also doesn't have much of a case to make the 53-man roster as of now. He did rack up 1,435 yards and two touchdowns across 53 kick returns during his time at Texas to go with 362 yards and a score on 44 punt returns, though, so if he makes the practice squad and is elevated or if he eventually signs to the active roster, he could make a splash too.

title: Same Problem Returning for Steelers' Roman Wilson
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Disappointment is the first word that comes to mind when evaluating the Pittsburgh Steelers' second preseason game against the New York Jets.
From quarterbacks to the line, every member of the Steelers offense looked out of sorts and discombobulated. Calling anyone from that contest a standout player would be disingenuous.
For young players like quarterbacks Will Howard and Drew Allar, those struggles are expected and embraced. It's one thing to watch Eli Heidenreich make a mistake or Doneiko Slaughter take an ill-timed penalty. The big problem is when veterans who are supposed to be integral pieces of the regular season roster flash warning signs. Unfortunately for wide receiver Roman Wilson, that same problem returned against the Jets.
The monster reared its ugly head for Wilson. Over his first two seasons, it felt like Wilson was undeservedly in former head coach Mike Tomlin's doghouse. But after watching his performance against the Jets, maybe Tomlin's frustrations were warranted.
Wilson is an excellent athlete and hard worker, but his mastery of the position leaves so much to be desired. He doesn't recognize the small nuances and differences in coverages and situations, and because of that inability, he often puts himself in poor positions to help the offense.
This is precisely what happened during Howard's first interception of the game. As the team was driving downfield, Wilson worked a route across the middle of the field, Instead of moving toward the incoming pass intended for him, Wilson drifted toward the endzone and waited for the ball to come to him.
As a result, the creeping safety was able to read the play and jump the route. Howard made a poor throw, but Wilson did his quarterback no favors in the process.
The second interception truly lies on Wilson, in my opinion. Once again working against man coverage, Wilson's speed allowed him to gain a bit of separation, but instead of keeping his route perpendicular to the sidelines, he once again drifted upfield. The same criticism against Howard's first interception can be levied against him in this instance as well, as he should have led his receiver more. Once again, however, Wilson's sloppy route-running contributed to the turnover.
The Steelers enter the 2026 season with the expectation that they have more weapons for quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and Wilson was a key part of that. As the third receiver on the depth chart behind DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr., the offense is expected to take a significant leap in the coming campaign.
But if Wilson doesn't run routes with the precision Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy demand, he will quickly find himself relegated to the sidelines once more.
And that means the Steelers are again looking around for answers at the wide receiver position. Rookie Germie Bernard, the team's recent second-round draft pick, has looked like a polished professional in his first game action. That skill and confidence clashes with Rodgers' historical reliance on veteran receivers. Something has to give for the Pittsburgh offense, and Wilson could have made that decision so much easier.
As the preseason wraps up, the same issues are already emerging for Roman Wilson . It's a shame for the former third-round pick, because the talent and drive are clearly there. So too, is a flashing warning sign that McCarthy and the Steelers can't ignore.

title: Steelers Have a Massive Problem They Need to Fix
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The left side of the Pittsburgh Steelers' offensive line found their way in the second preseason game . Left tackle Troy Fautanu was already back to his All-Pro form, Mason McCormick has transitioned well to the left guard position, and Zach Frazier is, well, Zach Frazier.
The right side, however, looked even worse than they did in the preseason opener. Dylan Cook, the starting right tackle, has lost rep after rep in two appearances. Spencer Anderson has been up-and-down in his snaps, but neither has assured head coach Mike McCarthy that they can anchor the strong side of the offensive line. McCarthy rotated in Brock Hoffman and Broderick Jones during the first half, showing that he hasn't quite made up his mind when it comes to that tandem.
It's fair that McCarthy hasn't made up his mind. How could he? The options are grim right now, regardless of if you're discussing the starter or going further down the depth chart. With just one game separating this team from the regular season, the Steelers have a growing and concerning problem at right tackle.
It might be a bit dramatic, seeing as he hasn't played a game in the NFL yet, but the Steelers' final hope is first-round rookie Max Iheanachor. The 21st overall pick in the 2026 draft had the starting RT job nearly stolen from Cook, but an injury suffered early in training camp derailed his early ascension.
But now, the Steelers are being forced to rely on the inexperienced Iheanachor as the starter on the offensive line opposite Fautanu.
That's a tall order for Iheanachor. Not because he doesn't have what it takes, but because the pressure is quickly turning all the way up in Pittsburgh. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers and company want to make a legitimate run for the Lombardi Trophy. In order to get there, they need to solve this right tackle issue. Iheanachor is currently their best, and perhaps only, remaining in-house option.
With the Steelers and general manager Omar Khan, the trade market can never be discounted. They've taken multiple big swings via trade over the past few seasons, and with the team all-in for the 2026 campaign, it might make sense to dial the phones once again.
The only problem is that the Steelers might not have a willing trade partner right now. Teams are still deciding on their final 53-man rosters ahead of the regular season, and some teams might not be willing to part with anyone while they figure things out. By the time they are, who knows what type of return they will seek for a starting-caliber tackle.
For the Steelers, the trade market is a dangerous route to pursue.
There is one last resort the Steelers could pivot to, but admittedly, it doesn't inspire confidence or represent an obvious upgrade. A few free agents are still available on the open market, and could be a short-term solution while Iheanachor makes his way back to 100%.
One player is former Cincinnati Bengals first-round pick, Jonah Williams. He was a solid tackle in Cincinnati before injuries derailed his past two seasons with the Arizona Cardinals. The last thing the Steelers need is another quasi-healthy right tackle in the mix, but if he had a clean bill of health, he brings 74 games of starting experience to a needy position.
Another player with starting experience who could be had for cheap is former Cleveland Browns lineman Jack Conklin. With 114 starts over his NFL career with the Browns and Tennessee Titans, he would be a true veteran mentor for Iheanachor and Fautanu. Injuries are also a concern for Conklin, but if the Steelers are desperate enough, he might be worth a shot.

title: 5 Winners, 4 Losers From Steelers Loss to Jets
full_text:
After blowing out the Green Bay Packers in the first game of the preseason by a score of 28-9, the Pittsburgh Steelers were on the other side of a beatdown this time around.
The New York Jets walked into Acrisure Stadium and dominated the Steelers at every turn, resulting in a shutout 17-0 loss for the latter. Pittsburgh cleaned up the penalties after they were a major issue vs. Green Bay, but the offensive line floundered once again while the unit as a whole went 5-of-16 on third downs.
With that, here are five winners and six losers from the contest for the Steelers.
Regardless of if he is a 53-man roster lock or not , Howard did himself zero favors against the Jets.
The 24-year-old had some flashes, including a 16-yard strike to Ben Skowronek for a first down in New York territory, but he followed it up a few plays later with his first of two interceptions on the night.
Howard's lack of standout arm strength was evident on both of his picks, and overall it was a game to forget for the former sixth-round pick as his hopes of winning the backup quarterback job over Mason Rudolph seem all but dashed.
Bruener is a key component of Pittsburgh's special teams units, but he appears to be making some strides on the defensive side of the ball as well.
The inside linebacker logged just one defensive snap as a rookie last season. After logging a pass breakup and a sack on back-to-back plays during the Jets' final drive of the first half, however, Bruener is starting to prove that he can hold his own on that side of the ball.
Jones had a real rough go of it against New York. Whether it was David Bailey crushing him for a sack on 3rd-and-9 with a little under five minutes to go in the first quarter or Nate Lynn logging a sack of his own on him in the fourth quarter, the 2023 first-rounder's struggles were on full display as he took on another heavy workload.
It was never going to be pretty for Jones while building back his strength after suffering a significant neck injury last November that required spinal fusion surgery.
That doesn't excuse his poor play, though, and there have to be some serious questions about his viability moving forward.
Compared to most of his Steelers teammates, Sawyer has little to play for in the preseason when it comes to securing a larger role, considering he's set as the team's No. 4 EDGE rusher.
Still, Sawyer went out there and made his presence known with some impressive stops against the run all while registering a sack of Cade Klubnik at the end of the first half.
Though the Jets failed to gain possession on the sideline, Wetjen's fumble on a kick return during the closing seconds of the first quarter was simply inexcusable.
The fourth-round rookie also didn't have a single target or catch at wide receiver a week after posting 79 yards and a touchdown, putting him in somewhat of a treacherous spot leading into the preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills.
McCarthy made it a point to challenge Wetjen while talking to the media this week by stating, "We've got to get him to clean up his everyday stuff, the mental errors," but the Iowa product didn't rise to the challenge vs. New York.
Jenkins played like he knew his chances of cracking Pittsburgh's 53-man roster were on the line.
The 32-year-old, who's entering the 10th season of his career, was all over the field and caused a ton of pressure while being utilized as a blitzer by defensive coordinator Patrick Graham.
From forcing an intentional grounding call on Klubnik to finishing with two quarterback hits and making plays against the run, Jenkins' stock is pointing upwards.
Driscoll, in all likelihood, was never going to make the Steelers' 53-man roster.
For a veteran with 18 starts and nearly 1,500 offensive snaps under his belt, however, he looked surprisingly unpolished as he gave up a sack and generally was beat far too often in pass protection throughout the contest.
A practice squad candidate who wasn't exactly stout vs. Green Bay either, Driscoll has been a disappointment so far this preseason.
After signing a one-year deal last week to return to Pittsburgh following a one-year stopover with the Las Vegas Raiders, where he played for Graham, Roberts reminded everyone why he has the potential to be such a force in the middle of the defense.
The 32-year-old single-handedly wrecked New York's initial offensive series of the second half, showing off his recognition skills against the run before clicking and closing into the flats to stop the Jets one yard short of a first down on 4th-and-3.
The fact that he remained on the field through the fourth quarter was surprising to say the least, but Roberts made the most of the opportunity.
Not only did Spears-Jennings force an incompletion with a big hit on Jets running back Sam Scott halfway through the third quarter, but he also drew a block in the back penalty while serving as a gunner on Pittsburgh's punt team.
The seventh-round rookie was one of the stories of training camp for the Steelers, and that's carried over to the preseason thus far.

title: Time to Say Goodbye to Steelers' Will Howard
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers gave second-year quarterback Will Howard the golden opportunity he's been waiting for. In the team's second preseason game against the New York Jets, Howard started and worked with the first-team offense. The hope was that he would prove he was ready to leapfrog Mason Rudolph and assume backup duty responsibilites.
That's not quite how things turned out for the Steelers' 2025 sixth-round draft pick. The crowd at Acrisure Stadium provided a hero's welcome, but the on-field performance didn't live up to the hype.
Instead, Howard may have played himself out a job in Pittsburgh.
Credit to the young quarterback, who called out his own disappointing performance after the team's 17-0 loss to the Jets.
"Things to learn from. Just the performance wasn't up to par," he said. "It's a shame because those were both good drives and I thought we were moving the ball really well. And one of the first things we talk about is protecting the football... Just gotta be better and learn from it."
Howard has never lacked intelligence or the professionalism that many covet for the starting quarterback position. If only that were the determining factor in making the Steelers' 53-man roster, but the on-field performance speaks for itself. He finished the game 10-of-15 passing, throwing two interceptions. One was a characteristic turnover from a young quarterback who failed to read the defense correctly.
The second one is up for debate regarding who is responsible, but the fact remains that he failed to lead any touchdown drives in a start he absolutely needed to deliver. As a result, his chances of making the roster have hit rock bottom.
The Steelers have been toying with the potential of keeping four quarterbacks on the roster.
That possibility and line of thinking have likely ended after the second preseason game. It's not all Howard's fault, and he was far from the only player who struggled. The problem is that no one was under more pressure to perform well.
Howard wasn't able to seal the deal, and he might be looking for a new NFL franchise. There is, however, a small chance that he can redeem himself in the preseason finale.
The team will likely play both youngsters against the Buffalo Bills, much like they did against the Jets. If Howard is given the chance to start again, he can salvage his chances in Pittsburgh. He'd have to be picture-perfect, but it would be his last chance to continue playing for the Steelers.

title: Will Howard Sends Message After Steelers Loss
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Will Howard had his opportunity to shine for the Pittsburgh Steelers and couldn't take advantage.
The second-year quarterback threw two interceptions and completed 10 of 15 passes for just 74 yards as the Steelers lost 17-0 against the New York Jets.
It wasn't the night Howard was looking for, and maybe the one that ends his chances of making the Steelers' roster. But he's not stressing out about the situation. As he says, playing quarterback comes with ups and downs, and being able to ride the waves of a game, even when things turn out poorly.
"Listen, I mean, you play quarterback in the NFL, you're going to throw interceptions," Howard said after the game. "I’ve played quarterback my whole life. I've thrown a lot of interceptions. It comes with the game. I feel like I've been through enough and seen enough that getting down after one pick isn't going to help anything. It's all about how you come back. Obviously, you don't want to have a second one, but you got to come back after that. I mean, I think it's just banked reps. I've done it before and been able to bounce back. That gives you, kind of, confidence to — it's intrusive confidence, believing in yourself no matter what.
"I felt support from my teammates. They were patting me on the helmet, [saying] 'We got you.' I got to give a shoutout to them for picking me up, but really I don't blink. It's football. Bad things are going to happen. In a regular-season game, if I was playing the whole game, I'd have to come back in the second half and go win the game. That's the reality of it. Again, learn from, grow from, get better."
This is a wait-and-see answer. Howard has one more week and a game against the Buffalo Bills to prove he belongs on the roster in 2026. It'll require an even better performance now, but not one that's impossible to come up with.
Howard has the support of his teammates and his coaching staff, but he's not fighting with his back against the wall. Really, the perfect time to prove he's able to fight back as a quarterback.
It's the most important week of his young career. One that will likely decide if he's got a real shot to eventually be a starting quarterback in Pittsburgh, or if he's headed to the practice squad with a lot of uncertainty moving forward.

title: Five Takeaways: Will Howard Loses Steelers Roster Spot
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers fall to 1-1 in the preseason as their explosive offense against the Green Bay Packers died down against the New York Jets.
The Steelers offense couldn't produce any points in their 17-0 loss to the Jets at Acrisure Stadium. But truthfully, the defense didn't help much.
It was a dud of a ballgame for the black and gold, but in the preseason, that happens. And the Steelers are grateful to be able to work through their concerns now instead of during the regular season.
Leaving the game and heading into the final game of the preseason, here's what stood out about the Steelers' loss to New York.
The Steelers might have a pretty decent third safety. Rayshawn Jenkins started in place of Jaquan Brisker, and while he didn't do much in coverage, he got into the backfield on multiple occasions to disrupt plays.
Jenkins might not be the interception machine that the Steelers need at the position, but he's definitely someone who can make plays as a run supporter. In Patrick Graham's defense, where disguises are endless, he might fit well.
Mike McCarthy didn't hold back last week when talking about the Steelers' fourth-round pick Kaden Wetjen. His message was clear - Wetjen needs to be able to do more than return kicks and punts in order to be on this team.
Well, he didn't do that. And not only did Wetjen produce nothing on offense in his second preseason game, but he became a liability on special teams as well.
Wetjen fumbled on a punt return, seemingly handing the ball to a Jets defender along the sideline. While the Jets player didn't get both feet in bounds before going out of bounds, the play looked brutal for the rookie.
Keeping a player who's only a returner is tough to do, but it's impossible for a team to do if that returner isn't good at returning. That's becoming the case for Wetjen.
The Steelers desperately need their first-round pick to return from injury this week. If not, it's time for them to start looking for help at right tackle , but their options on the current roster aren't good enough.
Everyone is talking about Broderick Jones giving up a brutal sack to Will Howard against David Bailey, but he was only half of the problem. Dylan Cook got beat on almost every rep, with his worst play coming on the interception from Howard to Andre Cisco.
Cook ends the rep off his own two feet and back over 10 yards from where the ball was snapped. It was tough, but it wasn't out of character.
The Steelers either need Iheanachor to return or they need to start making phone calls. Otherwise, they're in a lot of trouble because their right tackle position is the clearest weak link on the roster.
Will Howard just simply doesn't have what's needed to be the team's backup quarterback. He plays the role well, and he definitely has the mental makeup to succeed, but the arm strength isn't there, and it's so noticeable.
Howard finished the night completing 10 of 15 passes for 74 yards and two interceptions. On both turnovers, he stared down the wide receiver, leading to what looked like easy interceptions.
This was Howard's one shot to prove he belongs on the team and he couldn't shine. What does it mean? Well, chances are, it means he's going to be off the roster in the next few weeks.
Keeping four quarterbacks was hard to justify. Now, it might be impossible.
JETS GET AN INTERCEPTION 🔥 (via @nyjets ) pic.twitter.com/rQlHnDgjTI
Drew Allar is now through two preseason games and continues to look like everything the Steelers wanted. He's not a starting quarterback just yet, but he's progressed throughout his time in Pittsburgh, and his showings in-game prove he's capable of making plays with the ball in his hand.
Allar was moving out of pressure while keeping his eyes downfield throughout the second half, and most of the time, his offensive line wasn't helping much. Still, even when getting hit, Allar made passes that had the crowd roaring and kept the Steelers' drives alive as much as he could.
Drew Allar dime 🎯 (via @steelers ) pic.twitter.com/cuTyPYUcoG
Now, it's time for Allar to start. He's shown what he can do against opponents' third- and fourth-string players; now he needs to play against first- and second-team players. And the Steelers' preseason finale in Buffalo is the perfect place to do so.
Pittsburgh should put Allar out there as the starter against the Bills and see how he does. He's on the roster without even needing to do anything more, so they might as well give him a bigger test than they have had through two exhibitions.

title: Report: Steelers Make Will Howard Decision
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers already have a plan in place with Will Howard when it comes to their 53-man roster.
According to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac during an appearance on DVE's pre-game show, the Steelers have made the decision to keep Howard on the roster before they begin their second game of the preseason against the New York Jets at Acrisure Stadium.
"It's a question of whether they wanna keep four or three," Dulac said . "But I will tell you, they have already decided they are keeping their two young quarterbacks, Will Howard and Drew Allar."
If Pittsburgh is in fact locked in on the idea of holding onto four quarterbacks heading into the regular season, which is a rather unusual roster quirk around the league, Howard wouldn't have to worry about being cut and/or made available for trade as the odd man out if he were to lose the backup job to Mason Rudolph.
Perhaps the Steelers could give Howard some ease of mind should that be the case, which would allow the 2025 sixth-round pick to play more freely.
Still, the 24-year-old is on the horn when it comes to making up ground in the race for the No. 2 role with Rudolph in addition to proving himself as a potential long-term solution in the Steelers' quarterback room.
Howard was impressive in his preseason debut against the Green Bay Packers last week, throwing for 86 yards and completing seven of his nine attempts through the air.
He'll need to build on that performance against the Jets as the starter , however, and keep stacking good days as he continues to develop in Mike McCarthy's offense.
Otherwise, Howard would run the risk of losing the backup job and being a gameday inactive throughout his second year in the NFL.
Rudolph isn't suiting up against the Jets after McCarthy stated he, "saw what he needed to," from the 31-year-old vs. Green Bay, serving as additional proof that he has the inside track for the backup job behind Aaron Rodgers.
Though Howard now appears to be a lock for the 53-man roster, it's hard to imagine Pittsburgh moving Rudolph unless another team comes in with an enticing trade offer.
"I can't imagine them not keeping Mason Rudolph," Dulac said. "I just can't in any situation. But I guess that's something they still have to sort out."
The Steelers are clearly fans of what Rudolph brings to the table, which is why they seem to be attached at the hip with him and will keep him in all likelihood, but maybe some conversations still are yet to be had.

title: Steelers' Christian Kuntz Makes Bold QB Claim
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The biggest challenge for Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy is identifying and developing the next franchise quarterback.
The Steelers are giving him a bit of a head start, with a pair of young, internal options to work with. Will Howard and Drew Allar have earned high praise and compliments from teammates and the coaching staff over the course of training camp.
So much so, that it’s led one of their teammates to make a bold proclamation. Steelers long snapper Christian Kuntz recently claimed on his podcast, The Christian Kuntz Podcast, that the team’s next franchise quarterback is already on the roster.
”What a situation to walk into. You’re a 23-year-old quarterback and you get to learn from Coach McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers,” he said, “Just to come into that room for those guys, man, is special. It’s an opportunity. And I think the future quarterback of the Steelers is in-house right now. One of those three guys I truly think is the future of the Steelers.”
This was a quote that’s sure to feed the preseason conversation mill. Kuntz is clearly focusing a lot of this statement on the youngsters, but he ends it by referring to “those three guys,” when referring to the options for a future franchise QB.
Maybe he was referring to Allar, the team’s recent third-round pick. He had the most impressive debut of of any rookie quarterback in the preseason, throwing for two touchdowns and running for an additional one himself.
Now, he’s set to play a whole half of football against the New York Jets, ready to prove that he’s the guy to invest in long-term. There’s no denying the strides he’s taken under McCarthy, but has it been enough to convince Kuntz and the rest of the Steelers that he’s QB1 of the future?
Maybe Kuntz was referring to the second-year player, Will Howard . Howard is set to make his first ever NFL start, albeit in a preseason contest, and face the stiffest competition of his young career.
He’s being, quite literally, thrown into the fire. If he succeeds, he will seriously disrupt the team’s plans for quarterback, but that’s a big if.
As the team awaits the next kick-off, maybe Kuntz was sharing his and the organization’s belief in Howard as the heir apparent at quarterback.
Kuntz may have been taking a diplomatic approach when he said that there were three options for the next franchise quarterback, but there continues to be a growing belief in Mason Rudolph . Both his teammates and the coaching staff continue to shine a light on the 31-year-old gunslinger,
Maybe it’s a ploy to get trade value for Rudolph. Maybe it’s a reflection of the fact that this organization has a significant level of belief in Rudolph, both now and moving forward.

title: Sam Darnold Reveals What Makes Jadarian Price 'Special' After Joint Practice
full_text:
Anytime a team uses a first-round pick on a running back, there will be plenty of skepticism. Often considered one of the easiest positions to replace on offense, running backs don't always get the respect they should when it comes to the draft. Those questions only grow louder when that first-round pick is used on a running back who wasn't the starter for his collegiate team.
That was the case for the Seattle Seahawks this year when they decided to use the 32nd overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft on Jadarian Price out of Notre Dame. While Price has all the tools to be a feature back , he happened to share the field with Jeremiyah Love, who was the third overall pick for the Arizona Cardinals.
In Seattle, Price is vying for the starting spot and is battling with George Holani while Zach Charbonnet recovers from ACL surgery . We have yet to see Price play in an NFL game after he sat out the preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys . If we do see him on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans, however, Sam Darnold believes he will prove to be "special."
Following their joint practice with the Titans on Friday, Darnold had plenty of praise for the rookie running back. Darnold especially loved how Price can run between the tackles as well as outside, but also sees him as a threat in the passing game.
"He's a special player," Darnold said via Ari Horton and John Boyle of the Seahawks' official website . "He's a really special player. He brings a different facet to the offense that only a guy like him can bring. Whether it's catching passes out of the backfield, catching screens, running in between the tackles, outside of the tackles, he can really do it all. And I know he's just going to continue to get better and learn."
Price made several grabs during the session, including a big gain during seven-on-sevens. He also ripped off a long run during 11-on-11, which was an encouraging sight after he missed time during camp.
As for his versatility, this should come as no surprise to anyone who watched Price at Notre Dame. While he didn't get many targets as a receiver, he made the most of them as he had 87 yards and two touchdowns on just six receptions in 2025. He also proved to be a weapon on special teams, scoring two touchdowns while averaging 37.5 yards per return on kickoffs .
Price proved to be capable of helping his team in multiple ways at Notre Dame and should do the same with the Seahawks.

title: 4 Seahawks Fighting For a Roster Spot in Preseason Week 2 vs. Titans
full_text:
After facing off with one another in a joint practice on Friday in Nashville, the Seattle Seahawks and Tennessee Titans will take the field for a Preseason Week 2 matchup on Sunday night.
Preseason games might not always be full of excitement, but that doesn't mean there aren't reasons to watch, especially for diehard fans interested in roster construction. While the coaching staff learns plenty during training camp and joint practices, players can still make a strong case for themselves during the preseason.
That's especially true for the following four Seahawks players who will enter Sunday night's meeting with the Titans fighting for their place on the roster.
Signed this offseason as a free agent to give Seattle depth at offensive tackle, Bobby Hart is already in danger of not making the team. Hart hasn't stood out in camp but what really has him feeling the heat is his performance against the Cowboys in Week 1. Hart gave up a sack against James Houston and struggled to slow down rookie Malachi Lawrence.
The one thing that helps him is that Seattle doesn't have anyone else proving to be a vastly superior option, but Hart is definitely entering this game with plenty of weight on his shoulders.
After the Seahawks signed Trevon Diggs, both Nehemiah Pritchett and Noah Igbinoghene find themselves on the roster bubble. Of the two, however, Pritchett might be in the most immediate danger. While Diggs will likely move ahead of each, Seahawks On SI's Jeremy Brener noted that Igbinoghene's work in the slot shields him slightly from Diggs' addition since the former NFL interception leader plays primarily on the outside.
That means Pritchett enters Week 2 of the NFL preseason feeling the pressure. He already finds himself fighting for his spot on the team with players such as rookie third-round pick Julian Neal already ahead of him. This latest addition only makes it tougher for him to find a path to the 53-man roster .
Jadarian Price was expected to be the RB1 this season while Zach Charbonnet recovers from ACL surgery, but George Holani had different plans. Holani was a standout throughout camp and inserted his name into the conversation. The question is whether that remains the case after he averaged just 3.5 yards per attempt against the Cowboys last week. The offensive line did him no favors, but if Holani really wants to hold off Price, he needs a better showing this weekend.
Behind Price and Holani is Emanuel Wilson, who signed with Seattle in the offseason . Wilson has yet to make his debut, but has a chance to see some action on Sunday, assuming he's recovered enough from his hamstring injury. If he does play, he needs to prove he deserves to be in the rotation. If he sits out again, his chance to earn a significant role early in the year could begin to fade.

title: How Does ESPN Rank the Seahawks by Position Group?
full_text:
We’re almost done with the NFL offseason, so any and all offseason-coded content should get pushed out now before it’s too late. Yesterday, ESPN published an article exploring every team’s roster, ultimately ranking every positional group individually. Let’s see how the Seahawks come out here, and sort each ranking into one of three categories
These rankings strike me as appropriate. Wide Receiver at sixth reflects a belief that Rashid Shaheed will take big steps forward this year and produce more in line with what he did in New Orleans, as well as Cooper Kupp possibly having a resurgence after an impressive training camp. EDGE ranking low, but not at the bottom, is also reasonable given the question marks.
The interior defensive line coming in at first is a no-brainer in my mind, and we got a writeup in the article for it as well. Mike Clay gives love to Leonard Williams , Byron Murphy II, and Jarran Reed, as well as their elite run defense, but didn’t mention Rylie Mills. Throw in what he figures to do this season, and Seattle is head and shoulders above anyone else here.
I’m not sure how Sam Darnold can be considered a bottom half of the league starter after two straight successful seasons and a super bowl. And if this list is also supposed to factor in backups, it becomes even more dubious. For some reason, Ernest Jones can’t get any respect this offseason despite making All-Pro, and there’s no love for Knight as a quality backup.
Assuming the safety ranking includes Nick Emmanwori, which I suspect it does, that should be higher as well given how good Julian Love is when healthy, which many have seemingly forgotten. And while I can understand not buying Elijah Arroyo as an impact player yet , A.J. Barner alone should fetch more than the 18th best tight ends in football.
It’s not a huge difference, but between inexperience and injury I feel our running back room is bottom five. The article actually identified running back as a unit to watch, pointing out Price’s inexperience as a pass catcher and Charbonnet’s torn ACL . Given the scrambling the team has done in recent weeks at cornerback, top five seems high there as well.
The offensive line is tricky. I could see the unit as a whole being worthy of the 8th spot, but that’s mostly because of the continuity the group has together. Individually, I don’t think the talent level is quite there, although it’s not far off either. So, it’s all a matter of perspective.
