title: 3 Takeaways as Titans Bounce Back in a Major Way in Joint Practice With Seahawks
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans held their second joint practice of the preseason today against the Seattle Seahawks. Last week's meeting with the San Francisco 49ers resulted in punches thrown and, overall, an underwhelming outing from the Titans.
With a game under their belts and the benefit to host this time, Tennessee had all the makings of a recovery entering Friday's two-team meeting.
Recover, they certainly did. Here are three major takeaways from the Titans' practice as the team now prepares to face Seattle on Sunday night.
We knew it was going to be a good day when Cam Ward reportedly hit Elic Ayomanor for a score on a cross-body on the opposite side of the field. Tennessee's scoring unit needed a big outing in the worst way, and save for one would-be pick-six from Ward, they got it.
In addition to Ward finding Ayomanor (as well as a notable TD to Daniel Bellinger in a two-minute drill), Mitch Trubisky found Chimere Dike for a toe-tapping touchdown on a rollout, as well as Xavier Restrepo on a 40-yard long ball. Will Levis even got involved, also hitting Restrepo for a 15-yard gain in a highlight play for two guys teetering on the roster's edge.
Tennessee also excelled on the ground. New signee D'Ernest Johnson worked his way into the end zone for a five-yard score, while Tony Pollard and Julius Chestnut also carved avenues to score.
Even veteran back Michael Carter got in, fielding extensive work with both Trubisky and Levis' units. There were a few turnovers to clean up, as well as a weaker second 11-on-11 period when starters re-took the field, but this was a net positive day for Tennessee's offense.
Tennessee's secondary has endured their fair share of loud criticism this past week after an unproductive few days with the San Francisco 49ers. In today's event with the Seahawks, Alontae Taylor helped lead an encouraging response.
In addition to nabbing a pick-six from Sam Darnold late in practice, the Titans' $58 million man reportedly managed to break up a few passes in what was almost certainly his best showing of the preseason so far. At one point, the Titans had allowed just one touchdown in 12 snaps in the red zone.
Cor'Dale Flott continued to struggle, with Darnold at one point throwing a touchdown over his head to running back George Holani. But even if worries about Flott's own hefty contract continue, the unit as a whole came out strong against Seattle and posted a few much-needed signs before Sunday.
Lastly, Carnell Tate thankfully returned to play vs. the Seahawks. While he would end up with a relatively quiet day - save for a jumping catch on the sideline - Tennessee's rookie receiver returning after a missed practice earlier this week elicits a massive sigh of relief.
Tate is someone that fans specifically are looking forward to seeing on Sunday, after he failed to catch a single pass in the Titans' preseason opener. His quick comeback confirms prior reports that he had been held out for stiffness only.
This means we may see Tate's first reception in a live game on Sunday. Robert Saleh's prized fourth-overall pick should be ready to ramp things up with a Titans team that just had exactly the sort of practice we needed to see.

title: Titans Sign DE Tanoh Kpassagnon and LB Milo Eifler: What Fans Need to Know
full_text:
Last week, the Tennessee Titans' already down-and-out secondary took another hit when safety Nazeeh Johnson was hit with a six-game suspension for violating the NFL's Performance-Enhancing Substances Policy. Johnson was most likely set to contribute in a depth role, but the Titans have still been forced to react to this change.
As a result, Tennessee placed Johnson on Reserve/Injured, releasing tight end Matt Lauter in the process to clear the way for two new pickups. Jim Wyatt reported that the Titans have signed defensive end Tanoh Kpassagnon and linebacker Milo Eifler on Friday.
The dual-signing comes right on the edge of Tennessee's joint practice with the Seattle Seahawks today, and just two days before the team face off on Sunday. Robert Saleh's defense loses one piece and gains two just over a week out from the roster-cut deadline.
The @Titans have signed DE Tanoh Kpassagnon and LB Milo Eifler. The team has released TE Matt Lauter and placed DB Nazeeh Johnson on Reserve/Injured. READ https://t.co/gIm19EUtQg pic.twitter.com/7GPJZmrkle
Here's everything you need to know about the two newest Titans.
Eifler's case is a little less complex than Kpassagnon, so we'll start there. The 28-year old linebacker's last appearance in the regular season came all the way back in 2022, where he competed in 10 games with the Washington Commanders. Eifler totaled four sacks that season.
Before being released by the Arizona Cardinals last May, Eifler appeared in brief stints with the New York Jets, Miami Dolphins, and Atlanta Falcons, too. He's a real journeyman at the LB position,  and will most likely end up in a short-term depth role for Tennessee.
Kpassagnon, on the other hand, could have an outside shot at some staying power in Nashville.
Since beginning his career with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2017, Kpassagnon has competed in every single regular season since, to varying degrees. He's broken the three-sack mark three times, most recently notching 3.5 with the New Orleans Saints in 2023.
After suffering a torn Achilles tendon in May of 2024, Kpassagnon's on-field presence seriously dwindled. He played in just four games with the Chicago Bears last season, logging five total tackles and one sack.
At 32 years old, the ceiling is only so high for Kpassagnon from here on out. But with a little time left to test the waters in the preseason, his signing makes sense if he were to stick around on a smaller deal. He clearly isn't out of gas just yet and is worth keeping a thumb on as the offseason winds down.

title: 3 Titans Players to Watch Closely in High-Stakes Joint Practice With Seahawks
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans' joint practice last week felt like the team getting their feet wet more than anything else. We saw a few early trends begin to develop against the San Francisco 49ers - trends that resulted in talking points from the preseason opener - but that was still just the beginning.
Now, just a little more than a week later, the stakes have been drastically heightened. With just nine days until roster cuts will be made, players have long left the preseason grace period and are now working for either an elevated role or a spot on the Titans' 53-man roster.
In today's joint practice with the Seattle Seahawks, ahead of Sunday's matchup in Nashville, three players are each fighting three unique battles.
Carmona has become one of the most consistent mentions for the Titans this summer. After being taken out of Arkansas in the fifth round of the NFL Draft, the right guard slowly climbed up Tennessee's depth chart. Currently, he's the favorite to win the starting gig over Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater.
That's what makes this joint practice - and really this weekend - so important. Carmona will have a shot this season either way, but another solid turn from him in live competition all but guarantees he'll be out on the first drive next month with the Titans offense.
It's been an unexpected ascension for the rookie, although an entirely welcome one given the state of the offensive line entering this offseason. Fingers crossed for another strong showing today.
On the opposite end of the spectrum compared to Carmona, Flott is a veteran cornerback who Tennessee paid handsomely to hold things down in the secondary this year. His questionable outing in last week's joint practice gave way to a game that saw him burned by Niners rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling. His 74 yards allowed (six completions on six targets) was impossible to spin.
The Titans' entire secondary needs a better week, but it's Flott specifically who stood out in the worst way in the opener. Starting with Friday's joint practice, he's the guy under the hottest light to improve in that unit.
Beating the Levis drum has become popular toward the end of camp, but you simply can't leave him off a list like this. With Trubisky seemingly healthy at the QB2 spot behind Cam Ward, Levis appears to be firmly out of the picture in Tennessee's quarterback room.
The only thing that could feasibly earn him a seat at this point would be a real knockout finish to the preseason. Even if Levis is essentially auditioning for other teams at this point, arguably nobody on the roster has more to play for than he does this week.
That makes Levis worth special attention in joint practice. It's all or nothing for a guy who was starting for the Titans just two seasons ago.

title: Titans' Running Back Room Dealt Perfect Bulletin Board Material for 2026 Season
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are set to return nearly the same running back room from last season in 2026, as Tony Pollard will be the starter and Tyjae Spears will likely be the backup. Rookie Nicholas Singleton could also receive snaps and serve as quality depth behind the two top backs.
Pollard is one of the most underrated backs in the league. The veteran has tallied four straight 1,000-yard campaigns, including two since joining Tennessee in free agency in 2024. However, it would be nice if Spears or Singleton could establish themselves as a solid No. 2 to take some pressure off Pollard and provide the offense with another dynamic playmaker.
The Titans have the potential to have a productive rushing attack this season, but Pro Football Focus doesn't have much faith in the running back group.
PFF recently released its preseason rankings of NFL running back rooms , and the Titans came in at No. 22. Tennessee's AFC South rivals, the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars, were lower, while the Indianapolis Colts were No. 9.
Tennessee's running backs, especially Pollard, should feel disrespected by this ranking . The position group is filled with exciting and versatile talent and is headlined by a player who has been one of the most productive rushers of the past few seasons.
The passing game should be a major weapon for the Titans, but don't rule out the running game as the possible engine of the offense. If the passing attack struggles, as we saw in the opening preseason game, offensive coordinator Brian Daboll will need Pollard, Spears, and his rushers to step up.
With the regular season on the horizon, the Titans running backs should use these rankings as bulletin board material. The position group isn't getting much love ahead of the season, and that disrespect should turn into powerful fuel.

title: 5 Winners, 4 Losers From Commanders’ Preseason Loss to Lions
full_text:
The Washington Commanders' 17-13 loss to the Detroit Lions was meaningless in the record books and priceless for roster evaluation . There were some good signs and some bad ones. The team also exposed a problem or two in the running game and several roster competitions. Some players were able to capitalize on the cases they had already built in camp, while others failed to take advantage of the opportunities they got. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn certainly got some meaningful film on Saturday.
Athan Kaliakmanis Saturday gave Athan Kaliakmanis the strongest evidence that the rookie deserves the competition he has with Sam Hartman for Washington's third spot behind Marcus Mariota. On the day, Kaliakmanis was 11-of-14 passing for 162 yards, with no turnovers and a 114.9 passer rating. It should be noted that he also took no sacks from behind an offensive line filled with replacements. The three longest plays of the day Saturday came from Kaliakmanis' passes: one to Nick Nash for 55 yards, Jaden Bradley for 30, and then another to Antonio Williams for 21. Kaliakmanis helped direct the team on an 11-play, 78-yard third-quarter scoring drive in which he looked the part. Verdict : Kaliakmanis definitely helped his case, as there is no realistic way the team can ignore that he has a firmer grasp on playing quarterback than Sam Hartman does at this point in their respective careers. Maurice Hurst II At a time when the team is looking for a pass-rushing defensive tackle after Johnny Newton went down with an injury, Maurice Hurst jumps out with two sacks in the Lions game. The Commanders were without Odafe Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson, and Dorance Armstrong, among others, on the defensive front. Verdict : His possible depth status could see an increase in reps after two sacks. Amik Robertson Washington's first touchdown was a product of both Daronte Jones seeing the issue and the Lions leaving Amik Robertson unguarded on a blitz off the left edge. The contact on the quarterback created the fumble that ultimately Joshua Josephs recovered in the end zone for a touchdown. Washington now has six takeaways through two preseason games, along with a better sense of how to create them, thanks to Jones' mentality through the scheme. Verdict : Robertson may not be the biggest player on the field, but it's not always about the size of the dog. Sometimes, it's about the fight inside that dog. And from what I can see, Amik Robertson comes to play every down.
WHAT A START ‼️ 📺 #WASvsDET @wusa9 pic.twitter.com/0MxloPVkd7
Jaden Bradley While Jaden Bradley's roster chances are as slim as that room is deep on the depth chart, his performance Saturday was worth noting after bringing in two receptions on three targets for 42 yards, both on Washington's best offensive drive. Bradley also made a tremendous one-handed, 30-yard catch going to the ground while being held by the defender. Later in that same drive, Bradley grabbed a 12-yard reception and also recorded a special teams tackle in the game. Verdict : He did not change the roster math with his performance, but he did make the bottom of that room a bit more uncomfortable as he brought attention to himself once more.
JADEN. BRADLEY. 📺 #WASvsDET @wusa9 pic.twitter.com/P3BjL7SG6A
Joshua Josephs Joshua Josephs has been building on days since the summer started and is now becoming a player fans recognize as a developmental pass rusher with upside. Josephs was involved in the game's early drama after Amik Robertson created a fumble; Josephs recovered it in the end zone for the touchdown. Even after getting caught peeking too far into the backfield on Josh Dobbs' 50-yard read option run, he continues to find his way in and around the football. Verdict : Joshua Josephs continues to be my surprise of camp and the draft so far. He is still ultra-raw, so the process may take a while to get him where he needs to be.
Robert Henry Jr. No one had the complete opposite day from the opener quite like Robert Henry Jr. did against the Lions. After having 75 yards and a touchdown against the Dolphin , and that most of hte defenisve , Henry left Detroit with minus three yards on four attempts. The offensive line didn't help much with their run blocking either, but Henry also fumbled a kick return with Washington down four and getting the ball back for its final possession with 2:15 remaining. Verdict : While the rushing total is bad, it could have been overlooked given the offensive line's issues, but the kickoff fumble is close to a fatal flaw with as much emphasis as these guys put on special teams and securing the football. Julian Good-Jones Julian Good-Jones has done more to hurt his situation over the last two weeks than to help, even with what is likely his career lying in his lap currently. In the first half, he allowed a linebacker through who likely should have gotten a sack, but Jayden Daniels was able to get rid of the ball fast enough to avoid it. In the second half, he false-started on third-and-10 during Kaliakmanis’ best drive, creating third-and-15 before the quarterback eventually bailed the offense out. Verdict : It's still odd to me that Matt Gulbin isn't being given more of a shot at this position, at least as the primary backup to Nick Allegretti. The fact that Good-Jones is not that guy, but they keep putting him out there over Gulbin, tells me who they trust, but that doesn't help block people. Something needs to be done here as the red flags are waving. Sam Hartman While Sam Hartman played decently, going 9-of-11 for 67 yards, Kaliakmanis clearly outplayed him in a game where the team was trying to gauge what it had in a direct comparison. Hartman's drives produced short gains, while Kaliakmanis generated 162 yards and repeatedly attacked the defense downfield. Hartman’s second-quarter sack-fumble did not help his situation. Verdict : While Sam Hartman did not lose his developmental QB role Saturday, Kaliakmanis clearly gained ground and, at this point, has just about won the competition. Washington’s Rush Game — On Both Sides of the Ball No matter what looked good, Washington's collective problem was all across the board. The team had severe issues with the rush game on both sides of the ball Saturday. Offensively, the team rushed it 17 times for 35 yards, which is a 2.1-yard average, good enough to get even the best back a seat on the bench. Rookie Kaytron Allen led Washington with 30 yards on 10 carries. Defensively, the team allowed 169 yards rushing on 35 attempts, which is a really bad 4.8 yards per carry, while giving up nine rushing first downs and allowing both of their touchdowns on the ground. It should be noted that 50 of those yards did come on Dobbs' untouched touchdown run, and that most of Washington's defensive front did not play . Verdict : Unknown at this point. Washington played this game with much of their starting defensive front on the sideline.
GO DJ ‼️ pic.twitter.com/yVDlNUGgGO
Washington can legitimately take serious positives from the five sacks, the now-six preseason takeaways, and several young players standing out through two exhibition games, even if the last one was a loss. title: Everything Dan Quinn Said After Commanders’ Preseason Loss to Lions
full_text:
The Washington Commanders lost their second preseason game to the Detroit Lions, 17-13, on Saturday. After the game, Quinn discussed the offensive line, quarterback competition, defensive takeaways, Amik Robertson, Jaden Bradley, and more. Here is everything Quinn said after the loss:
"Offensively, a few of the explosive passes. Negative-wise, there's a lot to be desired run game-wise, offensively. Didn't like the pass pro, obviously, on the first series. And then the penalties, especially in the return game, that kept pushing us back. And that is one of the things that we have hit the mark on a lot. So, to have some penalties, felt like the drive, now we're back to the 10, back four. And then the last piece, the third- and fourth-down execution. I thought we lost both sides of that and wasn't up to the level that I would like."
Just the way the game started offensively, was there any thought of having Jayden Daniels come out for a second series?
"No. Going into it, I knew this was, if it was going to be 10 plays or three plays, that's how we were going to do it. Same thing defensively. So, I just kind of stuck to the game plan of what we had. Fortunately, he's throwing an excellent camp, and so I've been pleased with what I've seen from him. It's important to get these looks, but I wanted to, if I set a plan up, I was going to stick to it."
Last week you talked about the defense always thinking turnover. What did you think of seeing that show up again to start the game?
“Yeah. To see that was a great play by Amik, and I know there was a big fight for the ball as it got towards the end. I think that Josephs was the one that ended up getting it. But even in there to go dig for it and battle, that was a big deal. And obviously with Quan having another one, that has to be just part of what we're doing and how we're thinking and the way we practice. So, I like seeing those. And I thought having some chances to get some fourth-down stops today, those are the ones I look back — I'm looking forward to watching the tape tonight."
What did you see from Sam Hartman and Athan Kaliakmanis over the last couple weeks, particularly in this game?
“Yeah. The thing that I liked, I did see some explosive plays that were shots down the field. I think one was to Nash, another one to Bradley. I liked the catch that went to Williams. So, I thought I'm seeing that in some man-to-man, to see some of the accuracy of where to go. So, that part I was pleased with. And when you play a lot of man-to-man, those are the opportunities that you want to get. So, they're battling for it. There'll be a bunch of things we're going to want to look at to keep digging in, and another game coming up. It's so important for them, honestly, in the game. For those guys, managing the clock, working it all, being in tough scenarios, feeling the rush — they don't do that in practice. So, the next practice, the next game, will also be super valuable for both of them."
What did you see from the offensive line, both from the group that started and the other combinations throughout the game?
“Yeah, there's a lot of groups that went in and out. And so, the first crew of Conerly and Cosmi, I thought I liked how they're playing together, their communication. And Sam's really having a good camp. He's maybe playing the best that I've seen him play in the couple, three years. His technique, he's on it. I like what I'm seeing on the outside at left tackle. So, we got work to do to figure out where we want to get to at center. But with a lot of people in there, it wasn't like a one line, two line. So, Wylie played some and then we moved. You probably saw different guys at left tackle, right tackle. We rotated guys at guard. So, today was about opportunities, giving guys their opportunities, and I'll look forward to taking a look."
How tricky is it to balance wanting Jayden Daniels to get work with knowing Week 1 is what matters?
“Yeah, you want to thread the needle as close as you can. And there's times in practice where he may take as many of the reps as he can. I think we had a tough practice Wednesday and Thursday, and he might have took 40, 45 of the plays, just runs, passes, just so he's getting into the game shape and the rhythm. So, it helps with the joint practices. He can take a lot of those. But, you know, all along the plan was to get him some work in this one, too.”
With the offense and defense only playing one series, what was the deciding factor in how much work you wanted them to get?
“I think it's important going through the whole process, getting ready to go. New looks, tackling, all the space to go. You'd love to break it up. Okay, you'd play eight-and-a-half plays, this guy plays some, but it's not really how it goes. So, I set the course of this is how we'd go, and then when we hit that, I said, okay, this is how we're going to go."
On Amik Robertson's competitiveness
"Yeah, I just think it speaks to the competitor of who he is. I love what he's added to our team. I love seeing him and Mike battle for it, but he is a legit dog-ass competitor. I love that he brings that."
What did you think of Jaden Bradley's catch?
"Yeah, it was fun. There was a lot of energy. I don't know if you guys could see it on the sideline, there was a lot of people yelling, ‘And-one.’ So, there's a foul. So, it was nice to see a deep play like that. And as a receiver, you want your chances for the shot play. So, yeah, the guys were excited for him on that one, and Nash as well."
Beyond the catch, what has Jaden Bradley done on special teams and elsewhere to catch your eye?
"He has, in terms of a competitive nature, and that was from the beginning. He wanted to return kicks. He wanted to be back for punt, knowing that there was going to be a spot for special teams. So, I like, JP, the way he's competing. And that's what's called upon. And so, then to be rewarded with a big play like that, just competing, he stands for that. And so, he's developing. Bobby's doing a good job with him of more and getting to the action. So, we like where he's headed."
From the first preseason game to today, what have you seen from Sonny Styles?
"Sonny. Yeah. So, I thought, one, he's in excellent shape. We had two really tough practices back-to-back. That was kind of the peak of camp for us into that space. Seeing him get vocal with the down guys, the communication has just ramped up, I felt, defensively over the last couple of days. Daronte has some checks that they get in and out of calls. And so, being in charge and doing that, I felt like that was at a higher level over the week. And I was certainly glad to see that."
How encouraging was it to see the front seven create pressure even with several players missing?
"Yeah, it's important because when you're trying to look at it to say, all right, who beat somebody in pressure? Was it singled up? Was it a pass stunt that got them there? But the execution of that improved pass rush-wise. I thought in Week 1, in the second half, it felt slower to go. And so, knowing Eric Henderson and their guys and Pags really dug in on that, I thought they took a step forward. And so, I expect that to go again.”
The defense has five takeaways through two preseason games. What will it take to translate that into the regular season?
"Yeah, I think number one, what I'd like to see more of is some forced fumbles into the contact. The second, the third guy in, more shots at it because that's all part of it. And we've been training hard in that way. And what sometimes happens in practice, you're thinking about it, and then you get into the game and you're just, okay, I'm on to the next play and thinking about the call. And I want to make sure, finish through the runner going all the way down and having that mindset to take your shot. So, I'm looking forward to seeing how many shots on the ball, batted passes, PBUs, punches at it that are there. Because the end result of two is nice, but I want to make sure…

title: Commanders Studs and Duds From First Half vs. Lions
full_text:
The Washington Commanders traveled to Detroit to take on the Lions for Preseason Game 2. But in reality, this was always going to be a mass evaluation. Washington’s defense was able to provide most of the first-half highlights, creating turnovers and consistently finding ways to pressure Detroit’s quarterbacks. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels played one series, in which the line did not look good. That said, here are the studs and duds from the first half of the game.
Stud No. 1 On the 2nd play, Amik Robertson made a sack of Lions backup quarterback Josh Dobbs around the left side, unblocked. The result of the play was a sack-fumble that rookie Joshua Josephs recovered for a touchdown. The Lions were called for an illegal procedure penalty on the play, which Washington declined. Robertson set the tone immediately, creating Washington’s first defensive touchdown opportunity just two plays into the game.
WHAT A START ‼️ 📺 #WASvsDET @wusa9 pic.twitter.com/0MxloPVkd7
Stud No. 2 Josephs recovered the Dobbs fumble for a touchdown. Impressed by how he fights at the line before dropping back into coverage. His combination of speed and awareness is a bit scary, but raw still. Josephs bit on a zone-read that Dobbs took for a long 50-Yard TD later in the first. Together, those two plays were a good snapshot of Josephs right now: disruptive enough to make game-changing plays, but still developing the discipline that comes with experience. Stud No. 3 Quan Martin made an interception on a pass that Dobbs should never have thrown from back across his body. Martin seems locked in so far this preseason with his second interception in as many games. Stud No. 4 At the beginning of the second quarter, T. J. Maguranyanga had a sack of Luke Altmyer that led to a nine-yard loss for Detroit. This is huge for TJ, who is trying to make the roster, while also being eligible via the International Pathway Program (IPP) . Stud No. 5 Javontae Jean-Baptiste sacked Altmyer with nine minutes left in the second. This is exactly the type of play he needed to keep his name fresh in the discussion.
Dud No. 1 Center Julian Good-Jones almost gave up a sack right through the A-gap on play one. This is bad for Good-Jones at a moment when the spotlight is shining the brightest. The team has to do something at this spot, and soon. Dud No. 2 John Bates gave up a sack on play-action. He just could not hold his block. Bates recently returned from a hamstring injury, but not being able to hold blocks isn't normally something that feels normal to write next to his name.
GO DJ ‼️ pic.twitter.com/yVDlNUGgGO
Dud No. 3 The offensive line was a disappointment overall, but Nicholas Petit-Frere gave up a sack of Sam Hartman, who fumbled. If simply losing the rep wasn't bad enough, Hartman losing the ball was the kicker. Thankfully, the half was almost over. For Petit-Frere, it's a bad look at a time when the team is looking for reliable reserves.
Van Jefferson limps off the field and is being looked at by trainers
The team had issues stopping the run and protecting the quarterback, with the starting offense playing only three snaps. It was not an impressive half offensively. The defense was able to keep things level with two turnovers, including one that resulted in a touchdown. title: Amik Robertson Remembers Jayden Daniels Being a ‘Headache’ for Lions — Commanders Daily
full_text:
For Amik Robertson , returning to Detroit on Saturday brings mixed emotions, but he has a much different perspective heading back there with Jayden Daniels as a teammate , rather than an opponent. Robertson was part of the 2024 Lions defense that faced Daniels in Washington's divisional-round game that the Commanders won by two touchdowns. When Robertson was asked what he remembered most about preparing for Daniels , his response was direct: "F****ng Headache." "A f****ng headache. It was a headache, bro. A quarterback that young, of course, we saw what he did at LSU. I'm a Louisiana guy. I watch LSU. But to see him do that at the next level, you're not surprised, but you're like, ‘Wow,’ right? You're like, man, to see he's that young, to be able to go out there and be able to see the game, slow the game down," Robertson said. "For a rookie, it's not too many quarterbacks that can come out there and do that. And just watching tape on him, we game-planned for him the whole week. I mean, it didn't work, but we game-planned for him the whole week, man. And he was at the biggest stage, and he was able to be successful. Like I tell everybody, I'm just glad I'm on this team now."
What Commanders CB and former Detroit Lion Amik Robertson thought of Jayden Daniels when facing him in the 2024 divisional playoffs … 😂 pic.twitter.com/xN8Fq45atv
Now, after spending an entire training camp watching him work, Robertson believes that Daniels' desire to be perfect is one of the traits behind what Detroit experienced firsthand in the playoffs. Robertson used Daniels' lone interception in camp to make his point more clear, saying Daniels was visibly frustrated after throwing the pick because of the standard he holds himself to. "But he was hot about that. But that just goes to show you how he attacks his work each and every day," said Robertson. "He wants to be perfect. He wants to be the best. He feels like when he makes a mistake, he let the team down. But of course, he's not letting us down. We're always rooting for him. We're always going to run through a wall for him as well. But that just shows you how much he wants to be great." These days, it's no longer Robertson's job to solve the problems Daniels presents, and he gets to watch the quarterback progress through his habits daily. Robertson credits the Lions with helping him rediscover himself as a player and putting him on a larger stage, but understands he wears Burgundy and Gold now. "When I think about it, Detroit was a team that really helped me find myself again, right? A team that believed in me, a team that put me on a bigger stage and believed in me." Saturday will mark an odd full-circle moment for Amik Robertson as he returns to Detroit alongside the quarterback who once gave his former defense a "f****ng headache."
Laremy Tunsil may not be a participant in Saturday's game while he recovers from a triceps injury , but that did not stop him from receiving recognition from the NFLPA, which named Tunsil its offseason Community MVP Friday for his annual Single Mothers’ Wellness Event through Divine Tree. The event was designed to give single mothers a day focused entirely on their own well-being, including a styling suite, relaxation lounge, guided yoga, and wellness and beauty gifts. While Washington waits to get its starting left tackle back on the field, Tunsil’s latest recognition highlights the impact he continues making away from it.

Reaves comes from a military family; his father served in the U.S. Army and his mother in the U.S. Air Force. For Reaves, he wasn't sure what to expect: "At first, I didn’t know what to expect. Me knowing a lot about what was going on down in D.C. and how much history there is down there, I was kind of unsure of what I was going to be looking at," said Reaves. "Then, getting down there and getting to see it all—and how they’ve meshed it up and blended it so well with what is already down there and part of the historical side of the capital—it was really cool, man." title: 5 Biggest Questions Still Unanswered Entering Commanders Preseason Week 2
full_text:
The Washington Commanders find themselves in a position where they've learned quite a bit from training camp and the opening preseason game , but still have several of their more important roster questions unsettled. While injuries have certainly wreaked havoc , particularly in the trenches on both sides of the ball, along with the running back situation, other competition has just failed to supply a clear winner yet. Below are the five questions Saturday's second preseason game against the Detroit Lions can either begin answering or further complicate things when final roster cut-day arrives.
The center position has become more than a question mark at this point after projected starter Nick Allegretti missed most of camp ; Julian Good-Jones absorbed the majority of that load, while rookie Matt Gulbin continues to make his own push. The problem is, Good-Jones didn't look very, well, good in the first preseason game against Miami. That doesn't change how the staff views him, but it certainly suggests they aren't comfortable with him as the center. Allegretti returned to practice this week, but before that session ended, he had what Quinn called "a light setback," which causes even more delays in getting Jayden Daniels ready for the season, as the two must build some sort of chemistry. Allegretti's injury opened the door for Quinn to notice the guys behind him. "Both guys are really starting to make a move," Quinn said, with Gulbin coming off a clean preseason opener and Good-Jones having accumulated significant work since early in camp. "So, over the next two weeks, or maybe two and a half weeks, we’ll call it," he said. "I’d like to see what that rotation looks like with the three of these guys." The Real Question : Can Gulbin or Good-Jones create actual separation while Allegretti’s availability remains inconsistent?
In many ways, Washington will not be able to replace Laremy Tunsil. His leadership abilities and capabilities as a teammate are unmatched in most locker rooms. When you add in the fact that Allegretti is also missing from the situation, things start to get dicey. Shifting Brandon Coleman over to left tackle was the right move , but if he was well on the way to winning that job at left guard, Washington is now looking at a left side that is completely changed from where it started. Signing Daniel Brunskill, Nicholas Petit-Frere, and Max Scharping gives Washington more experienced options, but Quinn has already stated those guys were brought in to increase the competitiveness at the bottom of the depth chart, not replace Tunsil. "We actually wanted to see if we could raise up the competition level in that back group, to see who could go," he said. "It was not injury-related. It was more like, ‘let’s battle this thing out and see where we can go.’" The Real Question : Who will step up and be the leader on the offensive line in 2026?
This will be a tough one to call. Running back was already viewed as one of the top skill position groups Washington has had before Robert Henry Jr. had the game he did in the opener . Between the two rookies, the running back competition tightened up overnight after Henry ran 12 times for 75 yards and a touchdown, while Allen carried 23 times for 85 yards and a score against Miami. The performance left Quinn impressed: "As far as Robert goes, he and Kaytron both, I thought, had a nice night," he said. "Also, Jerome Ford went out. We had three backs for the game, and so when Jerome was out, there was really no flinch from these guys playing on teams, returning, and so that was a good sign." This week, not only is Jeremy McNichols unavailable , but so is Rachaad White, leaving the door wide open once again for the healthy backs who play to gain ground in the competition. The Real Question : Which healthy running back will take advantage of their situation the most?
All 12 of rookie RB Robert Henry Jr's carries from Friday night. More impressive from the endzone view. He ran with vision and made some big time cuts. I love the stutter step that helps him get the edge on the 22-yard TD. pic.twitter.com/Y3T0Ow0GUL
This week, defensive tackle Johnny Newton received horrible news about his injured pectoral muscle. Newton will miss a significant amount of time, leaving Washington down a man in their rotation . Of course, their rotation also includes Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw, Charles Omenihu, Tim Settle when healthy, Byron Cowart, Maurice Hurst II, and others. Truth is, Commanders GM Adam Peters stacked that room with talent, but none gives Washington the same interior disruption Newton was expected to provide. Omenihu could be effective, given his ability to move all along the defensive front. Washington loaded the deck for new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones to use multiple fronts, and will now have to employ an option as the primary. Newton produced five sacks and 27 pressures last season, so replacing the number of snaps he played is considerably easier than replacing the interior pass-rush disruption those snaps produced. The Real Question : With the depth Washington has on the defensive front, can someone they trust step into a pass-rusher's role?
Marcus Mariota’s MCL sprain may have removed him from being able to guide the offense, but in the process, Washington will be able to evaluate what they have in rookie Athan Kaliakmanis versus what they've been able to develop in Sam Hartman since he signed with the team as a UDFA in 2024. This competition now has merit; if Mariota cannot go in Week 1, the winner of this roster battle would be one step behind starting quarterback Jayden Daniels . Right now, I'd say Kaliakmanis has the advantage, as Hartman just hasn't done enough to make me see much improvement or to believe that he is better than Kaliakmanis. The Real Question : Can the rookie stay calm enough to outplay a Sam Hartman who will be playing for his football life?
Athan Kaliakmanis links up with Jacoby Jones! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZHCLtaTx8o
While Washington doesn't need the answer to all five of these questions Saturday, they do need to see progress. The Lions mean nothing outside of being the opposing team; the focus is elsewhere because the center position, the reconstructed offensive line, the running back room, Newton’s replacement plan, and backup quarterback all need additional evidence. title: Johnny Newton's Injury Further Exposes Commanders' Poor 2024 NFL Draft Returns
full_text:
The Washington Commanders hoped to leverage the 2026 preseason to vault back into the rest of the NFL's good graces, but the early wear and tear of training camp action has put the team with plenty to prove through the wringer.
They're seemingly losing a notable contributor every day over their slow succumbing to the injury bug, making it easy for a young defensive tackle like Jer'Zhan "Johnny" Newton to get lost in the shuffle while more notable contributors like recent entrant running back Rachaad White and starting center Nick Allegretti deal with their own ailments, but his is an absence to worry about.
Now the question is how the Commanders' coaching staff plans to fill their needs on the fly, and why they worry that they don't have enough pieces worthy of deployment. Washington is teetering on a hole of their own making, another reminder that NFL Draft returns will always come back to bite those who don't strengthen their ranks the old-fashioned way.
The Commanders had big things planned for Newton entering year three. The defensive tackle seemed to be slowly coming into his own as a rotational sophomore, tallying five sacks and 27 pressures across 17 appearances and two starts- just enough to keep fans hopeful that he could continue ascending with another offseason of work.
He'd yet to tab a full-time starting role alongside positional peer Tim Settle , but his recently announced pectoral muscle tear has already required surgery while demanding a lengthy rehabilitation process. With Week 1 of the regular season waiting just weeks away, it seems safe to assume that getting anything out of Newton in 2026 will be a win for the Commanders' thinly spread roster .
Sources: #Commanders DT Johnny Newton underwent surgery for a torn pectoral muscle and is expected to miss significant time. The former Illinois standout has 82 tackles, 7 sacks (5 last year), 2 forced fumbles, and a fumble recovery in 33 career games. pic.twitter.com/OVq4mvoxYT
He really needed a step-up campaign, especially considering what he represents to the franchise as a patience-testing prospect. Newton was the second player ever scooped up by this front office, right behind star quarterback Jayden Daniels , earning the 36th-overall selection out of the 2024 NFL Draft .
That could have been a vicious one-two punch for Commanders fans looking to bolster both sides of the ball, a potentially defining combination even if Newton were half as productive as Daniels was during his Offensive Rookie of the Year-winning effort . Alas, not all timelines add up as outsiders hope, leaving Newton to continue attempting to prove himself as a workable asset to a business-minded front office and a less-than-complacent fan base.
What's less forgivable, though, is the trend that Newton unknowingly contributed to among new-coming Commanders.
Outside of Daniels and his regular star flashes, that year's draft class remains a mishmash of semi-playable talents who've yet to convincingly win over the football-consuming populous. Fellow draftees like Mike Sainristil , Luke McCaffrey , and Brandon Coleman remain ancillary pieces who occasionally look disruptive, but are generally lacking much consistency to go around.
He'll still have a chance to earn his stripes upon his return, whenever that's mapped out to be, but the Commanders' need for Newton goes beyond their patchy, reworked defense. Good teams like the 12-5 2024 squad stay on top by continually connecting on their draft swings, and Daniels ' incandescent upside has successfully distracted many viewers from the slew of questionable evaluations that led the organization to this point.

title: Commanders Rookie QB Athan Kaliakmanis Making Strong Push Up Depth Chart
full_text:
Anyone running down the Washington Commanders' depth chart will have a harder time finding a surer thing than Jayden Daniels as the squad's starting quarterback.
Just two years into the former Heisman winner's NFL career, Daniels is already the face of the legacy franchise. Reaching such esteemed ground isn't always hard at the game's most critical position, but Daniels has already backed up his lofty draft intrigue with an Offensive Rookie of the Year win and multiple seasons of star-caliber play.
As is the case on most rosters around the league, Washington's evaluators have seen little reason to invest heavily in their quarterback depth beyond Daniels. But given the injuries and absences that decorated his sophomore campaign, a quick roll call down his list of understudies is worth noting, especially considering some other inter-positional developments that have peppered ongoing training camp and preseason festivities.
Daniels has always had Marcus Mariota at his side throughout his young Commanders stint, and you can do a lot worse than the well-traveled backup who's still happy to step up and distribute the football whenever he gets a shot. Just last season, he took advantage of Daniels' ailments by making eight starts in 11 appearances, passing for 10 touchdowns in a pinch.
But following Mariota's MCL sprain , as well as the continued demise of Sam Hartman's attempt to stick around as Daniels' locker room buddy, a new challenger appears to be complicating the quarterback pecking order. Athan Kaliakmanis has approached the preseason with momentum, and he has the chance to ride his strong strides into an upset finish as the squad’s QB3 by the time the Commanders officially kick off next month, perhaps even serving as the emergency QB2 if Mariota is not ready.
Few fans were overly familiar with Kaliakmanis ' game before the Commanders hosted the Miami Dolphins for a D.C. preseason debut last week.
The quarterback, who'd previously split his four collegiate seasons between Minnesota and Rutgers, threw enough touchdowns on impressive-enough completion numbers to woo the Commanders' more devoted scouts. He heard his name called on Day 3 of this past NFL Draft, going down as the seventh pick of the ordeal's final round in commencing his professional journey.
He was a perfectly serviceable game manager as a steadily improving Big Ten arm, combining positive release power and positional size to reach a 20:7 touchdown-to-interception ratio as a senior. Even if his spotty accuracy and decision-making held him back from earning a handshake and hat earlier in this past draft, he's unafraid to put the ball in play downfield, and there's value in that fearlessness for rookie backups looking to make the most of their snaps.
Kaliakmanis wasn't able to post any otherworldly stats in his preseason opener, with the fourth-stringer splitting opportunities with Hartman after Mariota left the 20-7 win early . At the very least, he hit on his easier reads and had no problem finding Jacoby Jones deep out of play-action for one of the matchup's bigger completions.
Athan Kaliakmanis links up with Jacoby Jones! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZHCLtaTx8o
In the few days since he could perform in front of referees and cameras, his in-house standing seems to have ballooned. He's taken on some second-team reps in practices since that Dolphins exhibition , accepting his role as the top non-Daniels quarterback prospect, and should Mariota remain unavailable for Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles, expect Kaliakmanis to look ready to go as Daniels ' next-man-up.
Things are going about as well as anyone could have hoped for the Commanders' seventh-round draftee by this point. He never had a shot at unseating the franchise's centerpiece, but he seems to have carved out a more straightforward route to tasting live NFL action than he was facing out of the draft amid complications among his peers.

title: Dan Quinn Says ‘Good Amount’ of Washington's Starters Will Play vs. Lions — Commanders Daily
full_text:
Many of the players who sat out the preseason opener will get work against Detroit, according to Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn. The Commanders held 26 players out of the first game against Miami , making Saturday a much better chance to evaluate some of the roster's more well-known pieces. Quinn used a portion of his presser on Thursday to address the situation: "A lot of the guys who sat out for Miami will get an opportunity to get some work for this week," he said. "All obviously different amounts." That sounds like a very different mindset coming from Quinn this week. While Quinn has discussed different players participating, he has stopped short of naming quarterback Jayden Daniels in the conversation. Quinn has said the Daniels decision will be handled separately and will depend on the condition of those around him, especially the banged-up offensive line . Even if Daniels does not play, the Lions game will give a better look at some of the projected starters. Saturday will be the biggest step the team has taken toward the regular season. Snaps may vary from player to player, but overall, Quinn has made clear that Saturday will look very different than last Friday night in terms of who actually takes the field.
🕺🕺🕺 @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/VLzkpyM1Zd
One group Quinn mentioned specifically: the receivers. That group remains healthy and deep behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, which makes the evaluation process both easier to do and harder to figure out the end with the amount of competition . Quinn specifically mentioned two receivers who caught his attention against Miami. "I liked what I saw with some of the receivers from the opening game. Lane was somebody that, in the first game, I thought had some nice catches, some nice movements. Same with Van." While Lane and Jefferson are at different spots in their careers, both are trying to give Washington reasons to keep them involved in a receiver room where there are more viable options than available roles. Saturday will give the staff more chances to evaluate every aspect, not only catching, but also route execution, blocking, play on special teams, and how each receiver fits with different personnel packages, including different quarterbacks. With only two games remaining in the preseason , the competition is currently at its maximum level with this group, making the Detroit game the best chance for Washington's receivers to move from promising camp work into something that can actually change where they stand on the depth chart.
